problem:
Across Benin City, Edo State, and many other communities in Nigeria, maintaining clean, hygienic, and healthy homes, workplaces, institutions, and public spaces remains a significant challenge. Many households, offices, schools, commercial establishments, and newly completed buildings lack consistent access to reliable, affordable, and professionally delivered cleaning services. In other cases, individuals and organizations do not have the time, appropriate equipment, trained personnel, or specialized cleaning materials required to maintain proper hygiene standards.
The consequences of poor sanitation extend far beyond an untidy appearance. Dirty homes, offices, schools, and commercial spaces can become breeding grounds for bacteria, fungi, dust mites, mould, and disease-carrying pests such as mosquitoes, rodents, flies, and cockroaches. These conditions can increase exposure to respiratory problems, skin infections, allergic reactions, food contamination, unpleasant odours, and other hygiene-related illnesses. Where waste is improperly handled or toilets, kitchens, drains, and frequently touched surfaces are inadequately cleaned, the health and safety of residents, workers, customers, and visitors may be placed at risk.
Unclean clothing also presents serious personal hygiene and health concerns. Clothes that are not properly washed, dried, treated, or stored may retain sweat, dirt, bacteria, allergens, and fungi. This can contribute to skin irritation, rashes, fungal infections, persistent body odour, discomfort, and reduced personal confidence. The problem is particularly significant for busy professionals, families, students, hospitality businesses, and other customers who depend on reliable laundry services but frequently experience poor garment handling, inconsistent quality, damaged clothing, delayed delivery, and excessively long turnaround times.
Post-construction cleaning is another major and often underestimated challenge. Newly built or renovated properties are commonly left with fine dust, cement deposits, paint stains, adhesive residue, broken materials, packaging waste, and other construction debris. Ordinary sweeping and mopping are usually insufficient to prepare such properties for safe occupation. Fine construction dust and chemical residues may remain on surfaces and circulate within the building, potentially affecting air quality and causing discomfort, irritation, or respiratory difficulties. This work requires trained professionals, suitable equipment, specialized chemicals, and careful attention to surfaces that may be damaged by the wrong cleaning method.
Pest infestation further threatens the health and comfort of households and businesses. Mosquitoes, cockroaches, rodents, bedbugs, ants, and other pests can contaminate food, damage property, interrupt business activities, disturb sleep, and spread disease. However, many residents and organizations struggle to find fumigation services that are dependable, properly executed, safety-conscious, and supported by clear instructions for preparation and re-entry.
Beyond physical health, dirty and disorganized surroundings can negatively affect mental and emotional well-being. Living or working in an unhygienic environment may create feelings of stress, embarrassment, discomfort, frustration, and loss of control. It can reduce concentration, lower morale, disrupt productivity, and make homes and workplaces less welcoming. Likewise, wearing poorly maintained clothing may affect a person's self-esteem, confidence, social interaction, professional appearance, and willingness to participate fully in work, school, religious, and social activities.
The sensory quality of an environment is also frequently neglected. Many cleaning providers concentrate only on removing visible dirt without considering the complete experience of the customer. Persistent unpleasant odours can make an otherwise cleaned environment feel uncomfortable, while fragrances that are too harsh or unsuitable for a particular space may cause irritation or dissatisfaction. There is therefore a need for thoughtful scent application that complements cleanliness and creates a fresh, calm, and welcoming atmosphere without overwhelming the occupants.
At the same time, youth unemployment and financial hardship remain serious challenges in Edo State and across Nigeria. Many university students and young adults require flexible and dignified work opportunities to meet their educational expenses and basic needs, especially when their parents or relatives cannot provide adequate financial support. The shortage of such opportunities can increase dependency, interrupt education, deepen poverty, and prevent young people from acquiring practical workplace skills.
These problems are closely interconnected. Poor access to professional cleaning affects public health, personal dignity, workplace productivity, property value, environmental safety, and quality of life. Unemployment affects the ability of young people to sustain themselves and contribute meaningfully to the economy. There is therefore a clear need for a professional environmental hygiene company that can deliver dependable cleaning, laundry, post-construction cleaning, and fumigation services while simultaneously creating employment, supporting young people, and contributing to cleaner and healthier communities.
solution:
Kleentrance was founded to provide a clean transformation to residents, households, businesses, institutions, and property owners in Benin City, Edo State, and beyond. Our mission is not simply to remove dirt but to restore cleanliness, tranquillity, confidence, safety, and comfort through comprehensive environmental hygiene services.
We provide professional home and commercial cleaning, post-construction cleaning, fumigation and pest-control support, and high-quality laundry services. These services are designed to address the different but connected hygiene needs of individuals and organizations through one dependable company. By combining trained personnel, appropriate cleaning materials, specialized chemicals, suitable equipment, careful supervision, and strong attention to detail, we help customers maintain spaces and clothing that are clean, safe, presentable, and comfortable.
Our home and commercial cleaning services focus on creating hygienic environments through thorough dust removal, surface cleaning, floor care, toilet and kitchen sanitation, disinfection of frequently touched areas, odour control, and proper waste handling. We carefully assess each location because different surfaces and problem areas require different treatment methods. Areas that require special chemicals are handled with suitable products and procedures to achieve effective results while reducing the risk of damage.
Our post-construction cleaning service prepares newly built and renovated properties for safe and comfortable use. We remove construction dust, cement residue, paint stains, adhesive marks, debris, and other materials left behind by building work. Rather than applying the same method to every surface, we consider the nature of tiles, glass, fittings, walls, floors, and other finishes before selecting the appropriate equipment and chemical treatment. This helps protect the property while delivering a complete transformation.
Through our fumigation services, we help households and organizations manage pests that threaten health, property, comfort, and business operations. We approach each assignment according to the type of infestation and the needs of the premises, while providing customers with appropriate safety and preparation guidance. Our aim is to create cleaner and more secure environments in which families, employees, customers, and visitors can live and operate with greater peace of mind.
Our laundry operation provides fast, professional, and reliable garment care for busy individuals, families, students, and businesses. We understand that clean clothing affects more than appearance; it supports personal hygiene, comfort, confidence, and professional presentation. We therefore prioritize proper sorting, washing, treatment, drying, ironing, folding, and careful handling, using quality materials and trained workers. Our goal is to deliver immaculate results within a dependable turnaround time while preserving the condition of each customer's clothing.
A distinctive part of the Kleentrance experience is our practical knowledge and intentional use of scent technology. We select fragrances according to the nature of the service, the type of environment, and the desired customer experience. We understand that cleanliness should be both visible and pleasantly experienced. Appropriate scents can help create an atmosphere that feels fresh, peaceful, welcoming, and cared for. Our approach is careful and balanced, recognizing that fragrances should complement a clean environment rather than overpower it or cause discomfort.
Through these services, Kleentrance restores more than physical cleanliness. A properly cleaned home can give families peace of mind. A clean workplace can improve employee morale, customer perception, and productivity. Fresh and properly maintained clothing can improve self-esteem, social confidence, and professional appearance. A pest-controlled property can improve comfort and reduce hygiene risks. These outcomes reflect our belief that cleanliness contributes meaningfully to dignity, well-being, productivity, and spiritual peace—captured in the principle that cleanliness is next to godliness.
Kleentrance currently operates through a lean, home-based business model, allowing us to deliver professional cleaning, laundry, post-construction cleaning, and fumigation services across Benin City while keeping operating costs low. Customers primarily book our services through phone calls, WhatsApp, Instagram, and referrals, enabling us to validate market demand without the overhead of a physical commercial location. This approach has allowed us to focus on delivering excellent service, building customer trust, and generating repeat business as we prepare for our next phase of growth.
Our impact also extends to employment and youth empowerment. Since inception, Kleentrance has engaged 45 university students through flexible contract work, alongside five full-time employees. Many of which are students who need flexible income opportunities to support their tuition, educational materials, transportation, feeding, accommodation, and other basic needs when family support is insufficient. Through dignified work, practical training, and income-generating opportunities, we help young people remain productive, gain experience, develop professional discipline, and reduce their vulnerability to poverty.
In this way, Kleentrance contributes to Nigeria's economic development while supporting several United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG 1: No Poverty, SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being, SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation, SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth, and SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities. Our work promotes healthier living conditions, supports sanitation, creates jobs, strengthens local economic participation, and contributes to cleaner communities.
To meet growing demand and expand our impact, Kleentrance is seeking grants, sponsorships, strategic partnerships, equity investment, and shareholder participation. The support received will help us acquire modern cleaning and laundry equipment, improve transportation and logistics, increase operational capacity, strengthen staff training and safety procedures, adopt more environmentally responsible products, improve service delivery, establish additional service centres, and create more employment opportunities.
With the right support, Kleentrance can serve more homes, offices, schools, institutions, construction companies, hospitality businesses, and communities across Edo State and beyond. Our vision is to become a leading Nigerian environmental hygiene company known for reliability, quality, innovation, customer care, job creation, and measurable social impact.
Specific investment offers, partnership structures, equity arrangements, and other terms can be discussed directly with interested grant providers, sponsors, investors, shareholders, and strategic partners.

mvpDescription:
Joja Farm MVP: 50-head startup version*
Component	MVP Spec	Why this is "minimum"
**Herd**	10 sows + 1 boar + 38 grower spaces	10 sows = ~200 piglets/year. Enough for cash flow but not overwhelming. Buy bred gilts to get piglets in 4 months vs waiting 1 year
**Housing**	Hoop barn or pole barn, 1500 sq ft total. Deep bedding system	$8k-$15k build vs $50k+ confinement. Deep bedding = no lagoons, manure handled dry
**Feed system**	Hand-feed with bulk bins + used feeder troughs	Auto-feeders later. Start manual to watch intake + health closely
**Water**	Nipple drinkers + 1000L tank with float valve	No expensive plumbing runs yet
**Sales channel**	1 abattoir contract + 1 monthly farm-gate sale	Prove both wholesale + direct-to-consumer work before scaling
**Goats + Fish**	5 does + 1 buck, 1 small 20x20ft pond for tilapia/catfish	Just enough to test the "Hoof & Fin" cross-sell without extra labor
**Labor**	You + 1 part-time worker, 3 hrs/day	Keeps labor <15% of costs at MVP stage
**Record keeping**	Notebook + Google Sheet: FCR, ADG, deaths, sales	Data is your traction proof. No fancy software yet
*What this MVP proves in 6-9 months*
1. *Can you raise pigs to 250 lbs in <180 days* with <3.2 FCR?
2. *Will people actually buy* from Joja at prices that cover costs?
3. *Do pigs + goats + fish work together* without disease/extra hassle?
4. *Cash flow*: Can 1 batch pay for the next batch’s feed?

*What’s NOT in the MVP*
- Breeding your own replacements — buy gilts first
- On-farm butchery — too much regulation/cost
- Agritourism, bacon smoking, etc — cool, but phase 2
- 50 actual market hogs day 1 — you’ll ramp to that

*Cost to hit MVP*: Roughly *$25k-$40k* total: stock $8k, housing $12k, feed for 6mo $10k, misc $5k. 

*Goal*: If after 2 batches you’re at 15%+ gross margin and sold out every pig, your MVP worked. Then you scale to full 50-head capacity.

Want me to lay out the month-by-month timeline from empty barn to first sale for this MVP?
tractionMetric:
By *"key traction"* you likely mean the main metrics that prove your 50-head pig farm is working and ready to grow. Investors, lenders, or even you need these to track progress.

*Key traction metrics for a pig farm startup*
Metric	What it shows	Good target for 50-head farm
**Feed Conversion Ratio (FCR)**	Lbs of feed to gain 1 lb of weight	**2.8 - 3.2** for growers. Below 3.0 = excellent
**Average Daily Gain (ADG)**	How fast pigs grow	**1.6 - 1.9 lbs/day** from wean to market
**Mortality rate**	% pigs lost before market	**<5%** nursery, **<3%** grow-finish
**Pigs weaned/sow/year**	Breeding herd productivity	**22-26** if you have sows. Industry avg = 24
**Days to market**	Birth to 250-270 lbs	**160-180 days**. Faster = less feed cost
**Cost/lb produced**	Total cost ÷ total lbs sold	**$0.60-$0.80/lb** live weight depending on feed
**Sale price vs cost**	Margin health	**>20% gross margin** after feed, meds, labor
**Sell-through rate**	% of market-ready pigs sold within 1 week	**>90%**. Shows you have real buyers
*Non-financial traction that matters early*
1. *Buyer agreements*: 1-2 butchers or restaurants pre-committed to take your first 2 batches
2. *Repeat customers*: Direct-to-consumer buyers coming back for 2nd/3rd pork box
3. *Low vet intervention*: <2 treatments per 50 pigs = good health/biosecurity 
4. *Cycle consistency*: You hit target weights on schedule 3 batches in a row

*For Joja with pigs + goats + fish*: 
Your unique traction is *cross-sell rate*. Example: 40% of pork buyers also buy goat meat or tilapia. That proves your "Hoof & Fin" model works.

*Bottom line*: With 50 pigs, traction ≠ total revenue yet. Traction = "we can raise pigs efficiently and already have people who want more."

problem: Benin City generates over 200 thousand tons of recyclable waste every day, yet there is no coordinated system that connects households, community waste collectors, and recycling companies. As a result, recyclable materials are often mixed with general waste, disposed of in drains or landfills, or recovered inefficiently through informal channels. This creates environmental challenges, limits income opportunities for waste collectors, and leaves recycling businesses with an inconsistent supply of quality recyclable materials. Without an accessible and organized collection infrastructure, recycling remains inconvenient for residents and difficult to scale across the city.
solution: TrashPoint is a community-driven recycling network developed by Kyrus Recycling Ventures to make recycling simple, rewarding, and scalable. Rather than starting with technology, we first validated the model through an offline pilot that connects households with trained community aggregators and Kyrus' recycling operations. Residents are able to separate recyclable waste, hand it over through organized collection channels, and receive incentives for participating. The grant will enable us to transform this proven operational model into a digital platform that streamlines collections, rewards users, tracks recycling activity, and expands the network across Benin City, creating the infrastructure needed for mainstream recycling.
mvpDescription: Our MVP is an operational pilot of the TrashPoint recycling network that has been successfully tested offline. The pilot connects households with trained community aggregators, who collect and sort recyclable materials before transferring them to Kyrus Recycling Ventures for processing. Collections, user participation, and reward tracking are currently managed manually using structured operational processes. This pilot has validated demand, collection workflows, and the incentive model. The next phase is to digitize these operations through the TrashPoint platform, enabling user registration, collection requests, reward management, real-time tracking, and performance analytics.
tractionMetric: Successfully validated the TrashPoint model through an offline pilot in ekosodin community, Benin, engaging 15 households and 4 trained community aggregators, generating approximately ₦600,000 in monthly revenue while integrating recovered recyclables into Kyrus Recycling Ventures' processing operations. This demonstrates both market demand and the operational feasibility of a technology-enabled recycling network.
teamExpertise: Our five-member team combines practical experience across recycling operations, logistics, business development, finance, and community engagement. Since founding Kyrus Recycling Ventures in 2022, we have built and managed a functioning recycling operation that processes approximately 3.5 tonnes of PET waste monthly, serves established industrial buyers, and generates an average monthly revenue of ₦2 million. Through these operations, we identified the critical challenge of inconsistent recyclable material supply and developed the TrashPoint model, which has been successfully piloted by coordinating households, community aggregators, and our recycling facility using structured offline processes. This hands-on operational experience gives our team a deep understanding of the technical, commercial, and community requirements needed to build a scalable recycling infrastructure for Benin City.
challenges: Our biggest challenge is the lack of the infrastructure required to scale an organized recycling network across Benin City. While our offline pilot has demonstrated demand and operational viability, limited collection logistics, an insufficient number of community collection hubs, and the absence of a dedicated digital platform restrict our ability to serve more households efficiently. We also need to expand and equip our network of community aggregators and increase public awareness to encourage wider participation. Addressing these gaps will allow TrashPoint to transition from a successful pilot into a city-wide recycling infrastructure.

This investment will transform our validated offline pilot into a scalable, technology-enabled recycling network capable of serving significantly more communities across Benin City.
growthTargets: Over the next 12 months, we aim to transform TrashPoint from a validated offline pilot into a fully operational, technology-enabled recycling network across Benin City. revenueModel: TrashPoint operates a supply-driven revenue model by aggregating recyclable materials from households and community collection hubs and supplying them to recycling and manufacturing companies through Kyrus Recycling Ventures. socialImpact: TrashPoint creates environmental and economic value by making recycling more accessible while generating sustainable livelihoods within local communities. sustainabilityPath: TrashPoint is designed to become self-sustaining because it addresses a proven supply constraint within an existing and growing recycling market. problem:
Every year, over 400,000 Nigerian university students relocate to new campuses, and over 300,000 NYSC corpers are posted to unfamiliar states for their service year. Both groups face the same urgent, high-stakes problem: finding safe, affordable accommodation and basic essentials in a place they have never lived, often within days.
The current solutions are broken. Students rely on unverified WhatsApp broadcasts, exploitation by off-campus agents charging commission fees of 10–20% on top of rent, and word-of-mouth that rarely extends beyond their immediate social circle. NYSC corpers are even more vulnerable; they arrive in states with no social network at all and no reliable way to verify whether a landlord, listing, or agent is legitimate before paying.
The consequences are significant: students and corpers routinely fall victim to housing scams, overpay due to information asymmetry, or settle for unsafe accommodation because they lacked better options. There is no dedicated, verified, student-focused platform addressing this in Nigeria.
solution:
Habi Naija is Nigeria's first video-verified accommodation and student marketplace platform. A direct-connection platform that puts students and corpers in contact with landlords and sellers, without agents, without commission, and without the trust gap that makes the current process dangerous.
What makes Habi Naija different is the verification layer. Every listing on the platform requires a short video walkthrough uploaded by the property owner or seller. Our team reviews each video before the listing goes live; meaning every listing a student sees has been human-verified before they ever contact the owner.
Beyond accommodation, Habi Naija also serves as a peer marketplace where students can buy and sell items; furniture, electronics, textbooks, appliances and other things they need when they arrive and sell when they leave. This creates a circular economy within the student community and gives the platform utility beyond the one-time accommodation search.
The platform is free for students and corpers to use. Monetisation comes from Verified Property Partners (landlords and hostel operators who pay a subscription for priority placement and a verified badge) and Verified Sellers (consistent marketplace sellers who pay for featured listing access). This model aligns our incentives with quality: we only earn when supply-side participants want to stand out, which motivates them to list accurately.
mvpDescription:
Habi Naija is a fully deployed, live platform accessible at habinaija.ng. It is not a prototype or wireframe, it is a production application with the following capabilities:
For students and corpers (demand side):

Search and filter listings by state, city, price range, property type, category, and availability
View detailed listings with photos, video tours, amenities, and pricing
Contact owners directly through an in-platform messaging system with no third-party involvement
Save conversations and manage ongoing discussions through an inbox

For landlords and sellers (supply side):

Create accommodation or item listings through a guided 4-step process
Upload up to 5 photos and a mandatory video walkthrough (up to 60 seconds)
Manage their listings: edit, toggle availability, view enquiry messages

Trust and safety layer:

Every listing undergoes admin review before going live
Video verification is mandatory. No listing is approved without a video walkthrough
Users must accept messaging guidelines that disclose admin oversight before they can contact anyone
A report system allows users to flag suspicious listings or behaviour
Platform administrators can deactivate users, remove listings, and review flagged content

Platform infrastructure:

Live at habinaija.ng with SSL-secured HTTPS
Mozilla Observatory security grade: A+ (115/100)
Automated deployment pipeline (GitHub Actions to Contabo VPS)
Built with Laravel 11 (backend API) and Vue 3 (frontend)
tractionMetric:
Our primary traction metric at this stage is platform readiness and supply-side quality, measured by the number of verified listings live on the platform at launch. A student marketplace has no value to demand-side users (students) unless supply-side listings are available and verified. Our pre-launch focus has therefore been on recruiting Verified Property Partners and ambassadors who will seed the platform with quality listings before we open registration to the public.

Secondary metrics we will track from month one: registered users, listing creation rate, message send rate (a direct indicator of listing quality; users only message when they see something worth enquiring about), and listing-to-enquiry conversion rate.
teamExpertise:
We are a six-person founding team combining technical depth, creative capability, business strategy, and quality assurance to build and grow Habi Naija.
CTO / Technical Co-founder: Responsible for the full-stack architecture, development, and deployment of Habi Naija. Built the entire platform including the backend API (Laravel 11), frontend single-page application (Vue 3), database design, security implementation, CI/CD pipeline, and server infrastructure. The platform's A+ Mozilla Observatory security grade and complete feature set delivered in a short development timeline demonstrates both technical depth and execution speed.
Product Manager / Business Co-founder: Responsible for product strategy, user research, partnership development, and go-to-market planning. Identified the NYSC corper segment as an underserved high-value cohort, a strategic insight that differentiates Habi Naija from general property platforms. Leads ambassador recruitment and institutional partnership conversations.
Marketing Manager: Leads the platform's growth and user acquisition strategy. Responsible for digital campaigns, community outreach at universities and NYSC orientation camps, and managing the campus ambassador network. Brings experience in marketing to young Nigerian audiences across social media and on-ground activations.
Brand Identity Designer: Responsible for the visual language of Habi Naija across the platform, marketing materials, and social media. Ensures that every touchpoint communicates trust and reliability, two qualities that are essential for a platform where students make financial decisions based on what they see.
User Experience Analysts (x2): Responsible for testing every feature of the platform from a real user's perspective before and after each release. Identify usability gaps, edge cases, and accessibility issues that technical testing alone does not catch. Their work ensures the platform works as expected for a student in Edo, a corper in Kebbi, and a landlord in Lagos, not just on a developer's machine.
Together, the team has taken Habi Naija from concept to a fully deployed, security-hardened, live production application without external funding. This demonstrates capital efficiency and the ability to execute, two qualities that matter significantly at the scale-up stage this grant supports.
challenges:
1. Supply-side seeding (the cold start problem)
A marketplace needs both supply and demand to have value for either side. Our biggest challenge is seeding enough verified listings before we activate demand-side marketing. If students arrive and find an empty platform, we lose them permanently. The grant will allow us to pay stipends to campus ambassadors and property partner coordinators who will actively recruit and onboard landlords and sellers in each target location ahead of the student intake season.
2. Awareness in target communities
Nigerian students and corpers are not yet aware that Habi Naija exists. Building awareness within tight-knit university and NYSC communities requires a ground presence; physical activations, ambassador relationships, and word-of-mouth seeding. This requires people and materials on the ground, which requires funding.
3. Operational costs during zero-revenue phase
Server infrastructure, domain costs, and the admin overhead of manually reviewing every listing video (our quality guarantee) have real costs that cannot be deferred. Without funding, we are forced to limit how fast we can onboard new listings, which directly throttles our growth.
fundUsage:
The ₦5,000,000 grant will be deployed across six categories, each directly tied to the platform's path from zero users to sustainable traction.
Ambassador Stipends: ₦1,440,000. This covers 12 campus and NYSC ambassadors at ₦20,000 per month each for 6 months. Ambassadors are our ground-level supply acquisition force, responsible for recruiting verified landlords and sellers in their assigned locations. Without seeded listings, the platform has no value for students arriving to search. This is our highest-priority spend.
Marketing and Awareness: ₦1,500,000. This covers social media advertising targeted at university students and NYSC corpers, physical activations at campus gates and NYSC orientation camps, printed onboarding materials for landlords, and partnerships with student-facing content creators. Awareness spend is timed to university resumption and NYSC posting cycles for maximum impact.
Server and Infrastructure: ₦360,000. This covers 12 months of VPS hosting, domain renewal, CDN, email service, and uptime monitoring for the production platform. These are non-negotiable operational costs that must be covered for the platform to remain live and reliable.
Content Production: ₦400,000. This covers video explainers showing how the platform works, safety guides for students, and onboarding walkthroughs for property owners. Trust-building content is essential for a platform where users share accommodation details and negotiate financial arrangements with people they have never met.
Operations and Admin Overhead: ₦600,000. Every listing video must be reviewed by a team member before the listing goes live. This is our quality guarantee and it has a real labour cost. This allocation also covers customer support during the early growth phase and ambassador coordination.
Legal and Compliance: ₦200,000. This covers professional legal review of our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, and any business registration or compliance filings required as we formalise operations.
Contingency Reserve: ₦500,000. A buffer retained for unexpected costs in the first 6 to 9 months of live operations, including platform issues, ambassador replacement, or opportunity costs that arise during the growth phase.
Total: ₦5,000,000.
growthTargets:
By the end of the 12-month grant period, we target:

500 verified listings live on the platform across accommodation and items (this is our supply-side foundation metric)
3,000 registered users across our target states
300 monthly active users by month 12 (defined as users who searched, viewed a listing, or sent a message in the past 30 days)
15 Verified Property Partner subscriptions generating the first recurring revenue
12 active campus and NYSC ambassadors across 6 states
3 institutional partnerships with university student affairs offices or NYSC state coordinators who formally recommend Habi Naija to their students and corpers
Platform launch timed to coincide with at least one NYSC orientation camp cycle and one university resumption period to maximise demand-side activation

These targets are deliberately conservative. They are achievable without assuming viral growth. We are building for sustainable word-of-mouth within tight communities, not paid acquisition at scale.
revenueModel:
Habi Naija operates a freemium marketplace model with two primary revenue streams:
1. Verified Property Partner Subscription
Landlords, hostel operators, and accommodation managers who consistently list on the platform can subscribe to a Verified Property Partner plan. Benefits include a gold verification badge on all their listings, automatic featured placement (their listings appear first in search results), and access to listing performance analytics. Pricing is structured as a monthly or annual subscription.
2. Verified Seller Plan
Regular marketplace sellers (students selling furniture, electronics, or other items) can subscribe to the Verified Seller tier for featured listing placement and a seller verification badge. This is positioned as a low-cost subscription accessible to students with multiple items to sell.
Future revenue streams (Phase 2 and beyond):

Promoted listings: one-time payment for short-term featured placement without a full subscription
NYSC-specific partnerships: partnering with state NYSC coordinators or orientation camp providers
Institutional partnerships: universities recommending Habi Naija to incoming students as a verified housing resource

The free tier for basic listing and searching is intentional and permanent. It is our moat; agents cannot compete with a free platform. The paid tier rewards quality supply-side participants with visibility they cannot get elsewhere.
socialImpact:
Habi Naija addresses a specific and recurring form of economic vulnerability that affects over 700,000 young Nigerians every year. The students and NYSC corpers who must navigate unfamiliar housing markets without information, without protection, and without recourse when things go wrong.

Direct impact:

Reduces housing scam risk by requiring video verification of every listing before it goes live; a safeguard that does not exist on any current platform serving this demographic
Eliminates agent commission fees for students, saving each renter ₦10,000–₦50,000 per transaction that would otherwise go to an intermediary who added no verification value
Creates income for student-age sellers who can list items they no longer need to incoming students who need exactly those items; a peer economy within the student community

Systemic impact:

Increases price transparency in student housing markets where information asymmetry currently advantages agents and landlords over students
Builds a documented, searchable record of housing supply in university towns Currently this information exists only in informal networks
The NYSC ambassador model embeds platform representatives in every state where corpers serve, creating a national network of student-focused housing resources over time
sustainabilityPath:
Habi Naija becomes self-sustaining through the Verified Property Partner and Verified Seller subscription tiers, which are designed to activate naturally as the platform grows.
The economic logic is straightforward: as more students use Habi Naija to find accommodation and items, landlords who list on the platform get more enquiries and faster tenant acquisition. When they see this value, they become willing to pay a subscription for the enhanced visibility that the Verified Partner tier provides. The first 15 paying Property Partners at a conservative ₦10,000/month per subscription generates ₦150,000 monthly, enough to cover server and operational costs without external funding.
Beyond subscriptions, the platform's verified video content creates a quality flywheel: better verified listings attract more serious tenants, which makes the platform more valuable to landlords, which brings better listings, which attracts more tenants. problem:
Nigerian small and medium-sized businesses are the backbone of the country's economy, yet they operate in an information vacuum. In Nigeria alone, over 100,000 retail pharmacies and Patent & Proprietary Medicine Vendors manage complex, high-stakes inventory (drugs with expiry dates, controlled substances, temperature-sensitive stock) almost entirely on paper.
The consequences are severe and compounding. Without real-time inventory tracking, pharmacies routinely suffer losses from expired products they did not see coming. Without accurate sales and profit data, owners cannot distinguish which products are growing the business from which are quietly draining it. Without structured debt records, customer credit extended informally is rarely recovered systematically. And without any of this data formalized, these businesses remain completely invisible to banks and lenders — unable to access working capital no matter how long they have been in operation.

Existing software solutions in the market are either too generic to address pharmacy-specific operational complexity, too expensive for the average SME owner, or built for markets with reliable infrastructure that Nigeria does not always provide. The result is a massive, underdocumented market segment operating below its potential — not for lack of ambition, but for lack of the right tools.
Trahka exists to fix this.
solution:
Trahka is a back-office operating system for African SMEs, purpose-built to replace the pen-and-paper systems that keep small businesses invisible, inefficient, and locked out of formal financial markets.
For Nigerian retail pharmacies (our beachhead market), Trahka delivers four core capabilities: real-time inventory management with expiry tracking and low-stock alerts; a sales recorder that captures every transaction accurately; a customer debt tracker that systematically manages informal credit extended to buyers; and an automated profit & loss reporting engine that gives owners a true picture of their business performance for the first time.

The platform is designed for the African operating environment — offline-first, mobile-friendly, and asset-light, running on hardware pharmacy owners already possess. There is no new device to purchase and no dependence on stable internet connectivity.
Beyond the operational layer, Trahka is building a financial infrastructure play. As SMEs use the platform, they generate structured transaction data for the first time in their business history. Trahka uses this data to underwrite embedded working capital loans — connecting business owners to credit that traditional banks have never been able to offer them because the data to assess them simply did not exist.
Trahka's solution is already live at trahka.com. We are not proposing to solve this problem, we are already solving it.
mvpDescription:
Trahka's Minimum Viable Product is live and accessible today at trahka.com. It is a unified back-office platform built for Nigerian retail pharmacies, centered on four core modules that address the most acute operational pain points confirmed through direct customer discovery interviews with pharmacy owners in Edo state.

Inventory Manager — Users can log their entire product catalogue, track stock levels in real time, set low-stock alerts, and monitor expiry dates. For pharmacies managing hundreds of SKUs including temperature-sensitive and controlled substances, this replaces the guesswork of manual stock counts with a live, accurate view of what is on the shelf and what needs attention.

Sales Recorder — Every transaction is captured accurately at the point of sale, giving owners a reliable record of daily revenue, product movement, and sales trends over time. Users can identify their best and worst-performing products and make restocking decisions based on data rather than instinct.

Customer Debt Tracker — Pharmacies routinely extend informal credit to loyal customers. Trahka gives owners a structured system to log, monitor, and follow up on outstanding balances, dramatically reducing the revenue lost to untracked debt.

Profit & Loss Report Engine — Users generate automated P&L reports that show true business performance — not just revenue, but actual profit after cost of goods — many of them seeing a clear picture of their margins for the first time.

The platform is offline-first, mobile-friendly, and runs on hardware pharmacy owners already own — requiring zero new device investment to get started.

solution: TapnGo is an NFC travel card that lets students tap to pay for campus transport in under a second, no cash, no change, no failed transfers. Drivers enter the fare, students tap, and the transaction clears instantly on a closed-loop network built to work even in low-connectivity zones where mobile wallets fail. Students top up via mobile banking or USSD; drivers get instant settlement; universities get real-time visibility into transport revenue that was previously untracked. We are already live at the University of Ibadan and the University of Ilorin with 1,000 travel cards issued and ₦0.5M in monthly transaction volume, proving the model is deployable, sticky, and ready to scale.
mvpDescription:
TapnGo's MVP is a live, working transport payment system deployed at the University of Ibadan and the university of ilorin. It has three parts: an NFC travel card issued to students, a driver-side terminal for accepting payments, and a backend platform that processes transactions and tracks revenue in real time. 
Students can top up their travel card via mobile banking or USSD, then tap to pay their fare in under a second, no cash or change needed. Drivers enter the fare amount, accept the tap, and receive instant settlement. Universities and operators can monitor transaction volume, reconcile payments automatically, and access real-time reporting on transport revenue.
tractionMetric: Transaction Volume
teamExpertise:
TapnGo is built by a team that covers the four disciplines a campus payments company actually needs: regulation, venture-building, design, and engineering.
Our CEO is a legal and policy researcher with deep experience in regulatory analysis, corporate law, and emerging technology. In a payments business, regulation is the game, and she leads on exactly that: navigating financial and data rules, structuring university and transport-union partnerships, and keeping the company compliant as it scales across states and campuses. She pairs that legal foundation with proven strength in grant writing, stakeholder engagement, and startup strategy, which is the core of the CEO's job here: unlocking institutional access, raising capital, and turning a complex product into partnerships that close. She sets the vision and owns the relationships that get TapnGo onto each new campus.
Supporting her is a growth and operations lead who built companies inside an Abuja venture studio, bringing the discipline to take an idea from zero to a launched, revenue-generating product. She owns go-to-market: the deployment playbooks, driver onboarding, and repeatable model we use to enter each new university. Alongside her, our head of design (based in Rwanda) makes the card, the terminal, and the top-up flow effortless for students and drivers, because in a market where trust and simplicity drive adoption, design is a moat rather than a nice-to-have. And our lead software engineer (based in Benin) builds and maintains the NFC payment infrastructure, transaction backend, and reporting platform, keeping payments clearing in under a second and the system reliable even in low-connectivity zones.
Together the team spans three countries and combines regulatory credibility, venture-building discipline, design, and deep technical execution: the exact mix needed to scale campus payments across Africa.
challenges: Three things. First, hardware capital: each NFC terminal has an upfront cost, and scaling to more transport routes means fronting device costs before transaction revenue catches up. Second, driver and student onboarding: adoption depends on both sides trusting the card, so we need boots on the ground to educate and convert. Third, working capital to move faster than we currently can on partnerships already in our pipeline.
fundUsage:
NFC terminals and travel cards (~₦2.5M): deploy additional devices across new transport routes and print the next batch of cards.
Field onboarding and driver training (~₦1M): agents on the ground to onboard drivers and students at launch points.
Product and backend improvements (~₦1M): strengthen the top-up flow, reliability, and reporting dashboard.
Operations and contingency (~₦500K): logistics, connectivity, and buffer.
Every naira goes toward capacity that directly drives transaction volume.
growthTargets: Expand from 1 to 3+ university campuses, grow active cards from 30,000 toward 100,000, and lift monthly transaction volume from ₦2.5M toward ₦15M+ as we deepen usage on existing routes and add new ones.
revenueModel: Two streams. Card issuance (₦1,500 to ₦5,000 per card, paid by the university or student) and a transaction fee (₦10 to ₦20 per tap). Transaction fees scale with student spending, giving us recurring, volume-driven income that grows without linear cost.
socialImpact: We cut wasted time and cash-handling fees for students, bring unbanked transport earnings into a trackable digital system, and give universities visibility into revenue they previously lost to leakage. We also push financial inclusion by making cashless payments the default for students and informal transport operators alike.
sustainabilityPath: Transaction fees are the engine. As active cards and daily taps grow, fee revenue compounds while our per-transaction cost stays flat, so margins improve with scale. Card issuance funds each new campus rollout, and once a campus reaches steady daily volume, it becomes self-funding. The grant gets us to the transaction volume where fee revenue covers operations, after which we scale on our own cash flow and reinvest into new campuses.

problem: Despite Nigeria’s vast agricultural potential, the country faces a serious gap between pork demand and supply. The majority of local pig farmers operate on small scales with minimal access to modern farming tools, high-quality breeding stock, or disease management systems. This results in:Low productivity and poor-quality meat output.High mortality rates due to preventable diseases.Inconsistent supply to meet the needs of consumers and commercial buyers.Limited economic opportunities for rural youths and farmers.Nigeria currently imports a significant portion of its processed meat products, draining valuable foreign exchange that could be retained locally through efficient domestic production. Furthermore, the lack of organized and hygienic pig farming systems has led to consumer concerns about food safety and meat quality.
solution: JOSAM GRAZELAND is addressing these challenges head-on by establishing a model pig farm designed for productivity, sustainability, and community impact. Our farm will:Produce high-quality pork locally, using improved breeding techniques, effective disease prevention, and hygienic processing standards.Utilize locally sourced feed ingredients, supporting nearby crop farmers and reducing feed costs.Promote youth employment and training, offering hands-on skills development for aspiring farmers and agripreneurs.Adopt eco-friendly waste management practices, converting animal waste into organic fertilizer to support crop farming.Ensure animal welfare and ethical farming standards, reinforcing trust and quality in the marketplace.Through these initiatives, JOSAM GRAZELAND will bridge the pork supply gap, strengthen Nigeria’s food system, and create sustainable livelihoods for the Okpella community and beyond.
mvpDescription:
Josam Grazeland’s MVP is the breeding and sales of high quality pigs to smallholder farmers and meat vendors in Edo State.

At this stage, we operate a pilot pig breeding and fattening unit. We breed quality sows to produce healthy piglets, and we also raise pigs to market weight in 7-8 months for sale.

How it works:
1.  Product: Healthy weaner pigs, grower pigs, and mature pigs
2.  Customers: Local farmers looking for better genetics, and meat processors/butchers who need consistent supply
3.  Revenue Model: Direct sales of piglets and table-size pigs

Why this MVP matters:
It proves there is strong demand for improved pig breeds in Nigeria. Our pigs grows 30% faster, have larger litters, and lower mortality than local breeds. This helps farmers earn more and increases local pork supply.

This MVP has already validated our market and is now ready to scale with funding for more pens, breeding stock, and feed.
tractionMetric:
Our key traction metric is demand and pre-orders.  
We have a waiting list of 20+ farmers requesting piglets, and we currently operate at full capacity. This shows clear market demand that we cannot meet yet without expansion funding.
teamExpertise:
Josam Grazeland has a team of 6 with hands-on experience in pig farming, breeding, and farm operations.  
We have skills in livestock management, animal care, sales to local farmers and meat vendors, and agribusiness management.  
This expertise enables us to produce healthy Landrace hybrid pigs and meet market demand.  
With funding, we will add a veterinary consultant to strengthen our technical capacity.
challenges:
1. Limited Space: We currently operate from a rented facility that is too small and at full capacity. This restricts expansion and proper pen management.
2. No Equipment: We lack basic farm equipment for feeding, waste management, and record keeping. Everything is done manually and locally, which reduces efficiency.
3. No Biosecurity Measures: Without proper structures and equipment, it is difficult to implement biosecurity. This increases disease risk for our Landrace hybrid pigs.

    Construction of standard pig pens with proper ventilation, drainage, and biosecurity to move out of the rented facility and increase capacity.

    Purchase of essential farm equipment: feeders, drinkers, wheelbarrows, and weighing scale.
3.  Feed & Operations - ₦1,000,000

5.  Contingency & Record Keeping - ₦200,000 
    Farm management software, record books, and contingency for emergencies.

Expected Impact:  
This investment will triple our pig production, move us into our own facility, implement proper biosecurity, and create 4 direct jobs for youth in Edo State.
growthTargets: With the ₦5M grant, Josam Grazeland targets 300% growth in production and market reach within the next 12 months.
revenueModel:
Josam Grazeland operates a livestock sales model with 3 main income streams:

1. Sale of Piglets  
We breed and sell quality piglets to smallholder farmers in Edo State.  
Price: ₦40,000 per piglet. Target: 200 piglets/year

2. Sale of Market-Weight Pigs  
We raise pigs to 70-100kg and sell to meat vendors, restaurants, and consumers in Edo State.  
Price: ₦150,000 - ₦200,000 per pig. Target: 150 pigs/year

We offer paid breeding services using our quality boars to other farmers.  
Fee: ₦10,000 per service

With ₦5M, we will expand pens, buy more breeding stock, and move out of the rented facility. This increases output, reduces cost, and improves profit margins.

Projected Annual Revenue in 12 months: ₦15,500,000+
socialImpact:
Economic Impact:
1. Job Creation: The ₦5M grant will create 4 direct jobs for youth and 10+ indirect jobs in feed supply, transport, and construction.
2. Income Generation: We project ₦15.5M in annual revenue within 12 months, which will be reinvested to scale the farm and support local suppliers.
3. Market Supply: Increasing pig and piglet production will reduce reliance on imports and stabilize meat prices for consumers in Edo State.

Social Impact:
1. Youth Empowerment: We provide training and decent jobs for young people, reducing unemployment and rural-urban migration.
2. Food Security: By increasing local pork production, we contribute to protein availability and nutrition for households in Edo State.
3. Farmer Support: We supply quality hybrid piglets and breeding services at affordable rates, helping smallholder farmers increase their own income.

With this grant, Josam Grazeland will grow from a small rented facility into a sustainable agribusiness that creates wealth, jobs, and food for our community
sustainabilityPath:
1. Reinvestment of Profits  
Revenue from piglet sales, market pigs, and breeding services will be reinvested into feed, replacement stock, and expansion. After 12 months, farm operations will be fully self-funded from sales.

2. Cost Efficiency  
Moving from a rented facility to our own pens reduces rent costs. Bulk feed purchase and proper biosecurity will lower mortality rates and production cost per pig, improving profit margins.

3. Diversified Income Streams  
We are not dependent on one product. With 3 income sources — piglets, market-weight pigs, and breeding services — cash flow remains stable even if one market slows.

4. Capacity Building 
Training youth staff and working with a veterinary consultant ensures proper animal health and record keeping. This reduces losses and increases long-term productivity.

5. Market Linkages  
We are building direct relationships with farmers and meat vendors in Edo State to secure consistent demand and offtake agreements.

With the ₦5M grant, we will establish the infrastructure needed to become profitable and sustainable within 18 months.

problem:
Many women and young people desire to look stylish and confident but are limited by the high cost of quality fashion and the lack of affordable, modest clothing options. In addition, many struggle to find outfits that suit their personality, body type, and different occasions due to limited access to personalized styling guidance. This often affects their confidence and ability to express themselves through fashion.
Linah Fashion Hub exists to bridge this gap by providing affordable, quality, and modest fashion alongside personalized fashion consultation, making it easier for customers to look good, feel confident, and express themselves without exceeding their budget.
solution:

Our goal is to make quality, modest fashion accessible to everyone while helping women and young people build confidence, express themselves authentically, and feel seen through what they wear.

teamExpertise: Linah Fashion Hub is currently led by me, Ehimen Glory, the Founder and CEO. problem:
A large number of hotels, serviced apartments, shortlets and restaurants in Nigeria still manage reservations manually through phone calls, notebooks, spreadsheets and WhatsApp conversations.

This creates several problems. Businesses may respond late to potential customers, overlook reservation requests, accept conflicting bookings or lose important customer information. A customer may be interested in booking at night or while staff members are busy, but because no one responds immediately, that customer moves to another business.

Apartment owners and booking agents also spend considerable time repeatedly confirming whether particular dates are available. Restaurants face similar challenges when managing table reservations, menus and guest requests.

Existing international booking platforms are often expensive, difficult for smaller operators to adopt or not designed around the way many Nigerian hospitality businesses operate.
solution: Rezora solves this problem by providing a simple, locally relevant platform through which hospitality businesses can manage availability, bookings, reservations, customers and payments from one place. It reduces dependence on manual communication while allowing business owners to focus more of their time on delivering a good guest experience.
mvpDescription:
Rezora is a Nigerian hospitality software company building digital infrastructure for lodging and dining businesses.

For lodging businesses such as hotels, resorts, serviced apartments and shortlets, Rezora provides tools for managing room or apartment availability, bookings, unavailable dates, customer records, payments and booking calendars.

For dining businesses such as restaurants, lounges and bars, the platform supports table reservations, menus, service options, customer information and reservation management.

Businesses can also receive bookings through direct online links instead of relying entirely on phone calls or manual WhatsApp conversations. Rezora is being developed to fit the needs of Nigerian hospitality businesses, including smaller operators that may not have the resources to purchase expensive international software.

The product has been built and is currently at the early-growth stage. We are working on increasing adoption, improving the platform based on feedback from hospitality businesses and building a stronger network of hotels, apartments and restaurants across Nigeria.

problem:
Nigeria is experiencing a growing burden of poor nutrition and post-harvest food losses. Millions of people consume highly processed snacks that are high in sugar, salt, and unhealthy fats but low in essential nutrients, contributing to rising cases of obesity, diabetes, and other diet-related diseases. 
At the same time, an estimated 40–50% of fruits and vegetables produced in Nigeria are lost after harvest due to inadequate processing, storage, and market access, resulting in significant income losses for smallholder farmers and increased food waste.
Despite increasing consumer demand for healthier food choices, there remains limited access to affordable, nutritious, and locally produced snack options. This creates an opportunity to develop innovative products that improve nutrition while creating value from surplus agricultural produce.
Venn Biscuits addresses this challenge by transforming locally sourced tropical fruits such as coconut, ginger and dates into high-fiber, preservative-free biscuits.
solution:

We produce 'Venn Biscuits' fortified, high-fiber, preservative-free biscuits made from fresh locally sourced tropical fruits and nutrient-rich ingredients such as coconut, ginger and dates. We transform surplus agricultural produce into shelf-stable, nutritious snacks that promote healthier eating while reducing post-harvest losses.
Our biscuits provide a healthier alternative to conventional sugar-filled snacks and are fortified with essential vitamins and minerals to help address hidden hunger, particularly among women and children. By sourcing directly from smallholder farmers, we create reliable market opportunities, increase farmer incomes, and strengthen local value chains.
Through sustainable packaging and responsible production, Venn Biscuits delivers a solution that improves nutrition, reduces food waste, supports rural livelihoods, and contributes to a more resilient and sustainable food system.
Venn Biscuits aligns with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by advancing Zero Hunger (SDG 2), Good Health and Well-being (SDG 3), Decent Work and Economic Growth (SDG 8), Responsible Consumption and Production (SDG 12), and Climate Action (SDG 13). problem:
The Confluence of Inflation, Protein Deficiency, and Supply Chain Fragility
Achieving food security requires that essential nutrition remains consistently available and financially accessible. Today, the supply chains for Africa’s two most critical dietary staples—affordable protein (poultry and eggs) and vital cooking lipids (palm oil)—are facing unprecedented pressure.
High inflation, skyrocketing costs of imported feed ingredients (like maize and soybeans), and fragmented, middleman-heavy logistics have driven production costs to historic highs. This has forced local farms to downsize, creating a severe supply deficit. Consequently, millions of households are priced out of basic daily nutrition, worsening protein malnutrition and driving up the cost of living.
solution:
A Vertically Integrated, Low-Cost Agribusiness Model
We solve this dual challenge through a resilient, vertically integrated agribusiness model designed to drive down unit production costs and bypass predatory middlemen.
Our solution stabilizes food security through three core strategic pillars:
 Cost-Efficient Poultry Scaling: By scaling our flock capacity (transitioning to a highly optimized 2,500-layer operation) and implementing localized self-milling for feed formulation, we bypass expensive commercial mills and slash production costs by up to 20–30%. This allows us to supply high-quality, affordable eggs and meat to local markets at highly competitive rates.
 Direct-to-Market Palm Oil Distribution: We streamline the palm oil value chain by sourcing directly from optimized, actively managed plantations and distributing straight to regional wholesale hubs. Cutting out speculative middlemen allows us to stabilize wholesale pricing and maintain a reliable, year-round supply of cooking oil.
 Circular Agricultural Integration: We utilize a closed-loop system where nutrient-rich poultry manure is recycled as organic fertilizer. This ecological synergy minimizes waste, slashes input costs, and enhances soil productivity.

Our integrated agribusiness operates at the intersection of economic growth and social development. By scaling our poultry farm to 1,000 layers and maintaining our direct-to-market palm oil distribution, this project directly addresses critical socio-economic challenges within our local community.
Our social impact is structured around three main pillars:
1. Combating Food Inflation & Nutritional Poverty (Zero Hunger)
 The Problem: Animal protein and high-quality lipids are increasingly priced out of reach for average families due to high inflation.
 Our Impact: Eggs are the most complete, affordable source of high-quality protein, and palm oil is a daily dietary staple. By utilizing localized self-milling to bypass commercial feed markups, we can supply 840 crates of fresh eggs monthly and 75 liters of premium palm oil monthly directly to local vendors. This direct-distribution approach keeps food retail prices competitive, directly protecting household purchasing power and combating local protein-energy malnutrition.
2. Micro-Entrepreneur & Market Women Empowerment
 The Problem: Small-scale market traders and retail women ("market women") struggle with erratic supplies and expensive middlemen markups that eat into their daily livelihood margins.
 Our Impact: We sell 100% of our daily egg and monthly palm oil inventory directly to a pre-validated network of local market retailers. By eliminating intermediary brokers, we offer these micro-entrepreneurs reliable, consistent, and lower-cost wholesale farm-gate prices. This increases their daily retail margins, boosting their household incomes and stabilizing local commercial micro-economies.
3. Youth Employment & Skills Transfer (Decent Work)
 The Problem: Youth unemployment in Nigeria remains a critical challenge, with a lack of practical, hands-on enterprise-level training in modern agribusiness.
 Our Impact: Our planned farm expansion to a 1,000-layer capacity creates immediate opportunities for local labor. Beyond direct employment, our farm serves as a practical model for sustainable agricultural practices (such as utilizing chicken manure as highly nutritious organic fertilizer for crop processing). We plan to offer hands-on training to local youth interested in modern poultry husbandry and crop processing, building capacity in self-milling and circular farming techniques.
sustainabilityPath:
Our path to long-term sustainability is built on a clear transition from donor dependency to commercial self-sufficiency. By strategically combining our two distinct agricultural value chains (poultry and palm oil), we insulate our business from external market shocks while generating internal capital for expansion.
1. Financial Sustainability: Self-Funding Restocking Cycles
The greatest risk to any layer farm is the high capital cost of restocking birds at the end of their laying cycle. We address this directly through our hybrid cash-flow model:
 The Restocking Fund: Daily egg sales from our initial 350-layer flock will comfortably cover daily operational costs (feed, veterinary care, and utilities) while yielding a steady net profit.
 Asset Liquidation Recycling: At the end of the 72-to-80-week cycle, we will liquidate our "spent" hens into the high-demand local meat market. The cash injection from these bulk sales, combined with retained profits from our monthly palm oil distribution, will fully fund the acquisition of our next, expanded batch of Point of Lay (POL) hens. This makes our poultry operations 100% self-funding after the initial grant.
2. Operational Sustainability: Localized Self-Milling
Since commercial feed represents up to 80% of poultry running costs, buying pre-made feed is a threat to long-term viability.
 To secure our margins, we are implementing a localized self-milling strategy, sourcing bulk grains (maize, soy, and agricultural bi-products) directly from farming communities.
 This drops our feed production costs by 20% to 30% compared to commercial alternatives. This structural advantage ensures that even during periods of high economic inflation, our cost of production remains low enough to protect our profitability and keep retail prices affordable.
3. Ecological & Circular Sustainability

problem:
Nigeria generates large volumes of metal waste from households, construction sites, industries, and workshops, yet much of it is poorly managed, discarded, or sold through inefficient informal channels. This contributes to environmental pollution, wasted valuable resources, and lost economic opportunities.
At the same time, scrap collectors often struggle to find reliable buyers who offer fair prices, accurate weighing, and prompt payment, while manufacturers and recycling companies face inconsistent supplies of quality recycled metals. This gap in the recycling value chain limits income opportunities, reduces recycling efficiency, and increases dependence on newly mined or imported raw materials.
Our solution addresses these challenges by creating a reliable metal collection, sorting, and processing business that connects suppliers with industrial buyers, improves recycling efficiency, creates jobs, and promotes a cleaner and more sustainable environment.
solution:
My solution is a metal recycling business that collects, sorts, processes, and supplies recyclable metals such as aluminum, copper, brass, stainless steel, and iron. We source scrap metals from households, construction sites, factories, workshops, and independent collectors, then separate and prepare them to meet the quality requirements of recycling companies and manufacturers.
By turning discarded metal waste into valuable raw materials, the business reduces environmental pollution, conserves natural resources, and supports sustainable industrial production. The solution also creates jobs, provides income opportunities for local scrap collectors, and strengthens the recycling value chain by ensuring a reliable supply of quality recycled metals.
mvpDescription:
Our Minimum Viable Product (MVP) is a working metal collection and trading operation that purchases scrap metals from households, workshops, construction sites, and independent collectors. The metals are sorted, weighed, cleaned, and sold to recycling companies and metal dealers.
We have already tested the business model by working with customers and suppliers, proving there is consistent demand for quality recycled metals. The MVP demonstrates that we can reliably source scrap metals, process them efficiently, and generate revenue while providing fair prices to suppliers and dependable service to buyers. The grant will enable us to scale this proven model by increasing collection capacity, purchasing better processing equipment, and expanding into new markets.
tractionMetric:
Our key traction metric is the volume of scrap metal collected and sold each month. We currently measure success by the number of kilograms (or tonnes) of recyclable metals purchased, processed, and delivered to buyers, as well as the growth in our customer and supplier base.
Since launching our MVP, we have built relationships with scrap collectors and buyers, completed regular transactions, and demonstrated consistent demand for our services. Our goal is to increase monthly metal collections, expand our network of suppliers and buyers, and grow revenue while maintaining reliable service and quality standards.
teamExpertise:
Our team has practical experience in the metal recycling and scrap trading industry, with expertise in sourcing, identifying, sorting, weighing, and processing recyclable metals such as aluminum, copper, brass, stainless steel, and iron. We understand market pricing, quality standards, and the logistics involved in collecting and supplying scrap metals to recycling companies and manufacturers.
In addition to technical knowledge, our team has experience in customer relationship management, supplier engagement, inventory management, and business operations. This combination of industry experience and operational skills enables us to run the business efficiently, build trusted partnerships, and scale the enterprise sustainably.
challenges:

Access to funding will enable us to increase inventory, acquire better equipment, improve logistics, and expand our operations, allowing us to serve more customers efficiently and grow the business sustainably.
fundUsage:
If awarded the ₦5 million grant, we will use the funds to scale our metal recycling business by increasing the purchase of recyclable metals such as aluminum, copper, brass, stainless steel, and iron from collectors and industrial sources. The grant will also be used to acquire essential processing equipment, including industrial weighing scales, cutting and sorting tools, safety equipment, and storage facilities. growthTargets:

revenueModel:

sustainabilityPath:

problem:
Problem Statement

Edo State is home to a vibrant and growing creative industry, with many entrepreneurs, artisans, startups, government programmes, and community initiatives making meaningful contributions to economic and social development. However, many of these stories, achievements, and opportunities are not effectively documented or promoted due to limited access to affordable, high-quality visual content creation.

Many small businesses and organizations struggle to produce professional photographs, documentaries, and digital media that can attract investors, customers, development partners, and wider audiences. This limits their visibility, competitiveness, and growth potential in an increasingly digital world.

At the same time, many talented young people in Edo State are interested in careers in photography, videography, and documentary filmmaking but lack access to industry-standard equipment, practical training, mentorship, and opportunities to gain real-world experience. As a result, creative talent remains underutilized, and unemployment among young creatives continues to be a challenge.

Dephilips Filmworks was established to address these gaps by providing professional visual storytelling services that document impact, preserve culture, promote businesses, and support development initiatives across Edo State. The company has worked with government agencies, development partners, and private organizations to produce compelling visual content that showcases the state's progress and opportunities.

Despite increasing demand for our services, limited production equipment and operational capacity restrict our ability to serve more clients, mentor emerging creatives, and create sustainable employment opportunities. solution:

problem: I discovered this problem while working as a graphic designer for a newly opened hotel in January 2026. One of my first jobs was designing and printing their paper menu. Just a few days later, they called me back because some prices had changed, so the menus had to be redesigned and printed again. This kept happening until they eventually stopped reprinting them and started covering old prices with tape, which didn't look professional. That experience made me realize this wasn't just one hotel's problem. Many restaurants struggle with constantly updating menus, tracking available stock, monitoring sales, and knowing exactly what their staff are doing. I saw an opportunity to build something that would help restaurants manage all of these from one place instead of relying on paper and manual records.
solution: My solution is Stack Menu, an all-in-one restaurant management platform that replaces paper menus with digital QR menus and helps restaurants manage their daily operations from one dashboard. Customers simply scan a QR code to view the menu and place orders, while restaurant owners can manage live orders, update menus instantly, track inventory, monitor sales, manage staff, record cash payments, and run promotions without the stress of manual processes. The goal is to help restaurants save time, reduce errors, and run their businesses more efficiently.
mvpDescription:
Our MVP is a working version of Stack Menu that restaurants can already use. Restaurant owners can create digital QR menus, receive live customer orders, manage their menu, track inventory, monitor sales, manage staff, record cash payments, and run promotions from one dashboard. Customers simply scan a QR code to view the menu and place orders, while the restaurant receives those orders in real time. We have already deployed the MVP and are currently onboarding restaurants to gather feedback and improve the product.

More details about this is on our new social account on TikTok https://www.tiktok.com/@stackmenu?_r=1&_t=ZS-982vwtzuW1Z
tractionMetric: Our key traction metric is customer adoption. We already have over 10 restaurants and hotels waiting to start the 14-day free trial of Stack Menu. Our first customer, Miami Haven Hotel, is currently testing the platform in a real business environment before we roll it out to the wider market. This early demand validates the problem we're solving and gives us valuable feedback to improve the product before scaling.

challenges:
Our biggest challenge right now is funding. We have been bootstrapping Stack Menu from personal savings and borrowed funds because we believe in the problem we're solving. Although we've launched our MVP and already have businesses waiting to use it, we're currently fixing a few bugs discovered during our first real-world deployment before opening the platform to more customers.

Another challenge is the cost of development. Our team works remotely from different locations, and unreliable electricity and internet access often slow down development and testing. We also have to cover the cost of hiring technical talent to keep improving the product.

Finally, we need resources for marketing and customer onboarding. We've personally visited restaurants and hotels to introduce Stack Menu, and we've already seen strong interest from businesses in different cities like Lagos, Abuja and Port Harcourt. With adequate funding, we can complete product improvements, onboard more businesses, and scale our marketing efforts much faster.
fundUsage:
