Team Support & Operations – ₦700,000: Our team has been building Stack Menu through personal sacrifice and bootstrapping. This allocation will help support the core team with stipends, internet, electricity, software subscriptions, and operational expenses, allowing us to stay focused on building and supporting the platform as we begin generating sustainable revenue.
growthTargets:
Over the next 12 months, our goal is to onboard at least 300 restaurants, hotels, cafés, lounges, and other food businesses across Nigeria. We plan to build a strong field marketing team that will introduce Stack Menu directly to businesses, while also growing through referrals and partnerships.

We also aim to continuously improve the platform by adding new features based on customer feedback, maintaining reliable system performance, and providing excellent customer support. Our target is to convert free trial users into paying subscribers and build a sustainable recurring revenue model.
Beyond customer growth, we want to create employment by expanding our team of marketers, customer support staff, and technical professionals. 

Our long-term vision is to make Stack Menu one of Africa's leading restaurant management platforms, helping thousands of food businesses manage their operations more efficiently and grow their businesses through technology.
revenueModel:
Stack Menu operates on a subscription-based revenue model with multiple income streams. After a 14-day free trial, businesses can subscribe to one of our monthly plans: ₦7,500 for small businesses, ₦15,000 for growing businesses, and ₦25,000 for businesses that need our complete feature set.

Beyond subscriptions, we also generate revenue from branded hardware and onboarding materials. We design and sell QR code stickers, table tent stands, and premium acrylic QR table stands that restaurants and hotels use within their businesses. This has already generated revenue during our early deployments, with over ₦49,000 earned from hardware sales for a single customer.

As we expand, we also plan to build a network of local vendors across different states who will produce and distribute these materials, creating additional business opportunities while helping us scale faster.

Our long-term vision is to expand beyond Nigeria into other African countries and international markets, where Stack Menu will be offered through localized subscription plans priced in the appropriate currencies. This gives us a scalable recurring revenue model supported by complementary product sales and customer onboarding services.
socialImpact:
Stack Menu is helping restaurants and hotels move away from inefficient manual processes by giving them affordable digital tools to manage their businesses. Our platform reduces paper waste from constantly reprinting menus, helps business owners track sales and inventory more accurately, improves transparency in staff operations, and enables faster customer service through digital ordering.

Beyond helping businesses become more efficient, we are also creating employment opportunities for marketers, developers, designers, customer support staff, and local vendors who produce our QR stickers and table stands. As we expand across Nigeria and Africa, we hope to support thousands of hospitality businesses with technology that helps them grow, increase their revenue, and deliver a better experience to their customers.
sustainabilityPath:
Our goal is to build a business that can sustain itself through the value it provides to customers. As more restaurants and hotels subscribe to Stack Menu, the recurring subscription revenue will cover our operational costs, product development, customer support, and team salaries.

We also generate additional income from the sale of QR code materials such as stickers, table stands, and acrylic displays, which complements our subscription model. As we expand, we plan to work with local vendors in different states to produce these materials, creating a sustainable distribution network.

We know we are still in the early stages, and there is still a lot to improve. Right now, our focus is on building a reliable product, listening to customer feedback, and growing one business at a time. We believe that by solving a real problem consistently and keeping our customers satisfied, Stack Menu will become a sustainable business without depending on grants in the long term.

problem:
ROYAL SIGNATURE FASHION HUB is a visionary fashion empowerment and production 
center designed to support fashion designers, tailors, fashion students, creative entrepreneurs, and 
upcoming clothing brands by providing access to professional sewing equipment, workspace, and 
essential fashion production facilities at affordable daily or scheduled rates.
The vision behind this project is to create a standard and accessible fashion hub where individuals 
who cannot afford sewing machines or a complete workspace can still practice, learn, produce 
quality garments, and grow their businesses.
solution:
ROYAL SIGNATURE FASHION HUB is not just a business venture; it is a community 
empowerment project aimed at reducing unemployment, supporting creativity, empowering young 
talents, and contributing to economic development within the fashion industry. 
ROYAL SIGNATURE FASHION HUB is designed to bridge this gap by creating a centralized 
fashion workspace where designers can access professional facilities and equipment at affordable 
rates.
mvpDescription:
Royal Signature Fashion Hub – Minimum Viable Product (MVP)

MVP Objective

Launch a functional shared fashion workspace with the minimum equipment required to serve independent tailors while validating market demand before scaling.

Equipment Required (Phase 1)

Item| Quantity
Industrial Sewing Machines| 10
Overlocking (Weaving) Machines| 2
Pressing Stations (Iron & Ironing Board)| 3
Cutting Tables| 2
Tailors' Chairs| 10
Power Supply (Generator/Inverter)| 1
Shelves/Storage Units| 2
Reception/Waiting Area| 1

What the MVP Offers

- Daily workspace rental for professional and intermediate tailors.
- Access to industrial sewing equipment.
- Access to overlocking machines.
- Professional cutting and pressing facilities.
- Reliable power supply.
- A clean, safe, and conducive working environment.

Target Customers

- Independent tailors.
- Freelance fashion designers.
- Home-based tailors.
- Fashion entrepreneurs who need a temporary workspace.

Revenue Model

- Daily access fee.
- Weekly access package.
- Monthly membership package.

MVP Success Indicators

- 20–30 active paying tailors within the first three months.
- At least 60% customer retention.
- Daily utilization of more than 70% of available workstations.
- Positive customer referrals and repeat usage.

Future Expansion

Once demand is validated, Royal Signature Fashion Hub will expand by increasing the number of sewing machines, opening additional locations, introducing fabric and accessories sales, equipment rental services, storage lockers, meeting spaces for client fittings, and other value-added services.

Mission: To make professional fashion workspaces affordable and accessible for every tailor.

Vision: To become Africa's leading shared fashion workspace, empowering thousands of fashion entrepreneurs to build sustainable businesses without the burden of high startup costs.
tractionMetric:
Key Traction Metric

Monthly Active Paying Tailors (MAPT)

The primary traction metric for Royal Signature Fashion Hub is the Monthly Active Paying Tailors (MAPT)—the total number of unique tailors who pay to access and use the hub's shared sewing workspace within a calendar month.

This metric measures customer adoption, validates market demand, demonstrates repeat usage, and reflects the overall sustainability and growth potential of the business. As the number of active paying tailors increases, it provides clear evidence that the hub is solving a real problem for independent fashion professionals and gaining acceptance in the market.

Supporting Traction Metrics

- Daily workstation occupancy rate.
- Customer retention and repeat usage rate.
- Monthly recurring revenue.
- Average number of bookings per week.
- Customer referrals and new user acquisition.
teamExpertise:
Team Expertise

Royal Signature Fashion Hub is supported by a lean, skilled, and service-oriented team responsible for delivering a secure, efficient, and professional workspace for independent tailors.

Founder / Operations Manager
Provides strategic direction and oversees the overall management of the hub. Responsibilities include business development, operational planning, customer experience, financial oversight, and ensuring that the facility consistently meets the needs of its users.

Administrative Officer (Secretary)
Manages the day-to-day administrative operations of the hub, including customer registration, workstation allocation, payment processing, record keeping, scheduling, and customer support. This role ensures an organized and seamless experience for every user.

Technical Supervisor / Maintenance Officer
Oversees the functionality, maintenance, and safety of all equipment within the hub. Responsibilities include routine inspection of sewing machines and other equipment, preventive maintenance, troubleshooting and repairs, and verifying that all assets are in good condition before and after customer use.

Security Personnel (Two Officers)
Two trained security officers provide continuous security coverage through morning and evening shifts. They are responsible for controlling access to the facility, safeguarding equipment and other assets, monitoring activities within the premises, and ensuring a safe and secure working environment for customers and staff.

Together, this team combines operational management, customer service, technical maintenance, and facility security to ensure that Royal Signature Fashion Hub operates efficiently while providing a dependable and professional workspace for fashion entrepreneurs.
challenges: Securing sufficient startup funding to establish and equip the Fashion Hub while attracting enough paying tailors to achieve sustainable operations.

- Recruit core staff.

revenueModel:
Revenue Model

Royal Signature Fashion Hub operates a pay-per-use business model designed to make professional sewing facilities affordable for independent tailors while ensuring the long-term sustainability of the hub.

Each industrial sewing machine is rented at ₦4,000 per day. With an initial capacity of 10 machines, the projected revenue is as follows:

- Daily Revenue: ₦40,000 (10 machines × ₦4,000)
- Weekly Revenue (7 days): ₦280,000
- Monthly Revenue (30 days): ₦1,200,000
- Projected Annual Revenue: ₦14,400,000

The primary objective of this model is not solely to generate profit but to empower young and independent tailors by providing affordable access to professional equipment, eliminating the high cost of renting shops and purchasing machines. Revenue generated will be reinvested into expanding the hub, increasing machine capacity, improving facilities, and creating more opportunities for fashion entrepreneurs across Nigeria.
socialImpact:
Social and Economic Impact

Royal Signature Fashion Hub is transforming the fashion industry by removing the financial barriers that prevent talented young tailors from succeeding. Through affordable access to professional sewing equipment and a fully equipped shared workspace, the hub eliminates the high cost of renting, furnishing a shop, and purchasing industrial machines, enabling fashion entrepreneurs to focus on growing sustainable businesses.

Beyond providing workspace, the hub serves as a catalyst for entrepreneurship, job creation, and economic inclusion. Within its first year, Royal Signature Fashion Hub projects the creation of at least 10 direct jobs and support for over 100 indirect jobs, while helping independent tailors increase their productivity, income, and business capacity.

In the long term, the hub will become a strategic partner for government agencies, development organizations, and private institutions by serving as a dedicated centre for youth empowerment and workforce development. Through collaborative empowerment programmes, the facility will provide a practical environment where aspiring fashion entrepreneurs can acquire industry-relevant skills, creating lasting economic opportunities and contributing to the growth of Nigeria's creative economy.
sustainabilityPath:
Path Path to Sustainability

Royal Signature Fashion Hub will achieve sustainability through its affordable pay-per-use model, generating consistent revenue from daily workstation rentals to cover operations, maintenance, and staff costs. As demand grows, revenue will be reinvested to expand capacity, improve facilities, and establish strategic partnerships with government and development organizations, ensuring long-term financial sustainability and social impact.

problem:
Millions of Nigerians struggle to find essential medicines when they need them most. Patients often visit several pharmacies before locating prescribed drugs, wasting valuable time, transportation costs, and sometimes abandoning treatment altogether.
This challenge is especially dangerous for emergency medications, chronic disease management, and hard-to-find medicines. Pharmacies also lose customers because they have no efficient way of informing nearby patients about available stock. The healthcare system lacks a unified, real-time medicine availability network, creating inefficiencies for patients, pharmacists, and healthcare providers.
solution:
XtraLife provides a digital marketplace and medicine discovery platform that enables users to:
Search nearby pharmacies in real time
Check medicine availability
Compare prices
Reserve medicines
Chat with licensed pharmacists
Request delivery through partner logistics providers
Receive medication reminders
Access verified health information
For pharmacies, XtraLife offers inventory management tools, customer acquisition, analytics, and increased visibility to nearby customers.
mvpDescription: The platform has completed product planning and is in MVP development, with core features including medicine search, pharmacy listings, inventory management, and pharmacy onboarding being implemented. The next phase focuses on onboarding pharmacies, validating product-market fit, and expanding across Edo State before wider rollout.
tractionMetric: Although XtraLife is currently in the MVP stage, we have completed customer discovery and early market validation. Eight pharmacies have committed to participating in our pilot launch, confirming the demand for a platform that improves medicine visibility and customer acquisition. We have also built an early community of interested users, primarily students and young professionals, who have expressed willingness to use the platform. Our immediate focus is to convert these early commitments into active users while expanding our pharmacy network across Edo State.
teamExpertise: Our team combines expertise in pharmacy, healthcare, business strategy, and product design. As a 500 level Pharmacy student, I bring deep knowledge of medication access challenges, pharmaceutical care, and the Nigerian healthcare system, ensuring XtraLife addresses real-world needs. Our Business Lead contributes expertise in business modeling, partnerships, financial planning, and sustainability, while our Design Lead specializes in UI/UX design, product mockups, branding, and user-centered digital experiences. Together, we are supported by technical collaborators responsible for software development, enabling us to build and scale a practical, impactful digital health solution.
challenges: Our biggest challenge is securing the resources needed to complete product development and achieve meaningful market adoption. Building a reliable, real-time medicine availability platform requires significant investment in technology, pharmacy onboarding, and user acquisition. As an early-stage health startup, attracting pharmacies and reaching a critical mass of users simultaneously is essential for network effects to take hold. This grant will enable us to complete our MVP, onboard pilot pharmacies across Edo State, validate our business model, and accelerate adoption.
fundUsage: The ₦5 million grant will be used to build, launch, and validate XtraLife as a scalable digital health platform that improves access to essential medicines. The funding will primarily support completion of our MVP, ensuring the platform delivers a reliable experience for both patients and partner pharmacies. problem: Nigerian fashion designers and brands have no platform that matches the quality, ambition, and cultural pride of their work. They are forced to sell through generic marketplaces like Jumia or via Instagram DMs — platforms that strip away brand identity, offer no curation standard, and fail to position Nigerian fashion as a prestige product. Meanwhile, Nigerian consumers who want to show their status through fashion have no trusted destination that signals taste, quality, and cultural authenticity in one place. The result is a fragmented, undervalued market despite Nigeria's fashion e-commerce sector being worth over $5 billion.
solution: Nióre is Nigeria's first curated aspirational fashion marketplace — a platform where every brand listed has been vetted for authenticity, quality craftsmanship, and a compelling story. We sell only wearable fashion items (clothing, shoes, watches, jewellery, and accessories) made by Nigerians, for Nigerians and the diaspora. Every brand on Nióre meets one uncompromising standard — no exceptions. Wearing Nióre is not just a purchase; it is a statement of wealth, taste, and Nigerian identity. We have built a working MVP, assembled a co-founding team of five specialists, and developed a complete UI/UX design system ready for launch.
mvpDescription: Nióre's MVP is a fully designed and functional fashion marketplace platform with both web and mobile interfaces. Key features include a curated brand onboarding flow (application-based, with quality and authenticity assessment), a product browsing and discovery experience, a checkout system integrated with multi-courier logistics via the Shipbubble API for both domestic and international delivery, and a complete UI/UX design system built around Nióre's luxury brand identity. Users can browse curated Nigerian fashion brands, view products, and complete purchases. The platform is in pre-launch phase but technically functional and ready for brand and user onboarding.
tractionMetric: Our key traction metric at this stage is brand onboarding pipeline — the number of curated Nigerian fashion brands committed to listing on Nióre at launch. As a pre-launch marketplace, supply-side readiness directly determines launch quality. Secondary metrics we are actively tracking include MVP completion rate and social media audience growth ahead of our public launch campaign.
teamExpertise: Nióre is built by a co-founding team of five specialists. John Ugheighele Osewhbaheme (CEO & Founder) leads vision, strategy, and brand positioning — a 200-level linguistics student at the University of Benin with deep cultural insight into Nigerian identity and consumer behaviour. Vincentpaul Omorogbe (Lead Engineer) leads platform architecture and full technical execution. Julius Destiny Onyedikachi (Head of Marketing) drives brand voice, growth strategy, and community building. Ogunlana Micheal Ayo-Oluwasubomi (UI/UX Designer) designed the complete luxury design system and user experience. fundUsage: ₦2.5M (50%) — Marketing & Brand Launch: influencer seeding, content production, Instagram/TikTok launch campaign, and PR to establish Nióre as a prestige destination from day one. ₦1.5M (30%) — Platform & Tech Completion: payment gateway integration, Shipbubble logistics API deployment, mobile optimisation, and brand onboarding system. ₦750k (15%) — Logistics & Operations: packaging, first-order fulfilment setup, and delivery partner onboarding. ₦250k (5%) — Legal & Admin: CAC registration, IP protection for the Nióre brand, and seller agreement templates.
growthTargets: Within 12 months of receiving this grant, Nióre targets: (1) 50+ curated Nigerian fashion brands onboarded across clothing, shoes, watches, and jewellery. problem:
In early childhood development, storytelling is one of the most powerful tools for building literacy, empathy, and imagination. However, modern children's literature faces several critical limitations: 

1.) Lack of Personalization & Representation: Traditional children's books feature generic characters and storylines. Parents struggle to find stories that feature characters who look like their child, represent their unique family structure, or address their specific life events (such as moving to a new city, starting school, or overcoming a fear).

2.)The "Passive Consumer" Trap: Children are increasingly drawn to passive, screen-based entertainment (like short-form videos) because static books fail to capture their immediate interests. There is a lack of tools that invite children to actively participate in creating the stories they consume.

3.)High Barriers to Customization: While parents and educators have wonderful ideas for custom stories, they lack the professional writing skills, artistic illustration talents, and technical expertise required to turn those ideas into visually stunning, cohesive books. Custom illustration commissions are prohibitively expensive and take weeks to complete.
solution:
Stelar AI is a state-of-the-art children's storybook generator that democratizes storytelling by turning imagination into fully illustrated, professionally formatted books in seconds.

Instant Cohesive Story Generation: Using advanced language models, Stelar AI drafts engaging, age-appropriate children's stories based on simple user prompts, structured plots, or imported texts, automatically segmenting them into beautifully paced pages.
Character Consistency & Personalization: Through specialized image generation workflows, users can design unique characters (specifying names, descriptions, and visual features) and generate them consistently across every single page of the story.
Rich Curated Art Styles: Stelar AI goes beyond generic AI images by offering curated, child-friendly design systems—ranging from classic watercolor and papercut crafts to retro 16-bit pixel art and whimsical 3D claymorphism.
Accessible and Flexible Pricing: With plans designed for parents (Starter), creators (Storyteller), and power users (Family/BYOK), Stelar AI makes personalized reading affordable for every family and school.
mvpDescription: The users inpute a single prompt, and the AI generates a full story for them. Next, the story is split into scenes, and each scene is generated using AI. By the end of the generation, the full storybook can be exported in PDF format or Flipbook

Another huge part of the grant will be put toward adverts and promotion of the saad. We could also onboard more developers to see that the website follows modern standards and is always up to date with new features. also the server/technical costs will be taken care of.
growthTargets:
the first half of the year (Months 1–6), the primary growth driver will center on organic acquisition fueled by viral sharing loops. Because every storybook created on Stelar can be shared publicly via custom links (/s/[slug]) and read using the interactive digital flipbook, each completed book acts as a natural recommendation. By prompting readers of shared stories to create their own custom tales, we aim to onboard 1,000 active free users and convert a bulk from those numbers into active monthly subscribers on our Starter and Storyteller plans, establishing a solid baseline of recurring revenue (MRR).

In the second quarter (Months 4–8), the growth strategy will expand into B2B and educational partnerships. By marketing directly to primary school teachers, educators, and children's libraries, Stelar will launch classroom-specific features, including multi-profile management and collaborative group-creation modes. The target for this phase is to pilot Stelar in different schools, offering group licensing that allows teachers to design custom reading material aligned with their weekly lesson plans, thereby positioning the platform as a valuable tool for early childhood literacy.

By the third quarter (Months 7–10), Stelar will transition from a digital-only tool to a full-service custom publishing house by introducing direct-to-door physical book printing. While PDF and ZIP exports are useful, providing parents and grandparents the option to order high-quality hardcover or softcover copies of their child's custom book opens a high-margin physical revenue stream. The goal is to achieve a 20% conversion rate from digital book completions to physical orders, creating an ideal gift-giving loop for birthdays, holidays, and family keepsakes.

Ultimately, the 12-month target is to hopefully surpass 5,000 generated stories, 2,500 active paid subscribers, and establish a profitable print-on-demand fulfillment network. The social impact of this growth will be profound: thousands of children from diverse backgrounds will see themselves represented as the heroes of their own stories, parents will enjoy meaningful bonding experiences creating tales with their children, and educators will have an unprecedented ability to tailor reading materials to individual learning speeds and interests.

sustainabilityPath:
1. Optimized AI Unit Economics & Cost Control
To protect gross margins against high AI compute fees (text generation and image rendering APIs), Stelar AI implements strict unit economics:

Tiered Model Usage: The system defaults to cost-effective, high-speed models (like Nano Banana 2 Lite via KIE) for initial story creation and character drafts. High-cost, premium models are reserved exclusively for final, high-resolution print-ready exports.
Credit Reservation Engine: Using our built-in balance and credit reservation system, every story generated reserves a capped credit budget. This prevents runaway API usage and ensures that the server cost of running a user's generations is always lower than their subscription fee.
2. Transitioning to High-Margin Physical Merchandising
While digital-only SaaS products have low overhead, physical products carry high perceived value and willingness-to-pay.

Fulfillment Margins: Parents are willing to pay a premium (e.g., ₦10,000–₦15,000) for a printed, bound hardcover copy of their child's custom book. By partnering directly with local digital print-on-demand shops, Stelar AI can maintain a 50%+ gross margin on physical prints, utilizing physical product sales to subsidize digital infrastructure costs.
3. High-Value B2B School & Institutional Contracts
B2C subscription models (parents) often experience seasonal churn. To build predictable, year-round revenue:

School & Library Licensing: We will market annual group licenses to private schools, learning centers, and libraries. These annual contracts provide predictable, high-value cash flow with minimal churn, securing the baseline operational capital needed to sustain the platform.
4. Cost-Neutral Power Users (BYOK)
For creators, authors, and classrooms that generate massive quantities of stories:

Bring Your Own Key (BYOK): Stelar AI provides a BYOK integration (for Groq, OpenRouter, and KIE keys). When enabled, all API compute costs are billed directly to the user's personal accounts. This makes power-user generation 100% cost-neutral to Stelar, allowing us to capture a pure-margin platform fee for the software interface.

problem:
E-commerce in Nigeria has grown so fast since COVID, making last mile delivery a bigger part of everyday business. However, fuel powered delivery bikes are making this hard to keep up with. As fuel costs keep rising, delivery fees are rising too, making many customers cancel their orders the moment they see the delivery fee.
SMEDAN records show that Edo State has over 898,084 MSMEs who depend on delivery to reach their customers. Benin City alone has over 1,200 fuel-powered bikes, which produce an estimated 7,000 metric tonnes of CO2 every year.
This means the current logistics system costs businesses and customers more, as well as harming the environment
solution: Turbo Logistics solves this with an electric delivery fleet and one flat rate: ₦2,000 to anywhere in Benin City. No fuel cost, no guessing, no cancelling at checkout nd no pollution. Just fast, affordable, and clean delivery for Benin City businesses.
mvpDescription:
How Our MVP Works

Turbo Logistics is a web based last-mile delivery platform that enables individuals and businesses to book, manage, and track deliveries within Benin City.

Step 1: Visit the Website
A customer visits the website @www.turbologisticglobal.com to access our delivery service. From the homepage, users can choose between two booking options:
Book via WhatsApp for a quick one-time delivery without creating an account.
Register or Log In as a business vendor to access the full delivery management dashboard.

Step 2A: Book via WhatsApp

Customers who select Book via WhatsApp are redirected to a WhatsApp chat with Turbo Logistics. They provide the pickup address, recipient's details, delivery address, and package information. They are informed of the ₦2,000 flat delivery fee for any location within Benin City. Once payment is confirmed, the dispatch team assigns a rider, who picks up and delivers the package. The customer receives delivery confirmation upon successful completion.

 Step 2B: Register or Log In

Businesses that make frequent deliveries create an account by providing their business information. Once registered, they can securely log in to their vendor dashboard.

Step 3: Create a Delivery Request
From the dashboard, the customer clicks "New Delivery" and enters the required information, including:
* Pickup address
* Recipient's name and phone number
* Delivery address
* Package description
* Special delivery instructions (if any)
The system instantly displays the delivery fee of ₦2,000, which is our flat-rate price for deliveries to any location within Benin City. Once the customer confirms the request, a unique order ID is generated.

 Step 4: Payment
The customer pays the fixed ₦2,000 delivery fee  through the available payment option before the order is processed. Once payment is confirmed, the delivery request is submitted to the dispatch system.

Step 5: Rider Assignment
The dispatch team receives the request and assigns the nearest available rider. The customer can view the rider assignment and the current delivery status from the dashboard.

Step 6: Package Pickup
The assigned rider arrives at the pickup location, verifies the package details, collects the parcel, and updates the order status to Picked Up

Step 7: Delivery
The rider transports the package to the recipient anywhere within Benin City. Throughout the process, the customer can monitor the progress of the delivery from their dashboard.

 Step 8: Delivery Confirmation
Once the package is delivered, the rider marks the order as Delivered. The customer immediately receives a delivery confirmation, and the completed order is automatically saved in their delivery history

Step 9: Dashboard and Order History
Customers can access their dashboard at any time to:
* View active deliveries
* Track completed orders
* Access delivery history
* Monitor delivery statistics
* Book additional deliveries

This workflow demonstrates the core functionality of our MVP by allowing customers to either book a delivery instantly through WhatsApp or manage deliveries through the web platform, pay a transparent flat fee of₦2,000for deliveries anywhere within Benin City, monitor the delivery process, and receive confirmation once their goods have been successfully delivered.
tractionMetric: Our key traction metric is over 250 completed deliveries per month, generating approximately ₦500,000 in monthly revenue. We currently receive more than 25 delivery requests daily, but due to our limited fleet capacity, we are only able to fulfill about 10–12 deliveries per day, declining 13–15 delivery requests daily. This demonstrates that our primary challenge is not customer demand but the ability to meet existing demand. Our flat-rate delivery model has attracted strong market interest, and additional fleet capacity would enable us to serve more customers, increase revenue, and scale our operations.

problem:
68% of people who start a fitness routine quit 
within 5 months. The root cause is not laziness 
— it is identity. People stop exercising because 
they never truly begin to see themselves as 
someone who moves consistently. Every existing 
fitness product — smartwatches, running apps, 
gym memberships — tracks behaviour without ever 
addressing this deeper belief gap. Nobody has 
built a product that makes a person feel like 
they are becoming someone different. This is the 
problem STRYDE was built to solve. It affects 
2.8 billion physically inactive adults globally, 
and in Nigeria — where non-communicable diseases 
linked to inactivity are rising rapidly — it is 
not just a lifestyle problem. It is a public 
health crisis.
solution:
STRYDE is a smart running shoe with three embedded 
technologies — a weight sensor, a step tracker, 
and GPS — that connect automatically to a mobile 
app via Bluetooth. Every morning when the user 
puts the shoes on, their weight and activity data 
appear instantly. An AI coach powered by Claude 
then reads that real data and delivers a 
personalised identity message — not a generic 
tip, but a specific statement about who this 
person is in the process of becoming. During 
runs, the coach detects fatigue in real time and 
can be called by voice — "Hey Stryde Coach" — 
responding through the user's earphones with 
live coaching based on their actual numbers. 
STRYDE does not just track fitness. It builds 
the identity of someone who moves — one morning 
at a time.
mvpDescription:
The STRYDE MVP is a fully functional Android 
mobile app currently built and running. It 
includes five screens: a home dashboard showing 
weight, steps, distance and a daily AI coach 
message; a holographic body scan screen that 
simulates the morning shoe connection ritual 
with live weight and BMI display; a live run 
tracker with GPS mapping, step count, distance 
and pace; a full AI coach chat interface powered 
by the Anthropic Claude API that responds with 
personalised coaching based on real user data; 
and an athlete profile screen with shoe 
connection status via Bluetooth 5.3. The AI 
coach is already integrated and responding with 
real coaching messages. The Supabase backend is 
in active configuration. This is not a mockup 
or a concept — it is a working prototype with 
AI already live inside it.

security, systems architecture, and product

modules. The idea is proven. The software works. 
The gap between where we are and a physical 
prototype is engineering expertise and funding.

These three streams create a business 
that grows in revenue even when hardware 
sales slow — because the subscription 
base compounds monthly.

inactivity — one of the leading drivers 
of non-communicable diseases across

change at scale.

Beyond health — STRYDE proves that a 
world-class AI-powered hardware product 
can be conceived and built in Nigeria 
by young Nigerians. Every unit sold is 
evidence that Nigerian youth can compete 
and lead in the global technology and 
wearable market.

The economic impact extends to the 
jobs created, the engineers trained, 
and the ecosystem built around a 
product that originates from Edo State

and production begins, each unit sold 
funds the next stage of growth.

The second is the app subscription. 
At $9.99 per month, every shoe owner 
becomes a recurring revenue source. 
The AI coaching system costs a fraction 
of the subscription to run — making 
the margin on software extremely healthy.

These two streams working together mean 
STRYDE does not depend on continuous 
grants or external funding to operate 
once the product is in market. The 
hardware brings the customer. The 
subscription keeps them. The business 
sustains itself.

problem:
## Statement of Problem

Reading is the foundation of learning, yet many children struggle to acquire this essential skill. Every year, we meet children who have spent several years in school but still cannot recognize letter sounds, blend words, read fluently, or understand what they read. These challenges affect not only their academic performance but also their confidence, motivation, and overall attitude toward learning.

One of the biggest problems is that many struggling readers are not identified early enough or do not receive the support they need. While schools work hard to meet the needs of all learners, large class sizes and limited time often make it difficult to provide the individualized attention that children with reading difficulties require. At home, many parents genuinely want to help but lack the knowledge, resources, or confidence to teach reading effectively.

Without intervention, these learning gaps continue to widen. Children who cannot read confidently often struggle across other subjects because they cannot access the information in their textbooks or classroom materials. Over time, this can lead to frustration, low self-esteem, and disengagement from school.

His Vine Learning Center was established to bridge this gap by providing structured, research-based reading intervention for children who need additional support. Through systematic phonics instruction, guided reading, literacy activities, and parent coaching, we help children build the skills and confidence they need to become successful readers. We believe that every child can learn to read when given the right instruction, encouragement, and opportunity.

Over the years, we have witnessed remarkable transformations in children who once struggled with reading. However, the demand for our services continues to grow, and many families who need intervention cannot afford specialized support. Limited funding also affects our ability to expand our programs, develop more learning resources, train educators, and reach more children in underserved communities.

This grant will enable us to increase access to quality reading intervention, provide essential teaching and learning materials, strengthen parent engagement, and support more children in becoming confident, independent readers. By investing in foundational literacy, we are not only helping children succeed in school today but also equipping them with a skill that will benefit them for the rest of their lives.
solution:
## Solution

At His Vine Learning Center, we believe that every child deserves the opportunity to become a confident reader, regardless of where they are starting from. Our approach is to identify learning gaps early and provide structured, engaging, and personalized reading support that meets each child at their level.

We provide systematic literacy intervention through phonics instruction, phonemic awareness, guided reading, fluency practice, vocabulary development, and reading comprehension. Children receive support in small groups or one-on-one, allowing us to tailor instruction to their individual needs and monitor their progress over time.

We also recognize that learning does not stop when a child leaves the classroom. Parents are an important part of the learning process, so we equip them with practical strategies and resources to support reading at home. This partnership helps children receive consistent encouragement and practice, leading to stronger and more lasting results.

One of our most impactful initiatives is **The Reading Trail**, a structured literacy program designed to guide children from the very basics of reading to fluent, confident reading through clear, step-by-step instruction. The program also empowers parents and educators with easy-to-follow lessons and activities, making quality reading instruction more accessible both at home and in the classroom. By combining research-based teaching methods with practical application, The Reading Trail helps children build strong reading foundations while giving adults the confidence to support their learning journey.

With grant funding, we will expand access to our reading intervention services and The Reading Trail program, develop more learning resources, train educators, and reach more children who are struggling to read. Our goal is to ensure that more children receive the support they need early, so they can develop the skills, confidence, and love for reading that will serve them throughout their education and beyond.
mvpDescription:
## Minimum Viable Product (MVP)

Our Minimum Viable Product (MVP) is **The Reading Trail**—a structured, phonics-based reading program developed by His Vine Learning Center to help children build strong foundational literacy skills. The program was created in response to a recurring challenge we observed: many children were progressing through school without the ability to read confidently or independently.

The Reading Trail provides a clear, step-by-step pathway that takes children from letter-sound recognition to fluent reading. It includes systematic phonics instruction, guided reading activities, reading comprehension exercises, and practical teaching guides that enable both educators and parents to support children's learning effectively. The program is designed to be engaging, easy to follow, and adaptable to learners with different reading abilities.

Over the past year, The Reading Trail has been piloted through our reading intervention programs at His Vine Learning Center, where it has helped **more than 50 children** improve their reading skills and become more confident readers. We have also received encouraging feedback from parents, many of whom have shared that their children now read more willingly, participate more confidently in class, and show greater enthusiasm for learning.

These early results have validated both the need for the program and its effectiveness. They have also demonstrated that when children receive structured instruction and consistent support, significant progress is possible.

With grant funding, we will refine and expand The Reading Trail by developing additional learning resources, producing high-quality instructional materials, training more educators, and increasing access for children and families who would otherwise be unable to benefit from specialized reading intervention. Our goal is to make The Reading Trail an accessible and scalable literacy solution that helps many more children develop the confidence and skills they need to succeed in school and beyond.

* Parents have reported noticeable improvements in their children's reading confidence, fluency, and willingness to read independently at home.

challenges:
## Biggest Challenge

Our biggest challenge is scaling our impact with limited resources. As demand for our reading intervention programs continues to grow, we face three key constraints.

First, recruiting and retaining qualified literacy educators who share our vision and have the skills to deliver high-quality, evidence-based reading instruction has been difficult. Strong literacy instruction requires specialized knowledge, and finding educators with both the expertise and passion for this work is a significant challenge.

Second, limited funding restricts our ability to expand our programs, invest in learning materials, train educators, and reach more children who need support. As a founder-led organization, balancing program delivery with fundraising and organizational growth is an ongoing challenge.

Finally, creating awareness remains a major hurdle. Many parents are unaware that reading difficulties can be addressed through early intervention, while others are unfamiliar with the structured support that The Reading Trail provides. Increasing awareness is essential to ensuring that more families seek help before learning gaps become more difficult to close.

Addressing these challenges will enable us to reach more children, strengthen our team, and make quality reading intervention accessible to more families.
fundUsage:
## Programme Delivery and Use of Funds

The ₦5 million grant will be strategically invested to strengthen the delivery and reach of The Reading Trail, making high-quality literacy support more accessible to children, parents, and educators.

**1. Digital Infrastructure and Internet Connectivity**
A significant portion of the funding will be used to install a reliable high-speed internet solution, such as Starlink. Stable internet connectivity will enable us to deliver one-on-one virtual reading intervention, train parents and teachers remotely, host live literacy workshops, and provide ongoing coaching to educators beyond our immediate location. This investment will allow us to expand The Reading Trail to learners and educators across Nigeria and, ultimately, to families and schools in other countries.

**2. Solar Power Infrastructure**
Reliable electricity is essential for delivering consistent online instruction and maintaining uninterrupted learning. We will invest in a solar energy system to ensure that power outages do not disrupt virtual classes, teacher training, content creation, or day-to-day operations. This will improve the quality and reliability of our services while reducing long-term operating costs.

**3. Training and Capacity Building**
We will recruit and train literacy educators in The Reading Trail methodology, ensuring that every child receives structured, evidence-based reading instruction. We will also develop training resources that equip parents and teachers with practical strategies to support children's reading development.

**4. Awareness and Community Engagement**
Funding will support awareness campaigns that educate parents, schools, and communities about the importance of early literacy intervention. Through both digital and community outreach, we aim to increase access to The Reading Trail and encourage more families to seek support before reading difficulties become long-term learning barriers.

These investments will create a strong foundation for sustainable growth, enabling His Vine Learning Center to deliver high-quality literacy instruction consistently, expand its reach, and support significantly more children, parents, and educators than is currently possible.
growthTargets:
## 12-Month Goals

Over the next 12 months, His Vine Learning Center aims to strengthen and expand The Reading Trail, increasing access to quality literacy intervention for children while equipping more parents and educators with the skills to teach reading effectively.

Our key goals are to:

* **Support at least 200 children** through The Reading Trail, helping them build strong foundational reading skills and greater confidence.

* **Train at least 100 parents** with practical, evidence-based strategies to support their children's reading development at home through workshops and virtual coaching sessions.

* **Train at least 50 educators** in The Reading Trail methodology, enabling them to deliver structured, high-quality reading instruction in their classrooms and learning centres.

* **Establish a reliable virtual learning system** by investing in high-speed internet and solar power, allowing us to provide uninterrupted online reading intervention, teacher training, and parent coaching.

* **Expand our digital presence and community awareness**, reaching at least 5,000 parents and educators through literacy campaigns, webinars, and educational content that promote the importance of early reading intervention.

* **Strengthen and refine The Reading Trail** by developing additional teaching resources, assessment tools, and parent guides based on learner outcomes and feedback.

By the end of the 12-month period, we aim to have established The Reading Trail as a trusted literacy intervention program that is improving reading outcomes for children while building the capacity of parents and educators to support literacy development within their homes, schools, and communities.
revenueModel:
## Revenue Model

His Vine Learning Center operates as a social enterprise with a diversified revenue model designed to ensure long-term sustainability while making quality literacy intervention accessible to children and families.

Our primary source of revenue is tuition from our reading intervention programs, including one-on-one and small-group literacy sessions delivered through The Reading Trail.

As The Reading Trail grows, we will generate additional revenue by offering professional development and certification training for teachers, schools, and learning centres seeking to implement our structured literacy methodology. We will also provide parent workshops and coaching programs that equip families with practical strategies to support children's reading development at home.

The Reading Trail curriculum, instructional guides, workbooks, and other literacy resources will be available for purchase by parents, educators, schools, and partner organizations. These resources will support both in-person and online learning while creating an additional source of earned income.

We also plan to establish partnerships with schools, educational organizations, and NGOs that require literacy intervention services, teacher training, or curriculum support. These partnerships will create opportunities for institutional contracts and program delivery.

While grants and philanthropic funding will play an important role in helping us expand our reach, our long-term strategy is to build a financially sustainable organization through earned income generated from our programs, training services, educational resources, and strategic partnerships.
socialImpact:

The impact of The Reading Trail is best seen in the lives of the children and families it serves. In less than six months, the program has supported more than 50 children on their journey to becoming more confident readers, with many demonstrating significant improvements in reading fluency, confidence, and classroom participation.

Children like **Peniel, Zion, Jaden, Vinah, and Yovani** represent the reason we do this work. Each came to us with unique reading challenges, but through structured instruction, consistent practice, and family involvement, they have made remarkable progress. Their success has not only improved their reading ability but has also increased their confidence, willingness to learn, and participation both at home and in school. Their parents have shared encouraging testimonials describing the transformation they have witnessed in just a few months.

Beyond individual success stories, The Reading Trail creates a ripple effect. Parents gain practical skills and confidence to support learning at home, while educators who adopt our methodology are equipped to help many more children become successful readers. As more teachers are trained, the impact extends far beyond the learners we work with directly.

The grant will also contribute to economic impact by creating new jobs for literacy educators and operational staff while generating opportunities for trained facilitators to deliver reading instruction within their communities. By improving foundational literacy, we are helping children build the skills they need for future academic achievement and lifelong opportunities, while strengthening the capacity of families and educators to support the next generation of readers.

Every child who learns to read confidently has the potential to change the course of their education. Every parent who learns how to teach reading becomes a lasting partner in that child's success. Through The Reading Trail, we are creating both immediate and long-term impact—one child, one family, and one community at a time.

His Vine Learning Center is committed to building a sustainable literacy enterprise that continues to create impact long after the grant period ends. While grant funding will provide the resources needed to strengthen and expand The Reading Trail, our long-term sustainability strategy is built on diversified income, strategic partnerships, and continuous innovation.

Our primary source of sustainability will be earned income from reading intervention programs, including one-on-one and small-group literacy sessions delivered through The Reading Trail. As awareness grows and more families recognize the value of early reading intervention, we expect enrollment to increase steadily.

In addition, we will establish partnerships with schools, educational organizations, NGOs, and corporate partners to deliver literacy programs, educator training, and community-based reading initiatives. These partnerships will expand our reach while creating sustainable opportunities for program delivery.

To ensure quality as we grow, we will continue to invest in educator training, monitor learner outcomes, and refine The Reading Trail based on feedback from children, parents, and teachers. By maintaining high standards and demonstrating measurable impact, we will strengthen our reputation, attract new partners, and build the trust needed for long-term growth.

Our vision is to make The Reading Trail a widely accessible literacy solution that equips children to read confidently while empowering parents and educators to become active partners in every child's reading journey.

The stoves are designed to significantly reduce smoke emissions, improve fuel efficiency, and lower cooking costs while minimizing exposure to harmful indoor air pollution.
By using less charcoal than traditional stoves, our solution helps families save money, protects users' health, and reduces pressure on forests by lowering charcoal consumption. The stoves are durable, easy to use, and suitable for both urban and rural communities.
Beyond selling the stoves, we create awareness on clean cooking practices, educate customers on their economic and health benefits, and build a distribution network that makes the product accessible to underserved communities. Through this solution, we aim to improve public health, support environmental sustainability, create employment opportunities, and contribute to Nigeria's transition to cleaner household energy.

problem:
In Nigeria, the failure of our education system is no longer silent. Each year, the majority of candidates who sit for JAMB score below the threshold needed for meaningful university admission a statistic so alarming it signals a national learning crisis. We are quietly breeding a culture of the “olodo uprising,” where children move through school without understanding, and a generation across Africa gets duller every day. 
In Nigeria alone, over 20 million school-age children are either out of school or severely underserved academically. Those who remain in school often lack access to supplementary learning support that could close the performance gap. Parents who want better for their children have no affordable, intelligent, and locally relevant solution.
This is not only Nigerian. Across Africa and lower-income communities worldwide, families face the same gap: expensive tutoring, overloaded schools, and no affordable way to support early learning and real schoolwork. Nova by KTribe starts in Edo to break this cycle locally, then scales globally as a low-cost AI learning layer so no child becomes an “olodo” simply because of price.
The result: academic underperformance, low confidence, and generational cycles of educational inequality, all of which could be broken with the right technology.
solution:
Nova is an AI-powered learning app that gives every child a world-class, private "lesson teacher" on their phone or tablet, available 24/7.
Instead of paying ₦30,000+ for a human tutor who comes twice a week, Nova provides an interactive AI tutor named Aria for a highly affordable monthly subscription. Aria doesn't just give answers; she patiently teaches the child step-by-step until they understand.
Here is how Nova solves the problem for the average Nigerian student:
1. The "No Guesswork" Placement Test: When a student joins, Nova gives them a quick test to find their exact weaknesses. Whether they are in Primary 4 or SS3, Nova identifies their true level (Tiers 1 to 5) and builds a personalized timetable to fix their specific gaps.

2. The 24/7 Patient Teacher (Aria): If a student is stuck on a difficult WAEC Mathematics or Physics topic at 11:00 PM, they can tell Aria. Aria will explain it in simple English (or their native language) and ask, "Should we start from the beginning, or do you want to try a practice question?

3. 100% Aligned to the Nigerian Curriculum: Unlike foreign apps, Nova is programmed with local curriculums. Students aren't just learning random topics; they are preparing directly for their continuous assessments, Common Entrance, WAEC, NECO, and JAMB.

4. Interactive & Addictive Learning: Nova stops learning from being boring. When Aria teaches a topic, she generates short Explainer Videos, creates instant practice worksheets, marks them immediately, and rewards the student with XP points and interactive games when they pass.

5. World-Class Standard, Locally Priced: Nova is a global platform built for 50+ languages, meaning a child in Nigeria gets the exact same world-class AI technology as a child in Canada or Japan, but priced for the African reality.
In short: Nova replaces the expensive, unreliable private home tutor with a patient, brilliant AI companion that helps students actually understand their subjects, pass their exams, and enjoy learning again.

problem:
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) are the backbone of Nigeria's economy, accounting for 96.9% of all businesses, contributing 46.3% of GDP, and providing 87.9% of national employment. A significant proportion of fashion and tailoring businesses operate within this MSME segment, yet many remain largely informal and underserved by technology. 
Nigeria's fashion industry has evolved into one of Africa's largest creative sectors, creating employment, fostering entrepreneurship, and driving local economic activity. Despite this growth, the majority of independent tailors and fashion entrepreneurs still rely on paper measurement books, notebooks, spreadsheets, and memory to manage their daily operations. As their customer base grows, misplaced measurements, missed delivery dates, forgotten balances, and inefficient production become increasingly common.
These operational challenges cost businesses revenue, reduce customer trust, and limit their ability to grow beyond a single location.
At TechMarho, our conversations with local tailoring businesses revealed that the problem is not a lack of talent. It is the absence of affordable digital tools designed specifically for how African tailoring businesses operate. Existing software is often too expensive, too generic, or built for industries that do not reflect the unique workflow of fashion entrepreneurs.
Smart Tailor was created to bridge that gap.
solution:
Smart Tailor is a business management platform built specifically for African fashion entrepreneurs.
Rather than replacing how tailors work, Smart Tailor digitizes the processes they already understand. It brings together customer measurements, order management, production tracking, payments, inventory, and business records into one simple platform that can be accessed from anywhere.
The vision extends beyond software. We are building the digital infrastructure that enables fashion entrepreneurs to operate professionally, serve more customers with confidence, and grow sustainable businesses.

problem: Nigerian secondary school students preparing for WAEC and JAMB often rely on AI study tools that are fragmented into separate features such as notes, chat, quizzes, and exam simulators. Students must constantly switch between these tools, which breaks learning continuity, slows down studying, and provides little sense of progress. Early feedback highlighted three major issues with existing experiences: they felt repetitive, slow, and scattered, making exam preparation less efficient and more frustrating.
solution: Xenon is an AI-powered study platform that unifies the entire learning journey into a single guided experience called Xenon Flow. Instead of jumping between disconnected tools, students study one topic through a continuous sequence of notes, inline AI explanations, instant knowledge checks, quizzes, targeted remediation, and mastery resources. The platform also tracks mistakes, personalizes revision, measures exam readiness, and provides realistic exam simulations, all while maintaining a calm, mobile-first experience designed specifically for WAEC and JAMB students.
mvpDescription:
The MVP focuses on delivering the core Xenon Flow experience for science subjects (Physics, Chemistry, and Biology). Students can:
Select a WAEC/JAMB topic and progress through a guided learning path.
Study structured notes with inline AI explanations.
Complete instant micro-checks and topic quizzes.
Receive targeted remediation based on incorrect answers.
Track mistakes in a centralized Mistakes system.
Unlock mastery resources including exam tips, mnemonics, formulas, and flashcards.
Continue unfinished study sessions and revisit completed ones through Flow Replay.
View their study progress and readiness from a mobile-first dashboard.
The MVP validates Xenon's central idea: replacing disconnected AI study tools with one seamless, personalized learning journey.

Xenon's early version attracted 40+ Nigerian secondary school students, who generated dozens of AI-powered notes and quizzes. Feedback from these users identified key pain points; repetitive content, slow workflows, and fragmented learning which directly informed the redesign into the current Xenon Flow experience. The platform now has a live Next.js build with core features, including Flow, Mistakes tracking, remediation, Mastery guides, and a mobile-first interface.

problem: Nigerian gyms lose revenue and members daily because they run on WhatsApp, cash, and paper logbooks. Members pay inconsistently, walk in without valid memberships, and churn silently because there's no system tracking expiry or renewal. Gym owners have no visibility into who's paid, who's active, or how much revenue they're actually collecting. Existing gym software is built for Western markets, priced in dollars, and ignores the realities of Nigerian payment infrastructure and gym operations.
solution: DotFit is a gym management platform built specifically for Nigerian gyms. Members self-onboard via a Progressive Web App, pay through Paystack (money goes directly to the gym owner's account via subaccount splits), and check in using a rotating QR code on a tablet kiosk — with their photo displayed for identity verification. Gym owners get a real-time dashboard showing member status, revenue, check-in activity, and automated email notifications for expiry warnings, payment confirmations, and renewals. The system eliminates cash leakage, automates membership lifecycle management, and gives gym owners data they've never had before.
mvpDescription: DotFit is a fully functional, live product with three surfaces: (1) A member-facing PWA where gym members sign up, select a plan, pay via Paystack, view payment history, manage their membership, and generate a TOTP QR code for check-in. (2) A tablet-based kiosk that displays a rotating QR code every 30 seconds — valid members get a green flash with their photo displayed, expired members get a red flash and an automatic renewal email. (3) An owner dashboard for member management, revenue tracking, plan configuration, staff access control, pause approvals, and a live check-in feed. The backend runs Django on Fly.io with 554 passing tests, Celery for automated tasks, and full CI/CD via GitHub Actions.
tractionMetric: Gym onboarding rate — we're targeting 5 gyms onboarded within the first 3 months of sales operations, with a break-even target of 27 gyms at ₦40,000/month each.
teamExpertise: Emmanuel Omoragbon (Founder/CTO) — Senior Backend Engineer with experience building production-grade systems. B.Sc. Computer Science, University of Benin. Built the entire DotFit platform end-to-end: Django backend, Next.js frontend, Paystack integration, automated billing, CI/CD pipeline. Currently also Lead Software Engineer at a social platform startup. Philip Ndubisi Dumzo-Ajufo (Sales Partner) — handles direct gym outreach, demos, and relationship management across Lagos gyms.
challenges: (1) Sales velocity — we need to onboard gyms faster but are currently limited by a two-person team and limited transport logistics. (2) SMS-based authentication — many gym members don't have email addresses, so we need to integrate SMS login via Termii to remove the biggest adoption friction. (3) Hardware provisioning — gyms need an Android tablet for the kiosk check-in system, and subsidising tablets would accelerate onboarding. (4) CAC business registration is in progress but not yet complete.

growthTargets: 27 gyms onboarded (break-even), 1,500+ active gym members on the platform, ₦1,080,000 monthly recurring revenue, expansion beyond Lagos into Abuja and Port Harcourt, launch of multi-location tier for gym chains.
revenueModel: Monthly SaaS subscription. Standard plan: ₦40,000/month per gym location. Multi-Location plan: ₦75,000/month. One-time setup fee: ₦20,000 per location. All member payments flow directly to gym owners via Paystack subaccount splits — DotFit charges the gym, not the members.
socialImpact: DotFit formalises an informal industry. Nigerian gyms currently operate without systems, losing revenue to cash leakage and member churn. By digitising payments, membership tracking, and check-ins, DotFit increases gym revenue by 15-30%, improves member retention, and gives gym owners the operational data needed to grow sustainably. This directly supports small business growth, employment in the fitness sector, and financial inclusion through cashless payments. Each gym onboarded protects 3-10 existing jobs and creates conditions for the gym to hire more staff.
sustainabilityPath: DotFit reaches break-even at 27 gyms (₦1,080,000 MRR against current burn rate). The SaaS model generates predictable recurring revenue with low marginal cost per additional gym. Once the platform is proven in Lagos, expansion to other Nigerian cities requires only sales — the product is already multi-tenant and location-agnostic. Long-term revenue expansion includes premium features (analytics, trainer management, smart access control) and transaction-based revenue from in-gym purchases processed through the platform.

problem:

While they have valuable messages, products, or services to share, many do not have access to professional media coverage or the digital skills needed to promote their activities effectively.

As a result, many important events are poorly documented, receive little online engagement, and miss opportunities to connect with people beyond those who attend physically. This limits their visibility, growth, and long-term impact in an increasingly digital world.
solution:

We offer videography, photography, live streaming, video editing, audio editing, graphic design, and social media content creation to ensure every event is professionally documented and effectively presented.

problem: In Benin City, there is a pervasive and accepted culture of mediocrity in the printing and branding industry, where poor finishing is treated as the norm rather than as a failure. I have seen, time and time again, how local entrepreneurs including myself are forced to source our printed and branded materials from as far away as Lagos, Abuja, or even Kano just to escape the cycle of substandard quality here in Benin city. This finishing gap is more than just an inconvenience it is a significant barrier to businesses in Benin City. When a brand’s physical materials do not reflect its true value or worth, it loses authority, and its potential for market dominance is stifled. At OnoseBrands, I have witnessed firsthand the frustration of businesses settling for less because they lack a reliable local partner who refuses to compromise. We are currently operating in a landscape where printing is treated as a commodity transaction, rather than the vital brand-building asset that it is. This disconnect where the quality of delivery consistently fails to meet the standard of the vision is the fundamental problem that OnoseBrands was built to eradicate.
solution:
At OnoseBrands, we are shifting the industry narrative by replacing the 'it will do' culture with a rigorous, uncompromising standard of excellence. We aim to staturate the market with our own products. Our solution is built on a simple, non-negotiable philosophy, If I wouldn’t accept the work for my own brand, I will never send it to a client.

We have replaced the industry’s tolerance for error with a culture of intentionality and precision. Every project is subjected to a strict quality-control process, if a product doesn’t meet our '1% executive standard, we reproduce it at our own cost until it is perfect. By acting as both a premium producer and a demanding gatekeeper for quality, we are proving that businesses in Benin City no longer need to outsource their branding to Lagos or Abuja to get world class results. We are not just selling print services we are selling the peace of mind that comes with knowing your brand’s physical touchpoints. We exist to ensure that when a local business hands over their business card or presents their products, they do so with absolute confidence, knowing they are making a lasting, professional impression for their brand.
mvpDescription: Our MVP is a premium print A5 soft or hardback jotters tailored for entrepreneurs, businesses, and corporate/social events. We identified a critical market need for high-quality, professional and excellent print and our jotters have become our bestseller because we deliver a 'sharp quality' direct imaging (DI) print finish that stands out significantly from competitors in the region. In the last month we produced over 700 copies of jotters altogether for 4 different clients.
tractionMetric: In the last 30 days, we successfully scaled our production to over 700 units of custom-branded jotters for 4 distinct corporate and event clients. problem:
For millions of visually impaired Nigerians, the simple act of stepping outside their front door is a high-risk gamble. Independent navigation requires a level of predictability that simply does not exist on the average Nigerian street, yet the visually impaired are forced to navigate this complex environment using mobility tools that fundamentally fail to match their lived reality. Leaving home shouldn't require a leap of faith, but without reliable assistance, every journey is burdened with the anxiety of the unknown.
The most common tool at their disposal, the traditional white cane has remained largely unchanged for decades and is entirely reactive. A cane can only alert a user to a hazard after physical contact has already been made, offering no forewarning, context, or alternative routing. It cannot differentiate between a harmless discarded box and an open, hazardous drainage trench. Furthermore, relying on a cane permanently occupies one of the user's hands and visibly marks them as vulnerable, while providing absolutely no spatial awareness or directional guidance if they become disoriented.
While modern assistive technologies exist globally, they are overwhelmingly designed for predictable, first-world environments and fail entirely in a local context. These imported smart devices are not only prohibitively expensive for the average Nigerian, but they are also practically useless when faced with local infrastructure challenges. Built on the assumption of ubiquitous high-speed internet, reliable electricity grids, and standardized sidewalks, these devices completely break down in the face of Nigeria's fluctuating power, spotty connectivity, and the specific chaos of its urban centers.
Because both the cane and imported tech fail them, users are left highly vulnerable to dynamic daily hazards. A route memorized flawlessly on Monday can become treacherous by Tuesday due to sudden road excavations, shifting market stalls, or unexpectedly parked motorbikes blocking the path. Without proactive, real-time feedback, visually impaired individuals are forced to rely heavily on outdated mental maps or the unpredictable goodwill and intervention of passing strangers to avoid stepping into danger.
Ultimately, the absence of a localized, proactive, and offline-capable navigational tool creates a severe gap between merely surviving a walk and navigating with true autonomy. This technological void does more than just present a physical danger; it actively strips visually impaired Nigerians of their safety, dignity, and confidence. It forces many to limit their movement and participation in society entirely, highlighting an urgent need for a solution built specifically for the realities of the world they actually walk in.
solution:
Across Nigeria and much of the developing world, rapid transformation is underway. Massive infrastructural projects, road expansions, and drainage constructions are constantly reshaping the urban environment. While this development signals progress, it creates a chaotic and ever-changing daily hazard for the visually impaired. Memorized routes can become dangerous overnight. IRIS is engineered specifically for this reality. It acts as an intuitive, wearable companion that actively interprets a fast-changing landscape. It steps in where traditional tools fall short to turn a precarious walk through a busy, unpredictable street into a safe and manageable journey.

The foundation of IRIS lies in its total independence from the local grid. Imported smart gadgets are built on the assumption of ubiquitous WiFi and standardized sidewalks. This causes them to fail entirely when faced with spotty connectivity or unexpected local roadwork. IRIS processes its environmental data entirely offline, right on the device. Whether a user is navigating heavy city traffic, dodging unexpectedly parked motorbikes in a crowded market, or walking through a remote rural community, the core navigation remains unbroken. By bypassing high data costs and network dead zones, it provides a consistent safety net that never disconnects.

Physically, the device challenges decades of stigma by replacing the highly visible white cane with a sleek, comfortable wristband. Rather than waiting for a physical collision with a newly dug drainage trench or a misplaced market stall, IRIS uses gentle, intuitive haptic pulses on the wrist to guide users smoothly around obstacles long before they reach them. This hands-free approach keeps the user's hands completely free to carry items or navigate doors. It also allows them to move through public spaces without immediately being marked as vulnerable, preserving their dignity and privacy.

To make spatial navigation effortless, IRIS features a conversational voice assistant that describes the world in natural, human-like language. Instead of robotic prompts, it speaks to the user the way a sighted friend would, pointing out hazards and outlining the path ahead. As the user walks, IRIS learns and remembers their frequent routes, adapting to their routines. When an unexpected challenge does arise, such as an entirely blocked road, a single tap opens a live voice or video connection to a trusted caregiver. This allows loved ones to see what is happening in real time and assist remotely.

Ultimately, IRIS is more than just a local intervention. It is a statement that Nigerian engineering is ready to export groundbreaking innovation to the world. By solving mobility for the complex, offline, and highly dynamic realities of our own environment, we have built a system far more resilient than expensive Western alternatives. If IRIS can safely guide a visually impaired user through the rapid infrastructural transformations and bustling streets of our local cities, it can scale seamlessly to Nairobi, Mumbai, or anywhere else on the globe. This is a homegrown, AI-powered hardware solution ready to show the global market that technology engineered for our toughest local challenges is exactly what the rest of the developing world has been waiting for.
mvpDescription:
The IRIS MVP is a fully functional wearable navigation system built for real-time, fully offline operation. It combines a portable compute pack, an onboard AI processor, and depth-sensing vision sensors to perform live object detection and spatial mapping without needing internet connectivity, allowing it to function reliably even in areas with poor network coverage or unstable power.
The device delivers guidance through gentle haptic feedback on the wrist rather than audio alone, alerting users to obstacles before contact, along with a conversational voice assistant that describes the surrounding environment in natural language. An emergency caregiver feature is also fully functional: a single tap opens a secure live video or voice stream to a trusted caregiver through a remote dashboard, allowing real-time remote assistance when the user encounters an unexpected obstacle or gets disoriented.
We are currently on our third working prototype, refining hardware durability, obstacle detection accuracy, and battery performance based on field testing ahead of our first pilot deployment.
