revenueModel:
Core Model: B2B2B2C. Hardware reaches end users at zero cost; monetization happens upstream through nine interconnected revenue streams.

I. Hardware Distribution & Sales

Corporate Sponsor Bulk Sales: Banks and telecom foundations purchase the IRIS Base Model in bulk at a discount. Units are distributed free to visually impaired users through the National Association of the Blind (NAB). Sponsors participate to fulfill CSR/ESG compliance mandates.
Diaspora & Domestic Retail: Direct sales of Lite, Base, and Pro tiers to Nigerians abroad purchasing for relatives at home, financially capable domestic buyers, and through hospital/healthcare facility partnerships.
BNPL Installment Partnerships: Partnerships with Nigerian fintechs (Carbon, FairMoney, Kuda) offering payment plans from 5 months to 2 years. Vhorde receives full device price upfront, minus a 3 to 5% facilitation fee; the fintech partner absorbs credit risk and collections.
International Grants & Subsidies: Non-dilutive funding pursued from bodies like ATscale, World Bank, and FCDO, used to subsidize hardware for users who fall outside the sponsor and retail channels.

II. Recurring Software Revenue

Caregiver App Subscriptions: The base companion app is free. Premium tier (₦1,500/month) adds call recording, history logs, and activity reports for up to 3 caregivers. HD Video tier (₦3,500/month) adds HD live video and the H-Bands health dashboard for up to 5 caregivers.

III. High-Margin Data Licensing

Sensory Data Licensing: Opt-in, fully anonymized African urban movement data (e.g., navigating Lagos traffic, obstacles like open gutters) licensed to global robotics and AI training firms at a 92% gross margin.
GPS Urban Mapping Data: Anonymized GPS routing and pedestrian movement data sold to urban planning agencies, logistics companies, and government infrastructure developers at a 92% gross margin.

IV. Spin-Off Product Lines

IRIS Dev Board Sales: Standalone edge AI vision boards sold to students, indie developers, IoT builders, and telecom companies, priced from ₦5,000 to ₦350,000. Spins off into its own entity after Year 2.
IRIS H-Bands Consumer Sales: Haptic wristbands repositioned as a standalone fitness wearable at ₦65,000, undercutting imported Fitbits. Targets the general wellness market before spinning off into its own entity after Year 5.
socialImpact:
Vhorde Technologies addresses a severe poverty crisis affecting millions of Nigerians. The country has 6.2 million visually impaired citizens as of 2026, with 32,650 new cases added annually. Of these, 75% currently rely on street begging to survive, and for every visually impaired person, at least one family member is forced to abandon their own economic activity to become a full-time caregiver, expanding the real economic footprint of this crisis to over 12 million Nigerians.
IRIS restores independent mobility to visually impaired users through offline-first navigation, obstacle detection, and emergency alerts in local languages (Pidgin English, Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo), delivered at zero cost through the sponsor channel. This in turn frees up family caregivers to return to work or education, directly reversing the poverty multiplier effect. Because the model is B2B2B2C, cost, the single biggest barrier to assistive technology in emerging markets, is removed entirely for the end user.
The impact scales fast: Year 1 targets 30,000 units deployed, growing to 233,515 active users by Year 5, achieved by capturing just 5% of the ₦46.5 billion CSR/ESG budget pool already committed by NGX-listed companies. Beyond direct impact, the model creates local manufacturing jobs through vocational assembly centres that require no advanced technical training, positions Nigeria as a source of unique African datasets for the global AI and robotics industry, and helps corporates meet legal obligations under the Discrimination Against Persons with Disabilities Prohibition Act 2018.
IRIS's mission aligns with several UN Sustainable Development Goals, including SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-Being), SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities), and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals)
sustainabilityPath:
Vhorde Technologies is built for rapid, self-sustaining profitability rather than long-term dependency on external funding. Phase 1 validation reaches operational break-even after just 157 units sold, and IRIS Year 1 breaks even at approximately 10,090 units out of a 30,000-unit target, meaning the majority of Year 1 sales generate pure net contribution. This is achieved through a deliberately staged manufacturing strategy: Phase 1 uses pre-built, off-the-shelf components to minimize upfront capital risk, while a one-time ₦13,700,000 investment in an in-house PCBA machine at the 10,000-unit milestone permanently cuts manufacturing costs by 57.4% and lifts gross margins to a target of 52.1% across all hardware tiers.
Financial resilience comes from revenue diversification rather than reliance on any single stream. Corporate sponsor sales, diaspora and domestic retail, BNPL instalment partnerships, and international grants fund the hardware layer; Caregiver App subscriptions generate recurring, high-margin (85%) software revenue; and anonymized sensory and GPS data licensing, unique African datasets with no meaningful global competition, adds a 92% gross margin revenue layer at near-zero incremental cost. This means no single channel failing (for example, a slowdown in corporate CSR budgets) would be fatal to the business.
The model is also structurally designed to become progressively more self-funding over time. The IRIS Dev Board and IRIS H-Bands begin as internal product lines seeded through free giveaways to build market credibility, then convert to standalone revenue-generating businesses that eventually spin off into independent entities (Dev Board after Year 2, H-Bands after Year 5), diversifying Vhorde's long-term value beyond the core assistive hardware mission. Nigeria's Economic Development Incentive (EDI) tax credit further supports sustainability by returning 5% annually on qualifying capital expenditure as the company scales its physical manufacturing infrastructure from Year 3 onward.
By Year 1, the company is projected to reach a 22.9% net profit margin, growing to a stable ~23.4% average through Year 5, with cumulative 5-year net profit of approximately ₦207.6 billion. This level of profitability, reached organically through diversified, high-margin revenue streams, is what ultimately makes IRIS sustainable independent of continued grant or investor support after the initial capital injection.

problem:
Accessing laboratory services can be difficult for many people, especially those with busy schedules, mobility challenges, health conditions, or limited transportation options. In many cases, patients have to travel long distances and spend valuable time waiting at healthcare facilities just to provide samples for routine tests.
As a result, many people delay important medical tests or avoid them altogether, leading to late diagnosis and delayed treatment. This challenge is particularly common among working professionals, elderly individuals, pregnant women, and people living in underserved communities.
There is a growing need for a more convenient and accessible way to access laboratory services without compromising quality, accuracy, or professionalism. Healthcare should be available when and where people need it most.
solution:
Solution 

Rosette Mobile Lab brings professional laboratory services directly to people's homes, offices, schools, and communities. Instead of requiring clients to visit a laboratory, our trained personnel travel to them for sample collection, eligible rapid testing, and result delivery.
Our service is designed to save time, reduce stress, and make healthcare more accessible. By eliminating unnecessary travel and long waiting periods, we help individuals access important diagnostic services conveniently and comfortably.
We are committed to providing reliable, professional, and confidential laboratory services while maintaining high standards of quality and patient care. Through this approach, Rosette Mobile Lab encourages early testing, supports timely diagnosis, and helps improve health outcomes within the communities we serve.
mvpDescription: At Rosette, samples are collected by our well trained phlebotomists and transported safely back for investigation by our scientists, afterwards results are released timely to our clients without delays or long waiting period.
tractionMetric: Rosette Mobile Laboratory's key traction metric is the number of patients and organizations served through our mobile laboratory services. Since launching, we have seen growing demand for home and office sample collection, rapid diagnostic testing, and timely result delivery. We also track repeat customers, referral rates, and partnerships with businesses that require convenient healthcare testing services for their staff. These metrics demonstrate increasing trust in our services and validate the need for accessible laboratory solutions outside traditional healthcare facilities
teamExpertise: Rosette Mobile Laboratory is led by a team with experience in laboratory science, healthcare service delivery, customer relations, and business operations. Our team understands the importance of accurate testing, timely results, patient confidentiality, and quality healthcare services. We have the technical knowledge required for sample collection, rapid diagnostic testing, result processing, and client support. Beyond medical expertise, we are committed to making healthcare more accessible by bringing laboratory services directly to homes, offices, schools, and communities. Our combined experience allows us to provide reliable, convenient, and professional healthcare solutions while maintaining high standards of safety, accuracy, and customer satisfaction.
challenges: Our biggest challenge is acquiring the resources needed to scale our operations and reach more people who need convenient laboratory services. We currently face limitations in purchasing diagnostic equipment, expanding our mobile service capacity, and increasing awareness of our services. Transportation and logistics costs also affect our ability to efficiently serve clients across different locations, this is as a result of us relying on the paid services of other laboratories to carry out operations and not owing our own. Additionally, building trust and educating the public about the benefits of mobile laboratory services requires significant outreach efforts. Addressing these challenges will enable us to provide faster service, improve operational efficiency, and make quality healthcare more accessible to underserved communities.

socialImpact:

problem:

Customers frequently receive cakes that are poorly designed, do not match what they ordered, arrive late, or are made with low-quality ingredients. Many also have to visit different vendors to buy cakes, souvenirs, gift packages, and other celebration items, making the entire process stressful, time-consuming, and expensive.

Another challenge is that people living with diabetes and other health conditions, such as diabetes, cannot consume regular cakes made with sugar, leaving them with limited options and causing them to miss out on celebrating special moments with their loved ones.

These challenges reveal a clear gap in the celebration industry: customers need a trusted, reliable, and quality-focused brand that delivers premium celebration products, offers healthier alternatives, and provides a seamless experience from order to delivery.

We also cater to customers with special dietary needs by offering sugar-free cakes sweetened with natural honey instead of refined sugar, ensuring that people living with diabetes and other health conditions can celebrate safely without compromising on taste or quality.

To meet increasing customer demand and maintain consistent quality, we plan to invest in commercial baking equipment and a solar-powered energy system. problem:
Nigeria is witnessing a growing burden of lifestyle-related diseases such as hypertension, diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular conditions, many of which are linked to unhealthy dietary habits and poor nutrition. According to the World Health Organization, 36.1% of Nigerian adults aged 30–79 are living with hypertension, while 12.4% of adults are obese, underscoring the urgent need for healthier dietary choices.

In Benin City, Edo State, awareness of healthy living and nutrition is steadily increasing. More people are seeking healthier alternatives that support disease prevention and overall wellness. However, access to fresh, nutritious, affordable, and convenient meals remains limited, with many consumers still relying on fast food and highly processed meals because they are more readily available. This gap between growing health awareness and limited healthy food options creates a significant opportunity for innovation. 
Nutriplace&veg was established to bridge this gap by providing fresh, nutritious, and convenient meals and beverages that make healthy eating easier and more accessible. By encouraging healthier food choices, Nutriplace&veg contributes to preventive healthcare, helping individuals reduce their risk of diet-related diseases while promoting healthier lifestyles within the community.
solution:
Nutriplace is a preventive nutrition and wellness enterprise dedicated to reducing the growing burden of lifestyle-related diseases by making healthy eating accessible, convenient, and enjoyable. We believe that good nutrition is one of the most effective forms of preventive healthcare, and our mission is to empower individuals to make healthier food choices before disease develops.

Our solution is to provide freshly prepared, nutrient-rich smoothies, cold-pressed juices, salads, healthy bowls, grilled meals, and other wholesome food options made from fresh, locally sourced ingredients. These products are designed to meet the needs of busy professionals, families, students, fitness enthusiasts, and individuals seeking to prevent or better manage diet-related health conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular disease.

Beyond providing healthy meals, Nutriplace&veg promotes nutrition awareness through wellness education, healthy eating campaigns, and practical guidance that encourages sustainable lifestyle changes. We aim to make healthy eating simple, affordable, and part of everyday life rather than an occasional choice.

As we grow, we will expand our impact by developing dehydrated fruits, vegetables, herbs, and natural seasoning blends. These shelf-stable products will increase access to nutritious food options across Nigeria, reduce post-harvest food losses, create additional income opportunities for local farmers, and make healthy nutrition available to communities beyond our physical locations.

Through innovation, preventive nutrition, and sustainable food solutions, Nutriplace&veg is building a future where healthier food choices are readily available, helping to reduce the incidence of lifestyle-related diseases while improving the overall health and well-being of Nigerians.

problem:
A lot of small and medium-sized enterprises still run their businesses with notebooks, calculators and handwritten receipts. Because of this, many business owners do not know their correct stock balance, daily profit, total expenses or what their staff are doing when they are not around.

Some shops lose money through stock theft, wrong pricing, unrecorded sales, expired products and poor record keeping. In many cases, the owner only discovers the problem when it has already become serious.

Another problem is that customers often move from one shop to another looking for a product without knowing where it is available. At the same time, many shops may have those products in stock, but customers outside their immediate area do not know.

Most existing Point of slae systems are either too expensive, difficult to use or require extra equipment. This makes it hard for small shops to start using a proper business-management tool.
solution:
Martly is a retail-management platform that helps shops record sales, manage stock, track expenses, generate receipts and monitor staff activities from a phone (telegram, whatsapp), tablet  or computer.

A small business can start with Martly Mobile and use only a smartphone to record sales and generate receipts on either Telegram or Whatsapp. As the business grows, it can move to other higher plans.
And with the included Buisiness Assistant (Yobo derived from 'Iyobo'), business analysis has never been much easier.  A business owner can monitor important activities even when away from the shop,  understanding sales, stock, expenses and business performance in simple language.

Martly also gives businesses the option to make their shops visible on the Martly Marketplace. Since Martly already knows what the shop has in stock, selected products can be shown to customers. A customer can search for an item and see nearby shops that currently have it available.

This means Martly does not only help businesses manage their shops; it also helps customers find products close to them.

Martly already has a working web platform that allows a business to create an account and manage sales, products, stock, expenses, purchases, customers, staff and reports.

A cashier can record a sale and generate a receipt. The business owner can monitor stock, view reports and see what is happening in the business.

The system also supports different staff roles, so each person only sees the part of the system related to their job.

Martly has low-stock alerts, expiry tracking, automatic reports and Telegram features. It also has a marketplace feature where a business can choose to make its shop and selected products visible to customers.

The platform is already built to support different businesses separately, with each business having its own secure account and records.

problem: Millions of women across Africa still lack access to continuous reproductive healthcare. Without timely support, many develop preventable reproductive health complications that affect their education, work, families, and overall well-being. Women in underserved communities are disproportionately affected.
solution: HerSync is an AI-powered reproductive health platform supporting women from menstruation to menopause. It combines personalized health insights, trusted care, telehealth, community support, health education and women’s health products into one connected ecosystem. Unlike standalone health apps, HerSync empowers women to understand their bodies, access the right care and stay supported throughout every stage of life.
mvpDescription:
HerSync's MVP is a live mobile application available on the Google Play Store and Apple App Store that helps women manage their reproductive health from menstruation to menopause. Users can track their menstrual cycles, ovulation, symptoms and moods, receive AI-powered personalized health insights, access reproductive health education, join community discussions, discover Women's Health Talks, securely store their health history, and connect with telehealth services, trusted healthcare providers and women's health products, including our upcoming Synca menstrual pain relief device. 

The platform has onboarded over 8,000 registered users. It is validating both its B2C model through subscriptions and its B2B2C model through ongoing engagements with HMOs, employers, and healthcare providers, including AXA Manzard, Clearline, and Redeem Health Centre.
tractionMetric: 3,500+ monthly active users (47% MAU rate) with over 8,000 registered users. Building a community of over 15,000 women and growing B2C validation through premium subscriptions while expanding B2B2C engagements with HMOs, employers, and healthcare providers.
teamExpertise: HerSync is led by Chioma Adeh (Co-Founder & CEO), a Medical Laboratory Technician with experience in reproductive health, and Philip Igboba (Co-Founder & CTO), a software engineering specialist with expertise in building scalable mobile and AI-powered digital health solutions. They are supported by a multidisciplinary team across product, engineering, marketing and operations, combining healthcare expertise with technology to improve access to reproductive healthcare for women across Nigeria.
challenges: Our biggest challenges are scaling user acquisition, commercializing the Synca menstrual pain relief device, and expanding partnerships with healthcare providers, employers, and HMOs. Additional funding will help us accelerate product distribution, strengthen marketing, and grow our team to reach more women across Nigeria.
fundUsage:
The ₦5 million grant will be used to accelerate HerSync's growth by strengthening our technology, expanding market reach, and preparing for commercial scale.

₦1,200,000 – Enhance the HerSync platform by improving AI-powered health insights, adding new features, and strengthening product infrastructure.
₦1,500,000 – Support pilot production and inventory for the commercial launch of the Synca menstrual pain relief device.
₦900,000 – Execute digital marketing campaigns, user acquisition initiatives, and community engagement to grow our user base.
₦500,000 – Expand Women's Health Talks and reproductive health outreach programmes across universities and underserved communities.
₦600,000 – Recruit and support key team members in product, marketing, customer support, and operations.
₦300,000 – Cover regulatory compliance, monitoring and evaluation, and contingency costs.

Total: ₦5,000,000

This allocation will enable HerSync to accelerate product adoption, expand access to reproductive healthcare, create new jobs, and position the business for sustainable growth.
growthTargets:
• Grow from 8,000 to over 50,000 registered users.
• Launch Synca commercially across Nigeria.
• Secure at least five enterprise partnerships with HMOs or employers.
• Increase monthly recurring revenue to over ₦5 million.

• Expand Women's Health Talks to additional universities and communities.
revenueModel: HerSync generates revenue through Premium subscriptions, sales of the Synca menstrual pain relief device, women's health products, marketplace commissions, telehealth consultations, and enterprise subscriptions through HMOs and employers (HerSync for Work).
socialImpact: HerSync improves women's access to reproductive healthcare through technology, health education, and affordable health products. Over the next 12 months, we aim to grow from 8,000 to over 50,000 registered users, deliver Women's Health Talks to more than 20,000 women, and improve access to trusted reproductive healthcare across Nigeria. The grant will also support the creation of 10 – 15 direct jobs while increasing productivity and reducing preventable reproductive health challenges through earlier intervention and education.
sustainabilityPath: HerSync operates a diversified revenue model built on Premium subscriptions, Synca device sales, women's health products, marketplace commissions, and enterprise partnerships with HMOs and employers. Over the next 12 months, we aim to reach more than 50,000 users, achieve more than ₦5 million in monthly recurring revenue, and establish at least 5 enterprise partnerships. This diversified model enables HerSync to scale sustainably while reducing long-term dependence on grant funding.

problem: Many people have important memories, achievements, photographs, and personal stories that deserve to be preserved and displayed, yet they lack access to affordable, high-quality, and personalized display solutions. As a result, certificates remain stored away, family photographs are forgotten on phones, and meaningful stories lose visibility over time. Additionally, there are limited products that allow people to celebrate their identity, culture, and personal journeys in a creative and lasting way.
solution: MemoryWalls creates personalized framing and wall décor solutions that help individuals, families, and organizations preserve memories, celebrate achievements, and express identity. Through custom-designed frames, printed displays, and the ENI Collection—which features a person’s name, its meaning, an inspiring quote, and an optional photograph—we transform ordinary memories and personal stories into meaningful pieces of art. Our products are affordable, durable, and designed to enhance homes, offices, schools, and public spaces while preserving moments that matter for generations.
mvpDescription:
MemoryWalls is a creative framing, printing, and wall décor company that helps people preserve memories, celebrate identity, and beautify their spaces through customized framing solutions. Our products include picture frames, quote frames, certificate frames, Spotify frames, and personalized wall décor.

Since launching in January 2024, MemoryWalls has served customers through a simple social-commerce model, allowing clients to order custom products via social media and direct consultations
In November 2025, we launched the ENI Collection, a personalized product line that features an individual’s name, the meaning of the name, an inspiring quote, and an optional photograph. The collection transforms personal identity and stories into beautiful display pieces for homes, offices, and gifting purposes.
Today, MemoryWalls combines design, printing, and craftsmanship to create meaningful products that preserve memories and enhance interior spaces
tractionMetric:
MemoryWalls was founded in January 2024 to help individuals, families, and businesses preserve memories and enhance their spaces through high-quality customized framing and décor solutions. Since launch, the company has sold over 2,000 products, serving customers across different sectors and building a strong reputation for quality craftsmanship, creativity, and personalization.
Building on this success, MemoryWalls launched the ENI Collection in November 2025, a culturally inspired product line rooted in Edo heritage. “Eni” is an Edo word meaning “name.” Each ENI piece celebrates identity and personal stories by featuring an individual’s name, the meaning of the name, a short inspirational quote, and an optional photograph. The collection transforms names and personal narratives into meaningful decorative pieces for homes, offices, and gifting purposes while promoting cultural appreciation and preserving identity through creative design.
Since its launch, the ENI Collection has recorded over 650 sales, demonstrating strong market demand for personalized and culturally relevant products.
teamExpertise: Our team of four combines expertise in graphic design, printing, framing, photography, branding, customer service, and business operations. We have hands-on experience in creating personalized décor products, developing creative concepts, managing production processes, and delivering quality customer experiences. The team oversees design, printing, product development, sales, marketing, and fulfillment, ensuring that every product meets high standards of quality and craftsmanship.
challenges: Our biggest challenges include scaling production capacity to meet growing demand, acquiring modern equipment to improve efficiency, expanding our market reach beyond our current customer base, and securing working capital for inventory, operations, and product innovation. We are also seeking support to strengthen our digital presence and develop systems that will enable us to serve customers more efficiently across Nigeria and beyond
fundUsage:
The ₦5,000,000 grant will be used to scale MemoryWalls’ production capacity, improve product quality, and expand market reach. A significant portion will be invested in acquiring modern production equipment, including framing and printing tools, to increase efficiency and reduce production time. Funds will also be used to purchase raw materials and inventory needed to meet growing customer demand.

Additionally, we will strengthen our marketing and digital presence to reach more customers across Edo State and Nigeria, while developing new culturally inspired products such as the ENI Collection. The grant will also support workforce development by creating employment opportunities for young creatives and artisans involved in design, printing, and production.

Through this investment, MemoryWalls aims to increase sales, serve more customers, preserve cultural identity through creative products, and contribute to the growth of Edo State’s creative and small business ecosystem.
growthTargets:

Our target is to sell at least 3,500 additional products, including custom frames and ENI Collection pieces, while growing revenue by over 100%. We plan to expand our distribution channels, strengthen our digital presence, and increase brand awareness through strategic marketing and partnerships.
We also aim to create 3–5 new jobs for young creatives and artisans in design, printing, framing, and customer service. In addition, we will introduce new personalized and culturally inspired products, improve production efficiency through equipment upgrades, and establish MemoryWalls as a leading creative décor and personalization brand in Nigeria.
By the end of the 12-month period, we expect to have served thousands of additional customers, significantly increased sales, and strengthened our contribution to Edo State’s creative economy.
revenueModel: MemoryWalls generates revenue through the sale of custom frames, personalized décor products, printing services, branding materials, and the ENI Collection. We earn income from direct customer orders, corporate projects, gift items, and interior décor solutions. Our business operates through both online and offline channels, allowing us to reach a diverse customer base. We also generate repeat sales through referrals, returning customers, and seasonal demand for personalized gifts and commemorative products.
socialImpact: MemoryWalls preserves memories, celebrates identity, and promotes Edo culture through creative products such as the ENI Collection. By transforming names, stories, photographs, and achievements into meaningful display pieces, we help individuals connect with their heritage and personal journeys. The business creates employment opportunities for young creatives, supports local suppliers and artisans, and contributes to the growth of Edo State’s creative economy. Through our products, we also encourage cultural appreciation and storytelling.

Investment in equipment, marketing, and workforce development will enable us to serve more customers efficiently while maintaining quality standards. Over time, these efforts will position MemoryWalls as a leading personalized décor and creative solutions brand in Nigeria.

problem:
At D-ULTIMATE FARM, we started with a simple observation: despite the increasing demand for quality pork and other livestock products, many farmers still struggle to produce enough because of the high cost of feed, limited access to modern farming practices, disease outbreaks, and inadequate funding. These challenges discourage many young people from venturing into livestock farming and reduce the ability of existing farmers to expand.

In our community, many households and businesses depend on livestock products, yet the supply often falls short of demand or is sold at prices that many families cannot afford. We believe this gap can be bridged through efficient and sustainable livestock production. Our farm is committed to raising healthy animals using improved management practices, reducing losses, creating employment opportunities, and contributing to food security. With the right support, we can expand our operations, increase production, and make quality livestock products more accessible while building a profitable and sustainable agricultural business.
solution:
D-ULTIMATE FARM is providing a practical and sustainable solution through modern livestock farming, with piggery as our primary focus. Our approach is centered on raising healthy animals using proper housing, quality feeding, routine veterinary care, and good farm management practices to improve productivity and reduce losses.

As we grow, we plan to expand into fishery, goat rearing, and crop production to create an integrated farming system where resources are efficiently utilized and waste is minimized. This will not only increase our production capacity but also improve sustainability and profitability.

Beyond food production, our goal is to create employment opportunities for young people, encourage more people to see agriculture as a viable business, and contribute to improving food security in our community. With the support of this grant, we will be able to expand our livestock facilities, purchase quality breeding stock and equipment, improve feed production and storage, and adopt better technologies that will enable us to produce more efficiently and serve a larger market.
mvpDescription:
Our Minimum Viable Product (MVP) is our operational piggery, where we have successfully begun raising pigs using improved management and feeding practices on a small scale. This has enabled us to validate the market demand for quality pork while gaining practical experience in livestock production and farm operations.

Although we are still in the early stage, our farm has demonstrated that there is a consistent demand from local consumers, meat vendors, and processors for healthy, well-raised livestock. The experience and feedback we have received have strengthened our confidence in the business model and highlighted the need to expand production.

The next phase is to scale our piggery operations, improve our infrastructure and equipment, and gradually integrate fishery, goat rearing, and crop production to build a sustainable, integrated livestock enterprise.
tractionMetric: Our key traction metric is our consistent monthly revenue of approximately ₦120,000, generated from pig sales and the sale of pig waste (manure). Since launching, we have sold 2 pigs, currently maintain 6 healthy pigs in our farm, and have served 9 customers, with 4 of them returning for repeat business. These early results validate the demand for our products and demonstrate the potential for growth as we expand our production capacity.
teamExpertise:
Our team combines practical livestock farming experience with strong leadership, business management, and community engagement skills. As the founder, I oversee the day-to-day operations of D-ULTIMATE FARM, including animal care, feeding, hygiene, record-keeping, customer relations, and sales. Through hands-on experience, I have developed a solid understanding of pig production, farm management, and the importance of maintaining healthy livestock.

Beyond farming, my background in leadership, human resource management, and public relations has strengthened my ability to manage people, build partnerships, communicate effectively with customers, and plan for sustainable business growth. As the farm expands, we intend to bring in additional technical and veterinary expertise to further improve productivity and operational efficiency.
challenges:
Our biggest challenge at the moment is limited access to funding to expand our operations. While we have successfully established the farm and are generating revenue, our current resources are not enough to increase our livestock capacity, improve housing facilities, purchase quality breeding stock, and invest in modern equipment.

Another major challenge is the rising cost of quality animal feed and veterinary care, which affects production costs and limits how quickly we can grow. We also need better infrastructure for efficient waste management and storage as production increases.

Despite these challenges, we have continued to operate, retain customers, and generate consistent income. With the right financial support, we are confident we can scale our production, create more jobs, and meet the growing demand for quality livestock products in our community.
fundUsage:
The ₦5 million grant will be used to scale the operations of D-ULTIMATE FARM and increase our production capacity. A significant portion of the funding will be invested in expanding our piggery by constructing additional pens, purchasing quality breeding stock, and improving our feeding and watering systems.

Part of the grant will also be used to purchase feed in bulk, acquire essential farm equipment, strengthen biosecurity and veterinary care, and improve waste management to ensure a healthier and more sustainable farming operation. In addition, we will invest in basic record-keeping and marketing to help us reach more customers and improve business efficiency.

This investment will enable us to increase livestock production, serve more customers, create employment opportunities, and build a stronger, more sustainable agribusiness that contributes to food security in our community.
growthTargets:
Over the next 12 months, our goal is to transform D-ULTIMATE FARM from a small-scale piggery into a more established livestock enterprise. We aim to increase our pig population from 6 to at least 30 healthy pigs, improve our breeding capacity, and consistently meet the growing demand from our customers.

We also plan to grow our customer base from 9 to over 50 active customers, increase our monthly revenue from approximately ₦120,000 to over ₦600,000, and create 2–3 direct employment opportunities within the farm. In addition, we intend to strengthen our farm infrastructure, implement better record-keeping and biosecurity measures, and begin laying the foundation for integrating fishery and goat rearing into our operations.

These targets will position D-ULTIMATE FARM for sustainable growth while contributing to food security, job creation, and increased access to quality livestock products in our community.
revenueModel:
D-ULTIMATE FARM generates revenue primarily through the sale of healthy pigs to individual buyers, meat vendors, and processors. We also earn additional income from the sale of pig waste (organic manure), which is used by crop farmers as fertilizer.

As the business expands, we will increase revenue by improving our breeding capacity, selling more pigs, and introducing complementary livestock enterprises such as fishery and goat rearing. This diversified revenue model will strengthen the business, reduce risk, and ensure sustainable long-term growth.
socialImpact:
D-ULTIMATE FARM is committed to improving food security, creating employment, and supporting sustainable agriculture in our community. By producing healthy, high-quality livestock, we help increase the availability of affordable animal protein while reducing dependence on supplies from distant markets.

Our farm also creates income opportunities for local workers, feed suppliers, transporters, and veterinary service providers. Through the sale of pig manure as organic fertilizer, we support crop farmers and encourage environmentally sustainable farming practices by turning waste into a valuable resource.

As we grow, we aim to empower more young people by demonstrating that livestock farming is a profitable and sustainable business, contributing to economic development and improved livelihoods within our community.
sustainabilityPath:
D-ULTIMATE FARM's path to sustainability is built on steady revenue growth, efficient farm management, and continuous reinvestment. Income generated from the sale of pigs and organic manure will be reinvested into expanding livestock capacity, improving farm infrastructure, and maintaining high standards of animal health and welfare.

We are also reducing business risk by gradually diversifying into fishery and goat rearing, creating multiple sources of income while making better use of available farm resources. As our customer base grows and more buyers return for repeat purchases, we expect to achieve stronger cash flow and long-term profitability.

Our goal is to build a financially independent agribusiness that continues to grow through good management, customer trust, and consistent product quality, ensuring lasting impact beyond the grant period.

problem:
Long Chain Problem in the Housing Market
The Mechanics: When a direct property caretaker posts a walkthrough video of a vacant apartment to an agent group chat, secondary agents scrape and repost it to their personal WhatsApp statuses and other social media platforms. This content-sharing cascades down multiple levels, creating an unregulated chain of speculative sub-agents.
The Financial Impact: When a house hunter finally discovers the listing through a downstream agent, every intermediary in the chain demands a payout for their "marketing effort". This artificial layering inflates agency fees by up to 400%, transferring an exorbitant financial burden to the tenant while creating a breeding ground for opacity and transaction fraud.
solution:
Roov is a video-first proptech platform that completely dismantles the exploitative "Long-Chain" network by digitizing the entire rental lifecycle.

Direct-to-Consumer Marketplace: We bypass predatory middlemen (Agents) by allowing primary property caretakers to list vacant apartments for free, capturing high-quality 1-minute video walkthroughs and mapping listings geographically so that house hunters can discover apartments directly.

The Tenant Management Model: We entirely eliminate upfront, inflated agency and inspection fees. Instead, we introduce a nominal annual Tenant Management Fee, shifting the financial model toward continuous administrative value, including maintenance coordination and dispute resolution.

Centralized Operations (SaaS): Roov moves the rental experience out of chaotic WhatsApp groups into a structured dashboard for automated rent collection, digital maintenance ticketing, and official tenant communications via Direct Messaging.

Trust via Escrow Infrastructure: In partnership with a licensed financial institution, we secure portable caution deposits in a neutral Escrow Wallet. This safeguards tenant funds and introduces portability, allowing tenants to seamlessly transfer their deposits to future properties.
mvpDescription:
Roov is built as an end-to-end client-server proptech platform optimized for low-latency marketplace operations.
The technical framework is powered by six core pillars:

1. Low-Latency Video-First Engine
How it works technically: Built as a video-first delivery architecture, Roov utilizes content delivery networks (CDNs) and optimized cloud storage buckets (R1) to stream asynchronous video content seamlessly under varying network conditions.
Functionality: House hunters can watch apartment tour videos without network issues or skip in the video.

The Whatsapp Status Rule: Property caretakers record and upload high-quality property walkthroughs capped at a maximum duration of 1 minute. Upon upload, our backend processing pipeline automatically compresses and optimizes the video files for mobile viewing without sacrificing visual clarity.
Functionality: House hunters can visually audit, tour, and access real estate options remotely before opting for a physical inspection for free.


2. Vacancy Data Map (Geospatial Mapping Engine)
How it works technically: Roov utilizes advanced mapping technologies and GIS data layers to plot real-time property availability across urban centers.
Functionality: When a property manager marks a unit as vacant, the system instantly updates a centralized geospatial database, anchoring the 1-minute video asset to a specific geometric coordinate. House hunters interact with an intuitive map interface to filter, pinpoint, and virtually tour vacant low-cost apartments without requiring a physical middleman.


3. Portable Escrow Wallet Infrastructure
How it works technically: in partnership with a licensed financial institution, this module utilizes secure API ledgers to isolate and hold caution deposits outside the landlord’s personal finances.

The "Portable" Logic: When a tenancy ends, instead of off-boarding the funds back into a commercial bank account which triggers transaction frictions, charges and delays, the deposit remains fluid within the Roov financial ecosystem. The tenant can seamlessly port their existing caution deposit balance directly to their next Roov-managed apartment, completely eliminating the need of paying a double deposit or Fraud.


4. Integrated Payment & Ledger Infrastructure
How it works technically: A robust Paystack transaction collection and routing engine integrated into Roov to handle automated, split, and recurring payments.
Functionality: The system automatically processes and reconciles monthly B2B SaaS subscription fees (₦2,000/unit or ₦24,000/unit), annual B2C inspection passes, and bulk rental payments while maintaining clean financial ledger logs for property managers and caretakers.

5. Instant Messaging & Communication Node
How it works technically: A lightweight, WebSocket-driven messaging framework designed to function optimally even in low-bandwidth environments.
Functionality: Replaces chaotic WhatsApp groups with organized, threaded communication channels. Property managers can broadcast global announcements to an entire building or initiate direct, timestamped instant messages with individual tenants.

6. Automated Maintenance & Repair Ticket Pipeline
How it works technically: A state-driven ticketing system that structures maintenance requests from creation to resolution.
Functionality: Tenants log repair issues through a simple interface. The platform automatically formats the request, flags it on the property manager's dashboard, tracks repair progress states, and documents completion logs.

In Nigeria, where grid supply remains unreliable and available generation is still far below business demand, many SMEs are forced to depend on petrol and diesel generators to keep operating. Recent sector reports placed national generation around 4,300MW during gas supply constraints in 2026, showing that businesses cannot rely on grid availability alone.

For offices, pharmacies, hospitals, retailers, and other commercial users, this creates a recurring energy burden. Many businesses spend between ₦600,000 and ₦10 million monthly on petrol or diesel fuel, in addition to grid electricity payments, maintenance, generator servicing, and unplanned downtime. With fuel and electricity costs now significantly higher than pre-subsidy levels, energy has become one of the biggest threats to SME profitability.

These recurring monthly expenses on power create a constant revenue leak, leading to:
Reduced profitability
Spoilage of goods, medicines, and temperature-sensitive products due to unreliable power supply
Increased cost of goods and services due to added energy costs
Budgeting uncertainty due to fuel price volatility
Poor customer retention due to affected service quality
Limited business growth and reduced job creation

Although solar adoption is growing, the cost of purchasing a full solar system remains a major barrier for many SMEs. Full ownership often requires large upfront payments or long repayment plans, forcing businesses to divert working capital away from inventory, staffing, expansion, and customer service. Many businesses need reliable clean energy, but they cannot afford to carry the full capital cost of ownership.
solution:
An understanding of the challenges faced by our target customers and the limitations of existing solutions led us to Green Band, an Energy-as-a-Service initiative under Safebox Energy Ltd.

Safebox Energy Ltd. has operated since 2020 and has served over 300 clients across 8 Nigerian states through solar energy deployments and clean-energy solutions. Green Band builds on this operating experience by giving businesses access to reliable solar power without requiring them to purchase a full solar system upfront.

Instead of relying on unstable grid supply, expensive petrol or diesel generators, or heavy solar ownership repayment plans, Green Band allows businesses to access 24-hour clean energy through a one-time commitment fee of ₦1 million and a fixed energy rate of ₦200 per kWh.

Green Band is a tool for business growth and profitability. We provide solar system deployment, energy monitoring, maintenance, billing support, and ongoing technical service, while customers focus on their core operations. For our target customer groups, at ₦200 per kWh, we provide reliable power at a cost that is competitive with, and in many cases less than, commercial grid tariffs once reliability and generator fallback are considered.

Compared to expensive generator dependence, high fuel-price exposure, and solar ownership models that can require over ₦18 million in upfront or financed system costs, Green Band reduces the capital burden of clean-energy adoption. With this in place, businesses can redirect a significant portion of the money previously lost to fuel, downtime, and maintenance into inventory, staffing, expansion, and customer retention.
mvpDescription:
Green Band is an Energy-as-a-Service initiative under Safebox Energy Ltd. It enables small businesses and commercial customers to access reliable, clean, and affordable solar energy without the high upfront cost of purchasing a complete solar system.
Safebox Energy Ltd. provides the operating foundation for Green Band, having served over 300 clients across 8 Nigerian states in the past 6 years. Green Band is the EaaS product being validated and scaled under this wider company experience.
The MVP includes:
Energy subscription management: Businesses can subscribe to a solar energy plan based on their energy needs.
Customer onboarding and energy assessment: Users can register and receive a customized energy solution based on their daily power consumption.
Solar system deployment: Green Band installs and maintains solar power systems at customer locations.
Energy monitoring: Customers can monitor their energy usage and system performance.
Digital payment and billing: Users can make recurring payments through flexible subscription or pay-as-you-go plans.
Maintenance and technical support: Customers can report issues and receive ongoing maintenance without additional service charges.
With this MVP, businesses can lower their operating costs, improve business productivity, and access clean energy without significant capital investment.

tractionMetric:
In the last 12 months of validating and scaling Green Band as an Energy-as-a-Service initiative, we have:
Secured 12 adopting business clients across offices, pharmacies, hospitals, and commercial users
Reached an estimated Green Band monthly revenue of ₦5.1 million
Deployed and managed 180 kW of solar capacity across customer sites
Achieved up to 70% reduction in customer energy costs compared to generator-heavy operations
Maintained strong customer retention through continuous monitoring, maintenance, and technical support
Built a waiting list of 26 additional business customers for the next deployment phase

Collectively, the team has over 36 years of combined experience delivering clean energy projects, managing business operations, developing innovative products, and scaling sustainable enterprises.
Peace Ekeinde, Chief Executive Officer: Environmental management professional with 6+ years of experience leading renewable energy projects, business development, and strategic partnerships.
Oluchi Odili, Chief Operating Officer: Cleantech entrepreneur experienced in operations, rural electrification, regulatory compliance, and sustainable infrastructure.

Joseph Ovwiokpe, Operations Manager: Experienced project and operations manager with expertise in execution, stakeholder coordination, and service delivery.
Hope Omesehin, Accountant: Finance professional with 4+ years of experience in financial planning, budgeting, investment strategy, and SME financing.
Peace Ikekhua, Human Resource & Customer Success Officer: Renewable energy customer relations specialist focused on client onboarding, retention, and post-installation support.

challenges:
Our biggest challenge is pushing market expansion and faster customer conversion.
Having validated demand for Energy-as-a-Service through 12 adopting business clients, our next challenge is expanding market awareness, strengthening our distribution network, and converting more SMEs that need reliable power but cannot afford full solar ownership.
Access to growth capital is critical to scaling our customer acquisition, improving monitoring and billing systems, strengthening technical support, and shortening deployment timelines as we reach underserved SMEs that require reliable and affordable energy solutions.
fundUsage:
While we have validated Green Band, we are now scaling its market presence, customer acquisition, and service delivery systems. The ₦5 million grant will be strategically invested to expand Green Band’s Energy-as-a-Service operations and convert more SMEs from generator dependence to reliable clean energy.
Marketing & customer acquisition: 50 % of funds that is 2,500,000 will be used to acquire more customers, increase online and offline brand presence, run targeted SME outreach, pursue strategic partnerships, and activate sales channels in business clusters such as pharmacies, offices, hospitals, retail stores, and commercial service providers.
Operations & technical support: A sum of ₦800,000 that is 16% will cover installation tools, preventive maintenance support, technician mobility, after-sales response, and service support across customer locations.
Product development & technology improvements: 20% of the funds (₦1,000,000) will be used to improve customer management, billing, usage tracking, payment reconciliation, energy monitoring, and reporting systems.
Distribution channels & logistics: A sum of ₦700,000, that is 14% covers the cost of  transportation, installation logistics, customer site visits, delivery coordination, and field operations required to activate new customers.
Expected Outcomes
With this investment, Green Band will:
Increase the number of SMEs and commercial customers adopting Energy-as-a-Service
Improve customer acquisition and conversion from the current waiting list
Expand our installed clean energy capacity
Reduce customer reliance on diesel and petrol generators
Lower customers’ monthly energy costs and improve business cash flow
Strengthen distribution and marketing channels for faster growth
Create new technical, sales, and operational jobs while building a more sustainable and profitable clean-energy business
growthTargets:
In the next 12 months, our key growth target is to increase Green Band adoption from 12 current adopting clients to 75 active business customers, while building a pipeline toward 150 customers.
This phased target is more realistic because Green Band is an asset-backed Energy-as-a-Service model that requires customer assessment, system deployment, installation logistics, monitoring, and ongoing maintenance. Our immediate goal is to prioritize high-value commercial users such as pharmacies, hospitals, offices, retailers, and service businesses with predictable energy needs.
At our current tariff of ₦200 per kWh, our present average monthly revenue of ₦5.1 million represents approximately 25,500 kWh of monthly energy demand. To reach ₦30 million in monthly recurring revenue, Green Band needs to supply approximately 150,000 kWh monthly. This is achievable with about 75 active customers averaging 2,000 kWh monthly, or with fewer customers where the mix includes higher-consumption hospitals and commercial facilities.
We also aim to expand more deeply within Edo State, while entering Lagos and Delta States through targeted business clusters, partnerships, and distribution channels. We aim to achieve at least 90% customer retention and create 46 direct and 9 indirect jobs in installation services, training, field sales, technical support, and logistics.
revenueModel:
Green Band generates revenue primarily through Energy-as-a-Service payments.
Our core revenue model includes:
A one-time customer commitment fee of ₦1 million
A fixed energy usage fee of ₦200 per kWh
Recurring customer payments based on monthly energy consumption
Installation and onboarding fees where applicable
Maintenance, monitoring, and technical support built into the service model
In addition to Green Band’s EaaS model, Safebox Energy also generates revenue from outright sales of complete solar systems, solar panels, and solar generators for customers who prefer full ownership. However, Green Band’s main growth focus is recurring revenue from businesses that need reliable clean energy without the heavy upfront cost of owning a solar system.
socialImpact:
The rising cost of goods and services is partly driven by the increasing cost of petrol and diesel, which many Nigerian businesses rely on for power generation. A product that costs ₦2,000 today can quickly become more expensive when a business has to absorb higher energy expenses, generator servicing costs, spoilage, and downtime. This places a heavy financial burden on businesses, forcing many to either pass additional costs on to consumers, reduce profit margins, or cut jobs to stay afloat.
Green Band Energy-as-a-Service improves the financial stability of these businesses by giving them predictable, reliable, and cleaner energy at a fixed rate of ₦200 per kWh. This helps businesses reduce generator dependence, protect inventory, improve service delivery, retain customers, and plan their monthly expenses more effectively.
For pharmacies and hospitals, reliable power also supports the safe storage of medicines, vaccines, laboratory samples, and other temperature-sensitive products. For offices and commercial users, it improves productivity, customer service, and working conditions.
As businesses become more stable, they are better positioned to grow, retain staff, create jobs, and keep prices tied to value rather than fuel inflation. By creating jobs such as sales agents, installers, technicians, and customer support officers, Green Band contributes to closing unemployment gaps in Edo State and beyond while accelerating the adoption of sustainable clean energy solutions.
sustainabilityPath:
We are capitalizing on the growing demand for affordable and reliable energy without the huge financial investment required to own a solar system.
Green Band’s sustainability is built on recurring revenue from Energy-as-a-Service. Customers pay a one-time commitment fee and a fixed usage-based energy rate of ₦200 per kWh. This gives the business predictable cash flow while giving customers reliable power without full system ownership.
Safebox Energy’s wider track record also strengthens Green Band’s sustainability. Since 2020, Safebox Energy has served over 300 clients across 8 Nigerian states, giving us practical experience in deployment, maintenance, customer support, and clean-energy operations.
We currently operate through recurring EaaS payments, installation/onboarding fees, and outright solar system sales for customers who prefer full ownership. Over the next phase of growth, we will strengthen recurring cash flow by expanding Green Band to more SMEs and commercial customers, including offices, pharmacies, hospitals, retail businesses, and event-based commercial users.
This diversification will increase revenue, improve asset utilization, strengthen market reach, and support the long-term financial sustainability of Green Band while expanding access to affordable, reliable clean energy.

problem:
Farmers in Edo State work hard and still struggle to make ends meet. Not because they are not producing, but because they rarely get to sell at a fair price.
Fresh catfish leaves my farm at wholesale rates. By the time that same fish gets to the market, customers are paying four thousand naira and above per kilogram, sometimes more depending on bargaining power. The farmer takes the lowest share of that chain. The people buying the food pay the highest price. The middleman sits comfortably in between.
Families in our communities pay more than they should for food that was grown nearby. FarmGate closes that gap.
Beyond affordability, Edo State has rich agricultural assets and a growing tourism agenda under Governor Okpebholo's SHINE programme. Yet there is no farm gate experience in Benin City that brings food, culture, and community together in one place. FarmGate is built to fill that space.
solution:
FarmGate is a direct-to-consumer retail, dining, and delivery experience built on Mohrz Farm's existing production. It removes the middleman, brings fresh produce to the community at accessible prices, and creates an authentic Edo food experience across two channels: at the farm gate and at your doorstep.
Selling through FarmGate increases revenue per fish by up to two to three times compared to wholesale. Same fish, same farm, significantly more value captured at source.
The farm already produces catfish, broiler/Noiler poultry, plantain, and a vegetable garden including ugu, bitter leaf, scent leaf, waterleaf, and pepper. FarmGate sells this directly to the community in three ways.
At the farm gate, two sessions daily:
Morning session: fresh whole fish, plantain bunches, eggs, live chickens, and farm produce sold directly to residents at rates below the open market. Two hours, farm direct, no queue, no middleman.
Evening session: freshly grilled catfish, Edo black soup made with farm-grown vegetables and our own catfish, chicken amd catfish peppersoup, roasted plantain, grilled Broiler/Noiler chicken, and palm wine. Dine-in and takeout. The black soup is the signature dish, an authentic Edo meal made entirely from what is growing on this farm.
Online ordering with rider delivery:
When the evening grill session begins, the evening order window opens. Customers place orders for soups, plantain, or grilled meals, and riders deliver directly to them. People who cannot come to the farm gate still get farm-fresh food at their door.
This delivery layer transforms FarmGate from a local food stand into a community food supply service. It expands reach beyond foot traffic, creates additional income for local riders, and builds a recurring order base that is not dependent on people passing by the farm.
Once fully operational, FarmGate projects daily revenue of fifty thousand naira and above across both in-person and delivery channels, growing as the order base builds.
mvpDescription:
Mohrz Farm's MVP is its integrated, multi-enterprise production and direct sales system, currently live and operating.
Three active catfish ponds with approximately 1,800 fish across different growth stages. A staggered stocking model ensures a rolling harvest cycle rather than a single seasonal sale event.
Broiler/Noiler poultry running in two staggered batches of 50 birds each, managed through to maturity.
Approximately 200 plantain stems across multiple plots in staggered production, providing a near-continuous harvest.
A vegetable and herb garden in development: ugu, bitter leaf, waterleaf, scent leaf, and three pepper varieties, all future FarmGate inputs grown on the same land.
A full-time farmhand managing daily feeding, water quality, and livestock care under a structured daily reporting system.
Sales already happening: fresh catfish sold directly to individual customers on demand, smoked catfish sold on order to regular customers each cycle, and wholesale catfish sold to bulk buyers. 
FarmGate is the infrastructure that converts this existing production into its highest-value output. The farm is the engine. FarmGate is the gear shift.
tractionMetric: Mohrz Farm tracks three key traction metrics. First, revenue per kilogram of catfish produced: current wholesale benchmark is N3,000 per kg, with a FarmGate target of N8,500 and above per kg through direct retail and grilled meal sales, representing a 2 to 3 times uplift from the same production. Second, repeat order rate: 7 of our active smoked catfish customers return every production cycle without being solicited, demonstrating organic demand for processed farm produce even before a formal retail channel exists. Third, customer growth: we have grown from zero to 23 active repeat customers across wholesale, smoked catfish, and fresh fish channels purely through word of mouth, with no marketing spend to date. FarmGate is designed to convert this existing demand base into a structured, daily revenue operation.
teamExpertise:
Myself, Owner and Operator: ten years of operations and business management experience, Certified Business Analysis Professional (CBAP, IIBA, 2026). Manages all farm planning, finances, procurement, and strategy.
Full-time Farmhand: handles daily feeding, pond monitoring, poultry care, and farm maintenance.
Contract Farm Labour: land preparation, weeding, and ploughing as needed.
Contract Processing Staff: fish cleaning, smoking preparation, and packaging on demand.
challenges:
The first challenge is value capture. The farm produces quality catfish, poultry, and plantain but currently has no infrastructure to sell finished product directly to consumers. Every kilogram sold at wholesale price instead of retail is margin that does not return to the farm.
The second challenge is breaking into premium buyer channels. Hotels, restaurants, and eateries already have established supplier relationships and rarely onboard new vendors. FarmGate bypasses this barrier entirely by building our own consumer channel rather than competing for space in someone else's supply chain.
The third challenge is batch-dependent cash flow. Current income arrives in large irregular amounts at the end of each production cycle. FarmGate's daily retail and delivery model converts batch income into consistent daily revenue.
The fourth challenge is capital. The FarmGate site is cleared, the plan is complete, and the team is identified. The only thing missing is the funding to build it.

FarmGate stand construction (cement floor, metal frame, raffia roofing, half-wall sides in matching material, two access points, basic carpenter-built seating and tables for 16 to 20 persons): N1,050,000
Grill and preparation equipment (grills, gas cylinders, prep tables, utensils, serving ware): N400,000
Cold storage (chest freezer for catfish holding, drinks refrigerator): N450,000
Aquaculture probiotic system setup and first three-month supply: N280,000
Poultry litter biochar unit for waste treatment and soil amendment: N220,000
Initial stock and inputs (catfish batch, palm wine, seasoning, packaging): N350,000
Staffing runway, five new staff for three months (grill hand, cashier, service attendant, two part-time processing staff): N750,000
Marketing and launch (photography, social media, opening promotion): N120,000
Online ordering setup and first three months of rider logistics: N180,000
Working capital buffer for the first 90 days: N200,000
Total: N5,000,000
growthTargets:
Month 1 to 3: FarmGate stand built and launched. Morning walk-in session and evening grill session begin. Online ordering and rider delivery activated for the evening session. Smoked and fresh fish order system formalised. First consistent daily revenue established.
Month 4 to 6: Aquaculture probiotics fully integrated across all ponds. Catfish stocking increases to a minimum of 2,000 juveniles per cycle with a dedicated portion reserved for farm gate and delivery orders. Plantain from approximately 200 stems feeding both daily sales and the evening menu.
Month 7 to 9: Noiler poultry added to the evening menu as grilled chicken. Vegetable garden supplying all seasoning and side dish needs for FarmGate. Multiple revenue streams running consistently.
Month 10 to 12: Packaged smoked catfish explored for small retailers and personal shoppers. Direct supply to schools, offices, and catering events explored. The model is designed to be replicable across other Edo State farm gate locations using the same operational system.
revenueModel: Mohrz Farm runs five income streams from one integrated farm location. Wholesale catfish sales absorb surplus beyond farm gate capacity. Fresh fish direct orders go to customers at rates below the open market. Smoked catfish on order is an existing channel being formalised. FarmGate dine-in and takeout is the highest-margin channel, serving grilled catfish, Edo black soup, catfish and chicken pepper soup, and grilled Noiler chicken at the evening session. Online ordering with rider delivery allows customers to receive farm-fresh produce or prepared meals at their door during evening session hours. The model is multi-channel deliberately so that if one stream slows, the others continue generating revenue.
socialImpact:
The most direct impact is on the people in the surrounding community. FarmGate gives residents access to fresh fish and farm produce at rates below what they would pay in the open market, with no compromise on quality because it comes straight from the source.
Five new jobs are created immediately: a grill hand, a cashier, a front of house attendant, and two part-time processing staff. Two existing roles are retained and formalised. These are daily revenue jobs, not seasonal ones.
FarmGate also carries a cultural dimension. Edo black soup, made here with farm-grown ingredients, served at the farm where those ingredients grow, is cultural preservation through commerce. It is the kind of experience that makes Edo State worth visiting and worth investing in.
This sits directly inside Governor Okpebholo's SHINE Agenda on agriculture and tourism. FarmGate is a private sector, youth-led response to what that agenda calls for, built on private land, with local labour, serving local people from Day 1.
SDG 1, 2, 8, 12, 13, and 15 are addressed through integrated farm production, direct community retail, job creation, and sustainable practices including probiotics and biochar.
sustainabilityPath:
Mohrz Farm does not depend on a single income source or a single harvest cycle. Five revenue channels run from one farm location, and the staggered production model means income arrives regularly rather than in seasonal spikes.
FarmGate's margin structure is the key to self-sustainability. Selling grilled meals and direct retail at two to three times the wholesale rate means the stand covers its own operating costs and contributes profit back to the farm from approximately Month 4 onward.
The delivery layer builds a recurring customer base that grows independently of foot traffic, giving the business a compounding revenue engine that strengthens month on month. Longer term, the operational model is designed to be replicable, either as a second Mohrz Farm location or as a framework other Edo State farmers can adopt for their own farm gate operations.

problem: There is a critical gap between what schools teach and what employers need, leaving youth unemployable despite years of formal education.
solution: We train, mentor, and connect young people to jobs and business opportunities through practical, in-demand skills.
mvpDescription: The MVP of NextGen Skill Hub is a 4-week intensive, hands-on training cohort for 20-30 youths in 2 high-demand skills (e.g., Graphic Design and Digital Marketing), delivered in a physical hub/classroom with practical projects, mentorship, and a final certificate plus job/business linkage.
tractionMetric: Our key traction metric is the number of trainees who complete training and earn income (job, freelance, or business) within 60 days of graduation. Our target for the MVP is 70% income linkage rate from the first 25 trainees
teamExpertise: Our team combines expertise in practical skills training, youth mentorship, community mobilization, and small business management with a combined 5+ years of experience in teaching, digital skills, and grassroots entrepreneurship.
challenges: Our biggest challenges are limited training equipment/space, affordability for low-income youths, and building strong job placement linkages.

growthTargets: To train 150 youths across 6 cohorts, achieve a 70% income-linkage rate, and become self-sustaining through paid cohorts and partnerships.

This is achievable with about 75 active customers averaging 2,000 kWh monthly, or with fewer customers where the mix includes higher-consumption hospitals and commercial facilities.
We also aim to expand more deeply within Edo State, while entering Lagos and Delta States through targeted business clusters, partnerships, and distribution channels. We aim to achieve at least 90% customer retention and create 46 direct and 9 indirect jobs in installation services, training, field sales, technical support, and logistics.
revenueModel:
Green Band generates revenue primarily through Energy-as-a-Service payments.
Our core revenue model includes:
A one-time customer commitment fee of ₦1 million
A fixed energy usage fee of ₦200 per kWh
Recurring customer payments based on monthly energy consumption
Installation and onboarding fees where applicable
Maintenance, monitoring, and technical support built into the service model
In addition to Green Band’s EaaS model, Safebox Energy also generates revenue from outright sales of complete solar systems, solar panels, and solar generators for customers who prefer full ownership. However, Green Band’s main growth focus is recurring revenue from businesses that need reliable clean energy without the heavy upfront cost of owning a solar system.
socialImpact:
The rising cost of goods and services is partly driven by the increasing cost of petrol and diesel, which many Nigerian businesses rely on for power generation. A product that costs ₦2,000 today can quickly become more expensive when a business has to absorb higher energy expenses, generator servicing costs, spoilage, and downtime. This places a heavy financial burden on businesses, forcing many to either pass additional costs on to consumers, reduce profit margins, or cut jobs to stay afloat.
Green Band Energy-as-a-Service improves the financial stability of these businesses by giving them predictable, reliable, and cleaner energy at a fixed rate of ₦200 per kWh. This helps businesses reduce generator dependence, protect inventory, improve service delivery, retain customers, and plan their monthly expenses more effectively.
For pharmacies and hospitals, reliable power also supports the safe storage of medicines, vaccines, laboratory samples, and other temperature-sensitive products. For offices and commercial users, it improves productivity, customer service, and working conditions.
As businesses become more stable, they are better positioned to grow, retain staff, create jobs, and keep prices tied to value rather than fuel inflation. By creating jobs such as sales agents, installers, technicians, and customer support officers, Green Band contributes to closing unemployment gaps in Edo State and beyond while accelerating the adoption of sustainable clean energy solutions.
sustainabilityPath:
We are capitalizing on the growing demand for affordable and reliable energy without the huge financial investment required to own a solar system.
Green Band’s sustainability is built on recurring revenue from Energy-as-a-Service. Customers pay a one-time commitment fee and a fixed usage-based energy rate of ₦200 per kWh. This gives the business predictable cash flow while giving customers reliable power without full system ownership.
Safebox Energy’s wider track record also strengthens Green Band’s sustainability. Since 2020, Safebox Energy has served over 300 clients across 8 Nigerian states, giving us practical experience in deployment, maintenance, customer support, and clean-energy operations.
We currently operate through recurring EaaS payments, installation/onboarding fees, and outright solar system sales for customers who prefer full ownership. Over the next phase of growth, we will strengthen recurring cash flow by expanding Green Band to more SMEs and commercial customers, including offices, pharmacies, hospitals, retail businesses, and event-based commercial users.
This diversification will increase revenue, improve asset utilization, strengthen market reach, and support the long-term financial sustainability of Green Band while expanding access to affordable, reliable clean energy.

problem:

The current property market is highly fragmented. There is no trusted digital marketplace focused on Edo State that brings verified property owners, ethical real estate agents, and property seekers together in one transparent ecosystem.

At the same time, many young people are unemployed or underemployed despite having the willingness and capacity to work. They often lack structured opportunities to earn legitimate income through real estate without significant startup capital.

These challenges reduce public trust in the real estate sector, increase transaction costs, and limit economic opportunities for young people.
solution:

The platform will enable users to:
- Search verified properties for sale and rent.
- Connect with trusted property owners and approved agents.
- Request inspections.
- Access transparent property information.
- Reduce unnecessary intermediary costs.

To expand access and create employment opportunities, Almagor Connect will be supported by our Student Ambassadorship Programme.
