problem:
Nigeria faces a growing demand for affordable, high-quality poultry products, yet many households, restaurants and retailers struggle with inconsistent supply, high prices and poor-quality poultry. Small-scale poultry farmers also face challenges such as rising feed costs, limited access to finance, inadequate production infrastructure and weak market linkages, making it difficult to scale their businesses and meet market demand.
AFENAT Farm addresses these challenges by producing healthy, high-quality broiler chickens using good poultry management and biosecurity practices. We aim to provide a reliable supply of affordable poultry products, create jobs, improve food security, and strengthen local agricultural value chains through a sustainable and scalable poultry farming model.
solution:
AFENAT Farm provides a sustainable poultry farming solution by producing healthy, affordable and high-quality broiler chickens using modern poultry management practices and strict biosecurity measures.
Starting with a 100-bird Minimum Viable Product (MVP), we are building a reliable supply of poultry for households, restaurants, retailers and local markets. Our model focuses on efficient production, low bird mortality, and consistent product quality.
Beyond supplying poultry, AFENAT Farm creates employment opportunities, supports local suppliers, and promotes food security by making quality animal protein more accessible. As we grow, we will expand production, strengthen distribution channels and establish long-term partnerships with commercial buyers to ensure a consistent and sustainable supply of poultry products.
mvpDescription:
At AFENAT Farm, our Minimum Viable Product (MVP) is a small-scale poultry operation designed to test the market, generate early revenue and validate our production model before scaling up.
The MVP consists of:
Raising 100 healthy broiler chickens per production cycle.
Operating from a clean, biosecure poultry house with essential equipment.
Following proper feeding, vaccination and health management practices to ensure high survival and growth rates.
Selling live birds and processed chicken directly to households, retailers, restaurants and local markets.
Gathering customer feedback on quality, pricing and demand to improve future production cycles.
This approach allows me to minimize startup costs, build customer trust, establish a reliable sales network and reinvest profits into expanding flock size, improving infrastructure and introducing additional poultry products over time
tractionMetric:
At AFENAT Farm, our key traction metric is the percentage of our 100 broiler birds sold per production cycle.
For our MVP, we aim to:
Raise 100 healthy broiler birds to market weight.
Achieve a 95% survival rate (at least 95 birds reaching market weight).
Sell 100% of market-ready birds within 14 days.
Secure at least 10 repeat customers (households, restaurants, retailers, and meat vendors) for future production cycles.
Achieving these targets demonstrates strong market demand, validates our business model and provides the revenue needed to expand production in subsequent cycles.
teamExpertise:
Our team combines expertise in poultry production, business operations and marketing to ensure the success of AFENAT Farm.
Farm Manager: Oversees daily poultry operations, including bird health, feeding, vaccination schedules, biosecurity and overall flock management to ensure high productivity.
Operations & Finance Officer: Manages procurement of feed and supplies, financial records, budgeting, inventory and production planning to keep the business efficient and sustainable.
Sales & Marketing Officer: Responsible for customer acquisition, marketing, order management and building relationships with households, retailers, restaurants and other buyers to ensure consistent sales and repeat business.
Together, the team combines technical poultry knowledge, sound business management and effective market engagement to grow AFENAT Farm sustainably.
challenges:
As a startup poultry farm operating with an MVP of 100 broiler birds, our biggest challenges are:
Limited Working Capital: Rising costs of day-old chicks, feed, vaccines and medications make it difficult to scale production.
High Feed Costs: Feed accounts for the largest portion of our production expenses and frequent price increases reduce profitability.
Market Expansion: While we have identified local buyers, we need stronger distribution channels and long-term supply agreements with restaurants, retailers and bulk buyers.
Infrastructure Growth: We require improved poultry housing and equipment to increase production capacity while maintaining high biosecurity standards.
Access to Finance: Limited access to affordable financing restricts our ability to expand from 100 birds to a larger commercial operation.
Addressing these challenges will enable AFENAT Farm to increase production, improve efficiency, and provide a reliable supply of quality poultry products to our customers.
fundUsage:
The ₦5 million grant will be strategically invested to scale AFENAT Farm from a 100-bird MVP into a sustainable and profitable poultry enterprise.
Proposed allocation:
40% (₦2,000,000): Purchase of day-old chicks, quality feed, vaccines, and medications to increase production capacity.
25% (₦1,250,000): Construction and expansion of poultry housing, drinkers, feeders and improved biosecurity facilities.
15% (₦750,000): Purchase of essential equipment, including a generator, water storage system and processing tools.
10% (₦500,000): Marketing, branding, packaging and distribution to secure new customers and strengthen market access.
10% (₦500,000): Working capital for labour, transportation and other operational expenses.
This investment will enable AFENAT Farm to significantly increase production, create employment opportunities, improve food security and build a reliable supply of high-quality poultry products for households, restaurants, and local markets.
growthTargets:
AFENAT Farm – Growth Targets for the Next 12 Months
Over the next 12 months, AFENAT Farm aims to grow from a 100-bird Minimum Viable Product (MVP) into a sustainable small-scale commercial poultry enterprise.
Our key growth targets are:
Increase production capacity from 100 to 1,000 broiler birds per production cycle.
Maintain a bird survival rate of at least 95% through strong biosecurity and flock management.
Achieve 100% sales of market-ready birds within two weeks of maturity.

problem:

‎
‎2. Lack of Convenience
‎   Most provision stores close early, have poor stock, or are far from residential areas. People waste time and transport money to get simple items.
‎
‎3. Poor Customer Service & Trust
‎   Many provision shops sell expired goods, give wrong measurements, or lack proper record-keeping. This makes customers lose trust.
‎
‎4. Limited Product Variety
‎   Small provision stores often don’t stock a wide range of brands or healthy options. Customers are forced to go to multiple places to get what they need.
solution:
‎1. Affordable Pricing + Bulk Buying
‎Problem: High cost of goods due to inflation  
‎Solution:  
‎- Buy directly from wholesalers and manufacturers to cut middlemen  
‎- Run weekly "combo deals" and family packs to help customers save  
‎- Offer credit/loyalty points for regular customers  
‎Result: Lower prices, more customers, repeat sales
‎
‎2. Convenience + Accessibility
‎Problem: Stores close early, poor location, no stock  
‎Solution:  
‎- Open early 7am - 10pm to serve workers and families  
‎- Stock fast-moving items always: rice, oil, noodles, drinks, toiletries  
‎- Add home delivery or WhatsApp ordering for busy customers  
‎Result: Customers can get what they need anytime, without stress
‎
‎3. Trust + Quality Assurance
‎Problem: Expired goods, wrong measurements, poor service  
‎Solution:  
‎- Strict stock rotation and expiry date checks  
‎- Use scales and proper packaging for transparency  
‎- Train staff on customer service and honesty  
‎Result: Customers trust your shop and refer others
‎
‎4. Wide Variety + Healthy Options 
‎Problem: Limited products, customers go to multiple shops  
‎Solution:  
‎- Stock multiple brands and sizes: budget, mid-range, and premium  
‎- Add healthy/specialty items: sugar-free, gluten-free, baby foods  
‎- Create sections: Food, Drinks, Toiletries, Cleaning

problem:
The aluminum fabrication industry faces increasing challenges in meeting the demands of modern construction, manufacturing, and consumer markets. Customers require high-quality, durable, and precisely engineered aluminum products that balance cost-effectiveness with sustainability. However, many fabricators struggle with:
‎
‎1. Material sourcing: Ensuring consistent supply of high-grade aluminum while managing fluctuating raw material costs.  2. Production efficiency: Reducing waste, optimizing cutting and welding processes, and minimizing turnaround times.  
‎3. Quality assurance: Maintaining strict tolerances and finishes to meet industry standards and customer expectations.  
‎4. Customization demands: Adapting to diverse client specifications across industries such as construction, automotive, aerospace, and consumer goods.  
‎5.Sustainability pressures: Addressing environmental concerns by reducing carbon footprint, recycling scrap, and adopting eco-friendly processes.  
‎6. Skilled labor: Recruiting and retaining experienced technicians capable of handling advanced machinery and complex designs.
solution:
To overcome industry challenges and remain competitive, an aluminum fabricator can implement the following strategies:
‎
‎1. Smart sourcing: Establish long-term contracts with trusted suppliers, diversify sources, and explore recycled aluminum to stabilize costs and ensure consistent material quality.  
‎
‎2.Lean manufacturing:  Adopt lean principles to reduce waste, optimize workflows, and improve efficiency. Techniques like CNC automation, laser cutting, and robotic welding can minimize errors and speed up production.  
‎
‎3.Advanced quality control: Implement digital inspection systems, non-destructive testing, and ISO-certified processes to guarantee precision and durability in every product.  
‎
‎4. Customization through technology: Use CAD/CAM software and modular design approaches to quickly adapt to diverse client specifications across industries.  
‎
‎5.Sustainability initiatives: Reduce carbon footprint by recycling scrap aluminum, investing in energy-efficient machinery, and adopting eco-friendly coatings and finishes.  
‎
‎6.Workforce development: Provide continuous training for technicians, invest in apprenticeship programs, and retain skilled labor by offering competitive wages and safe working conditions.  
‎
‎7.Customer-centric approach: Build strong client relationships through transparent communication, reliable delivery schedules, and after-sales support.  
‎
‎Core Outcome:
‎By integrating these solutions, as an aluminum fabricator i can achieve:
‎- Lower production costs  
‎- Higher product quality  
‎- Faster turnaround times  
‎- Stronger market reputation  
‎- Compliance with sustainability standards

problem:
Across many cities in Nigeria, access to reliable and trustworthy last-mile delivery remains a significant challenge for individuals, businesses, and SMEs.

Through market surveys, customer interviews, and direct engagement with merchants and riders, we identified several recurring problems that affect the delivery experience and limit business growth.

One of the biggest concerns is trust. Many customers are uncomfortable handing over valuable items to independent riders they know little or nothing about. There is often no way to verify who the rider is, whether their identity has been authenticated, or if they are operating legally.

We also found that many riders operate with expired driver’s licences, expired vehicle documents, or incomplete verification, exposing customers, businesses, and the riders themselves to unnecessary safety and legal risks.

Another major issue is the difficulty of finding a reliable rider when needed. Businesses and customers often spend valuable time making multiple phone calls or searching through personal contacts before they can secure a rider. This results in delays, missed business opportunities, and poor customer experiences.

Package visibility is another challenge. In many traditional delivery arrangements, once a package leaves the sender, there is little or no visibility into its location. Customers are left wondering where their package is, when it will arrive, or whether it has been delivered safely.

We also observed that many logistics operations still rely on manual and disorganized dispatch processes. Orders are assigned through phone calls or messaging apps without a structured system, leading to slow response times, rider confusion, inefficient route allocation, increased cancellations, and inconsistent service quality.

Customer support is another major gap in the industry. When deliveries are delayed, cancelled, or disputed, customers often have no dedicated support team to contact. This lack of accountability reduces confidence in logistics services and discourages repeat usage.

These challenges are even more difficult for small businesses that depend on reliable deliveries to serve customers and grow their sales. Without a dependable logistics partner, many businesses struggle to scale their operations.
solution:
QwikFleet Digital Technology Limited is building a technology-driven logistics platform designed to make last-mile delivery safer, faster, more transparent, and more reliable.

Our platform connects customers, businesses, and verified riders through a single digital ecosystem where deliveries can be requested, assigned, tracked, and completed efficiently.

Every rider on the platform undergoes a structured verification process, including identity verification, driver’s licence verification, and vehicle document verification, helping to improve customer trust and safety.

Through real-time GPS tracking, customers and merchants can monitor their deliveries from pickup to drop-off, giving them complete visibility and reducing uncertainty throughout the delivery journey.

QwikFleet also introduces an intelligent dispatch system that automatically connects delivery requests with the most suitable available rider based on location, reducing waiting times, improving operational efficiency, and increasing successful order completion.

To improve service quality, the platform provides dedicated customer support, allowing customers and businesses to quickly report issues, receive updates, and resolve concerns through an accountable support system.

Beyond solving today’s logistics challenges, QwikFleet is building the digital infrastructure that will enable businesses of all sizes—from local restaurants and pharmacies to supermarkets and e-commerce merchants—to integrate logistics directly into their operations through APIs and future technology solutions.

By combining verified riders, real-time tracking, intelligent dispatch, customer support, and scalable technology, QwikFleet is creating a trusted logistics ecosystem that improves customer confidence, supports business growth, increases rider earning opportunities, and contributes to the digital transformation of Nigeria’s logistics sector.
mvpDescription:
QwikFleet has developed a functional Minimum Viable Product (MVP) that enables customers and businesses to book, manage, and track deliveries through a simple and user-friendly mobile platform.

The platform allows users to:

* Book instant and scheduled deliveries.
* Get matched with verified riders in real time.
* Track their deliveries live from pickup to final destination.
* Communicate directly with riders through in-app calling and messaging.
* Make secure digital payments within the app.
* View delivery history and order status.
* Receive delivery updates and notifications throughout the delivery process.
* Access customer support whenever assistance is needed.

For riders, the platform provides:

* Rider registration and verification.
* Real-time delivery requests.
* GPS navigation to pickup and drop-off locations.
* Earnings tracking and delivery history.
* Secure communication with customers.
* A structured system for managing deliveries professionally.

The MVP is already being used by real customers, with active deliveries taking place through the platform. This early adoption confirms that users are embracing QwikFleet as a trusted and technology-driven logistics solution. Feedback from customers and riders has also enabled us to continuously improve the platform as we prepare to scale across more cities and expand our services.

This combination of a working product, active users, and continuous improvement demonstrates that QwikFleet has progressed beyond the idea stage and is building a scalable logistics technology platform for businesses and individuals across Nigeria.
tractionMetric:
Our key traction metric is market validation and early user adoption. Since launching our MVP, QwikFleet has received over 400 delivery requests, demonstrating strong customer interest and demand for our solution. We have successfully completed deliveries for customers through the platform, validating that users are willing to adopt a trusted, technology-enabled logistics service.

Many of the unfulfilled requests during this early stage were due to operational limitations, including a shortage of riders in certain locations and delivery requests originating from states where we have not yet commenced operations. These insights have helped us identify our biggest growth opportunity—expanding our verified rider network and geographic coverage to meet existing demand.

Our traction confirms that the market need exists, customers are actively using the platform, and QwikFleet has achieved early product-market validation. The grant will enable us to scale rider onboarding, strengthen operations, and convert a much larger percentage of existing demand into completed deliveries.

Problem Statement: Hair Dressing & Decoration
Hair dressing and decoration are essential aspects of personal grooming, cultural identity, and fashion. However, several problems persist in this industry:
•	Skill Gap Many practitioners lack formal training, leading to inconsistent quality of service and customer dissatisfaction.
•	Health & Safety Improper handling of chemicals, tools, and hygiene practices can cause scalp infections, hair damage, or allergic reactions.
•	Cultural Sensitivity Hairstyles often carry cultural significance, yet some stylists may not respect or understand these traditions, leading to misrepresentation or offense.
•	Accessibility Professional hair services are often expensive or unavailable in rural areas, limiting access for many communities.
•	Sustainability Excessive use of synthetic products, non-recyclable packaging, and water waste contribute to environmental concerns.
•	Innovation Gap While fashion evolves rapidly, many salons struggle to keep up with modern trends, tools, and customer expectations.
 Example Problem Statement
"Despite the growing demand for professional hair dressing and decoration services, the industry faces challenges such as inadequate training, health risks from poor hygiene and chemical use, limited accessibility in underserved areas, and lack of innovation. Addressing these issues is critical to improving customer satisfaction, ensuring safety, and promoting sustainable practices in hair care."

The main solutions to hairdressing and decoration challenges in Edo State include government-backed youth training programs, better salon management practices, and investment in modern equipment and technology. 
EdoJobs is already training thousands of youths in hairdressing, while salon owners can boost success through strategic location, financial planning, and client retention strategies.
Key Solutions for Hairdressing/Decoration in Edo State
1. Youth Training Programs
•	Edo State Government, through EdoJobs, plans to train 25,000 youths in 2025, with hairdressing as a major focus.
•	This initiative provides skills acquisition, apprenticeships, and empowerment, helping young people become self-sufficient.
•	Training covers hair styling, decoration, and fashion design, ensuring modern techniques are adopted.
2. Salon Business Management
•	Organization & financial stability: Salon owners must set clear objectives, simplify operations, and embrace technology.
•	Client retention: Offering loyalty programs, discounts, and personalized services keeps customers coming back.
•	Staff productivity: Training workers in both technical skills and customer service improves efficiency.
•	Technology adoption: Using salon management software (like Otawise) helps track appointments, inventory, and finances.
3. Proper Salon Setup
•	Strategic location: Choose high-traffic areas in Benin City or other urban centers for visibility.
•	Quality equipment: Invest in adjustable chairs, dryers, sterilizers, and decoration tools.
•	Legal compliance: Register with CAC, obtain health and safety permits, and meet local zoning requirements.
•	Hygiene standards: Strict sanitation builds trust and attracts more clients.
4. Cultural & Creative Innovation
•	Edo State has a rich tradition of hair decoration and styling, often linked to cultural festivals and ceremonies.
•	Modern salons can blend traditional Edo hair art (like coral bead decoration) with contemporary styles to attract diverse clientele.
•	This fusion preserves culture while meeting modern beauty demands.
Challenges & Risks
•	High startup costs: Equipment and rent can be expensive.
•	Unstable electricity supply: Salons often need generators or solar backup.
•	Competition: Many small salons operate informally, making pricing competitive.
•	Skill gaps: Without proper training, many stylists struggle to meet modern beauty standards.
Actionable Recommendations
•	Leverage EdoJobs training for skill acquisition.
•	Adopt business management software for efficiency.
•	Blend traditional Edo decoration styles with modern trends.
•	Form cooperatives or associations to access loans and bulk-purchase equipment.
•	Invest in renewable energy solutions to reduce power costs.

•	Fluctuations in the Naira exchange rate make these products unaffordable for many salons.
•	Limited access to quality local alternatives reduces service quality.
3. Inadequate Training
•	Many stylists lack formal education in modern techniques (lace frontal installation, advanced coloring, bridal decoration).
•	This leads to inconsistent service quality and difficulty meeting client expectations.
4. Competition from Informal Stylists
•	Street-side and home-based stylists offer cheaper services, often without overhead costs.
•	Formal salons struggle to differentiate themselves and justify higher prices.
5. Government & Policy Gaps
•	Lack of tailored government support or regulation for the beauty industry.
•	No subsidies for energy, no structured training programs, and limited access to small business loans.

•	Skilled stylists often leave to start their own businesses, creating instability.
•	Recruiting and retaining talent is a constant challenge.

problem:
Great talent is everywhere, but without infrastructure and structure, it can't be commercialized.
Despite Nigeria’s global dominance in the creative and music industries, emerging independent artists, vocalists, and session musicians—particularly within regions like Edo State—face a severe bottleneck. The creative ecosystem suffers from a fragmented talent pipeline, a lack of structured technical mentorship (such as professional vocal production, tracking, and arrangement), and prohibitive costs for high-end studio infrastructure.

Because of these gaps, brilliant local creatives remain informal, isolated, and unable to scale their skills into sustainable commercial careers. Sub-standard vocal tracking and production limit their export potential, leaving a massive pool of raw talent disconnected from the broader, multi-million naira commercial music market.
solution:
We built the community and the talent pipeline over the last three years; now we are scaling the technical infrastructure to monetize it.
The Community is a structured creative collective and professional ecosystem designed to bridge the gap between raw musical talent and the commercial industry. Founded in February 2023, we have built a functional talent pipeline by providing structured training, masterclasses, and networking infrastructure for vocalists and musicians.

With this grant, we are scaling our proven model by building a dedicated mini-studio and technical hub equipped with professional-grade vocal tracking, audio recording, and production hardware. This hub will serve as an incubation center where our curated collective can access subsidized, industry-standard equipment, receive advanced vocal production coaching, and collaborate on commercial projects. By combining structured community growth with physical creative infrastructure, we are transforming raw creative talent into an organized, highly employable, and exportable workforce.
mvpDescription:
The Minimum Viable Product for The Community is a structured, hybrid talent network and professional incubation pipeline for vocalists, songwriters, and session musicians. Launched in February 2023, our MVP focuses on consolidating fragmented independent talent into an organized collective.

Through this MVP infrastructure, we run peer-to-peer training cohorts, structured vocal masterclasses, and managed studio session bookings. Members are vetted, upskilled in vocal arrangement and studio tracking etiquette, and then actively matched with professional recording projects, voiceover gigs, and live performances. This serves as a functional, low-overhead blueprint that proves independent creatives can be successfully organized, upskilled, and commercialized.
tractionMetric: Our key traction metric is Talent Placement & Retention Rate. Since our launch in February 2023, we track how many independent vocalists and musicians complete our structured technical training and are successfully placed into paid studio sessions, commercial recordings, and live productions. This directly measures our ability to turn raw community engagement into tangible economic output.
teamExpertise:
Our team is structurally organized to combine deep technical creative industry experience with robust administrative, financial, and public relations expertise:

PRESIDENT & MUSIC DIRECTOR: A professional Music Director, vocal coach, and vocal producer with extensive experience arranging and tracking vocals, managing session musicians, and directing live/studio projects.

VICE PRESIDENT: Partners in strategic brand vision, enterprise growth, business development, and overall operational sustainability of the collective.

challenges:
Our two biggest bottlenecks are infrastructure constraints and production capacity.
While we have successfully built a thriving talent network and a solid training pipeline since 2023, we rely entirely on third-party commercial studios to record, track, and produce our projects. This heavily limits our operational hours, increases overhead costs, and slows down our ability to scale our practical incubation programs. Without a dedicated, controlled space equipped with professional hardware, we cannot meet the growing demand for subsidized, high-end vocal production and content creation for our community members.
fundUsage:
The ₦5,000,000 grant will be explicitly deployed to transition The Community from a decentralized network into a fully equipped, self-sustaining physical hub, broken down as follows:

First, ₦2,400,000 will be allocated to Audio Hardware and Production Gear, covering industrial-grade mixing consoles, professional vocal microphones (such as Shure series and condensers), MIDI controllers, studio monitors, and high-performance audio interfaces for clean tracking.

Second, ₦1,100,000 will be used for Acoustic Treatment and Studio Setup, which includes professional soundproofing, high-density acoustic panels, bass traps, and isolation shielding to ensure our vocal tracking meets rigorous industry standards.

Third, ₦900,000 will go toward Workspace and Power Infrastructure, focusing on a dedicated power backup system (inverter/solar or generator setup) to combat local grid instability, alongside essential studio furniture and multi-channel headphone distribution networks for session vocalists.

Finally, ₦600,000 will be utilized for Operational Launch and Masterclasses, covering marketing for the new physical hub, administrative setup costs, and subsidized funding to run our first two advanced technical training cohorts for local creatives.

revenueModel:
The Community will operate on a robust, multi-tiered B2B and B2C revenue model designed to commercialize creative talent:
COMMERCIAL STUDIO BOOKINGS (B2C): Offering competitive, paid studio time for external independent artists, voiceover actors, and content creators needing high-end vocal tracking and mixing.

CREATIVE MASTERCLASSES & PREMIUM COHORTS (B2C): Charging subsidized fees for our specialized, advanced training boot camps and masterclasses.

TALENT AGENCY & PRODUCTION COMMISSIONS (B2B): Earning a 10% to 15% placement or agency fee when corporate brands, advertising agencies, or major record labels hire our vetted, industry-trained collective members for commercial recording sessions, live events, or jingles.

problem: Avoidable expenses from in-person hospital consultations that could be handled remotely. Delays in getting quality healthcare, especially in semi-urban and rural areas of Edo State. Communication challenges due to language barriers between doctors and patients.
solution: Dockintor provides fast, reliable, and affordable online medical consultations in multiple local languages, with an integrated referral system when needed.
mvpDescription:
Dockintor has a functional Minimum Viable Product (MVP) that enables users to access healthcare remotely through secure telemedicine services in different local languages. The platform allows patients to create an account, search for licensed doctors, and book virtual consultations without visiting a hospital.

Key features of the MVP include secure user registration and login, preferred local language option, doctor profiles, appointment scheduling, real-time chat, voice and video consultations, and an in-app consultation timer that accurately tracks the duration of each session for transparent pay-per-minute billing. Users can also make payments within the platform and receive consultation records after their appointments.

Doctors can manage their profiles, accept consultation requests, communicate with patients in preferred local language option through chat, voice, or video, and monitor their consultation history and earnings as well as write a report of the consultation which can be downloaded by the user.

Dockintor is designed for individuals with non-emergency health concerns that do not need physical visits to the hospital, patients seeking second opinions, and healthcare facilities that require access to specialist advice. It provides a convenient, affordable, and reliable way for patients to connect with qualified doctors from anywhere, reducing travel time, long hospital queues, and delays in accessing quality healthcare.

As part of our expansion strategy, Dockintor is introducing the Diaspora Doctor  Connect Initiative, a feature that connects Nigerian doctors practicing abroad—beginning with Edo State indigenes—with patients and primary healthcare centres in Edo State through scheduled virtual consultation sessions. This initiative allows experienced diaspora doctors to volunteer or dedicate specific hours to provide expert medical advice, mentor local healthcare workers, and offer second opinions for complex cases. By leveraging the expertise of Nigerian medical professionals worldwide, the initiative aims to strengthen primary healthcare delivery, improve access to specialist care in underserved communities, and encourage meaningful diaspora contribution to healthcare development in Edo State.
tractionMetric:
Since launching its MVP, Dockintor has demonstrated early product-market validation by onboarding 37 registered users and 12 licensed doctors, generating ₦52,500 in revenue from telemedicine consultations. These early traction metrics show that both patients and healthcare professionals are willing to adopt and pay for a convenient, secure, and accessible virtual healthcare solution.

Beyond user acquisition, Dockintor has successfully deployed a fully functional telemedicine platform with real-world usage, validating the technical viability of the solution and confirming demand for digital healthcare services in Nigeria. These milestones provide a strong foundation for growth and continuous product improvement.

Building on this momentum, Dockintor is preparing to scale through strategic partnerships with hospitals, healthcare providers, and government stakeholders. The company is also in discussions with the Nigerian Medical Association (NMA) and has received positive feedback on its vision and approach, reinforcing confidence in the platform's potential to strengthen healthcare delivery. In addition, Dockintor will launch the Diaspora Doctor Connect Initiative, enabling Nigerian doctors in the diaspora—beginning with Edo State indigenes—to provide specialist consultations and mentorship, thereby expanding access to quality healthcare in underserved communities across Edo State.

While still at an early stage, Dockintor has moved beyond the idea phase to a working, revenue-generating platform with measurable user adoption. These achievements position the company for sustainable growth, increased healthcare access, and significant social impact.

challenges:
Dockintor's biggest challenge is access to growth capital. While we have successfully developed and launched a functional MVP with early paying users, limited funding has slowed our ability to scale. Additional investment is needed to enhance the platform, recruit key talent, expand our doctor network, execute marketing campaigns, and establish strategic partnerships across Edo State and Nigeria.

problem:
Customer support has become a major bottleneck for growing businesses. As companies acquire more customers, they also receive increasing volumes of inquiries across channels such as WhatsApp, website chat, and email. A large percentage of these inquiries are repetitive, yet support teams still spend valuable time responding to them manually.

This results in slow response times, overwhelmed support teams, inconsistent customer experiences, and lost sales opportunities. While many businesses adopt chatbots, existing solutions are often rule-based or lack access to business-specific knowledge, making them unreliable for handling real customer conversations.

Growing businesses need an intelligent, scalable solution that automates repetitive support while maintaining accuracy, reliability, and a seamless customer experience.
solution:
ProvidiusTech is an AI-powered customer support infrastructure platform that enables businesses to automate repetitive customer interactions across website chat, WhatsApp, email, and other digital channels.

Our AI is trained on each business's own knowledge base; including FAQs, policies, product information, and support documentation—to provide accurate, context-aware responses instead of generic chatbot replies. The platform also includes intelligent human handoff, ensuring that complex or sensitive conversations are seamlessly transferred to support agents.

By automating repetitive inquiries, ProvidiusTech helps businesses respond instantly, reduce support workload by up to 70%, improve customer satisfaction, and scale their customer support operations without proportionally increasing team size.
mvpDescription:
ProvidiusTech's MVP is an AI-powered customer support platform that helps growing businesses automate repetitive customer inquiries across WhatsApp, webchat, and email while ensuring complex conversations are seamlessly handed over to a human support agent.

The platform includes multi-channel support, AI-powered responses trained on a business's knowledge base, context-aware conversations, business-specific deployments, and intelligent human handoff. Businesses can upload their FAQs, policies, and support documentation, enabling the AI to provide accurate, business-specific responses rather than generic chatbot replies.

Rather than replacing existing customer support teams, ProvidiusTech integrates into a company's current support workflow and automates the repetitive layer of customer communication. Through our Early Access program, pilot customers receive end-to-end setup, AI configuration, channel integration, onboarding, and ongoing product improvements based on their feedback.

Our MVP is currently being prepared for pilot deployments with growing e-commerce businesses, SMEs, and SaaS startups to validate performance and refine the platform before a broader launch.
tractionMetric: Our primary traction metric is pilot customer acquisition. We have completed the development of our MVP and launched our Early Access Program to onboard our first cohort of pilot businesses. Our current focus is validating the platform in real-world customer support environments, measuring response accuracy, automation rates, and reductions in support workload. teamExpertise:

problem:

These issues limit the supply of high-quality poultry products, lower productivity, and raise production costs.
In order to address these issues, Dayo Akin Poultry Farm was founded. It produces healthy chicks, provides high-quality poultry feed, and encourages sustainable poultry farming methods. However, the company's existing limitations include a small manufacturing capacity and limited access to the cutting-edge equipment required to expand operations.
solution:
By raising healthy hens and distributing premium poultry feeds to homes, shops, restaurants, institutions, and smallholder farmers, Dayo Akin Poultry Farm offers a sustainable response to the rising demand for high-quality poultry products. To guarantee the production of safe and healthy birds, we employ good poultry management techniques, such as appropriate feeding, immunisation, biosecurity, and regular health monitoring. We are dedicated to implementing cutting-edge poultry technology including automated feeding and watering systems, better housing, and dependable power sources in order to increase productivity and efficiency. These investments will maintain high product quality while lowering production costs, minimising bird mortality, and increasing productivity.
In addition to providing poultry products, our company promotes food security, helps smallholder farmers expand by giving them access to high-quality feed, and gives young people in the agricultural value chain job possibilities. By growing, we hope to increase the availability and affordability of high-quality poultry products while encouraging sustainable farming methods that boost regional economies.
mvpDescription:
The Minimum Viable Product (MVP) of Dayo Akin Poultry Farm is a small-scale poultry production and feed supply company that offers local poultry farmers, merchants, restaurants, and families healthy live chickens and high-quality poultry feeds. The company has been running on a small scale since its founding in April 2023, providing services to clients and making steady profits while confirming consumer demand. Customers love having access to healthy birds, a consistent supply, and excellent customer service, as our MVP shows. To guarantee healthy chickens, we have created a repeatable production method that includes appropriate nutrition, immunisation, biosecurity, and regular flock management.
Our current activities' performance attests to the business model's feasibility. We are well-positioned to grow our business, boost sales, enter new markets, and have a bigger social and economic effect with more investment in cutting-edge poultry equipment and increased production capacity.

teamExpertise:

Feeding, immunisation, biosecurity, flock health monitoring, cleanliness, and regular farm maintenance are all under our team's purview. challenges:

problem:
Across Benin City, access to Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) remains inconvenient, time-consuming, and often unsafe for both households and businesses. Most times, consumers are usually required to transport themselves to gas stations, wait in long queues, transport heavy gas cylinders, and navigate inconsistent pricing and unreliable services. These challenges affect working professionals, students, elderly residents, restaurants, hotels, and other businesses that depend on uninterrupted cooking gas supplies.

In addition to these inconveniences, the LPG refill process is largely stressful and very inconvenient, offering little or no transparency and accountability. Digital payment options and real-time order tracking are also missing, limiting customer confidence and reducing operational efficiency.

For businesses, unexpected gas shortages can disrupt daily operations and negatively impact customer service.

Although LPG adoption is increasing as Nigeria transitions toward cleaner cooking energy, the supporting delivery infrastructure has not evolved to meet the growing demand for convenient, technology-enabled, and customer-centric refill services. Despite growing LPG adoption in Nigeria, the refill experience remains stressful and time consuming.
solution:
Ventus Energy Solutions Ltd is addressing these challenges by building a technology-driven LPG refill and logistics platform that simplifies access to cooking gas for both residential (B2C) and commercial (B2B) customers in Benin City.

Through our mobile application, customers can request an LPG refill without leaving their homes or businesses. Once an order is placed, the app automatically confirms the request, assigns the nearest verified delivery agent, facilitates secure pickup of the customer's cylinder, coordinates refilling at an approved partner gas plant, and returns the refilled cylinder safely to the customer.

Our app incorporates real-time order tracking, secure in-app payments, and a structured network of verified agents to ensure transparency, accountability, and operational efficiency throughout the refill process.

Ventus Energy Solutions LTD helps customers:

1. Eliminate the need to travel to gas refill stations.
2. Reduce waiting time and transportation costs.
3. Improves safety through standardized handling procedures and verified service agents.
4. Provides real-time tracking option into every stage of the refill process, increasing customer trust.
5. Support uninterrupted operations for businesses that rely on LPG.
6. Creates employment opportunities for local logistics agents while strengthening partnerships with licensed LPG plants.
7. Accelerates the adoption of clean cooking energy by making LPG more accessible, reliable, and convenient.

By digitalizing the entire process, it helps reduce the number of Benin city residents who rely on charcoal, wood and stove thereby reducing air pollution.
mvpDescription:

Our app allow users to place refill orders, make secure digital payments, track the status of their orders in real time, and receive notifications throughout the pickup, refill, and delivery process.

On the operational side, our app includes an agent management system that assigns verified delivery agents to customer requests, coordinates cylinder pickup and delivery, and integrates with approved LPG refill plants to complete the refill process safely and efficiently.

Core App Features:

1. Customer registration and profile management.
2. LPG refill ordering through the mobile app.
3. Secure in-app payment processing.
4. Automated assignment of the nearest verified delivery agent.
5. Real-time order tracking and status updates.
6. Pickup, refill, and doorstep delivery.
7. Admin dashboard for managing customers, orders, agents, and partner gas plants.

We intend to introduce advanced features such as subscription plans, scheduled refills and predictive reorder reminders as time goes on.

problem: Edo State faces a triple crisis in youth sports: (1) Over 60% of public school sports equipment in [Benin/Oredo/Egor LGA] is broken or unusable due to lack of local repair skills. solution:

· Repair: We establish a community sports equipment repair hub, extending the life of bats, balls, and boots by 12+ months—cutting replacement costs for schools by 40%.
· Train: We enroll 50 unemployed Edo youths in a 6-month hands-on program covering equipment maintenance, basic retail accounting, and junior coaching—certifying them as "Sports Micro-Entrepreneurs."
· Retail: We partner with local schools to supply affordable, refurbished gear, while graduates earn commissions as mobile repair agents, creating a self-sustaining ecosystem. Our solution tackles unemployment, waste, and sports access all at once.

---

· Set up the dedicated repair workshop and train our first 50 youths.

Phase 4 (Months 19–24): Diversification & Scale

Phase 5 (Year 3+): Full Self-Sufficiency

· We will no longer rely on grants, but continue to apply for partnerships that amplify our impact—not sustain our survival.

problem:
Growing up in Benin City, two things were always constant the noise of generators and the smell of exhaust fumes from vehicles on every street. I know this not just as an observation but as someone who lived it. Travelling alone to visit my aunt, the exhaust fumes inside a commercial bus triggered a medical emergency that landed me in hospital. That was the day I discovered I had asthma  a condition made worse by the very pollution we accept as normal on Edo State roads every single day.
Nigeria has over 13 million registered petrol vehicles. Our roads, our campuses, and our communities are filled with vehicles running on fuel that is becoming more unaffordable by the day. With petrol prices crossing ₦700 per litre, transportation costs have become a daily burden that students, traders, and working families in Edo State simply cannot escape. The lack of affordable, clean transportation options deepens inequality especially for students and everyday commuters who spend a disproportionate share of their income just to move from one place to another.
At the same time, existing vehicle-sharing and mobility systems in Nigeria are often expensive, unregulated, or unsafe. There is a clear need for a smart, affordable, and secure transport system that people can access in a controlled and trackable way — particularly on university campuses and within urban communities across Edo State.
Compounding all of this is Nigeria’s electricity crisis  a grid supplying less than 17% of national demand, leaving homes, businesses, schools, and healthcare facilities dependent on expensive, polluting generators to function. These two crises  unclean transport and unreliable electricity  do not exist in isolation. They compound each other daily, draining productivity and deepening poverty across Edo State. Torquenova was built to solve both but it is first and foremost an electric vehicle.
solution:
Torquenova is Nigeria’s first locally fabricated solar-powered electric vehicle, built from scratch in Benin City by young Edo State engineers using locally sourced materials. It is not imported, not assembled from foreign kits, and not designed for someone else’s roads. Every weld, every circuit, and every line of code was done here  by Nigerians, for Nigerians.
As an electric vehicle, Torquenova moves people cleanly and quietly across campuses, community streets, estates, and urban routes with zero exhaust, zero fumes, and zero fuel cost. The student who currently spends a significant portion of their allowance on transport fare, the commuter trapped in fuel-dependent commercial vehicles, and the institution looking for clean campus mobility  Torquenova serves all of them directly.
It runs on a 12kWh dual lithium iron phosphate battery system and a custom-built 10kW electric motor, delivering over six hours of continuous operation per charge. It recharges through high-voltage solar panels integrated into the vehicle roof, or through a standard mains socket giving users complete flexibility regardless of grid availability.
Beyond mobility, Torquenova carries a built-in 220V inverter that outputs enough electricity to power fans, televisions, laptops, and phones when the vehicle is parked offering a clean alternative to the generator for homes and small businesses. This is a secondary benefit that comes built into every unit, at no extra cost.
What truly sets Torquenova apart is its intelligence. An onboard AI system continuously monitors battery health, motor performance, and speed  alerting the driver with voice and display warnings before problems escalate into breakdowns. An autonomous SOS safety system detects collisions through built-in sensors, captures the scene with an onboard camera, and automatically sends the driver’s live GPS location to an emergency contact within three seconds  no driver action required.
Available in three variants  a commuter model for urban transport and individual ownership, a nine-seater campus model targeting Nigeria’s 609 tertiary institutions, and a sport model for golf courses and tourist resorts  all priced at ₦7 million per unit. That is 70% cheaper than any imported electric vehicle currently available in Nigeria, and built in a way that Edo State engineers can maintain, repair, and replicate independently.

The token-based drive system, GPS tracking, AI health monitoring, and SOS accident detection are all integrated and operationally confirmed. Every component was designed and fabricated by our team in Nigeria because if we build it, Nigerians can maintain it, repair it, and replicate it

problem:
Euler Educators was founded on May 5th, 2024 in Oredo, Benin City, on a simple conviction: a society fails in direct proportion to the quality of holistic education it offers its people. Nigeria is home to an estimated 10.5 million out-of-school children according to UNICEF, roughly a fifth of the global total, and millions more who are enrolled still lack the personalized, adaptive STEM instruction that shapes long-term opportunity.
But as Nigeria digitizes learning and assessment to close that gap, a second crisis is growing just as fast: whether the resulting credentials can be trusted. JAMB, which runs the national university entrance exam, drew 2.2 million candidates to 966 computer-based test centres this cycle, while the previous cycle produced 6,458 flagged results. Candidates altered photos to beat facial recognition, swapped fingerprints so stand-ins could sit exams, and in some cases hacked test centre networks to change live answers. This year alone, a cyber-fraud ring was arrested for breaching candidates' exam systems in Delta State. JAMB's own leadership has warned publicly that this fraud could collapse confidence in the entire admissions process.
In the age of AI, telling a student's genuine work from a manipulated result has never been harder. And it is the honest, underserved student, the one without access to the syndicates gaming the system, who stands to lose the most. When credentials stop being trusted, education stops being a ladder.
solution:
Euler Educators tackles both sides of Nigeria's education crisis: access to quality learning and trust in the results of that learning.
Our flagship product, Euler Edge, is a Digital Assessment and Integrity Software (DAIS) built to guarantee the credibility of computer-based examinations. Where existing systems rely on checks that fraudsters have already learned to beat, such as photo verification and fingerprint matching, Euler Edge uses AI behavioural proctoring and analysis throughout the exam itself. It studies how a candidate actually engages with the test in real time, flags irregularities and patterns consistent with impersonation, external assistance, or tampering, and produces an integrity report examiners can act on. In a crowd of thousands of candidates, it isolates the dishonest few without punishing the honest majority.
Around Euler Edge, we have built a complete learning ecosystem: a student portal that tracks each learner's growth and performance while serving them the resources they need, adaptive learning tools that meet students where they are rather than where the curriculum assumes they should be, and a thriving community of learners and educators. Together, these ensure that the student who studies hard is both well prepared and provably the author of their own results.
mvpDescription:
Euler Edge (live at euler-edge.vercel.app) is a functional digital assessment platform with integrity built into its core. Users can currently do the following:
Institutions and educators can create and administer computer-based tests, monitor candidates during the exam through AI behavioural proctoring that analyses candidate activity for signs of impersonation, external assistance, or manipulation, and receive integrity flags and reports on suspicious sessions so that irregular results are caught before they become certified credentials.
Students can sit secure digital exams, then use the student portal to track their growth and performance over time and access learning resources matched to their needs.
The MVP already serves a real user base of over 1,100 registered users, with 203 monthly active users, proving both demand and retention at this early stage.
tractionMetric: Our key metric is monthly active engagement: 203 of our 1,166 users are active every month, an engagement rate of roughly 17%, which is a bit strong for an early-stage education product where usage typically clusters around exam seasons. Also, return on enrolment (the revenue we generate from enrolling a student or an onboarding an institution).
teamExpertise: Our team combines technical depth with genuine roots in the Nigerian education system. Ogheneruemusua Gbakeji, Developer, Digital Marketer and  Operation Supervisor, brings 4 years of experience in software and AI engineering, social media marketing and business growth dynamics, and leads the development of Euler Edge's behavioural proctoring and Exam engine. Oghenetejiri Gbakeji, Education Specialist and Head of Operations, is a seasoned Mathematician and human right activist who has background in education / assessment / school administration, and ensures the product is built around how Nigerian exams actually run, not how outsiders imagine they run. Oghenemarho Gbakeji,  handles students growth and our adaptive learning curricula and online classes, and has grown our community to over 1,100 users largely through organic channels. Ogheneruemu is the Head of our Legal Department, ensuring that we are compliant with government directives and educational laws which includes student data privacy, child protection act, etc. We are based in Benin City and operate remotely, close to the students and institutions we serve, and every member of the team has personally experienced the examination system we are fixing.
challenges: Our biggest challenge is scaling infrastructure to match demand. AI behavioural proctoring is computationally heavy, and serving it reliably to hundreds of simultaneous candidates requires server capacity we cannot yet afford at the level we need. Second, institutional sales cycles are slow: schools and exam bodies move cautiously on anything touching examinations, so building trust takes sustained outreach, pilots, and demonstrations, building strategic partnership will really be helpful in building trust, credibility, and boost growth. Third, reaching a large audience especially students in secondary school have been very difficult. None of these are demand problems. The demand is proven. They are capacity problems, which is exactly what this grant would solve.
fundUsage:
₦2,000,000 (40%) — Infrastructure and product development. Cloud servers and GPU capacity to run AI proctoring at scale, security hardening, and moving Euler Edge from MVP hosting to production-grade infrastructure capable of handling institutional exam loads.
₦1,250,000 (25%) — Institutional pilots and partnerships. Funding structured pilot programmes with 20 secondary schools and tutorial centres in Edo State, including onboarding, training invigilators and administrators, and gathering the documented results we need to approach larger exam bodies. Also, hosting digital competitions that'll provide students the opportunity to test this first class platform and win prizes.
₦1,000,000 (20%) — Talent. Hiring such as one additional engineer and one part-time community/support officer to accelerate development and support our growing user base.
₦500,000 (10%) — Marketing and community growth. Targeted campaigns to grow our student user base ahead of JAMB/WAEC 2027, leveraging the exam-season demand spike.
₦250,000 (5%) — Operations and compliance. Legal, registration, and administrative costs of formalising institutional contracts.
growthTargets: Within 12 months we aim to grow from 1,166 to 10,000+ registered users and from 379 to 3,000+ monthly active users, driven by exam-season campaigns and school partnerships. On the institutional side, we target 10 to 15 paying schools and tutorial centres running assessments on Euler Edge, with at least two documented pilot case studies showing measurable reduction in examination irregularities. Financially, we aim to reach a minimum ₦500,000 in monthly recurring revenue and begin formal conversations with at least one state education board or national examination body.
revenueModel: We earn revenue through three streams. First, institutional licensing: schools, tutorial centres, and exam bodies pay per candidate per exam sitting, or on an annual licence, to run assessments on Euler Edge. This is our core stream, because integrity is a problem institutions pay to solve. Second, student subscriptions: learners pay a modest fee for premium access to the student portal, including performance analytics, adaptive practice, and learning resources, and competitive exams with a free tier keeping the platform accessible to underserved students. Third, as we grow, verification services: allowing universities and employers to confirm that a credential was earned under proctored, verified conditions.
socialImpact:
The deepest impact of examination fraud falls on honest, underserved students. When a candidate can pay a syndicate to hack results or send in a stand-in, the student in a public school in Oredo who studied by candlelight competes on a rigged field. Euler Edge levels that field. Every fraudulent result we prevent is a university place, a scholarship, or a job that goes to a student who earned it.
Beyond fairness, credible credentials have economic weight: employers and universities can trust what a certificate says, reducing the cost of re-testing and the quiet discounting of Nigerian qualifications at home and abroad. Our adaptive learning tools and free-tier portal extend quality STEM support to students who cannot afford private tutoring, chipping away at the access gap behind Nigeria's 10.5 million out-of-school children. And by building this technology in Benin City rather than importing it, we create skilled technology jobs in Edo State and keep the value of solving a Nigerian problem inside Nigeria.
sustainabilityPath: Sustainability is built into our economics. Examinations are recurring by nature: every school runs multiple assessment cycles a year, and national exams return annually with millions of candidates, so institutional revenue is recurring revenue. Our per-candidate pricing means income scales directly with usage while our marginal cost per additional candidate is low, so margins improve as we grow. The grant funds the bridge, infrastructure and pilots, that converts our proven user demand into paying institutional contracts. From there, each new school partnership funds the next stage of growth. Our 12-month target is for institutional and subscription revenue to fully cover operating costs, making Euler Educators self-sustaining without further grant dependence, with future funding sought only to accelerate expansion, not to survive.

problem:
Nigeria's identity infrastructure is fragmented. Every bank, hospital, telecom, and government office that needs to confirm someone is who they say they are builds and guards its own private copy of that person's most sensitive information — a new vault, on a new server, watched over by a new team who may or may not know what they're doing. Osamudiamen from Benin has done KYC with his bank, handed his ID to a hospital, registered a small business, and sat an exam — and each of those places now holds a full, disconnected copy of who he is. None of them talk to each other. Each one is a fresh target on its own.

This fragmentation is exactly what's now failing in public. In April 2026, hackers broke into the Corporate Affairs Commission and walked away with over 15 million records. Sterling Bank and Remita were hit in the same wave, exposing BVNs, NINs, and KYC documents that had been sitting in isolated silos with no shared standard for how they were protected. Somewhere in that data, real people's identities are now available to whoever wants to use them — to take a loan, register a business, or move money in someone else's name, with the real owner finding out only after the damage is done.

This is also why now matters. In June 2026, the Central Bank ordered every bank and fintech in Nigeria to keep this kind of data on Nigerian servers by January 2027, because scattering people's identity data across a hundred disconnected private vaults, some sitting outside the country entirely, has stopped being a company-level risk and become a national one. Nigeria doesn't have a shortage of institutions checking who people are. It has a shortage of one shared, trusted way for them to ask that question, instead of each one holding a private, breakable copy of the answer.
solution:
Before Interswitch, every bank in Nigeria had to wire itself directly to every other bank just so their ATMs could talk to each other. It didn't scale, and every extra wire was another way for something to go wrong. Interswitch became the one shared rail every bank plugs into instead.

IDEN does the same thing for identity. Instead of every bank, hospital, and school holding their own copy of Obi's ID, they all plug into IDEN. When Obi walks into a bank, IDEN simply tells the bank "yes, this is Obi, he's over 18, he's verified" — without handing over a copy of his ID for the bank to store, misplace, or leak. A hospital sees only what a hospital needs to see. An event ticket-checker sees only a green tick, nothing more. Nobody gets more of Obi's information than their job requires, and nobody is left holding a private vault for hackers to break into.

We're building IDEN on Wolf, a programming language we built ourselves, so the whole system runs on tools we own and control end-to-end, not ones rented from outside the country. That matters right now: the Central Bank just ordered every bank and fintech in Nigeria to keep this kind of data on Nigerian servers by January 2027, because scattering Nigerians' identity data across a hundred private vaults — some sitting outside the country — has become a national risk, not just a company one.

We're not guessing at this problem from the outside, I am a final-year Mechatronics Engineering student who built IDEN's core alone, and was selected into the iDICE Startup Bridge Founders Lab out of over 13,000 applicants, one of only 185. This has already survived being picked apart by one of the toughest startup programs in Nigeria.
mvpDescription: Right now IDEN has a working flow from end to end: an institution signs up, gets its own private and public key pair, then calls a single endpoint whenever it needs to check someone — and gets back a straight yes or no on whether that person is verified. We're currently building the next piece on top of this: a way to keep checking that someone is still who they say they are over time, not just once at signup. A friend running his own product has already agreed to plug IDEN in as the verification system running quietly behind his app — our first real integration, currently in progress.
tractionMetric: IDEN isn't an app people open every day, it's a connection layer that other institutions plug into. So the usual numbers like daily users or engagement don't tell the real story at this stage. We actually started out building just one piece of this — a way to keep checking someone is still who they say they are — but pivoted to build the full plug-and-play layer instead, so any bank, hospital, or business can verify a person without ever holding a copy of that person's data themselves, all handled under Nigeria's data protection law (NDPR) and the NIMC Act. Right now our clearest sign of traction is institutional interest: selection into the iDICE Startup Bridge Founders Lab (1 of 185 chosen from over 13,000 applicants), and active conversations with iDICE cohort companies about plugging into IDEN once it's live.
teamExpertise:
Divine Osarumwense Victor: Final-year Mechatronics Engineering student (UNIBEN, graduating August 2026), Huawei ICT Academy Campus Lead. Full-stack technical execution across cryptography (ECIES, zk-SNARKs), computer vision/ML (facial verification, bias analysis), and backend systems — built the entire IDEN architecture solo, from crypto layer to compliance positioning under the NIMC Act.

As of the time of this Application, I am currently looking to acquire a co-founder and a legal representative.
challenges: Formal legal/compliance clearance (NIMC Act positioning, data protection registration), securing pilot integration agreements with fintech partners for fine-tuning and traction, and funding the dataset work needed to close the Buffalo-L bias gap on darker skin tones.
fundUsage:
- Legal/regulatory setup and NIMC Act compliance filing
- Cloud infrastructure migration (FAISS → Qdrant at scale)
- Pilot integration with one healthcare or fintech partner
- Data collection/fine-tuning pass to reduce Buffalo-L's FRR gap on darker skin tones
- Marketing and outreach
growthTargets: Close 5–8 fintech integration pilots; secure a government introduction (via EYIF) for the federated brokerage mode; reach 1000+ verified enrollments; begin cross-border audit gateway conversations for diaspora use cases.
revenueModel: Per-verification API fees (private-sector mode), tiered subscription for continuous assurance products (Fintech Guard, Pension Verify), and licensing fees for sector-scoped card issuance. Phase 3 adds a cross-border audit gateway with USD-denominated fees for diaspora verification.
socialImpact: Identity infrastructure is the prerequisite switch for Nigeria's next credit wave — only ~12% of Sub-Saharan Africans have ever borrowed formally, and identity friction is a core reason why. IDEN also directly targets a measured facial-recognition bias against darker-skinned Nigerians, correcting a system that currently locks out the population it claims to serve.
sustainabilityPath: Recurring per-verification and subscription revenue from private-sector integrations, compounding via a data flywheel — each KYC verification improves the underlying model, which reduces false-rejection rates, which increases institutional trust and adoption.
