problem:
Millions of Nigerian secondary school students prepare for high-stakes exams WAEC, JAMB, NECO, GCE, and Post UTME every year with inadequate tools. Quality practice materials are either unaffordable, inaccessible in rural areas, or outdated. 
The few digital solutions that exist are poorly designed, lack real past questions, and offer no intelligent feedback. Students are left to rely on photocopied booklets and guesswork, resulting in high failure rates that close doors to university and opportunity before these students ever get a real chance.
solution:
Preplok is an AI-powered exam preparation platform built specifically for Nigerian secondary school students. It gives students access to thousands of real past questions across WAEC, JAMB, NECO, GCE, and Post UTME, timed mock exams that simulate real exam conditions, AI-generated hints and clear explanations for every answer, performance tracking so students can identify and improve weak areas, and offline access designed for students with poor or inconsistent internet connectivity. 

Preplok is available as an Android app on the Google Play Store and as a web platform at preplok.com, making it accessible across devices at an affordable price point designed for Nigerian students and families.
mvpDescription:
Preplok's MVP is a fully functional Android mobile application and companion web platform. Users can create an account, select their target exam (WAEC, JAMB, NECO, GCE, or Post UTME), and immediately begin practicing with thousands of real past questions organized by subject and year. 

The app features timed mock exams that replicate real exam conditions, AI-powered hints that guide students toward the correct answer without simply giving it away, detailed explanations for every question, and a performance dashboard that tracks scores and progress over time. 

Offline mode allows students to continue studying without an internet connection a critical feature for students in areas with poor connectivity.
tractionMetric:
User growth rate and exam simulation completion rate. Since launch, Preplok has achieved 300+ downloads with consistent week-on-week user growth and strong positive feedback from students across multiple Nigerian states. 
Exam session completion rate, the percentage of users who start and finish a full mock exam is our primary engagement indicator, reflecting genuine study behavior rather than passive downloads.
teamExpertise:
Preplok is run by a team of three.

Joy Oghogho: Founder & Lead Developer
Software Engineer with a B.Eng. in Computer Engineering from UNIBEN and 5+ years in mobile and web development. She independently built the entire Preplok platform, Flutter app, Firebase backend, AI integration, and Play Store deployment.

Content & QA Intern
A university student currently preparing for NECO who sources past questions from physical booklets in bookstores, cross-references them against the app, and verifies every question for accuracy against official published materials.

Social Media & Marketing Intern
A university student managing Preplok's presence across TikTok, Facebook, and YouTube handling content creation, scheduling, and community engagement to grow our student audience.
challenges:
Three primary challenges.
1. Content expansion, growing the question bank to cover more subjects, more years, and more exam types requires significant time and resources currently managed by one person. 
2. Marketing reach connecting with the students who need Preplok most, particularly in underserved and rural areas, requires investment in targeted outreach across social platforms and schools. 
3. iOS availability, Preplok is currently Android-only; expanding to the App Store would significantly increase the addressable user base, but iOS build resources have delayed this.
fundUsage:
The majority of the grant will be directed toward marketing and student outreach, as our primary goal is getting Preplok into the hands of the students who need it most across Nigeria.

Marketing & Student Outreach: ₦2,200,000
This is our largest investment. Funds will cover targeted social media campaigns across TikTok, Facebook, and YouTube where Nigerian students are most active, local radio and community announcements in Edo State and surrounding areas, school visits and in-person demonstrations at secondary schools, a student ambassador program where university students are paid to promote Preplok within their former secondary schools, and printed flyers and materials for schools and exam prep centres in areas with lower internet penetration.

Content & Question Bank Expansion: ₦1,000,000
Hiring subject matter experts to expand the past question bank across all WAEC, JAMB, and NECO subjects and years, ensuring comprehensive coverage for every student regardless of their subject combination.

iOS Development & App Store Launch: ₦800,000
Apple developer account fees, Flutter iOS build, testing, and full App Store submission to make Preplok available to iPhone users and significantly expand our addressable market.

AI Feature Development: ₦500,000
Improving the quality of AI-generated hints, adding personalised study recommendations, and building adaptive learning paths that adjust to each student's weak areas over time.

Infrastructure & Hosting: ₦300,000
Scaling the Firebase backend to support a larger user base, improving app performance, load times, and overall reliability.

Operations & Contingency: ₦200,000
Legal, administrative, and day-to-day operational costs.
growthTargets:
Within 12 months of receiving the grant, Preplok targets: 
10,000 registered users across Android, iOS, and web; launch on the Apple App Store. 
Expansion of the question bank to cover all major WAEC and JAMB subjects comprehensively. 
Partnerships with at least 10 secondary schools in Edo State and surrounding states and achieving consistent monthly revenue through subscriptions that covers operational costs.
revenueModel:
Preplok operates on a dual revenue model combining advertising and premium subscriptions.
The free tier is supported by Google AdMob ads integrated into the app, generating revenue from day one without requiring users to pay. This ensures the platform remains accessible to students who cannot afford subscriptions while still generating income at scale as the user base grows.

The premium subscription tier removes ads and unlocks unlimited past questions, unlimited mock exams, full AI hint access, and detailed performance analytics. Subscription plans are priced affordably for Nigerian students and families, providing an upgrade path for engaged users who want an uninterrupted study experience.

Future revenue streams include institutional licensing to schools and exam prep centres, and sponsored content partnerships with educational publishers.
This combination of ad revenue, subscriptions, and future B2B licensing creates a diversified income structure that reduces dependence on any single revenue source and supports long-term financial sustainability.
socialImpact:
Nigeria has one of the largest populations of secondary school students in Africa, with hundreds of thousands sitting WAEC and JAMB annually. Exam failure rates remain high, with many students unable to afford quality preparation. 
Preplok directly addresses educational inequality by providing affordable, intelligent exam preparation to students regardless of their location or economic background. Every student who improves their exam result gains access to university education, expanded career opportunities, and higher lifetime earning potential. 
Preplok's offline capability specifically targets students in underserved areas where internet access is unreliable ensuring the platform reaches those who need it most.
sustainabilityPath:
Preplok becomes self-sustaining through growing subscription revenue as the user base scales. The freemium model is designed to convert a percentage of free users to paid subscribers as they experience the product's value before high-stakes exams. 
As user numbers grow, the cost per user decreases while revenue per user remains stable, creating improving unit economics over time. Institutional licensing to schools and exam prep centres provides a B2B revenue layer that is less dependent on individual conversions. Within 18–24 months, subscription and institutional revenue is projected to cover all operational costs, making Preplok financially independent of grant funding

problem:
**Problem Statement**

For many Nigerians, ordering from a fashion designer or tailor is often a gamble. Customers worry about missed delivery deadlines, poor communication, abandoned orders, or even losing their payments and fabrics altogether. At the same time, many talented fashion businesses struggle to reach customers beyond their immediate communities because of limited digital access and low consumer trust. This lack of trust slows business growth, discourages online purchases, and leaves the industry without a reliable marketplace where both vendors and customers can transact with confidence.
solution: Zee Fashion is a digital marketplace that connects customers with verified local fashion designers and artisans across Nigeria. The platform enables vendors to showcase their products, receive secure payments, manage orders, and reach a wider market, while customers enjoy a trusted shopping experience with reliable delivery and order tracking.
mvpDescription:
**Minimum Viable Product (MVP)**

Zee Fashion is a live digital marketplace built to simplify fashion commerce in Nigeria. Verified designers and artisans can create branded stores, showcase their work, receive secure orders, manage sales, and reach customers nationwide from a single platform.

Beyond traditional online shopping, Zee Fashion introduces innovative features such as "Buy Together", which allows family and friends to contribute towards the purchase of a fashion item, and "Save to Buy", which enables customers to save gradually towards future purchases. Combined with secure payments, order tracking, wishlists, and in-app messaging, these features create a trusted and engaging shopping experience while helping local fashion businesses grow.
tractionMetric:
**Key Traction Metric**

Zee Fashion has achieved early market validation with **20 onboarded fashion artisans, 134 registered users, and partnerships with 3 logistics providers supporting reliable inter-state delivery**. The platform is publicly available on both the Apple App Store and Google Play Store, demonstrating that we have moved beyond the idea stage into a functional marketplace with real users, active vendors, and the infrastructure required for growth.
teamExpertise:
Zee Fashion is driven by a multidisciplinary team with expertise across technology, fashion, operations, marketing, and business development.

Nosakhare Atekha Endurance – Founder & CEO
A software engineer with over 10 years of experience building scalable digital products and technology solutions. He leads Zee Fashion’s vision, product development, and overall business strategy, leveraging his technical expertise to build a platform that solves real challenges within the fashion ecosystem.

Douglas Efe Elijah – Chief Technology Officer (CTO)
A technology professional with over 10 years of experience, responsible for supporting the technical direction, architecture, and scalability of Zee Fashion’s digital platform.

Blessing Chilaka – Chief Operating Officer (COO)
A fashion entrepreneur and shoemaker with over 5 years of experience in the fashion industry, combined with expertise in social media management and community engagement. She provides industry insights and supports vendor relationships, operations, and customer experience.

Desire Jephter – Chief Marketing Officer (CMO) & Legal Support
Responsible for marketing strategy, brand growth, partnerships, and supporting the company’s legal and compliance activities.

Together, the team combines technology expertise, fashion industry experience, operational knowledge, and market development capabilities to build and scale a trusted fashion marketplace for Nigeria.
challenges:
Our biggest challenge is scaling adoption and building stronger market penetration. While Zee Fashion has successfully launched its platform, onboarded artisans, acquired users, and established logistics partnerships, we need more resources to increase awareness, onboard more fashion businesses, improve customer acquisition, and strengthen our technology infrastructure.

Another key challenge is building trust and operational efficiency across the fashion ecosystem, including vendor verification, order fulfillment, and delivery coordination. With the right funding and support, we can accelerate growth, expand our network of artisans, and create a more reliable fashion marketplace for customers across Nigeria.
fundUsage:
The ₦5M grant will be used to accelerate Zee Fashion’s market expansion, increase user adoption, onboard more fashion businesses, and strengthen the platform’s ability to serve a growing customer base.

1. Marketing & Customer Acquisition – ₦2,000,000 (40%):
A significant portion of the funding will support targeted digital marketing campaigns, influencer partnerships, social media promotions, and community outreach initiatives to increase brand awareness, attract customers, and drive transactions on the platform.

2. Artisan Onboarding & Marketplace Growth – ₦1,250,000 (25%):
Funding will support the recruitment and onboarding of more fashion designers, tailors, and artisans across Nigeria, including vendor education and support to help them maximize the platform.

3. Product Development & Technology Improvement – ₦1,000,000 (20%):
The grant will be used to improve user experience, enhance platform performance, strengthen security, and develop features that improve customer trust and engagement.

4. Operations & Logistics Expansion – ₦750,000 (15%):
Funding will support logistics coordination, operational improvements, and partnerships that ensure reliable delivery and a seamless customer experience.

With this investment, Zee Fashion aims to significantly increase platform adoption, expand its artisan network, drive more transactions, and establish itself as a trusted digital marketplace for Nigerian fashion.
growthTargets:
Over the next 12 months, Zee Fashion aims to accelerate marketplace growth, increase customer adoption, and expand opportunities for fashion businesses across Nigeria.

1. Grow our customer base from 134 registered users to 10,000+ users through strategic marketing campaigns, partnerships, and community engagement.

2. Expand our artisan network from 20 onboarded fashion businesses to 500+ verified designers and artisans, enabling more local fashion entrepreneurs to access a wider market.

3. Increase completed transactions on the platform by improving customer acquisition, vendor participation, and overall marketplace engagement.

4. Expand our logistics network from 3 existing delivery partners to 10+ logistics partners to improve reliable order fulfillment and support wider market coverage.

5. Strengthen Zee Fashion as a trusted digital fashion ecosystem that empowers local businesses, creates economic opportunities, and makes it easier for customers to discover and purchase quality fashion products.
revenueModel:
Zee Fashion operates a multi-stream revenue model designed to create sustainable income while supporting the growth of fashion businesses on the platform.

1. Transaction Commission:
   Zee Fashion earns revenue by charging a commission on successful transactions completed through the platform. As more customers purchase from vendors, the platform generates recurring transaction-based income.

2. Vendor Subscription Plans:
   Fashion businesses can subscribe to premium vendor plans that provide additional tools, increased visibility, enhanced store features, and growth opportunities within the marketplace.

3. Custom Order Marketplace Fees:
   For customers who require customized fashion products, vendors can submit bids for custom orders. Zee Fashion generates revenue by charging fees associated with participating in these bidding opportunities.

4. Influencer Commerce System:
   Through our influencer system, content creators can promote fashion products and earn commissions from vendors for generating sales, while Zee Fashion facilitates and benefits from increased marketplace activity.

5. Referral Program:
   Our referral system encourages users and vendors to invite others to join the platform, helping accelerate marketplace growth and user acquisition.

6. Buy Together & Wishlist Commerce:
   Features such as Buy Together and Wishlist Collection increase customer engagement and purchasing ability by allowing users to collaborate with friends and family or plan future purchases. These features drive more transactions, increasing platform revenue through our commission model.
socialImpact:
Zee Fashion is empowering local fashion entrepreneurs by giving designers, tailors, shoemakers, and artisans access to a larger digital marketplace where they can grow their businesses beyond traditional limitations.

Many talented fashion creators struggle with visibility, customer reach, and consistent sales. By connecting them with customers and providing digital tools to sell, manage orders, and build trust, Zee Fashion helps transform small fashion businesses into sustainable income-generating ventures.

The platform also creates economic opportunities across the fashion value chain by supporting artisans, influencers, and logistics providers while making locally produced fashion more accessible to customers. As we scale, Zee Fashion will contribute to job creation, youth empowerment, and the growth of Nigeria’s creative economy.
sustainabilityPath:
Zee Fashion’s long-term sustainability is driven by building a high-volume digital marketplace where fashion businesses and customers continuously create value for each other. Our revenue model is designed around multiple income streams, including transaction commissions, vendor subscription plans, custom order bidding fees, and marketplace services.

As more artisans join the platform and more customers shop through Zee Fashion, we will increase transaction volume while creating recurring revenue opportunities. Our growth strategy focuses on expanding our vendor network, increasing customer adoption, strengthening logistics partnerships, and continuously improving the platform experience.

problem:

These issues limit growth despite the abundance of creative talent.
Key Problems Facing Photography Businesses in Edo State and Nigeria  
 Structural & Infrastructure Challenges
•	Poor power supply: Frequent blackouts increase operating costs, as photographers must rely on generators and alternative power sources.
•	Limited broadband access: Slow or unreliable internet hampers digital delivery, online marketing, and participation in global creative markets.
•	Inadequate studio facilities: Many photographers lack access to modern equipment and professional spaces, reducing competitiveness.
Financing & Business Structure
•	Lack of structured financing: Banks and investors rarely support photography businesses, leaving them underfunded.
•	Informal industry: Photography is often treated as a side hustle rather than a structured enterprise, limiting scalability.
solution:

•	Structured financing: Access to loans and grants tailored for creative businesses.
•	Policy advocacy: Push for state and federal recognition of photography as a formal industry.
•	Creative hubs: Establish centers in Edo to provide training, networking, and shared resources.
•	Digital platforms: Encourage adoption of online payment systems and marketplaces to reduce administrative burdens.

problem:
While working in two different laundry businesses, I observed a common challenge that many customers had accepted as normal: uncertainty.

Customers often dropped off their clothes without knowing exactly when they would be ready. Many made unnecessary trips to the laundry only to discover their garments were still unavailable, disrupting their schedules and forcing them to change personal or professional plans. This was especially challenging for students, busy professionals, and households whose daily routines depend on having clean clothes available when needed.

I also observed that many busy customers delayed picking up or dropping off their laundry because their work and academic commitments left them with little time for these errands.
solution:
FinesseKleen Laundry was established to eliminate this uncertainty by making laundry services predictable, reliable, and convenient.

Every customer receives a clear and specific turnaround time at the point of drop-off, ensuring they know exactly when their laundry will be ready. Customers are notified immediately once their clothes are completed, and in the rare event of a delay, they receive timely communication in advance so they can adjust their plans accordingly.

To further address the time constraints faced by busy professionals and students, FinesseKleen also provides a pickup and delivery service, allowing customers to focus on work, academics, family, and other priorities while we manage the entire laundry process.

By combining reliable service, proactive communication, and convenient logistics, FinesseKleen Laundry helps customers save time, reduce stress, and confidently plan their daily lives.
mvpDescription:
Minimum Viable Product (MVP)

FinesseKleen Laundry launched with a simple but differentiated service model focused on reliability rather than scale. The initial offering consisted of wash, dry, ironing, and folding services with a guaranteed turnaround time communicated to customers at the point of drop-off.

Instead of investing heavily in infrastructure, the business focused on validating one key assumption: customers value predictability and timely communication as much as clean clothes.

Customers could simply drop off their laundry, receive a confirmed pickup schedule, and return at the promised time with confidence, eliminating unnecessary trips and uncertainty.

As customer needs evolved, pickup and delivery services were introduced to better serve busy students and professionals who lacked the time to visit the laundry.

problem: Students often need a quiet place to work, study, or meet, along with quick access to services like printing, photocopying, scanning, and document processing. However, most cafes do not offer these business services, while business centers rarely provide a comfortable, relaxed atmosphere to sit and work. As a result, students are forced to move between multiple locations  a cafe to relax, a business center for printing, and a separate quiet space to study wasting time, money, and effort.
solution: Ultimate Cafe Business Center solves this problem by combining a comfortable cafe environment with essential business center services in one location, giving students a single, convenient space to study, relax, and handle their academic and personal document needs all at once.
mvpDescription:
The MVP is a single, small-scale physical location near a student population (e.g., close to a school, university, or student hostel area) that combines two core offerings just enough to test whether students actually want this combined solution, without building the "full" version yet.
Core features to include in the MVP:

Basic cafe setup
A small seating area (tables/chairs, Wi-Fi, power outlets)
A simple menu (snacks, drinks, coffee/tea) — doesn't need to be elaborate

Core business center services
Printing
Photocopying
Scanning
Basic document typing/formatting (e.g., assignments, CVs)
tractionMetric: Ultimate Cafe Business Center currently serves a customer base of 100 students, with 45 monthly active users generating ₦300,000 in monthly revenue — reflecting a 45% activation rate and demonstrating strong early demand for our combined cafe and business center model
teamExpertise: Ultimate Cafe Business Center is led by a solo student founder with direct, first-hand insight into the daily challenges students face from finding a comfortable place to study to accessing basic services like printing and document processing. This proximity to the target customer has shaped every part of the business, from service design to pricing, and has already been validated through real operations: a functioning MVP, a growing customer base of 100, and 45 monthly active users generating consistent revenue. As a hands-on founder managing both the cafe and business center operations directly, I bring practical, ground-level experience in customer service, daily business management, and problem-solving skills built through running the business itself rather than theory alone. This grant would support the next stage of growth: bringing in additional skills (finance, operations, or technical support) to scale what has already been proven to work.
challenges:
1. Limited capital for scaling equipment and space
Current operations run on minimal equipment (basic printer/scanner, small seating area). Growing demand means we need better-capacity printers, more seating, and improved cafe equipment all requiring upfront capital we don't yet have.
2. Low activation rate among registered customers
Only 45 of our 100 total customers are monthly active (45% activation). Converting the remaining 55 into regular users requires better awareness, possibly a referral or loyalty incentive resources currently limited by a lack of marketing budget.
3.. Solo founder capacity constraints
As a one-person team also studying, my time is split between running daily operations (cafe counter, printing, customer service) and growing the business strategically. This limits how much I can focus on expansion, partnerships, or process improvement at once.
4. Manual, non-digital operations
Tracking sales, print jobs, and customer visits is currently done manually (notebook/spreadsheet). This makes it hard to analyze patterns, forecast demand accurately, or scale without errors as customer volume grows.

problem:
Nigeria faces a critical talent paradox: a large population of unemployed and underemployed youths coexists with businesses, startups and SMEs struggling to find skilled, reliable talent in tech and digital sectors.

Many young people in Edo state and across Nigeria  graduate with theoretical knowledge but lack practical digital skills and access to fair hiring opportunities. Traditional recruitment platforms are expensive, biased, and inaccessible to most, leading to prolonged unemployment, frustration, and brain drain. At the same time, small businesses waste time and resources on inefficient hiring, slowing growth and innovation.

This problem is urgent because Edo State’s youthful population, if properly skilled and connected, represents a massive opportunity for economic development. Without intervention, we risk losing an entire generation to unemployment and migration.
solution:
Siliconverse is an AI-powered talent platform built to solve the talent paradox in Nigeria by connecting young talents to startups and SMEs through intelligent, bias-reduced matching and free upskilling.

How it works:
-For Job Seekers: Completely free platform with one-click applications and integrated Talent Accelerator Program(TAP) to bridge skill gaps and increase employability.
- For Employers: Affordable AI tools that vet, rank, and match candidates based on skills, fit and potential, reducing hiring time, bias, and bad hires.

Siliconverse is not just another job board, it is a complete talent ecosystem that creates fairer opportunities, builds real skills, and drives inclusive economic growth.
mvpDescription:
Our Minimum Viable Product (MVP) is a functional AI-powered talent matching platform that connects young tech talents with startups and SMEs in Nigeria.

Core Features of the Current MVP:

a)Free Talent Side: Job seekers can create profiles, browse opportunities, and apply with one click. They also have access to basic upskilling via Talent Accelerator Program(TAP).
-AI Smart Matching Engine: Analyzes candidate skills, experience, fit, and potential to recommend jobs

b)Employer Dashboard: Free basic posting and AI matching. They can also create skill assessments, to assess the expertise of the applying talents.
- AI vetting: For employers to vet multiple applications into the best 10s.

The MVP has validated our core value proposition: using AI to make hiring faster, fairer, and more accessible while helping young talents become job-ready.

We are now focused on improving matching accuracy, expanding upskilling content, and converting early users into paying employers through placement fees and premium subscriptions.
tractionMetric:
Our key traction metric is “Number of Successful Job Placements / Matches”.

This is the ultimate measure of value we deliver, not just sign-ups or activity, but real outcomes: young people actually getting jobs or internships through Siliconverse.
teamExpertise:
Siliconverse is powered by a lean but highly capable core team with complementary skills in technology, design, and business growth.

- Amaechi Chinonso (CEO & Co-Founder) leads Business Strategy and Growth. He drives product vision, community building, user acquisition, and partnerships. 

- Amadi Michael (CTO & Co-Founder) is our Technical Lead and Fullstack Developer. He is responsible for architecting and developing the core AI matching engine, ensuring scalability, performance, and low-bandwidth optimization.

- Ashini David (Head of UI/UX Design) designs intuitive, user-friendly interfaces that make the platform accessible, especially for first-time users and those in low-connectivity areas.

-Thompson Falowo (Frontend Engineer) implements responsive and efficient user interfaces, ensuring a smooth experience across mobile and web platforms.

Together, our team combines strong technical expertise with practical business acumen and user-centered design. This balanced composition enables us to build an inclusive, functional, and scalable AI talent solution tailored to Nigeria’s unique challenges.
challenges:
As an early-stage startup, Siliconverse is currently facing the following key challenges:

1. Limited Funding and Runway: Being self-funded, we have very constrained capital to improve our AI infrastructure and run consistent marketing, which slows down our growth pace.

2. AI Model Optimization and Data Quality: Improving the accuracy and bias-reduction capability of our AI matching engine requires more diverse training data and continuous testing, which is time-consuming and resource-intensive.

3. Building Strong Employer Trust and Partnerships: Convincing startups and SMEs  to fully adopt a relatively new platform remains a hurdle, especially in a market dominated by established players like Jobberman and LinkedIn.

These challenges are the main bottlenecks limiting our ability to scale faster and create greater impact. Support from the EYIF Grant would significantly help us address them.
fundUsage:
When awarded the ₦5 Million grant, we will allocate the funds strategically across four key areas to move Siliconverse from early beta to sustainable revenue and greater impact:

a) ₦2 Million (40%): Marketing and User Acquisition.
  Marketing and targeted outreach campaigns in Edo State and beyond, expand the Talent Accelerator Program (TAP), and host more physical and virtual events to grow our users and partners.

b) ₦1.5 Million (30%): Product & Technology Improvement
  Enhance our AI matching engine for better accuracy and bias reduction, develop mobile app v1.0, and improve low-bandwidth performance for rural users.

c) ₦1 Million (20%): Operations  
  Cover cloud hosting, tools and legal compliance.

d) ₦500,000 (10%): Team Expansion  
  Hire more AI/ML developers and community/sales support personnel to increase capacity and execution speed.


This allocation will help us achieve our immediate goals: convert more employers to paid users, generate consistent revenue through placement fees, and create measurable job opportunities for young people in Edo State and Nigeria.
growthTargets:
Over the next 12 months, Siliconverse aims to achieve the following ambitious and realistic growth targets:

-User Base: Grow from 500+ to 7,500 active registered users

- Employer Network: Onboard 500+ active employers (startups and SMEs), with at least 10 converting to paid users.

- Impact: Facilitate 2,000+ successful job and internship placements, directly helping young people in Edo State and across Nigeria secure decent work.

- Revenue: Generate ₦5.7 Million in total revenue, primarily through placement success fees (5% of first-year salary) and early premium subscriptions.

-Product & Community: Launch the mobile app v1.0, expand the Talent Accelerator Program to train 1,500+ youths, and establish partnerships with at least 5 key institutions (universities, tech hubs, or government agencies) in Edo State.

These targets will be achieved by focusing on organic community growth, improving AI matching accuracy, and running consistent outreach and training programs. Achieving them will position Siliconverse as a leading talent solution in the region and create measurable socioeconomic impact.
revenueModel:
Revenue Model

Siliconverse operates a placement/success fee model, designed to align our success directly with the success of our users.

How we make money:

a) Primary Revenue Stream: We charge employers a 5% success fee of the candidate’s first-year salary only after a successful hire is made through the platform. This is performance-based, employers pay nothing upfront.
b) Premium employer features: AI based skill Assessment and advanced analytics on a subscription basis.
c) Paid upskilling certifications and employer-sponsored training modules for talents

Currently, we are focused on increasing successful placements to build consistent revenue.
socialImpact:
Siliconverse is creating both social and economic impact by addressing youth unemployment and skills gaps in Edo State and Nigeria.

Social Impact:

- We have empowered over 100 young people through our tech talent program and internships, giving them digital skills, confidence, and real job opportunities.

- Our AI matching promotes inclusivity, helping underserved youths who are often excluded by traditional recruitment platforms.
- We foster a supportive community where young talents feel seen and valued.


Economic Impact:

- We help startups and SMEs in Edo State and beyond hire faster and better, reducing recruitment costs and improving productivity.

- Every successful placement contributes directly to decent work and economic growth (SDG 8), enabling young people to earn income, support their families, and contribute to the local economy.

- Our platform supports small businesses to scale by giving them access to affordable, quality talent.
sustainabilityPath:
Siliconverse’s path to sustainability is built on a clear transition from community validation to consistent revenue generation while maintaining our social mission.

We operate a performance-based success fee model, charging employers 5% of the candidate’s first-year salary only after a successful hire. The platform remains completely free for job seekers to ensure maximum accessibility and network growth.
Our long term plan is to achieve full financial sustainability through diversified income (placement fees + subscriptions + enterprise partnerships) while scaling to serve 10,000+ users.

problem:
Across Nigeria, millions of households, businesses, schools, hospitals, and commercial facilities rely on cleaning products every day. However, many available products are either expensive due to import dependence, inconsistent in quality, or ineffective, leaving consumers to choose between affordability and performance. Small businesses and institutions are especially affected, as high cleaning costs increase their operating expenses without guaranteeing better results.
At the same time, Nigeria continues to depend heavily on imported cleaning products despite having the capacity to manufacture high-quality alternatives locally. This limits the growth of indigenous manufacturers, reduces job creation, and contributes to foreign exchange pressures. Many promising local manufacturers also struggle with limited production equipment, inadequate access to capital, and weak distribution networks, making it difficult to meet market demand and compete with established brands.
Etonbra Global Enterprise was established to address these challenges by producing high-quality, affordable, and proudly Nigerian cleaning solutions that deliver professional results without the premium price. Through local manufacturing, we are creating value within Nigeria, reducing reliance on imported products, supporting local supply chains, and generating employment. With the right investment, we can scale production, reach more customers, and make trusted, locally made cleaning products accessible to homes, businesses, and institutions nationwide.
solution:
Etonbra Global Enterprise provides a locally manufactured range of high-quality, affordable cleaning products that deliver professional performance while remaining accessible to households, businesses, and institutions. Our product portfolio includes an all-purpose cleaner, glass cleaner, professional-grade car wash and wax, liquid starch, and other specialized cleaning solutions formulated to meet the everyday hygiene needs of our customers.
Our solution combines quality, affordability, and local innovation. By producing in Nigeria, we reduce dependence on imported cleaning products, shorten supply chains, and offer customers reliable products tailored to local conditions. Every product is developed with a focus on effectiveness, safety, and consistency, ensuring customers receive excellent value without compromising on quality.
Beyond manufacturing cleaning products, we are building a sustainable Nigerian brand that creates jobs, supports local suppliers, and strengthens the country's manufacturing sector. As we scale, we will expand our product range, increase production capacity, and grow our distribution network to ensure that more homes, schools, hospitals, hotels, offices, and commercial facilities across Nigeria have access to trusted, proudly Nigerian cleaning solutions. Our vision is to become one of Nigeria's leading indigenous cleaning products manufacturers, driving economic growth while improving hygiene and public health through quality, locally made products.
mvpDescription:
Our Minimum Viable Product (MVP) is a market-tested range of high-performance cleaning solutions designed to meet the everyday needs of homes, businesses, and institutions. Our product line includes an all-purpose cleaner, glass cleaner, professional-grade car wash and wax, and liquid starch, all formulated to deliver premium cleaning performance at an affordable price.
These products have moved beyond the concept stage—they are already being manufactured, branded, and sold to paying customers, with repeat purchases validating both their quality and market demand. challenges: Our biggest challenge is scaling production to meet growing market demand while maintaining consistent quality. Although our products have gained customer acceptance, we currently operate with limited production equipment, which restricts our manufacturing capacity and efficiency.

startupName: Closed Circuit Security (CCTV) on solar Light Installation
problem:
Integrating surveillance cameras into existing or new off-grid solar lighting systems significantly increases the continuous or semi-continuous load on the system's shared power chain. This frequently results in premature battery failure, insufficient power for nighttime illumination, and intermittent CCTV recording during periods of prolonged cloud cover or adverse weather.

Areas of Concern:

1. Shared-Energy Imbalance: Traditional solar lights are sized exclusively for lighting demands. Adding continuous power draws from wireless transmission modules (e.g., 4G/Wi-Fi) and 24/7 camera recording drains the battery, causing the system to fail.
2. Weather-Dependent Downtime: In regions like Benin City, Nigeria, prolonged heavy rainfall or cloudy days reduce photovoltaic (PV) charging efficiency. Without sufficient solar resources, the battery bank drops below optimal operational voltage, resulting in unreliable or completely inactive security coverage.
3. Connectivity and Data Transmission Drops: Transmitting high-definition video over a cellular network (e.g., 4G LTE) requires a consistent signal and consumes considerable power. In areas with weak or fluctuating cellular coverage, the data link drops, leading to unstable live streaming and failed remote access to security alerts.
4. Hardware Theft and Vandalism: Because solar-powered setups house batteries and controllers on public poles in remote areas, they are susceptible to vandalism. The theft of these core components leaves both the lighting and surveillance functionalities disabled.
5. Component-Specific Failures: Inadequate charge controllers often fail to protect batteries from overcharging or deep discharge, accelerating battery degradation. Furthermore, water ingress into the camera housing can short-circuit the sensitive electronics.
solution:
To address these limitations, system planners and engineers should implement the following targeted upgrades:

1. Smarter Load Management: Implement a digital control algorithm using Passive Infrared (PIR) Sensors. This lowers camera and lighting power consumption by operating at reduced baseline energy levels unless motion is detected.
2. Optimized Sizing Parameters: Upgrade to larger capacity batteries, specifically deep-cycle LiFePO4 (Lithium Iron Phosphate) Batteries, which have a longer lifespan and handle continuous charging and discharging cycles more effectively.
3. Local and Edge Storage: Enable Local MicroSD Card Storage as a primary fail-safe. This guarantees continuous video recording even when unstable network connections prevent data transmission to the remote control center.
4. Hardware Hardening: Install Tamper-Proof Hardware, including anti-theft bolts and secure, ground-level enclosures for batteries and wiring.
mvpDescription:
1. The Minimum Viable Product (MVP)

The MVP in solar CCTV represents the lowest-cost, functional prototype that solves the core user need: autonomous, reliable surveillance and lighting without grid dependency.
Hardware Core: An all-in-one unit combining an LED solar floodlight, a built-in high-definition (2MP to 4MP) camera, a solar panel (e.g., 20W–45W), and a rechargeable lithium battery (e.g., 20,000mAh).
Connectivity: Integration with wireless networks (e.g., local Wi-Fi or 4G LTE via SIM) for remote monitoring via mobile apps like V380 Pro or Eseecloud.
Core Features: Motion detection (PIR/Radar), night vision (IR/Full Color), two-way audio, and mobile alarm pushes.
MVP Goal: Validate that the solar panel and battery can consistently power the camera and lights 24/5/365, even through periods of low sunlight, without requiring complex physical wiring.

2. Measuring TractionTraction in this sector is the evidence that the target market (homeowners, estates, commercial businesses, or rural farmers) is actually using, buying, and depending on the product.
Pilot Deployments: Initial testing of the MVP in strategic local environments like residential perimeters, rural farms, or parking lots in and around Benin City to gather user feedback.
User Engagement Metrics: Tracking daily Active Users (DAU) on the companion mobile app—how frequently customers check live feeds, review playback, or respond to motion alerts.Sales & Revenue: Units sold and generated revenue, with consumer-ready systems commonly retailing in Nigeria between N110,000 and N115,000 (depending on wattage and dual-lens capacities).
System Resilience: Tracking zero-failure rates in battery life and solar charging capacity across weather fluctuations, verifying that the offline 4G connection remains stable.
Customer Feedback: Qualitative validation that the solution actively deters crime, reduces electricity bills to zero, and provides continuous peace of mind
tractionMetric:
Traction and performance metrics for solar-powered CCTV installations focus on three primary pillars:

Power & Energy Metrics Because solar-powered CCTV systems rely entirely on renewable energy and battery storage, monitoring the health of the power subsystem is critical.
Battery State of Charge (SoC): Tracks the energy reserve. It should rarely drop below 20% to prevent battery degradation. Standard setups require LiFePO4 batteries with a 3 to 5-day backup capacity during periods of poor weather or low solar irradiance.
System Autonomous Runtime: The number of hours the camera and lighting can function without any solar charging, usually measured in days.
Solar Panel Yield Ratio: The percentage of potential energy generated by the solar panel versus its rated capacity. It tracks the efficiency of solar panel positioning, angle, and absence of shading.Surveillance & Hardware Efficacy Tracking how well the system monitors and deters intruders ensures security ROI.
Alarm Response & Trigger Time: The duration from motion detection to the actual recording trigger or the delivery of a real-time push notification (ideal latency is ≤ 2 seconds).Motion Detection Accuracy: The percentage of true alarms versus false alarms caused by moving trees, animals, or weather changes.
Illumination Consistency: In integrated installations (where the solar system also powers LED floodlights), metrics track the maintained lux level (e.g., 800 lux) and the dusk-to-dawn operational stability of the light.
Vandalism & Tamper Rate: Frequency of physical attacks or tampering with the pole or camera enclosure.Network & Connectivity For remote or off-grid deployments (such as estates or rural sites), checking video transmission data is essential.
Communication Latency: The time lag between the camera capturing footage and the operator viewing it remotely via 4G/Wi-Fi. The average delay should ideally remain below 10 seconds for live monitoring.
Network Uptime & Signal Strength: For 4G SIM-based or wireless radio deployments, measuring the percentage of time the camera remains connected to the monitoring server.
Packet Loss & Frame Rate (FPS): Metrics checking the stability of the video feed, ensuring a steady framerate (e.g., 15-30 FPS) without corrupted or dropped frames during viewing or cloud uploading.

revenueModel:
A revenue model in Solar-Powered Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) combines equipment sales, installation labor, and recurring services. This approach generates continuous cash flow by packaging security with sustainable, off-grid LED lighting, making it highly attractive for remote or grid-unreliable areas across Nigeria.

Core Revenue Streams To maximize profitability, you can build your business model around the following foundational streams:Hardware Sales & Procurement: The upfront sale of the physical security and lighting equipment. This includes the solar panels, battery banks, charge controllers, inverters, LED floodlights, and 4G/IP PTZ (Pan-Tilt-Zoom) cameras. Sourcing directly from manufacturers (like LS VISION) or utilizing all-in-one kits (like Hikvision) provides excellent profit margins.Installation & Engineering Services: Professional labor charges for site assessment, pole mounting, wiring, system configuration, and testing. Because no electrical grid trenching is required, installation is streamlined but still commands premium technical service rates.Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMCs): Solar-powered CCTV requires preventative care, such as cleaning the solar panels (to prevent output drops), battery health checks, and connection tightening. Charging an annual flat fee secures recurring revenue and minimizes client downtime.Cloud Hosting & Data Subscriptions: Many solar cameras are wireless and operate on 4G cellular networks. You can act as an internet/data reseller or offer premium cloud storage and AI-analytics subscriptions (e.g., automated humanoid detection) via the camera’s application.Surveillance-as-a-Service (SaaS): A modern, zero-upfront-cost model where clients pay a fixed monthly fee (similar to EnGoPlanet). You retain ownership of the solar-CCTV asset while guaranteeing uptime, security, and lighting.Financial Considerations for the Nigerian MarketInitial Capital Required: The upfront cost for high-quality batteries and solar panels can be prohibitive. It is standard practice to require a minimum of a 70% to 80% upfront deposit before commencing any project to cover material costs.Autonomous Sizing: Battery banks must be sized for 3 to 5 days of autonomy to ensure the CCTV and LED lights operate optimally during heavy overcast or rainy periods. Factor these capacity costs into your pricing model
socialImpact:
Integrating Closed Circuit Security (CCTV) with solar light installations transforms community infrastructure into self-sustaining, off-grid security networks. This combination fundamentally drives down operational costs, creates stronger nighttime economies, deters crime, and addresses critical electricity deficits, particularly in developing regions.Here is the breakdown of the major social and economic impacts:

1. Economic ImpactsDrastic Cost Reductions: Traditional CCTV and grid-powered lighting require extensive trenching and continuous reliance on unstable grids or diesel generators. Solar-powered units eliminate trenching costs, reduce energy bills to virtually zero, and eliminate the need for expensive fuel.Business Growth: Well-lit environments and visible surveillance instill confidence, encouraging local businesses, markets, and hospitality sectors to extend operating hours into the night, which directly boosts local revenues.Increased Property Values: Communities and commercial real estate become more desirable as safety improves, driving up property values and attracting private investment.Fewer Emergency and Repair Costs: Decreased crime and safer streets reduce municipal expenditures on emergency services, police interventions, and infrastructure repairs resulting from vandalism.

2. Social ImpactsCrime Deterrence and Public Safety: Combining bright illumination with 24/7 surveillance fundamentally removes dark corners where criminals hide, significantly lowering nighttime outdoor crimes like theft, vandalism, and assault.Inclusive Community Engagement: Reliable lighting and monitoring make public spaces (e.g., parks and transit nodes) welcoming at night. It also empowers women, minority groups, and self-help networks to conduct evening activities and skill-development classes without fear.Continuous Surveillance Availability: Because solar lighting arrays are off-grid and backed by battery storage, security remains fully functional even during power blackouts and grid failures.Green Energy Transition: The use of renewable energy over fossil fuel-dependent generators lowers a community's carbon footprint, promoting environmentally sustainable development and better air quality.

3. Challenges to ConsiderHigh Initial Investment: While they save money over time, the upfront purchase and installation costs of commercial off-grid security systems can be initially prohibitive for smaller communities or private businesses.Environmental/Weather Constraints: Because they depend on sunlight, prolonged overcast or rainy periods can impact continuous power generation and camera operations if the battery storage is not properly optimized.
sustainabilityPath:
Achieving sustainability in Closed Circuit Security (CCTV) and solar light installations involves optimizing energy efficiency, utilizing durable hardware, and minimizing environmental footprints. By harnessing renewable energy, these systems eliminate grid reliance and ensure continuous, eco-friendly perimeter surveillance.Here are the critical components to consider for a sustainable, high-performing solar CCTV and lighting system:

1. Hardware and Energy StorageAdvanced Battery Chemistry: Avoid traditional lead-acid batteries, which have short lifespans and perform poorly in high temperatures. Opt for deep-cycle Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO₄) batteries, which offer an 8-to-10-year lifespan, high heat tolerance, and eco-friendly recyclability.High-Efficiency Solar Panels: Select Monocrystalline photovoltaic panels. They are highly efficient, performing better in low-light and cloudy conditions than Polycrystalline alternatives.

2. Intelligent System DesignMotion-Triggered Lighting: Instead of running floodlights at 100% brightness all night, integrate passive infrared (PIR) motion sensors. The light stays dimmed at a low power mode and automatically switches to full brightness only when movement is detected, conserving critical battery life.Low-Power Electronics: Choose CCTV cameras and LED lights specifically designed for "Green CCTV" using ultra-low-power electronics and sleep-mode capabilities to reduce daily energy drain.

3. Installation Best PracticesOptimal Orientation & Tilt: Mount the solar panels facing south (if located in the Northern Hemisphere) or north (if located in the Southern Hemisphere, like Nigeria) at an angle roughly equal to your latitude for maximum sunlight absorption.Shade Management: Ensure the panels have a clear line of sight with no obstructions from trees or surrounding buildings.Weatherproof Wiring: Secure all wiring in waterproof conduit pipes and use waterproof sealants to prevent environmental degradation and vandalism.

4. Smart Monitoring & MaintenanceRemote Health Monitoring: Utilize smart surveillance portals to remotely track system health (e.g., battery state-of-charge, camera connectivity) without needing on-site physical inspections, significantly reducing the carbon footprint of maintenance trips.Modular Infrastructure: Deploy modular systems featuring distinct LED light sources, battery packs, and solar panels so that single components can be replaced or upgraded rather than discarding the entire security unit.

problem:
Nigeria continues to face significant challenges in access to reliable and affordable electricity. Frequent power outages, an unstable national grid, and the high cost of diesel and petrol generators have negatively affected households, small businesses, educational institutions, healthcare facilities, and rural communities. Many individuals and enterprises are forced to rely on expensive and environmentally harmful fossil fuel generators, resulting in increased operating costs, reduced productivity, and limited economic growth.
At the same time, although Nigeria has abundant solar energy resources, the adoption of renewable energy solutions remains low due to the high upfront cost of quality solar systems, limited access to professional installation and maintenance services, and the widespread availability of substandard products in the market.
These challenges create an urgent need for reliable, affordable, and professionally delivered renewable energy solutions that can improve energy access, reduce dependence on fossil fuels, lower energy costs, and contribute to environmental sustainability.
Bil-Tech Trading and Contracting Ventures was established to address these challenges by supplying, installing, and maintaining high-quality solar power systems and inverter solutions for homes, businesses, institutions, and communities across Nigeria. Through affordable renewable energy solutions, the company aims to improve access to clean electricity, support business productivity, create employment opportunities, and contribute to Nigeria's transition towards sustainable energy.
solution:
Bil-Tech Trading and Contracting Ventures provides reliable, affordable, and sustainable renewable energy solutions through the supply, installation, maintenance, and after-sales support of high-quality solar power systems, inverters, batteries, and related electrical equipment. The business is registered in Nigeria to provide the supply, sales, and services of solar equipment and inverters.
Our solution is designed to reduce dependence on the unstable national electricity grid and expensive fossil fuel generators by enabling households, businesses, schools, healthcare facilities, and public institutions to generate clean and uninterrupted power through solar energy.

Our approach includes:
Supplying certified, high-quality solar equipment sourced from reputable manufacturers.
Providing professional system design, installation, testing, and commissioning to ensure maximum efficiency and long-term reliability.
Delivering preventive maintenance, technical support, and after-sales services to maximize system performance and lifespan.
Offering customized energy solutions based on each customer's energy requirements and budget.
Educating customers on energy efficiency and the long-term financial and environmental benefits of renewable energy.

Through this solution, Bil-Tech aims to make clean energy more accessible and affordable, reduce energy costs for consumers, improve business productivity, create skilled employment opportunities, and support Nigeria's transition toward a sustainable, low-carbon economy.

Our long-term vision is to become a trusted renewable energy solutions provider across Nigeria by delivering innovative, customer-focused, and environmentally responsible energy systems that improve lives and drive economic development.
mvpDescription:
Bil-Tech Trading and Contracting Ventures has developed a market-ready renewable energy solution focused on the supply, installation, and maintenance of residential and commercial solar power systems. Our Minimum Viable Product (MVP) is a complete solar energy package comprising high-efficiency solar panels, hybrid inverters, lithium battery storage systems, mounting structures, electrical protection devices, and professional installation services tailored to each customer's energy requirements.

The MVP is designed to provide customers with a reliable, affordable, and sustainable alternative to unreliable grid electricity and fuel-powered generators. Beyond supplying quality equipment, Bil-Tech delivers end-to-end services including site assessment, system design, installation, testing, commissioning, user training, and after-sales technical support to ensure long-term system performance.

Key features of the MVP include:
(1) Customized solar power system design based on customer energy needs.
(2) High-efficiency solar panels for maximum energy generation.
(3) Hybrid inverter technology with seamless switching between solar, battery, and grid power.
(4) Lithium battery storage for uninterrupted power during outages.
(5) Scalable system architecture that can be expanded as energy demand grows.
(6) Professional installation, testing, commissioning, preventive maintenance, and technical support.

With this solution, users can:
(1) Generate clean and reliable electricity using solar energy.
(2) Reduce or eliminate dependence on the national electricity grid and fuel generators.
(3) Store excess solar energy for use during power outages or at night.
(4) Power homes, offices, schools, healthcare facilities, farms, and small businesses with uninterrupted electricity.
(5) Lower electricity and fuel costs while reducing carbon emissions.
(6) Access ongoing maintenance and technical support to maximize the lifespan and performance of their solar systems.

The grant funding will enable Bil-Tech to scale this MVP by increasing inventory, expanding installation capacity, establishing a demonstration and service center, and making affordable renewable energy solutions accessible to more households, SMEs, institutions, and underserved communities across Nigeria. This MVP demonstrates both market demand and Bil-Tech's capability to deliver a scalable, high-impact clean energy solution.
tractionMetric: Bil-Tech's primary traction metric is the development of a qualified customer pipeline and strategic supplier partnerships. Since registering the business, we have focused on validating market demand through customer engagement, supplier sourcing, and operational planning. The strong interest received from residential, SME, and institutional customers confirms the growing demand for reliable and affordable solar energy solutions. The grant will enable us to convert this pipeline into paying customers by expanding inventory and service capacity.
teamExpertise:
Bil-Tech Trading and Contracting Ventures is led by a team with expertise in renewable energy solutions, procurement, project management, technical system integration, logistics, and customer support. The team combines experience in sourcing high-quality solar equipment, designing energy solutions, managing supplier relationships, and delivering projects from planning through installation and after-sales service.
Our technical capabilities include solar system assessment, system sizing, equipment selection, installation coordination, testing, commissioning, maintenance, and troubleshooting. We are committed to delivering reliable, high-quality renewable energy solutions that meet customer requirements and industry standards.
The team also possesses strong experience in business operations, contract management, supply chain coordination, and financial planning, enabling efficient project execution and sustainable business growth. As the business expands, Bil-Tech will continue to strengthen its technical workforce through strategic partnerships, industry certifications, and ongoing training to ensure the highest level of service delivery.
This combination of technical knowledge, operational experience, and customer-focused service positions Bil-Tech to successfully scale its renewable energy solutions and contribute to improving energy access across Nigeria.
challenges:
As an early-stage renewable energy startup, Bil-Tech Trading and Contracting Ventures is focused on building the capacity required to meet growing market demand. Our biggest challenges include:
(1) Limited access to startup capital to procure sufficient inventory of quality solar panels, inverters, batteries, and related components.
(2) Working capital constraints, which limit our ability to execute multiple projects simultaneously and offer flexible payment options to customers.
(3) Establishing a demonstration and service center where customers can experience our products, receive technical advice, and access after-sales support.
(4) Expanding market awareness and customer acquisition through effective marketing and community outreach, particularly in underserved areas.
(5) Scaling our technical workforce by recruiting and training qualified installation and maintenance technicians to support business growth.

Securing this grant will enable Bil-Tech to address these challenges by increasing inventory, strengthening operational capacity, creating employment opportunities, and accelerating the delivery of reliable and affordable renewable energy solutions to households, businesses, institutions, and communities across Nigeria.
fundUsage:
The ₦5 million grant will be invested directly into the growth and expansion of Bil-Tech Trading and Contracting Ventures to strengthen our capacity to deliver reliable and affordable renewable energy solutions across Nigeria.

Approximately ₦2,500,000 will be used to procure high-quality solar panels, hybrid inverters, lithium batteries, and essential installation materials, enabling us to execute more projects and reduce delivery lead times.

An estimated ₦750,000 will be invested in purchasing installation tools, testing equipment, safety gear, and other technical resources required to ensure professional and efficient project delivery.

A further ₦750,000 will be allocated towards establishing a small demonstration and service center where customers can view our products, receive technical consultations, and access after-sales support.

To accelerate market penetration and customer acquisition, ₦500,000 will be used for branding, marketing, digital promotion, and community outreach activities aimed at increasing awareness of our renewable energy solutions.

The remaining ₦500,000 will serve as working capital to recruit and train technical personnel, support day-to-day operations, and ensure the timely execution of customer projects.

This investment will enable Bil-Tech to increase inventory, create employment opportunities, expand access to clean and reliable energy, and build a sustainable renewable energy business that contributes to Nigeria's economic development and clean energy transition.
growthTargets:
Over the next 12 months, Bil-Tech Trading and Contracting Ventures aims to achieve the following milestones:

(1) Successfully complete 30–50 residential and commercial solar installation projects across Nigeria.
(2) Generate ₦20 – ₦30 million in annual revenue through the supply, installation, and maintenance of solar energy systems.
(3) Build strategic partnerships with at least five reputable manufacturers and distributors of solar panels, inverters, batteries, and renewable energy equipment.
(4) Create 5 – 10 direct jobs for engineers, technicians, sales personnel, and administrative staff, while supporting additional indirect employment through local suppliers and subcontractors.
(5) Establish a fully operational demonstration and service center in Benin City to showcase products, provide customer consultations, and deliver after-sales support.
(6) Expand our customer base to serve households, SMEs, schools, healthcare facilities, and community organizations across Edo State and neighboring regions.
(7) Achieve a customer satisfaction rate of over 90% through quality products, professional installations, and responsive after-sales service.

These targets will position Bil-Tech as a trusted provider of renewable energy solutions, strengthen our operational capacity, and contribute to improved energy access, job creation, and sustainable economic development in Nigeria.
revenueModel:
Bil-Tech Trading and Contracting Ventures generates revenue through the sale, installation, maintenance, and servicing of solar energy systems and related electrical equipment. Our primary revenue streams include the supply of solar panels, hybrid inverters, lithium batteries, charge controllers, mounting structures, and other renewable energy components to residential, commercial, institutional, and government customers.

In addition to equipment sales, the company earns revenue from system design, installation, testing, commissioning, preventive maintenance, repair services, and annual maintenance contracts (AMCs). We also provide energy assessments and customized solar solutions tailored to each customer's power requirements.

As the business grows, Bil-Tech will expand its revenue streams by securing supply contracts, partnering with corporate organizations, government agencies, NGOs, educational institutions, and healthcare facilities, while offering long-term maintenance agreements and technical support services.

This diversified revenue model ensures recurring income, sustainable business growth, and long-term financial stability while supporting Nigeria's transition to clean and reliable energy.
socialImpact:
Bil-Tech Trading and Contracting Ventures is committed to improving access to clean, reliable, and affordable energy while contributing to Nigeria's economic growth and sustainable development.

Our business will help reduce dependence on unreliable grid electricity and fuel-powered generators by delivering renewable energy solutions to households, SMEs, schools, healthcare facilities, agricultural enterprises, and underserved rural communities. Through quality products, professional installation, customer education, and ongoing technical support, the company will accelerate the adoption of renewable energy technologies across Nigeria and contribute to a more sustainable, resilient, and inclusive economy.
sustainabilityPath:
Bil-Tech Trading and Contracting Ventures will become self-sustaining by building a diversified and recurring revenue model based on the sale, installation, maintenance, and servicing of renewable energy solutions. As our customer base grows, revenue generated from completed projects will be reinvested into purchasing inventory, expanding operations, upgrading equipment, and strengthening our technical workforce.

In addition to one-time equipment sales and installations, Bil-Tech will generate recurring income through preventive maintenance services, Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMCs), system upgrades, battery replacements, and after-sales technical support. These recurring services will provide a stable cash flow and foster long-term customer relationships.

The company will also establish strategic partnerships with reputable manufacturers, distributors, financial institutions, corporate organizations, government agencies, NGOs, and development partners to secure larger projects and improve access to competitive products and financing opportunities.

To ensure long-term sustainability, Bil-Tech will continuously invest in staff training, customer satisfaction, innovation, and operational efficiency while expanding into new markets and underserved communities. By delivering high-quality products, reliable services, and exceptional customer support, the company will build a strong reputation, generate repeat business and referrals, and achieve sustainable growth without relying on external grant funding.

startupName: GIFTED ENGINEERING SOLUTIONS: Generator Services and Technical development center
problem: Nigeria's electricity supply is improving but remains unreliable in many areas. As a result, millions of homes, businesses and institutions still rely on generators as a critical backup power source. Keeping these generators safe, efficient and reliable helps businesses stay productive, protects livelihoods and reduces unnecessary replacement costs. However, many generator owners still face challenges accessing skilled technical services, quality spare parts and reliable maintenance, leading to frequent breakdowns, higher operating costs and generators being abandoned or replaced before the end of their useful life. There is also a growing need for practical industry exposure where engineering students, SIWES interns and aspiring technicians can better understand internal combustion engines and their real-world applications.
solution:
Gifted Engineering Solutions provides reliable generator diagnosis, repairs, preventive maintenance, workshop and home services, sales of new and quality fairly-used generators, generator rentals, generator buy-back and trade-in services, generator refurbishment and restoration, and supply of genuine spare parts.

Beyond providing these services, our long-term goal is to establish a Generator Services & Technical Development Centre where customers can repair, service, buy, rent, sell and trade generators, access genuine spare parts, and receive support for petrol, diesel and industrial generating systems in one place. The Centre will also create employment opportunities for skilled technicians, provide a standard workspace for specialists, and give engineering students, SIWES interns and apprentices practical exposure to internal combustion engines, power systems and real industrial working environments.

As we grow, we will also integrate digital technology to improve customer service through digital service records, inventory management, service bookings and maintenance reminders, making our services faster, more organized and more efficient.
mvpDescription: Gifted Engineering Solutions has a working generator service model where customers can bring their generators for diagnosis, repairs, preventive maintenance and servicing, request workshop or home services, buy new and quality fairly-used generators, rent generators, trade in or sell faulty generators, and purchase genuine spare parts. The business is already serving paying customers, demonstrating a growing demand for our services. With this grant, we will expand this proven model into a standard Generator Services & Technical Development Centre with improved equipment, technology and service capacity.
tractionMetric: Our business has gained customer trust through quality service, referrals and repeat patronage. While our growth has been constrained by limited funding, equipment and operating capacity, we continue to serve new customers and see increasing opportunities to expand. This grant will enable us to meet growing demand, improve service delivery and serve more customers efficiently.
teamExpertise: Our current team consists of four members with complementary skills. I lead the business, overseeing technical operations, generator diagnosis, repairs and business development. The team also includes a Graphic Designer, a Video Editor, and an Administrative Assistant who support branding, media production and daily operations. As the business grows, we plan to expand our team by bringing in a Software Developer and creating opportunities for technicians and specialists in diesel generators, industrial generating sets, electrical rewinding and related technical fields.
challenges:
Our biggest challenge is limited capital to expand our operations and meet the growing demand for our services. While we already have a working business with paying customers, we currently lack the resources to secure a larger facility, acquire modern tools and equipment, stock more generators and genuine spare parts, and introduce digital systems that will improve service delivery. Limited funding also slows our plans to establish a Generator Services & Technical Development Centre that will create jobs, provide a standard workspace for skilled technicians, and offer practical industrial exposure for engineering students, SIWES interns and apprentices. 

This grant will help us turn these plans into reality and increase our capacity to serve more customers effectively.
fundUsage:
The ₦5 million grant will be used to expand Gifted Engineering Solutions into a more standard and efficient Generator Services & Technical Development Centre. The funding will support the acquisition of modern diagnostic tools and equipment, expansion of our workshop, stocking of quality generators and genuine spare parts, and the introduction of digital systems for customer records, inventory management, service bookings and maintenance reminders.

The grant will also enable us to increase our service capacity, create employment opportunities for skilled technicians, provide a standard workspace for specialists in related technical fields, and create practical industrial exposure for engineering students, SIWES interns and apprentices. 

This investment will strengthen our operations, improve customer experience, and position the business for sustainable growth and even impact.
growthTargets: Within the next 12 months, we will secure and equip a standard workshop, increase our stock of generators and genuine spare parts, expand our generator rental services, employ more technicians and support staff, introduce digital systems for customer records and service management, and begin practical industrial exposure for engineering students, SIWES students and apprentices. We will also begin creating a standard workspace where specialists in diesel generators, industrial generating sets and electrical rewinding can provide their services. These milestones will increase our capacity, improve customer experience and position the business for long-term growth.
revenueModel: We generate revenue from generator repairs and servicing, generator sales, generator rentals, generator buy-back and trade-in services, generator refurbishment, and the sale of genuine spare parts.
socialImpact: Gifted Engineering Solutions is more than a generator service business. Our goal is to create opportunities for people. As we grow, we will create jobs, provide a professional workspace for skilled technicians, and support practical learning for young people interested in technical and engineering careers. We also believe that business growth should benefit the community, so part of our long-term vision is to reinvest in human capital development through skills training, mentorship and other empowerment initiatives that help more people build sustainable livelihoods. As the business grows, improved equipment, better service delivery and digital systems will help us serve more customers, increase our income and improve customer satisfaction.

problem: Events by Bloom operates within the event decoration and rental industry in Benin City, a sector where demand for quality décor assets — rugs, drapes, floral installations, furniture, lighting fixtures, and props — consistently outpaces supply. A key structural challenge facing decorators in this space, including our business, is the lack of capital required to build a sufficient inventory of rental-grade items. This limitation forces reliance on last-minute third-party sourcing, which raises operating costs, compresses profit margins, and restricts the volume and scale of events that can be serviced simultaneously. Without owned inventory, business growth remains constrained to labour output alone, with no capacity to develop compounding, asset-based revenue streams or expand service offerings to other players within the industry.
solution: With adequate funding, Events by Bloom will establish an in-house inventory of essential event assets — décor fabrics, rugs, floral pieces, backdrops, lighting equipment, and furniture — for use across our own events and for rental to other decorators and event planners. This transitions the business from a purely service-based model to an asset-backed rental model, generating recurring revenue from each item beyond a single engagement. As inventory expands and rental demand grows, this will create structured employment opportunities within Edo State, including roles in dispatch and delivery, sales, and inventory/rental management. It further positions Events by Bloom as a strategic supplier within the local events industry, strengthening the broader creative economy rather than competing solely within it.

teamExpertise: Our core team brings hands-on expertise in event decoration, styling, and on-site coordination, built through direct experience delivering weddings, birthdays, proposals, corporate events, and photoshoots. This flexible staffing model has allowed us to consistently deliver across a range of event sizes and types while keeping operations lean and cost-efficient.
challenges: Our biggest challenge is limited access to capital for building an in-house inventory of essential decor and rental items (rugs, drapes, florals, furniture, lighting, and props). This forces reliance on last-minute third-party sourcing, which increases costs, limits the number of events we can service simultaneously, and restricts our ability to scale into a full rental service for other vendors.
fundUsage: The grant will be used to acquire core rental inventory — decor fabrics, rugs, floral pieces, backdrops, lighting equipment, and furniture — that will serve both our own events and generate independent rental income by supplying other decorators and event planners.
