growthTargets: Within 12 months, we aim to build a fully stocked rental inventory covering the core categories of event decor, expand our client base across weddings, birthdays, corporate events, and photoshoots, and launch a standalone rental service for other decorators and planners in Edo State — establishing a second, recurring revenue stream alongside our event services.
revenueModel: Events by Bloom operates on a dual revenue model: (1) direct service fees from event decoration and planning packages for weddings, birthdays, proposals, corporate events, and photoshoots, and (2) recurring rental income generated by leasing decor inventory — rugs, drapes, florals, furniture, and lighting — to other vendors, decorators, and event planners.
socialImpact: Events by Bloom contributes directly to the local economy by creating employment opportunities within the events and creative sector, including roles in decor, logistics, sales, and inventory management. As the business scales through an asset-based rental model, it will support other small vendors and decorators by providing them access to rental equipment, reducing their own capital barriers to entry. This strengthens the wider event services ecosystem in Edo State, keeps spending within the local economy, and creates pathways for young people to gain skills and income in a growing creative industry.
sustainabilityPath: Events by Bloom becomes self-sustaining through a dual revenue model: income from client-facing event services (weddings, birthdays, proposals, corporate events, photoshoots) and recurring income from renting decor inventory to other vendors and planners. As the rental inventory grows, it generates revenue independent of new client bookings, creating a stable, compounding income stream that funds reinvestment, staff salaries, and further inventory expansion without ongoing external funding.

If awarded the ₦5,000,000 Build Track grant, I intend to deploy the funds across four key areas that directly address the capacity constraints currently limiting Urban Hayaa's growth as a solo-run business.

problem:
Problem Statement
Many communities have limited access to essential medicines and basic healthcare services. Residents often travel long distances to purchase common medicines or seek treatment for minor illnesses. This lack of convenient access can delay treatment, increase healthcare costs, and lead to worsening health conditions.
In addition, many people practice self-medication without proper guidance, resulting in the misuse of medicines, especially antibiotics and pain relievers. The circulation of counterfeit or substandard medicines in some areas also poses a significant risk to public health.
A patent medicine store addresses these challenges by providing easy access to quality, legally approved over-the-counter medicines, basic health advice, and timely referrals to healthcare facilities when necessary. The store helps improve access to essential healthcare products, promotes the responsible use of medicines, and contributes to better health outcomes within the community.
solution:
Improves access to basic medicines by making common over-the-counter medicines available, especially in underserved areas.
Provides first aid products such as bandages, antiseptics, pain relievers, and oral rehydration salts.
Offers basic health advice on the proper use of medicines and encourages responsible self-care.
Refers serious illnesses to hospitals, clinics, or qualified healthcare professionals when treatment is beyond the store's scope.
Promotes preventive healthcare by educating customers on hygiene, nutrition, disease prevention, and healthy living.
Saves time and travel costs by providing nearby access to commonly needed medicines.
Supports treatment adherence by reminding customers to use medicines according to instructions and complete recommended courses where appropriate.

In addition to selling genuine and affordable medicines, the store will provide customers with basic advice on the proper use of medicines and refer those with serious health conditions to hospitals or qualified healthcare professionals. The business will begin with a limited range of high-demand products and expand its inventory based on customer needs and feedback. This approach allows me to test the market, serve the community effectively, and grow the business gradually while maintaining quality service.

startupName: LAURA (Location-based AI-driven Urgent Risk Alert System)
problem: Highway kidnappings, bandit attacks, and armed robberies in Nigeria often occur without warning, especially in remote areas with limited communication and security presence. Victims and witnesses have no simple way to instantly alert other road users or nearby authorities, causing more people to unknowingly drive into danger and increasing casualties. There is a critical need for an affordable, reliable, and offline early warning system that enables citizens to share real time security alerts and prevent avoidable tragedies
solution: LAURA is an AI-powered, offline emergency warning device that enables travelers to instantly broadcast distress signals during kidnappings, bandit attacks, or highway robberies. Using long-range communication technology, LAURA alerts nearby road users up to 20-25 km away, allowing them to avoid danger, seek help, and notify security agencies. By combining real-time alerts with AI-driven risk analysis and hotspot prediction, LAURA creates a citizen-powered early warning network that saves lives and improves road safety.
mvpDescription: The MVP of LAURA is a portable, battery-powered emergency alert device with a one-touch panic button and long-range offline communication (20–25 km). When activated, it instantly sends distress signals to nearby LAURA devices, warning other travelars of danger ahead. The MVP also includes a basic dashboard for viewing incident reports and identifying security hotspots.
tractionMetric: 34 paying users, ₦894,200 total revenue generated, and ₦23,800 in monthly recurring subscription revenue over the last 9 months.

problem:
Across Edo State, excessive screen time is quietly becoming one of the biggest threats to early childhood development.

More children are spending hours every day on phones, tablets and televisions instead of engaging in the activities that develop their brains during the most important years of life.

As screen time increases, many children are experiencing:

delayed language development
reduced attention span
poor social interaction
weaker creativity
limited problem-solving skills
reduced physical activity
poor school readiness

Unfortunately, many parents depend on screens because they lack affordable alternatives that keep children engaged while learning.

Teachers also face a shortage of engaging teaching resources, making classrooms heavily dependent on rote learning instead of active exploration and discovery.

The result is a growing generation of children who are entertained by screens but are not developing the foundational skills needed for lifelong success.
solution:
House of Smart Fun addresses the growing challenge of excessive screen time among young children by providing affordable, play-based learning solutions that encourage children to learn through exploration, creativity, and hands-on experiences rather than passive screen use.

Our current solution focuses on two key areas:

1. Educational Learning Kits and Toys: We curate and supply age-appropriate educational toys, puzzles, flashcards, books, and learning materials that help children develop literacy, numeracy, creativity, critical thinking, fine motor skills, and problem-solving abilities through play.

2. Parent Education: As an early childhood educator, we educate parents on the importance of play-based learning, reducing excessive screen time, and creating meaningful learning experiences at home through digital content, and practical guidance.
mvpDescription:
House of Smart Fun has successfully launched its Minimum Viable Product (MVP) by curating and selling educational learning kits and play-based resources for children aged 0–8 years. Our MVP includes educational toys, puzzles, flashcards, learning games, books, writing tablets, and other hands-on learning materials carefully selected to promote literacy, numeracy, creativity, critical thinking, and fine motor development while providing healthy alternatives to excessive screen time.

Beyond product sales, we educate parents through social media, workshops, and one-on-one guidance on the importance of play-based learning, reducing excessive screen time, and supporting children's development at home.

Since launching, we have served parents seeking engaging, educational alternatives to passive screen use and have received positive feedback on the quality and developmental value of our learning resources. These early customer interactions have validated the demand for affordable, play-based learning solutions.

This MVP has enabled us to test our business model, understand customer needs, and build the foundation for expanding into additional services such as a Toy Library, Play-Based Learning Hubs, and Teacher Training Programmes.

My background enables me to design solutions that are developmentally appropriate, practical, and relevant to the needs of children, parents, and educators.

problem:
Nigerian tertiary institutions face a severe infrastructure crisis driven by explosive student populations and inadequate physical facilities. This structural mismatch leaves millions of students locked out of high-quality, continuous learning experiences and there is a growing demand across our campuses here in Nigeria to improve and bridge overall learning outcomes with technology. 

Lecturers in our schools are currently resorting to the use of generic mass messaging platforms like WhatsApp and Telegram to distribute academic resources and organize lectures, or the use of imported video conferencing apps. However, these tools are not designed for the unique applications and in most African institutions and deeply ineffective for effective learning. Most of them require immense data bandwidth that students in remote areas or localized campus networks simply cannot afford. 

Also in the age of AI a lot of students are using AI as a supplementary learning tool, but when students turn to generic AI chatbots (like ChatGPT or Gemini) to bridge these learning gaps independently, they encounter severe limitations. These generic global models completely lack contextual awareness of localized Nigerian university syllabi, course maps, and specific lecturer requirements, often generating academically irrelevant answers or misleading hallucinations.
solution:
Sckooly Digital is a purpose-built digital learning infrastructure built explicitly for African tertiary institutions to decouple education from physical constraints.

Our ecosystem completely redefines personal and collaborative study through "Prof. Sky," an autonomous, context-guided AI tutor. Unlike generic chatbots, students do not need to understand prompt engineering. They simply upload their lecture notes, and Prof. Sky transforms raw, boring PDFs into interactive, curriculum-guided learning sessions directly tailored to their exact university syllabus and localized lecturer requirements.

To fix instructional delivery, Sckooly replaces expensive, data-heavy imported software with optimized virtual classrooms. This low-bandwidth engine allows educators to seamlessly host massive digital lectures, ensuring remote or rural institutions with poor connectivity face zero instructional downtime.

Additionally, Sckooly integrates offline-capable Computer-Based Testing (CBT) modules. Lecturers can deploy structured mock examinations that students download once and practice with entirely offline completely eliminating continuous data dependency.

By blending an AI-moderated peer community with robust local tools, Sckooly shifts higher education from fragmented chat groups into a high-concurrency, resilient digital campus ecosystem.

problem:
Edo State is one of Nigeria's agriculturally rich regions, yet much of the economic value from its palm based resources remains unrealized. Thousands of smallholder oil palm farmers continue to face low farm gate prices, limited access to structured markets, inadequate value addition, and post harvest inefficiencies that reduce their incomes and discourage youth participation in agriculture. At the same time, households, restaurants, retailers, and food processors struggle to access consistently high quality, authentic, and traceable palm based products. The market is largely fragmented, with inconsistent quality standards, limited product differentiation, weak branding, and inadequate food safety and traceability systems. Climate change further intensifies these challenges by affecting palm productivity, increasing supply uncertainty, and placing additional pressure on rural livelihoods and food security.
AfrikSec was established to address these interconnected challenges through a climate smart, farmer inclusive value chain centred on premium Red Palm Oil, Ofada Oil Sauce, and Palm Kernel Oil. By aggregating produce from smallholder farmers, applying quality driven processing and packaging, and building trusted consumer brands, AfrikSec increases the value captured within Edo State while creating reliable market opportunities for farmers. Our model promotes traceability, reduces post harvest losses, strengthens food security, preserves indigenous culinary heritage, and expands access to healthier, authentic African food products. Beyond producing food, AfrikSec is building a resilient agricultural ecosystem that empowers young people, creates sustainable livelihoods, supports climate resilient farming, and positions Edo State as a hub for value added palm based products with national and international market potential.
solution:
AfrikSec provides an integrated, climate smart solution that transforms the oil palm value chain from a fragmented commodity market into a high value, inclusive, and sustainable food ecosystem. Rather than simply producing Red Palm Oil, Ofada Oil Sauce, and Palm Kernel Oil, AfrikSec addresses the root causes of low farmer incomes, weak market access, inconsistent product quality, and limited value addition by connecting every stage of the value chain from farm to consumer.
Our solution begins with partnering with smallholder farmers through structured sourcing, capacity building, and climate smart agricultural practices that improve productivity, quality, and resilience. We aggregate raw materials, apply rigorous quality assurance and value added processing, and package premium products that meet the growing demand for authentic, traceable, and health conscious African foods. Through branded products, efficient distribution, and strategic market partnerships, we create reliable market access for farmers while delivering consistent value to households, retailers, restaurants, food processors, and institutional buyers.
AfrikSec's solution is built on five strategic pillars: (1) climate smart and regenerative sourcing, (2) farmer inclusion and market linkage, (3) value-added processing and food safety, (4) trusted branding, traceability, and market expansion, and (5) digital systems that improve supply chain visibility, inventory management, and customer engagement. This integrated model increases farmer incomes, reduces post harvest losses, strengthens food security, preserves Africa's culinary heritage, creates employment opportunities for young people and women, and builds resilient agricultural value chains that generate lasting economic, social, and environmental impact.
By transforming indigenous agricultural resources into premium, trusted brands, AfrikSec is not only producing food it is building a scalable African food ecosystem where farmers prosper, consumers trust what they eat, communities retain more economic value, and sustainable agriculture becomes a driver of inclusive growth and long term prosperity.

solution:
1. Food Waste and Post harvest Losses: Open-air sun drying frequently results in heavy produce spoilage (up to 40% for smallholder farmers in regions like Nigeria) due to slow drying times. Solar dryers accelerate the dehydration process, dramatically reducing post harvest losses.
2. Hygiene and Contamination: Open sun-drying leaves food exposed to dust, insects, birds, and animals. Enclosed solar dryers protect products from these contaminants, preventing microbial growth and the development of toxic fungi.
3. Weather Dependency: Traditional sun drying is at the mercy of the elements. Rain or high humidity can quickly introduce mold before the food finishes drying. Modern solar dryers utilize controlled airflow and closed chambers to continue drying safely regardless of fluctuating outdoor weather conditions.
4. Nutritional and Quality Degradation: Leaving food in direct, uncontrolled sunlight can strip away essential vitamins (like Vitamin C) and cause produce to fade in color and flavor. Solar dryers use controlled thermal energy to better retain original taste, color, and nutritional value.
5. Energy Costs and Environmental Impact: Artificial mechanical drying is highly energy-intensive. Using solar power as a renewable energy resource limits over dependence on conventional fuels and drastically reduces carbon emissions typically generated by food processing.
6. Market Gluts and Profitability: During peak harvest seasons, local markets often become saturated, forcing farmers to sell perishables at a loss. Solar drying allows farmers to add value to surplus crops, extending shelf life and enabling them to sell out-of-season produce at premium prices.
mvpDescription:
In the context of technology and product development, the MVP (Minimum Viable Product) of my solar drying technology is the Direct Passive Solar Dryer. It represents the most basic, functional version of a solar dryer that proves the core concept of utilizing the greenhouse effect to dehydrate food and crops.The direct passive MVP typically consists of a simple, enclosed wooden or metal frame covered with a clear plastic or glass top, which allows sunlight to enter and heat the interior air and product directly.
Key Characteristics of the MVP 
1. Direct Exposure: The produce is laid out on food-grade mesh trays inside the enclosure and exposed directly to sunlight.
2. Passive Airflow: It relies solely on natural convection—hot air rises and escapes through vents or a small chimney, drawing in fresh ambient air.
3. Low Cost: Built using locally sourced, inexpensive materials like timber, plywood, and polyethylene, keeping the initial cost extremely low.
4. Core Value Proposition: It improves significantly upon open-air sun drying by protecting the produce from external contaminants like rain, dust, birds, and insects.
tractionMetric:
1. Drying Time (hours): The total time taken to reach the safe MC compared to open sun drying. Optimized systems are typically evaluated on reducing this time by up to 20% to 50%.
2. Thermal Efficiency (η): The ratio of energy utilized to evaporate moisture versus total solar energy available. Target baselines typically fall between 20% and 40%.
3. Specific Energy Consumption (SEC): Measures the energy used to evaporate a specific unit of water (kW ⋅ h/kg or MJ/kg). Lower values indicate superior, more cost-effective designs.
4. Payback Period (years): The time required for the savings in preserved produce and reduced fossil fuel/electricity usage to cover the Solar Dryer Market capital cost, which generally ranges from 0.4 to 1.5 years.

challenges:
The primary challenges in solar drying stem from reliance on fluctuating weather, poor moisture control, and physical contamination. These factors often cause product spoilage and uneven drying. To mitigate these hurdles, modern systems utilize hybrid heating, advanced air circulation, and intelligent monitoring to ensure consistent, premium-quality yields.
1. Solar Intermittency and Weather Dependency:
The most significant limitation of solar drying is its dependence on unpredictable sunlight. Cloudy days, rainy periods, and nighttime drops in temperature stall the drying process, leaving crops vulnerable to fungal growth and microbial spoilage.
Mitigation: Integrate hybrid solar dryers that combine solar thermal power with auxiliary heat sources (such as biomass heaters or electrical elements) to maintain continuous drying. Alternatively, using Phase Change Materials (PCMs) stores excess daytime heat to be released after dark.
2. Contamination and Pest Infestation Traditional open-sun drying exposes produce to rain, dust, wind-blown debris, rodents, birds, and insects. This leads to hygiene issues and high rates of post-harvest loss.
Mitigation: Transition to enclosed structures such as solar cabinet dryers, solar dome dryers, or inflatable chambers like the Solar Bubble Dryer. These barriers keep the product hygienic while still allowing moisture to escape.3. Inconsistent Moisture Control and Non-Uniform Drying Natural convection (passive airflow) often results in an uneven distribution of heat and moisture, leading to over-dried edges and under-dried centers. This makes crops prone to later infestations during storage.Mitigation: Upgrade to active solar dryers that use solar-powered fans or blowers to enhance airflow. Introducing a cross flow of air ensures uniform moisture extraction across all product layers.
4. High Initial Investment and Fabrication Costs: 
While operational costs are virtually free, the initial expense of purchasing or fabricating commercial-grade solar drying equipment, especially automated or large-capacity models, is often cost-prohibitive for smallholder farmers.
Mitigation: Explore government grants, agricultural cooperatives, or service-based drying models where farmers pay a fee to use centralized, high-capacity commercial dryers. Utilizing locally sourced materials for construction can also significantly reduce capital expenses.

problem:
In many communities across Nigeria, women face significant challenges in accessing high-quality, affordable, and well-tailored clothing that meets their needs for work, business, social events, and special occasions. Many available fashion options are either mass-produced with poor finishing, too expensive, or fail to reflect the customer's individuality and cultural identity.
At the same time, the fashion industry has the potential to create employment and develop practical skills, yet many talented young people—especially women—lack opportunities for training, mentorship, and sustainable livelihoods within the sector.
JOSEMA was established to address these challenges by producing high-quality women's clothing that combines creativity, craftsmanship, and affordability. Beyond designing outfits, the business aims to create employment, empower aspiring fashion professionals through skills development, and contribute to the growth of the local fashion industry. With grant support, JOSEMA will expand its production capacity, reach more customers, create additional jobs, and increase access to quality fashion products while strengthening economic opportunities for women and youth.
solution:
JOSEMA provides a practical and sustainable solution by designing and producing high-quality, affordable, and stylish women's clothing that meets the diverse needs of modern women. Our product range includes ready-to-wear outfits, bridal and reception dresses, corporate wear, dinner dresses, belle (maternity) dresses, and custom designs made from Ankara, lace, and other premium fabrics.
Beyond providing quality fashion, JOSEMA is committed to empowering women and young people through skills development and employment opportunities in the fashion industry. As the business grows, we will train aspiring fashion designers, create jobs, and promote local craftsmanship while maintaining high standards of quality and customer satisfaction.
With grant support, JISEMA Fashion will invest in modern sewing equipment, expand production capacity, improve product quality, and reach more customers. This will enable us to produce more garments efficiently, create additional employment opportunities, and make elegant, affordable fashion accessible to more women across our community and beyond.
mvpDescription:
JOSEMA Minimum Viable Product (MVP) is an operational women's fashion brand that designs and produces high-quality, stylish, and affordable clothing for women in Benin City, Edo State. Our MVP has been tested through real customer orders and has demonstrated market demand through satisfied and repeat customers.
Key features of our MVP include:
A collection of ready-to-wear women's outfits.
Custom-made bridal and reception dresses.
Corporate wear for professional women.
Dinner and occasion dresses.
Belle (maternity) dresses that combine comfort with elegance.
Ankara, lace, and other fabric-based designs tailored to customers' preferences.
Personalized measurements and fitting services for custom orders.
Quality craftsmanship with attention to detail and neat finishing.
Timely production and delivery of customer orders.
Customer consultation to ensure each outfit reflects the client's style, occasion, and personality.
Our MVP has proven that there is a strong demand for fashionable, well-tailored women's clothing that combines quality, affordability, and individuality. With grant support, JOSEMA  will strengthen its production capacity, expand its ready-to-wear line, invest in modern equipment, create employment opportunities, and serve a larger customer base across Nigeria.
tractionMetric: Average transaction value: ₦35,000 per customer. We currently serve an average of 10 customers per month, generating approximately ₦350,000 in monthly revenue.
teamExpertise:
JOSEMA is led by a dedicated team of three individuals who work together to deliver high-quality women's fashion products and excellent customer service.
The founder provides the overall leadership of the business, overseeing fashion design, product development, customer relationships, business strategy, and quality control. The second team member supports garment production, including cutting, sewing, and finishing, ensuring every outfit meets our quality standards. The third team member assists with operations, customer service, measurements, order coordination, and timely delivery, helping to ensure a smooth experience for every client.
Although we are a small team, we are committed, skilled, and passionate about creating elegant women's fashion. We work collaboratively to meet customer needs, maintain high standards of craftsmanship, and grow JISEMA Fashion into a trusted and impactful fashion brand. As the business expands, we plan to recruit and train more young people, creating employment opportunities while increasing our production capacity.
challenges:
JOSEMA a growing business with strong customer demand, but its growth is limited by a lack of essential equipment and adequate workspace. Currently, I do not own key production tools such as an industrial sewing machine, dress forms (mannequins), fitting mirrors, and other essential fashion-making equipment. These limitations reduce my production capacity, affect efficiency, and make it difficult to meet increasing customer demand.
Another major challenge is the lack of a dedicated and spacious workspace. Operating in a small workspace limits the number of garments I can produce, restricts the ability to take on larger orders, and makes it difficult to train or employ additional team members.
Despite these challenges, JOSEMA Fashion continues to serve customers with quality craftsmanship and creative designs. Receiving this grant would enable me to acquire the essential equipment, establish a more suitable workspace, increase production capacity, improve efficiency, and create employment opportunities for other young people while expanding the business.
fundUsage:
JOSEMA Fashion will use the ₦5,000,000 grant to strengthen its production capacity, improve product quality, and expand its market reach. The funds will be invested in the following areas:
Purchase of production equipment: Industrial sewing machines, an overlock (weaving) machine, dress forms (mannequins), pressing equipment, cutting tables, mirrors, and other essential tailoring tools.
Workspace improvement: Secure and equip a larger, more functional workspace that supports efficient production and accommodates future staff and trainees.
Raw materials: Purchase quality fabrics, Ankara, lace, lining materials, threads, zippers, buttons, and other production supplies to increase output.
Branding and marketing: Develop professional branding materials, improve our online presence, create promotional content, and implement digital marketing to attract more customers.
Business operations: Strengthen inventory management, packaging, logistics, and other operational systems to improve customer experience.
Job creation and skills development: Recruit and train young people interested in fashion design, creating employment opportunities while expanding the business's production capacity.
This investment will enable JOSEMA to produce more garments, serve more customers, improve operational efficiency, create sustainable jobs, and build a stronger and more competitive women's fashion brand.
growthTargets:
Over the next 12 months, JOSEMA aims to achieve the following milestones:
Increase production capacity by at least 60% through the acquisition of modern tailoring equipment and a better-equipped workspace.
Serve at least 200 customers with high-quality ready-to-wear and custom-made women's clothing.
Launch an expanded ready-to-wear collection to provide customers with more affordable and readily available fashion options.
Create 3–5 new employment opportunities for young people, particularly women interested in fashion design and garment production.
Train 10 aspiring fashion designers through practical skills development and mentorship.
Strengthen our online presence by actively marketing on social media and increasing sales through digital platforms.
Increase monthly revenue by at least 50% through improved production, stronger marketing, and a growing customer base.
Build partnerships with fabric suppliers, event planners, and retailers to expand market access and improve business sustainability.
These targets will position JOSEMA for sustainable growth while contributing to job creation, women's empowerment, and the development of Nigeria's fashion industry.
revenueModel:
JOSEMA generates revenue through the design, production, and sale of women's clothing. Our primary income comes from custom-made garments, where customers pay for outfits tailored to their measurements and preferences. We also earn revenue from the sale of ready-to-wear collections, making stylish and high-quality fashion accessible to a wider range of customers.
Additional revenue is generated through the production of bridal gowns, reception dresses, corporate wear, dinner dresses, belle (maternity) dresses, and garments made from Ankara, lace, and other premium fabrics. Customers also pay for services such as alterations, fittings, and garment adjustments when needed.
As the business expands, JISEMA Fashion plans to increase revenue by growing its ready-to-wear collection, reaching more customers through online sales and social media marketing, and introducing fashion training programs for aspiring designers. This diversified revenue model will support long-term business growth and sustainability.
socialImpact:
JOSEMA is committed to creating both social and economic value by empowering women and young people through fashion. By producing high-quality women's clothing, the brand helps women express confidence, professionalism, elegance, and cultural identity while providing stylish and well-crafted outfits for different occasions.
Economically, JOSEMA contributes to local development by creating employment opportunities, supporting local fabric and accessory suppliers, and generating income within the community. As the business grows, JOSEMA will recruit and train more young people, equipping them with practical fashion design and garment production skills that can lead to sustainable employment or entrepreneurship.
With the support of this grant, JOSEMA will increase its production capacity, create additional jobs, train aspiring fashion designers, and expand access to quality women's fashion. These efforts will contribute to youth employment, women's economic empowerment, and the growth of Nigeria's fashion industry while promoting inclusive and sustainable economic development.
sustainabilityPath:
JOSEMA is building a sustainable business by generating consistent revenue through the production and sale of high-quality women's clothing. Our income comes from custom-made outfits, ready-to-wear collections, bridal and reception dresses, corporate wear, dinner dresses, belle (maternity) dresses, and garments made from Ankara, lace, and other fabrics.
The grant will enable JOSEMA to invest in essential equipment and a better workspace, allowing us to increase production, improve efficiency, and serve more customers without significantly increasing operating costs. Higher production capacity and improved product quality will lead to increased sales and stronger profitability.
To ensure long-term sustainability, JOSEMA will continue to expand its customer base through referrals, repeat customers, social media marketing, and strategic partnerships. We will also reinvest a portion of our profits into purchasing materials, maintaining equipment, developing new product collections, and growing the business.
As revenue grows, JOSEMA will be able to cover its operating expenses, create additional employment opportunities, and continue expanding without relying on external funding. This approach will enable the business to remain financially sustainable while delivering lasting social and economic impact.

problem: Our firm supplies cow and goat meat parts per kilogram to hotels, eateries, restaurants, caterers, and food vendors. However, many vendors request supply on credit and delay payment for up to two weeks or more. This ties down our working capital, making it difficult to restock, serve other customers promptly, and maintain consistent delivery. The delay also affects trust, disrupts supply, limits growth, and can lead to loss of clients in a business where freshness and timely delivery are very important.
solution: Our solution is to create a more structured meat supply system with better order management, payment tracking, and vendor control. Vendors will be encouraged to make full or part payment before delivery, while reliable customers can be managed based on their payment history. With grant support, we will increase working capital, improve packaging and storage, restock faster, and introduce digital invoices/payment reminders. This will reduce delayed payments, improve trust, ensure timely delivery, and help us serve more hotels, eateries, restaurants, caterers, and food vendors consistently.
mvpDescription: We currently supply cow and goat meat parts per kilogram to food vendors, hotels, eateries, and caterers. The business already has market demand, but growth is limited by delayed payments and insufficient working capital. Our MVP is a structured meat supply model where vendors place orders, payments are tracked, and deliveries are made based on available stock and customer demand. The next stage is to improve the system with better packaging, inventory planning, and digital payment tracking.

teamExpertise: Our team has practical experience in sourcing cow and goat meat, processing meat parts per kilogram, packaging, delivery, vendor relationship management, and basic record keeping. We understand the needs of hotels, eateries, caterers, and food vendors, especially quality, freshness, fair pricing, and timely delivery.
challenges: Our biggest challenge is insufficient working capital to meet the growing supply needs of hotels, eateries, caterers, restaurants, and food vendors. Demand is available, but we do not always have enough funds to buy, process, package, and deliver the required quantity of cow and goat meat on time. As a secondary challenge, some vendors delay payment after supply, which further ties down our capital and affects our ability to restock quickly and serve more customers consistently.
fundUsage:
We will use the ₦5M grant to improve storage, logistics, packaging, marketing, and increase our stock capacity so we can meet growing supply demand from hotels, eateries, caterers, restaurants, and food vendors.

This will help us buy more cow and goat meat stock, preserve products properly, package them hygienically, deliver faster, and serve more vendors consistently.
growthTargets: Within the next 12 months, we plan to increase our active vendor customers from about 10–15 vendors to at least 40 vendors, including hotels, eateries, caterers, restaurants, and food vendors. We also aim to grow our supply capacity to at least 800–1,000kg of cow and goat meat monthly, reduce delayed deliveries by 50%, and ensure that at least 70% of vendors make part-payment or full payment before supply. With improved stock, storage, packaging, and logistics, we target steady monthly sales growth and plan to create 5 direct jobs within the business.
revenueModel: We generate revenue by buying cow and goat meat in bulk, processing them into different meat parts, and selling per kilogram to hotels, eateries, caterers, restaurants, and food vendors. Our profit comes from the margin between the bulk purchase cost and the selling price per kilogram after processing, packaging, and delivery expenses.
socialImpact: Our business helps hotels, eateries, caterers, and food vendors access fresh cow and goat meat consistently. It supports the local food supply chain, creates jobs for meat handlers, packagers, sales support, and delivery workers, and also supports livestock/meat traders. With better supply capacity, we can help small food businesses serve their customers reliably and reduce market delays.
sustainabilityPath: The business will become self-sustaining through repeat orders from vendors, improved stock capacity, better storage, and a structured payment system. We will encourage part-payment or full payment before delivery, track vendor payments properly, and use profits from regular sales to restock continuously. By increasing our customer base and reducing delayed payments, the business can maintain steady cash flow and grow without depending on grants long-term.

problem: In Ekpoma — a busy university town home to Ambrose Alli University — students, workers, and small businesses struggle to keep up with laundry alongside their studies or jobs. Existing options are often inconsistent, slow, or require customers to drop off and pick up themselves, wasting valuable time.
solution: Clean Touch Laundry Service offers a full range of laundry care — washing, dry cleaning, ironing, and fabric/duvet care — with convenient pick-up and delivery. We combine affordable pricing with fast turnaround, saving customers time without compromising quality. Our location near GloMast Junction gives us easy access to students, professionals, and small businesses across Ekpoma.
mvpDescription: Our MVP is a fully operating laundry service offering washing, dry cleaning, ironing, and fabric/duvet care, with pick-up and delivery available. Customers can contact us via phone or WhatsApp to schedule a pickup, and we deliver clean, pressed laundry back to them — a full-service, convenience-first laundry experience.
tractionMetric: 43 customers served in our first week of operation, generating an estimated ₦85,000 in revenue — an early sign of strong demand for a full-service, pick-up-and-delivery laundry option in Ekpoma.
teamExpertise: Our team of 5 combines hands-on experience in laundry and hospitality service delivery with practical skills in customer service, logistics, and fabric care. This blend allows us to manage pickup and delivery efficiently, handle different fabric types with care, and maintain strong customer relationships — all of which contributed to serving 43 customers in our first week of operation.
challenges:
Biggest challenges right now:
We currently operate with limited washing equipment and no dryer, which means we rely on line-drying — this slows our turnaround time, especially during rainy or humid weather, and limits how many loads we can process daily. As demand grows (43 customers in our first week alone), we also face challenges with transport for pick-up and delivery across Ekpoma, and limited working capital to stock up on detergents, packaging, and ironing supplies at scale.
fundUsage:
₦1,700,000 – Industrial dryers (2 units) and an additional washing machine for our current Ekpoma location, addressing our existing drying capacity gap
₦1,300,000 – Setup of a second branch in Benin City, including basic washing/drying equipment and initial space setup, to reach a larger, underserved customer base
₦700,000 – Delivery motorbike, fuel, and maintenance to support pick-up and delivery across both Ekpoma and Benin City
₦700,000 – Working capital for detergents, packaging, and ironing supplies across both branches
₦400,000 – Branding and local marketing for the Benin City launch and continued growth in Ekpoma
₦200,000 – Staff hiring and training for the new Benin City team
growthTargets: Within 12 months, we aim to grow from 43 customers in our first week to at least 500+ active monthly customers across two locations. We plan to open a second Clean Touch branch in Benin City — Edo State's capital and largest commercial hub — extending our reach beyond Ekpoma to serve a much larger customer base, including residents, students, and small businesses across the city..
revenueModel: Clean Touch Laundry Service generates revenue through per-load and per-item pricing across our core services — washing, dry cleaning, ironing, and fabric/duvet care — with additional fees for pick-up and delivery. This pay-per-use model means revenue scales directly with customer volume, and our early traction (43 customers in week one) shows strong, recurring demand. As we expand to a second location in Benin City, we'll apply the same proven pricing model to a larger customer base, with repeat customers and referrals driving consistent, predictable monthly revenue.
socialImpact: By expanding into Benin City and growing our Ekpoma operations, Clean Touch Laundry Service will create direct employment opportunities for youth in Edo State while providing an affordable, reliable laundry solution for students, working professionals, and small businesses. Our growth also supports local economic activity by increasing demand for supplies and services from other local vendors, and frees up time for our customers to focus on work, study, and running their own businesses.
sustainabilityPath: Our revenue model is built on repeat, everyday demand — laundry is a recurring necessity, not a one-time purchase, which gives us a steady, predictable income stream. With two locations generating revenue from per-load pricing and delivery fees, combined with growing repeat customers and word-of-mouth referrals, we expect to reach profitability and cover our own operating costs within the first 6–12 months after expansion, without ongoing dependence on external funding.

problem: Many people struggle to find affordable, durable, and high-quality footwear that meets their daily needs. Mass-produced shoes are often expensive, wear out quickly, or fail to provide the right fit and comfort. At the same time, many skilled local shoemakers have limited access to larger markets and modern production methods.
solution: Our solution is to design and produce affordable, durable, and comfortable handmade footwear that meets the needs of everyday consumers. We use quality materials and skilled craftsmanship to create shoes that last longer while remaining accessible to a wide range of customers.
mvpDescription: Our Minimum Viable Product (MVP) is a small collection of durable, handmade footwear designed to validate customer demand before scaling production. The MVP includes essential shoe styles such as casual sandals, slippers, and leather shoes made with quality materials at affordable prices. Customers can place orders through social media and WhatsApp, and their feedback is used to improve product design, comfort, durability, and sizing. This approach allows us to test the market, build a loyal customer base, and refine our products while keeping production costs low.
tractionMetric: Our key traction metric is the number of pairs of shoes sold and repeat customers per month. We measure business growth by tracking monthly sales, customer retention, and referrals, which indicate customer satisfaction and increasing demand for our products.
teamExpertise: Our team combines practical shoemaking skills, customer service, and business management experience. We have expertise in footwear design, pattern making, cutting, stitching, finishing, and quality control to ensure durable, comfortable, and high-quality products. We also manage customer orders, sales, and marketing through digital platforms, using customer feedback to continuously improve our products. As the business grows, we are committed to expanding our technical skills and training more young people in modern shoemaking techniques.
challenges:
Our Biggest Challenges Right Now

Our biggest challenges are limited access to funding, which restricts our ability to purchase equipment and quality materials in bulk, and limited production capacity, making it difficult to meet growing customer demand. We also face challenges in expanding our market reach, building brand awareness, and accessing modern machinery that would improve efficiency and product consistency. Addressing these challenges will enable us to scale production, create more jobs, and serve a larger customer base.
fundUsage:
If awarded the ₦5 million grant, we will use the funds to scale our shoemaking business by investing in equipment, raw materials, and business growth. Approximately 40% will be used to purchase modern shoemaking machines and tools to increase production efficiency. 30% will be used to buy quality leather, soles, adhesives, and other raw materials in bulk to reduce production costs. 15% will be invested in marketing, branding, and expanding our online sales channels to reach more customers. 10% will be used to train and employ young people in shoemaking, creating jobs and building local skills. The remaining 5% will support business operations, logistics, and inventory management.

This investment will enable us to increase production capacity, improve product quality, serve more customers, and create sustainable employment opportunities.
growthTargets:
Growth Targets for the Next 12 Months

Over the next 12 months, we aim to increase our monthly production and sales by at least 100%, expand our customer base through online and offline marketing, and introduce new footwear designs to meet different customer needs. We plan to strengthen our brand presence, establish partnerships with retailers and distributors, and improve customer retention through consistent product quality and excellent service. We also aim to create 3–5 new jobs, train young people in shoemaking skills, and build a sustainable business that is ready to scale into new markets.
revenueModel:
Revenue Model

Our business generates revenue primarily through the sale of handmade footwear, including sandals, slippers, and leather shoes, to individual customers and retail businesses. We also earn income from custom-made orders tailored to customers’ preferences. As the business grows, we plan to expand our revenue streams by supplying footwear to wholesalers and retailers, offering bulk orders for schools and organizations, and providing paid shoemaking training programs for aspiring artisans.
socialImpact:
Social/Economic Impact

Our shoemaking business creates social and economic value by producing affordable, durable, and high-quality footwear while generating employment opportunities for young people. Through skills training and mentorship, we help aspiring shoemakers gain practical experience that can lead to sustainable livelihoods and self-employment. By sourcing materials locally where possible, we support local suppliers and contribute to the growth of the local economy. As the business expands, we aim to reduce unemployment, increase household incomes, and make quality footwear more accessible to our communities.
sustainabilityPath:
Path to Sustainability

Our path to sustainability is built on consistent product quality, customer satisfaction, and disciplined financial management. We will reinvest a significant portion of our profits into expanding production capacity, purchasing quality materials in bulk, and improving our equipment. By strengthening our brand, growing our customer base through online and offline sales channels, and developing long-term partnerships with retailers and distributors, we will generate steady revenue. problem:
Every evening, when the sun goes down in many poor communities across Edo State, another struggle begins.

Many parents know they may not have light for the night. Children try to read with dim lamps or phone flashlights, while others give up because there is no light at all. Small shop owners close early because they cannot keep their businesses open in the dark. A dead phone can mean missing a customer, a job opportunity, or an important call from a loved one.

People often say, "Buy a generator." But for many families, that is not realistic. Fuel is expensive, and even when they own a generator, they cannot afford to run it every day. Some parents must choose between buying fuel and buying food for their children.

Power cuts do more than switch off the lights. They interrupt learning, reduce income, create fear at night, and make everyday life harder for families already struggling to make ends meet.

Many of these families do not need a large and expensive solar system. They need a simple, affordable, and reliable source of electricity that can keep the lights on, charge a phone, run a fan, and give them one less thing to worry about each day.
solution:
Solar Pad Mini was created with one simple dream: no family should have to choose between light and food.

It was born from a simple question: Why should a child stop dreaming just because the lights went out?

For many families, another power outage means another difficult night. It means a child closing their books before they are ready because darkness has filled the room. It means a mother trying to care for her children without light. It means a father missing a customer's call because his phone battery has died. It means another evening spent worrying about whether there is enough money for fuel or for tomorrow's meal.

Solar Pad Mini exists to change that story.

Instead of asking struggling families to spend their last money on petrol or pay to charge their phones every few days, Solar Pad Mini captures the sunlight that shines freely every day and turns it into clean, reliable electricity. It gives families something many have not had for a long time which is peace of mind.

With one portable unit, a child can finish homework after sunset. A market woman can keep her stall open a little longer. A student can prepare for an examination. An elderly person can sleep with a fan on a hot night. A family can charge their phones, light their home, and stay connected even when the national grid fails.

Solar Pad Mini is not just a solar device. It is a second chance for children to learn. It is extra hours of income for hardworking parents. It is relief for families who have lived with the daily uncertainty of power outages. It is dignity for people who deserve better than choosing between darkness and debt.

Because electricity should not be a privilege. It should be the light that gives every family the opportunity to learn, earn, grow, and hope for a better tomorrow.
mvpDescription:
The Solar Pad Mini MVP is the first working version of our product. It is a portable solar power system built to provide reliable electricity for families and small business owners who experience frequent power outages.

The MVP consists of a 100W solar panel, a 12V 20Ah battery, a 150W inverter, a charge controller, safety fuses, USB charging ports, and AC power outlets, all enclosed in a compact, portable box that is easy to carry and use.

During the day, the solar panel captures energy from the sun and stores it in the battery. When there is a power outage, users can safely power essential devices such as LED lights, mobile phones, small fans, laptops, and small televisions. The system is designed to be simple enough for anyone to operate without technical knowledge.

This MVP will be used to test the product's performance, reliability, affordability, and ease of use with real users. Feedback from households and small business owners will help improve future versions of Solar Pad Mini before large-scale production.

The goal of the MVP is to prove that a simple, portable, and affordable solar solution can give families dependable access to electricity for their most important daily needs, reducing their dependence on fuel generators and unreliable grid power.
tractionMetric:
Our main traction metric is the number of people who test Solar Pad Mini and the number of pre-orders we receive.

Our first goal is to build a working Solar Pad Mini and let families and small business owners use it. We will collect their feedback to understand what works well and what needs improvement.

We will also measure how many people want to buy the product after seeing a demonstration. This will help us confirm that Solar Pad Mini solves a real problem and that people are willing to pay for it before we produce more units.
teamExpertise:
We are two passionate co-founders with a strong desire to solve the energy challenges faced by low-income families and small businesses.

One co-founder has a background in Electrical and Electronics Engineering, with knowledge of electrical systems, power solutions, and energy technology. The other co-founder has a background in Mechanical Engineering, bringing skills in product design, building structures, and creating durable solutions.

We both have training and certifications in renewable energy, giving us the technical knowledge needed to design and develop clean, affordable, and reliable energy solutions.

Coming from a background where unreliable electricity is a daily struggle, we understand this problem personally. We have seen how power outages affect families, students, and small business owners — from children struggling to study at night to people losing opportunities because they cannot depend on electricity.

This is not just a problem we want to solve; it is a problem we understand. Our combined engineering skills, renewable energy knowledge, and personal experience with this challenge drive us to build Solar Pad Mini into a solution that gives families access to reliable power, dignity, and better opportunities.
challenges:
Our biggest challenge right now is moving Solar Pad Mini from a working MVP into a solution that can reach the families who need it most.

We have successfully developed our first working prototype, but we need more support to carry out wider testing, improve the product design, source quality components at a lower cost, and prepare for larger production and make it affordable enough for low-income families and small business owners.


Another challenge is reaching more families and small business owners who need affordable and reliable electricity solutions. We want to collect more user feedback, understand their needs better, and continue improving Solar Pad Mini based on real-life use.

With funding, mentorship, and the right support, we can move from a working MVP to a product that can reach more underserved communities and help more people access reliable electricity.

The funding will be used to purchase high-quality solar panels, batteries, inverters, charge controllers, and other components needed to manufacture more Solar Pad Mini units. We will improve the design and build additional units for testing.

A key part of the grant will be used to carry out user testing in both urban and rural communities. We will place Solar Pad Mini in real homes and small businesses, collect feedback from users, and observe how the product performs in different environments and weather conditions. Part of the grant will also be used for product certification, branding, packaging, and setting up a small-scale production process to ensure every unit is safe, reliable, and affordable.

Our goal is to use this funding to move beyond one working prototype and deliver a product that can improve everyday life for families, students, and small business owners who struggle with unreliable electricity.

socialImpact:
Social Impact: Solar Pad Mini will improve the quality of life for low-income families by providing reliable electricity for lighting, studying, and communication. It will reduce the use of petrol generators, helping to lower exposure to smoke and noise, which can contribute to better health and a safer home environment.

Over time, we plan to expand into other states in Nigeria and eventually other underserved communities across sub-Saharan Africa, using the same community-based distribution model. This approach will help Solar Pad Mini remain affordable, accessible, and financially sustainable while creating lasting social impact.

problem:
MEDNAV Problem Statement

Students in many Nigerian universities face significant challenges in accessing reliable health information and timely medical support. Many are unaware of nearby healthcare facilities, emergency contacts, blood donation services, mental health resources, and basic first-aid procedures. During medical emergencies, students often waste valuable time searching for information online or relying on inaccurate advice from friends and social media.

In addition, students struggle to find trustworthy academic medical resources for courses such as Anatomy, Physiology, Biochemistry, and related health sciences. Existing information is scattered across multiple platforms, making learning and healthcare navigation inefficient.

The absence of a centralized, student-focused digital health platform contributes to delayed healthcare decisions, poor health awareness, inadequate emergency preparedness, and increased academic stress. There is a growing need for an accessible, reliable, and easy-to-use solution that combines healthcare navigation, emergency assistance, mental health support, educational resources, and blood donor information in one platform.

MEDNAV addresses this gap by providing a comprehensive digital health companion designed specifically for students, empowering them to make informed health decisions, access emergency support quickly, and improve their overall well-being.
solution:
MEDNAV Solution

MEDNAV is a comprehensive digital health platform designed to make healthcare information and support easily accessible to students. It serves as a one-stop solution that connects students with trusted health resources, emergency services, and educational materials, helping them make informed decisions about their health and well-being.

The platform enables users to locate nearby healthcare facilities, access emergency contact numbers, learn essential first-aid procedures, connect with blood donors when needed, and monitor their mental well-being through self-assessment tools and wellness resources. MEDNAV also provides a curated library of reliable learning materials for medical and life science students, including subjects such as Anatomy, Physiology, Biochemistry, and related disciplines.

By bringing these essential services together in a single, user-friendly platform, MEDNAV reduces the time spent searching for reliable health information, improves emergency preparedness, promotes preventive healthcare, supports students' academic success, and encourages healthier lifestyles across university campuses.

MEDNAV's mission is to ensure that every student has quick, reliable, and affordable access to the health information and support they need—anytime, anywhere.
mvpDescription:
MEDNAV Minimum Viable Product (MVP)

The MEDNAV MVP is the first functional version of the platform, built to solve students' most urgent healthcare and academic needs with a simple, easy-to-use interface. It focuses on delivering core features that provide immediate value while allowing room for future expansion.

The MVP includes:

- A searchable directory of nearby hospitals, clinics, pharmacies, and emergency healthcare services.
- Quick access to emergency contact numbers such as ambulance, police, fire service, and university health centres.
- A first-aid guide containing step-by-step instructions for managing common emergencies before professional help arrives.
- A mental wellness section with self-assessment tools, stress management tips, and links to professional support services.
- A blood donor directory that helps users find compatible donors during emergencies.
- A medical learning hub with curated notes, videos, and educational resources for students studying health-related courses.
- User accounts that allow students to save useful resources and personalize their experience.

The MVP is designed to validate the need for an all-in-one student health platform, gather user feedback, and demonstrate that MEDNAV can improve access to healthcare information, emergency preparedness, and medical education within university communities.
tractionMetric:
Key Traction Metrics

Since MEDNAV is an early-stage startup, traction will be measured by user adoption, engagement, and impact. The key metrics include:

- Student registrations: Number of students who create accounts on the platform.
- Monthly Active Users (MAU): Number of users actively using MEDNAV each month.
- Healthcare resource usage: Number of searches for hospitals, pharmacies, emergency contacts, and first-aid information.
- Learning resource engagement: Number of educational resources viewed or downloaded.
- Blood donor connections: Number of successful donor requests or matches facilitated through the platform.
- User retention rate: Percentage of users who return to use MEDNAV after their first visit.
- University partnerships: Number of institutions, student associations, or health centres collaborating with MEDNAV.
- User satisfaction: Ratings, feedback scores, and testimonials indicating the platform's usefulness and reliability.

These metrics will demonstrate MEDNAV's adoption, user engagement, and real-world impact while guiding future product improvements and growth.
teamExpertise:

Economically, MEDNAV creates employment opportunities for young professionals, campus ambassadors, and technology talent while supporting partnerships with healthcare providers and educational institutions. By reducing delays in accessing healthcare and promoting preventive care, MEDNAV also helps lower health-related costs for students and contributes to a more productive and resilient youth population.
sustainabilityPath:

As our user base grows, these revenue streams will support ongoing platform development, operational costs, and expansion to more campuses. By balancing commercial partnerships with free core services, MEDNAV will remain financially sustainable while continuing to deliver accessible, high-quality healthcare support to students.

startupName: LAURA (Location Alert Unit for Risk Awareness)
problem: Highway kidnappings, bandit attacks, and armed robberies in Nigeria often occur without warning, especially in remote areas with limited communication and security presence. Victims and witnesses have no simple way to instantly alert other road users or nearby authorities, causing more people to unknowingly drive into danger and increasing casualties. There is a critical need for an affordable, reliable, and offline early warning system that enables citizens to share real time security alerts and prevent avoidable tragedies.
solution: LAURA is an AI-powered, offline emergency warning device that enables travelers to instantly broadcast distress signals during kidnappings, bandit attacks, or highway robberies. Using long-range communication technology, LAURA alerts nearby road users up to 20–25 km away, allowing them to avoid danger, seek help, and notify security agencies. By combining real time alerts with AI-driven risk analysis and hotspot prediction, LAURA creates a citizen-powered early warning network that saves lives and improves road safety.
mvpDescription:
The MVP of LAURA is a compact, portable emergency alert device that allows users to send an instant distress signal during kidnappings, bandit attacks, or highway robberies. The device features a single panic button, long-range offline communication (20–25 km), LED and buzzer alerts, and rechargeable battery power.

When the panic button is pressed, the device broadcasts an emergency signal to other nearby LAURA devices, warning approaching travelers of danger ahead and giving them enough time to turn back, seek assistance, or notify security agencies.

The MVP will also include a basic web dashboard that displays reported incidents, alert history, and a simple risk map. Initial AI capabilities will focus on identifying recurring hotspots and analyzing patterns in reported incidents to support future predictive security features.

The primary goal of the MVP is to validate three key assumptions:
1. Reliable long-range offline communication between devices.
2. User willingness to adopt and carry the device.
3. The effectiveness of community-driven early warnings in preventing additional victims.

problem: Africa's rich cultural heritage is under threat from deterioration, theft, conflict, environmental damage, and limited digital preservation. Many historical artifacts, sculptures, monuments, and cultural sites remain inaccessible to researchers, educators, museums, game developers, and the global public due to a lack of high-quality digital documentation. This creates a significant gap in cultural preservation, education, and the digital creative economy. AfroArt Studios addresses this challenge by using advanced 3D scanning, photogrammetry, and digital asset creation to preserve African cultural heritage while making it accessible for research, education, virtual exhibitions, gaming, film, and other digital applications.
solution: AfroArt Studios preserves Africa's cultural heritage by creating accurate, high-quality digital replicas of artifacts, monuments, and historical sites using advanced 3D scanning and photogrammetry. We transform physical cultural assets into detailed digital models that can be archived, studied, shared, and used in education, museums, virtual exhibitions, gaming, film, VR/AR, and 3D printing. By combining cultural preservation with modern digital technology, we ensure that Africa's history remains accessible to future generations while unlocking new opportunities for research, tourism, and the creative economy.
mvpDescription:
AfroArt Studios' MVP is a functional digital heritage platform that combines a virtual museum with a growing library of high-quality 3D-scanned African artifacts. Visitors can explore curated museum spaces through an immersive web-based virtual tour while interacting with authentic digitized cultural objects. The platform also enables users to view, license, and download selected 3D assets through online marketplaces, demonstrating demand for digital cultural heritage in education, research, gaming, film, and virtual exhibitions. The virtual museum is hosted online using CloudPano's immersive 360° tour technology, allowing visitors to explore exhibits from any internet-connected device. 

Current MVP capabilities:

Interactive web-based virtual museum showcasing African cultural heritage.

Collection of high-quality photogrammetry-based 3D artifact scans.

Online catalog of downloadable 3D assets via Fab, Sketchfab, and CGTrader.

Commercial licensing of digital heritage assets.

problem:
Small businesses, freelancers, students, and early-stage entrepreneurs in Nigeria often struggle to access affordable business support. They rely on multiple disconnected tools for bookkeeping, customer management, invoicing, inventory tracking, project management, and business advice. Professional consultants are often expensive or inaccessible, while existing software solutions are either too complex, designed for foreign markets, or lack localized business guidance.

As a result, many businesses make poor financial decisions, fail to maintain proper records, miss growth opportunities, and spend valuable time on administrative work instead of building their businesses.

There is currently no unified AI-powered platform that combines business management, intelligent automation, and access to verified business experts within a single ecosystem designed for African entrepreneurs.
solution:
IVIE is an AI-powered Business Operating System that serves as a virtual business consultant and operational assistant. Through a conversational AI interface, users can manage finances, track sales, monitor inventory, organize projects, generate invoices, maintain customer relationships, receive business insights, and access verified consultants when specialized expertise is required.

Unlike traditional business software, IVIE allows users to interact in natural language. The AI understands business context, performs tasks across multiple modules, provides proactive recommendations, and intelligently connects users with qualified consultants or service providers whenever human intervention is necessary.

The long-term vision is to build a complete business ecosystem where AI, automation, and professional services work together to help businesses start, operate, grow, and scale efficiently.
mvpDescription:
The current MVP is a functional web application that demonstrates IVIE's core business management capabilities. Users can create an account, complete role-based onboarding, interact with an AI business assistant, manage finances, record sales, maintain inventory, manage customers, organize projects, and explore a business directory.

The application includes AI-powered conversational interactions, role-based dashboards for entrepreneurs, freelancers, students, and corporate users, consultant handoff functionality, and a scalable architecture designed for future AI integrations.

The MVP validates the core concept of using conversational AI as the primary interface for business management while demonstrating how multiple business operations can be connected within a unified platform.
tractionMetric: The primary traction achieved to date is the successful development of a working MVP that validates the product concept and demonstrates AI-powered business management across multiple user personas. The platform has progressed from concept to a functional prototype with clearly defined product architecture, scalable system design, and readiness for pilot deployment and user acquisition.
teamExpertise: Our team combines expertise in product design, business development, entrepreneurship training, software architecture, and business process improvement. We have practical experience supporting entrepreneurs and SMEs through employability and entrepreneurship programmes, business advisory services, digital transformation initiatives, and product design. This combination enables us to build technology that addresses real business challenges rather than purely technical problems.
challenges: Our primary challenges include expanding the MVP into a production-ready platform, integrating advanced AI capabilities, conducting extensive user testing, acquiring early customers, strengthening backend infrastructure, and onboarding verified consultants to support the human expert ecosystem. Limited funding also constrains product development speed, cloud infrastructure, AI API usage, security implementation, and marketing activities.
fundUsage:
The grant will be allocated strategically to accelerate product development and market readiness:

• 35% – Software engineering, backend development, AI integration, and platform architecture.

• 20% – Cloud infrastructure, AI model usage, hosting, security, and development tools.

• 15% – UI/UX refinement, product testing, and quality assurance.

• 10% – User research, pilot programmes, and customer onboarding.

• 10% – Marketing, branding, and business development.

• 5% – Legal, compliance, and business registration requirements.

• 5% – Operational expenses and contingency.

This investment will enable us to launch a production-ready MVP, validate product-market fit, and prepare IVIE for commercial scale.
growthTargets: Within the next 12 months, we aim to successfully launch the production version of IVIE, onboard over 5,000 registered users, establish a network of more than 200 verified consultants and service providers, achieve recurring subscription revenue, launch the consultant marketplace, introduce embedded AI capabilities for external businesses, and validate product-market fit through continuous customer feedback and measurable business outcomes.
revenueModel: IVIE operates a diversified SaaS and platform business model. Revenue will be generated through monthly and annual software subscriptions, premium AI features, consultant marketplace commissions, featured business listings, enterprise licensing, embedded AI subscriptions, API usage, professional consulting services, training programmes, and strategic partnerships with organizations serving entrepreneurs and SMEs.
socialImpact: IVIE aims to democratize access to quality business support for entrepreneurs, freelancers, students, and small businesses across Nigeria and Africa. By providing affordable AI-powered business guidance and connecting users with verified experts, the platform will improve business survival rates, encourage formalization of SMEs, increase financial literacy, promote digital adoption, create employment opportunities for consultants and technology professionals, and contribute to sustainable economic development within the entrepreneurial ecosystem.
sustainabilityPath: IVIE is designed as a scalable recurring-revenue platform. Long-term sustainability will be achieved through subscription income, marketplace commissions, enterprise partnerships, embedded AI licensing, API monetization, and value-added services. As the consultant ecosystem and user base expand, network effects will strengthen customer retention and reduce acquisition costs, creating a sustainable business model with multiple recurring revenue streams.

problem: Across Africa, businesses face increasing pressure to improve customer service, reduce operational costs, and deliver faster services. However, most organizations, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), still rely on manual processes for customer support, administrative tasks, and workflow management. Existing AI chatbot solutions are often limited to answering questions and cannot securely interact with business systems to perform real tasks such as processing requests, updating records, scheduling appointments, or automating internal workflows. This gap prevents businesses from fully benefiting from artificial intelligence, leading to inefficiencies, slower service delivery, higher operational costs, and limited scalability. There is a growing need for accessible, affordable, and intelligent AI solutions that not only understand user requests but can also autonomously execute business processes through secure integration with existing digital systems.
solution: Nexus Botix is an autonomous AI platform that enables businesses to automate customer interactions and business operations through intelligent AI agents. Unlike traditional chatbots that are limited to answering questions, our platform combines conversational AI with workflow automation, allowing AI agents to understand requests, make decisions, and securely execute tasks across existing business systems. Through seamless integration with enterprise applications, databases, communication platforms, and third-party services, Nexus Botix enables businesses to automate processes such as customer support, admissions, appointment scheduling, order management, lead generation, and internal workflows. The platform is designed with a no-code approach, making advanced AI automation accessible to businesses without requiring specialized technical expertise. By reducing manual work, improving operational efficiency, and enabling businesses to scale their services, Nexus Botix empowers organizations across Africa to accelerate their digital transformation through affordable and intelligent AI automation.
