problem:
Many churches, campus fellowships, ministries, and faith-based organizations in Edo State still manage their operations manually using notebooks, WhatsApp messages, Excel sheets, paper attendance records, and verbal reports.

This manual system makes it difficult to manage members, track attendance, monitor departments and units, plan events, approve budgets, record income and expenses, and generate accurate reports. As these organizations grow, leaders often struggle with scattered information, delayed communication, poor financial transparency, missing records, and administrative stress on volunteers.

In many fellowships and churches, finance officers, secretaries, pastors, presidents, and unit heads work with disconnected tools, making it hard to know what is happening across the organization in real time.

Gatherly is solving this problem by providing a simple SaaS platform that helps churches and fellowships digitize member management, attendance, events, finances, budgets, approvals, notifications, departments, units, and reports in one organized system.
solution:
Gatherly is a SaaS platform that helps churches, campus fellowships, ministries, and faith-based organizations manage their operations digitally from one simple dashboard.

The platform provides tools for member management, attendance tracking, events, departments, units, finance records, budget requests, approvals, notifications, and reports. Instead of using notebooks, WhatsApp chats, Excel sheets, and paper records, leaders can manage their organization in a more organized, transparent, and accountable way.

With Gatherly, pastors, presidents, secretaries, finance officers, unit heads, and department leaders can easily access the information they need, track activities, monitor finances, approve requests, and generate reports.

The solution reduces administrative stress, improves communication, strengthens financial accountability, and helps faith-based organizations make better decisions with accurate data. Gatherly is designed to be simple, affordable, and easy to use for both small and growing churches or fellowships in Edo State and beyond.
mvpDescription:
Our MVP is a working version of Gatherly that allows churches, campus fellowships, ministries, and faith-based organizations to manage their basic operations digitally.

The MVP includes user registration and login, organization onboarding, role-based dashboards, member management, departments and units, attendance tracking, event management, finance records, budget requests, approval workflows, notifications, and basic reports.

Different users such as pastors, presidents, secretaries, finance officers, unit heads, department leaders, and members can access the platform based on their assigned roles. This ensures that each person only sees the features and information relevant to their responsibility.

The finance module allows leaders to record income and expenses, track budget requests, monitor approvals, and improve financial accountability. The attendance and event modules help organizations track participation and plan activities better.

The MVP is designed to prove that faith-based organizations can move from scattered manual records to one simple digital system that improves administration, transparency, communication, and reporting.
tractionMetric:
Our key traction metric is the number of active churches, campus fellowships, and faith-based organizations onboarded and using Gatherly to manage their operations.

This metric is important because it shows real adoption, not just interest. We will track how many organizations register, complete onboarding, add members, assign roles, record attendance, create events, submit budget requests, and use the finance/reporting features.

Our first-year traction target is to onboard at least 100 faith-based organizations in Edo State, with a focus on campus fellowships, small churches, and growing ministries in Benin City. We will also track active monthly usage, number of members managed on the platform, attendance records created, budget requests processed, and finance reports generated.

This will help us measure whether Gatherly is solving a real administrative and accountability problem for faith-based organizations.

marketer

problem: Classic-Lens Photography operates in a highly competitive photography industry where customers expect convenient online booking, quick communication, easy access to portfolios, and timely delivery of photographs. However, the business relies heavily on manual processes for client inquiries, appointment scheduling, payment tracking, and record management. This often leads to delays, booking conflicts, inefficient customer service, and difficulty in managing growing client demands.
solution:
The solution to the challenges facing Classic-Lens Photography is the development and implementation of an integrated photography management system. The system will automate key business processes such as online client registration, appointment scheduling, booking management, payment processing, photo gallery management, and customer communication.
The platform will also provide an online portfolio where potential clients can view previous work, select photography packages, request quotations, and make bookings from any location. In addition, it will include an administrative dashboard for managing customers, bookings, payments, staff schedules, and business reports.
mvpDescription:
The Minimum Viable Product (MVP) for Classic-Lens Photography is a web-based platform that provides the essential features needed to enable customers to discover, book, and interact with the photography business online while allowing the administrator to manage operations efficiently.
The MVP includes the following core features:
User Registration and Login – Customers can create accounts, log in securely, and manage their profiles.
Photography Portfolio – A gallery displaying previous photography work categorized by events such as weddings, birthdays, portraits, and corporate events.
Online Booking System – Clients can book photography sessions by selecting a date, time, location, and preferred service package.
Photography Packages – Customers can view available services, pricing, and package details before making a booking.
Contact and Inquiry Form – Visitors can send inquiries or request quotations directly through the platform.
Admin Dashboard – The administrator can manage bookings, customers, photography packages, and portfolio images from a centralized dashboard.
Booking Confirmation – Customers receive confirmation after successfully submitting a booking request.
Responsive Design – The platform is optimized for desktops, tablets, and mobile devices to ensure easy access from any device.
This MVP focuses on delivering the core functionality required to improve customer experience, streamline booking management, and establish a strong online presence for Classic-Lens Photography. Additional features such as online payment integration, customer reviews, automated reminders, live chat, and photo download portals can be incorporated in future versions based on user feedback and business growth.
tractionMetric:
The key traction metric for Classic-Lens Photography is the number of successful online bookings per month. This metric directly measures customer adoption of the platform and indicates whether the business is attracting and converting visitors into paying clients.
Other supporting traction metrics include:
Monthly active users (MAU): Number of customers who visit and interact with the platform each month.
Booking conversion rate: Percentage of website visitors who complete a photography booking.
Customer retention rate: Percentage of clients who return for additional photography services.
Revenue generated from online bookings: Total income earned through bookings made via the platform.
Customer satisfaction rating: Feedback and reviews provided by clients after each photography session.
Among these, successful online bookings per month is the primary traction metric because it best reflects the growth, effectiveness, and commercial success of Classic-Lens Photography.
teamExpertise:
Team Expertise (5 Members)
1. Photographer
The photographer is responsible for capturing high-quality images during events, studio sessions, and outdoor shoots. They are skilled in camera operation, composition, lighting techniques, and client interaction to produce creative and professional photographs.
2. Photo Editor
The photo editor enhances and retouches images using professional editing software such as Adobe Photoshop and Adobe Lightroom. Their expertise includes color correction, image enhancement, skin retouching, background editing, and preparing final images for print and digital delivery.
3. Lighting Engineer
The lighting engineer designs and manages lighting setups for both studio and outdoor photography. They ensure proper illumination, minimize shadows, and create the desired mood and visual effects to achieve high-quality photographs.
4. Makeup Artist
The makeup artist prepares clients for photography sessions by applying professional makeup that complements the shoot's theme, lighting, and camera settings. They help clients look their best while ensuring makeup remains flawless throughout the session.
5. Sound Engineer
The sound engineer manages audio equipment during video productions, interviews, and event coverage. They ensure clear, high-quality sound recording, reduce background noise, and synchronize audio with video during post-production.
Together, this multidisciplinary team combines expertise in photography, photo editing, lighting, makeup artistry, and audio production, enabling Classic-Lens Photography to deliver professional photography and multimedia services that meet clients' expectations.
challenges:

High Competition: Competing with many established photography studios and freelance photographers offering similar services.
Limited Brand Visibility: Reaching new customers and building a strong online presence requires continuous marketing efforts.
Seasonal Demand: Bookings tend to fluctuate, with peak periods during weddings, graduations, and festive seasons, and lower demand during off-peak periods.

problem: My mother has lived with diabetes for over eight years, and I watched her struggle with a question millions of Nigerians ask every day: "Can I safely eat this meal?" Despite following medical advice, there was no simple way to know how familiar Nigerian foods would affect her blood sugar or how to make them safer. Most diabetes nutrition apps focus on Western foods, while local resources are often static meal plans that cannot assess the meal someone is about to eat. As a result, people are left guessing portion sizes, food combinations, and healthier alternatives, leading to preventable blood sugar spikes, fear of eating familiar foods, and poor diabetes management. This gap highlights the need for an accessible, personalized solution built specifically for Nigerian diets.
solution: GluFloat is a web-based platform that helps people living with diabetes make informed food choices before they eat. Users can search for individual Nigerian foods or build an entire meal and instantly receive a simple green, yellow, or red safety rating based on its likely impact on blood sugar. The platform also provides recommended portion sizes, healthier food pairings, meal frequency guidance, and practical suggestions to improve a meal rather than eliminate it. Built specifically for Nigerian diets, GluFloat replaces guesswork with personalized, easy-to-understand guidance, empowering people to enjoy the foods they love while managing their diabetes with greater confidence. Here is the link to the MVP: glufloat.vercel.app
mvpDescription: GluFloat's MVP is a live, browser-based web application that helps people living with diabetes evaluate Nigerian meals before they eat. Users can search from a growing database of over 250 Nigerian foods or build a complete meal to receive an instant green, yellow, or red safety rating. The platform also provides recommended portion sizes using visual guides, healthier food pairings, meal frequency recommendations, and practical suggestions to improve a meal instead of avoiding it. The MVP is already functional, accessible without downloading an app, and operates on a subscription model with a 7-day free trial.
tractionMetric: My key traction metric is product readiness. I have built a fully functional MVP with a curated database of over 251 Nigerian foods, featuring food search, meal analysis, portion guidance, and personalized recommendations. I am currently validating the platform with registered dietitians before the public launch to ensure accuracy, strengthen the product, and build user trust.
teamExpertise: I am the sole founder of GluFloat. I have a background in pharmacy, which gives me a strong understanding of diabetes management, nutrition, and medication use. I combined this healthcare knowledge with AI-powered development tools to design and build GluFloat from concept to a working MVP, including defining the product, developing its features, and curating a database of Nigerian foods. To ensure the platform is scientifically accurate and trustworthy, I am currently working with registered dietitians to validate the food database and recommendations before launch.
challenges: As a solo founder, my biggest challenge is securing the resources needed to move from a validated MVP to a trusted, scalable product. I am currently funding development myself while working with registered dietitians to validate the food database and recommendations before launch. I also need funding to complete regulatory and data protection requirements, grow awareness among people living with diabetes, and continue expanding the platform's features and Nigerian food database.
fundUsage: If awarded the ₦5 million grant, I will use it to prepare GluFloat for a successful public launch and early growth. The funding will support the clinical validation of the food database and recommendations by registered dietitians, completion of regulatory and data protection compliance, and continued product development, including new features such as barcode scanning and saved meals. It will also fund user acquisition through targeted marketing and partnerships with healthcare professionals and diabetes communities, while expanding the Nigerian food database and improving the platform based on user feedback. These investments will help transform GluFloat from a validated MVP into a trusted digital health solution for people living with diabetes.
growthTargets: Over the next 12 months, I aim to publicly launch GluFloat, onboard at least 2,000 registered users, and convert a minimum of 500 into paying subscribers. I also plan to expand the Nigerian food database from over 251 foods to more than 500, complete clinical validation by registered dietitians, introduce new features such as barcode scanning and saved meals, and establish partnerships with hospitals, diabetes clinics, pharmacies, and healthcare professionals to drive user adoption and trust.
revenueModel: GluFloat operates on a subscription-based revenue model. Users receive a 7-day free trial before subscribing for ₦1,500 per month to access personalized meal analysis, food safety ratings, portion guidance, and nutrition recommendations. As the platform grows, I plan to introduce annual subscription plans to improve customer retention and predictable recurring revenue. Additional future revenue opportunities include partnerships with healthcare providers, corporate wellness programs, and premium nutrition services.
socialImpact: GluFloat improves health outcomes by helping people living with diabetes make safer food choices before they eat, reducing preventable blood sugar spikes and increasing confidence in managing their condition. By providing guidance tailored to Nigerian foods, the platform empowers users to maintain healthier eating habits without giving up the meals they love. Over time, this can contribute to better diabetes management, lower healthcare costs associated with preventable complications, and improved quality of life. Economically, GluFloat will create skilled jobs, support healthcare professionals through partnerships, and contribute to the growth of Nigeria's digital health industry.
sustainabilityPath: GluFloat is designed to be financially sustainable through a recurring subscription model. After a 7-day free trial, users pay ₦1,500 per month for continued access to personalized meal analysis and diabetes nutrition guidance. As the user base grows, recurring subscription revenue will fund product improvements, customer support, and expansion of the Nigerian food database. I also plan to introduce annual subscription plans, establish partnerships with healthcare providers and corporate wellness programs, and offer premium nutrition services, creating multiple revenue streams that support long-term growth and impact.

problem:
Nigeria’s agricultural and aquaculture sectors hold immense potential but remain trapped in systemic inefficiencies that limit productivity, profitability, and sustainability. Smallholder farmers and aquaculture operators — who produce over 70% of the country’s food — consistently capture only 15-25% of the final market value due to fragmented value chains, high post-harvest losses (often exceeding 40%), poor coordination between formal and informal markets, and weak traceability systems.

These challenges are particularly acute in aquaculture and fisheries, where the absence of a credible Self-Reporting Tool (SRT) has led to prolonged export bans (notably to the United States) despite Nigeria’s vast water resources and production capacity. Farmers face high input costs, limited market access, climate vulnerabilities, and inadequate cold chain logistics, resulting in massive economic leakage, food insecurity, and environmental degradation.

Traditional interventions have largely been siloed, technology-light, and extractive in nature — failing to address the root issue: the lack of a coordinated, sovereign market infrastructure that integrates real-time data, intelligent orchestration, and regenerative principles across the entire value chain.

This structural coordination gap prevents smallholders from accessing premium markets, fair pricing, and regenerative premiums, keeping them in a cycle of poverty while Nigeria continues to import over $1 billion worth of fish annually.

UMEI® was designed to solve this foundational problem by creating an integrated sovereign regenerative market operating system that connects ground-truth sensing, AI orchestration, immutable records, and participatory governance — enabling abundance circulation as the default economic logic.
solution:
Durandel Limited is building UMEI® (Universal Market Ecosystem Infrastructure) — Africa’s first sovereign regenerative market operating system that modernizes agricultural and aquaculture value chains by addressing the core problem of fragmented, extractive market infrastructure.

UMEI® is a complete layered platform consisting of:
- Sovereign Stack (Foundation Layer): Real-time ground-truth data from SQR Nanocam (multispectral + thermal edge sensors), sovereign agentic AI orchestration (Oria), immutable memory (Duralake), contribution-weighted identity (Docudd), and participatory governance (PAMIE).
- Utility Platform Modules: Grand (Global Commerce Registry), Noble (Sovereign Credit Scoring), Squared (Regenerative Logistics), Pamiefund (Tokenized Asset Marketplace), and Tor AI (Secure Privacy-Preserving Communication).

This integrated system enables verifiable calculation of the Regenerative Surplus Index (RSI) and Gross Regenerative Surplus (GRS), unlocking Regenerative Premiums and fair value distribution to participants.

CORE INNOVATION – THE AQUADUR INITIATIVE
We are deploying a fully integrated regenerative aquaculture solution that includes:
- PEAS (Probiotics-Enabled Aquaculture System) – “No Water Change” fish farming technology
- Regenerative Aquaculture Sanctuaries (RAS)
- Live Aquaculture Transport-as-a-Service (LATAAS)
- Live Aquaculture Storage-as-a-Service (LASAAS)

Supported by the Self-Reporting Tool (SRT) for export compliance and DuraGel Processing System for value addition and rapid ROI.

MVP DESCRIPTION
The Minimum Viable Product (MVP) of UMEI® (Universal Market Ecosystem Infrastructure) is a functional, integrated sovereign regenerative market system focused on aquaculture and crop value chains, ready for initial deployment on the Abidjan-Lagos Economic Corridor by Q4 2026.

Sovereign Stack Foundation
- Perception Layer: Deployable SQR Nanocam units (multispectral + thermal edge sensors) for real-time ground-truth data collection on farms and ponds.
- Intelligence Layer: Oria AI agentic orchestration engine capable of basic regenerative optimization and decision support.
- Memory Layer: Duralake immutable ledger for secure, tamper-proof recording of transactions and regenerative metrics.
- Identity Layer: Docudd sovereign identity system with contribution-weighted profiles.
- Governance Layer: PAMIE participatory governance module enabling community review and decision-making.

Key Utility Modules (Partially Activated)
- Squared: Regenerative logistics engine integrated with SQR Nanocam and SQR Tracker.
- Grand: Commerce registry and basic settlement functionality.
- Noble: Initial contribution-based credit scoring.
- Pamiefund: Basic tokenization and Regenerative Premium distribution.

Flagship Application – Aquadur Initiative

LATAAS & LASAAS – Live transport and storage-as-a-service logistics.
DuraGel Processing – Value-addition units for premium product creation.
SRT (Self-Reporting Tool) – Simulated and ready for pilot testing to support export compliance.

1) Real-time data collection and RSI calculation on at least 50 pilot sites.
2) Functional end-to-end flow from sensor → AI optimization → transaction recording → premium distribution.
3) Measurable improvement in productivity and income for 5,000+ smallholders.

This MVP represents a complete, sovereign, and operational market infrastructure layer that can be scaled corridor-wide and eventually continent-wide.

FEATURES
The UMEI® MVP is a functional, integrated sovereign regenerative market platform focused on aquaculture and crop value chains. It combines hardware, software, and governance tools to deliver immediate, practical value to users while laying the foundation for full-scale deployment.

Traceability & Compliance (Grand + SRT)

2) End-to-end traceability from pond/farm to market.
3) Simulated Self-Reporting Tool (SRT) for fisheries export compliance readiness.

Market Access & Value Circulation (Pamiefund + Grand)
1) Access to Regenerative Premium pricing for certified produce.
2) Transparent transaction recording and basic settlement.
3) Early tokenized co-ownership and dividend distribution mechanisms.

Participatory Governance (PAMIE)
1) Community members can participate in decision-making through simple mobile/web interfaces.
2) Contribution-weighted voting on cooperative matters.


What Users Can Do with the MVP
- Smallholder Farmers & Aquaculture Operators: Monitor their ponds/farms in real time, receive AI-driven optimization advice, reduce losses, and earn Regenerative Premiums on certified produce.

The MVP transforms users from isolated producers into active participants in a coordinated, regenerative market system — giving them better data, better decisions, better prices, and measurable regenerative impact.

revenueModel:
Durandel’s revenue model for UMEI® is a hybrid, multi-stream approach built on hardware infrastructure, platform services, and regenerative ecosystem participation. It is designed for strong unit economics, recurring revenue, and scalability as the network grows.

The model rests on three interconnected pillars:

Hardware & Edge Infrastructure Revenue
This includes the sale and deployment of SQR Nanocam units (multispectral + thermal sensors) and associated edge devices (SQR Tracker). Revenue will come from direct unit sales to cooperatives and individual operators, bundled starter kits for new clusters, and recurring income from calibration, maintenance, and hardware upgrades. This stream provides critical early-stage cash flow while creating a locked-in base of connected devices that feed the broader platform.

Platform Subscription & Intelligence Services
Once the Sovereign Stack and Oria AI are live, we will charge recurring subscriptions for access to core platform capabilities. This includes real-time technical assistance, regenerative optimization recommendations, market coordination support, RSI/GRS analytics, and traceability reporting. Aquaculture operators and farmer cooperatives will subscribe based on the number of ponds/farms monitored and the depth of AI-driven insights and logistics support they receive. This creates predictable, high-margin recurring revenue that grows with user adoption and usage intensity.

Regenerative Premium & Ecosystem Transaction Fees
The highest-margin and most scalable stream. Through Pamiefund, we earn a share of the Regenerative Premium (the additional market price paid for verified “Regenerative Origin” products). We also collect transaction fees on tokenized assets, dividend distributions, and value chain settlements processed via Grand. As more participants join and more volume flows through the network, this becomes a powerful flywheel — higher regenerative performance leads to higher premiums, which drives further adoption and network effects.

Overall Strategy
In the first 12–18 months, hardware sales and early platform subscriptions will dominate. From month 18 onward, ecosystem transaction fees and Regenerative Premium shares are expected to become the largest contributors as the network scales. The model is engineered for 65–80% gross margins at scale due to the high fixed-cost nature of the core infrastructure and low marginal cost of additional users.

This diversified, regenerative-first revenue model ensures commercial sustainability while directly aligning incentives with the creation of measurable regenerative surplus for smallholders, cooperatives, and the broader ecosystem.

sustainabilityPath:

Projected Break-Even & Profitability

The ₦5M grant serves as catalytic capital to reach critical mass — after which UMEI® becomes a self-reinforcing, commercially viable sovereign infrastructure platform capable of scaling across Nigeria and other AfCFTA corridors without further donor dependency.

This sustainability model ensures long-term impact while maintaining full African ownership and control of the infrastructure.

Nigeria faces growing challenges of food insecurity, post-harvest losses, low agricultural productivity, and youth unemployment. Smallholder farmers, who produce the majority of the country's food, often lack access to modern farming techniques, quality inputs, value addition opportunities, and reliable markets. As a result, a significant portion of harvested produce is wasted, farmers earn low incomes, and consumers experience rising food prices.

In Edo State, these challenges are compounded by the effects of climate change, including unpredictable rainfall, increased pest outbreaks, and declining soil fertility, which reduce crop yields and threaten livelihoods. Many young people are discouraged from pursuing agriculture because it is perceived as labor-intensive, unprofitable, and lacking innovation.
Pearls Max Agro Enterprise was established to address these challenges by promoting sustainable, climate-smart agriculture, reducing post-harvest losses through value addition and processing, and creating profitable opportunities for farmers and young entrepreneurs. Our goal is to build a more resilient agricultural value chain that improves food security, increases farmers' incomes, creates decent jobs, and contributes to the economic development of Edo State.

problem:

Academic records, attendance, assessments, and communication are often managed manually, resulting in delayed interventions, inefficient decision-making, and poor accountability.

Without access to real-time education data, school leaders struggle to identify at-risk students, teachers lack actionable insights to personalize learning, parents have limited visibility into their children's progress, and policymakers cannot accurately allocate resources or measure the effectiveness of educational interventions.

The absence of an integrated education data infrastructure contributes to persistent learning gaps, increased dropout rates, inefficient school management, and missed opportunities to improve educational outcomes at scale.

solution:
EduLedga is an AI-powered Education Operating System (EduOS) that digitizes and connects every aspect of school administration, learning, and education data management within a single intelligent platform.

The platform enables schools to manage student records, attendance, assessments, report cards, communication, and academic performance while providing teachers, parents, and administrators with real-time insights into student progress. Beyond school management, EduLedga leverages artificial intelligence and learning analytics to identify at-risk students, support early interventions, and improve learning outcomes.

For education authorities, EduLedga provides a centralized education intelligence layer that aggregates anonymized data across schools to support evidence-based policymaking, resource allocation, and system-wide performance monitoring. Planned capabilities include predictive analytics, geospatial school planning, school quality benchmarking, and AI-powered decision support aligned with global education standards.

problem: Because buying imported cars has become too expensive, there is an unprecedented surge in demand for affordable, reliable, locally used ("Nigerian-used") vehicles. tractionMetric:
Inventory Turnover Velocity (Days to Sale): The average number of days it takes from the moment a vehicle is purchased to the moment it is sold (Target: under 21–30 days).
 Net Profit Margin per Flip: The percentage of pure profit made on each vehicle after deducting purchase price, detailing, and minor repair costs (Target: 15% – 20%).
 Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC): The total amount spent on digital ads (WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram) to secure one buying customer (Target: Low, keeping marketing lean).

problem:
Managing a school is hard work. Every single year, a school creates thousands of records. This includes things like new student forms, daily attendance, staff details, test scores, and notes sent to parents.

1. The Price Barrier to Technology: Current digital school software is too expensive for low-to-mid-tier community schools, with prices ranging from ₦80,000 to ₦120,000 yearly. Because of this high cost, schools choose to stay with traditional, inefficient methods.

​2. High Reliance on Paper Files: Research shows that 88% of sampled schools still use traditional paper filing systems for daily tasks. This leads to heavy administrative overhead, duplicate work, and massive delays in sharing data between school departments.

​3. Loss of Vital Academic History: Because schools rely on paper, student academic records get damaged, torn, wet, or lost over time. This makes it hard or impossible for past students to get transcripts or report cards later in life.
​
4. Broken Systems and Communication Gaps: Schools use separate, disconnected tools like simple spreadsheets, paper logs, and random chat apps. This creates major communication gaps between teachers, parents, and school heads, while stealing valuable time away from helping children learn.
solution:
At TrosAl, we believe every school deserves access to modern technology, not just those with big budgets. That's why we've built a highly efficient cloud platform that keeps costs low, making it possible for even community schools to leave paper behind and embrace digital management without breaking the bank.

We also believe a school's history should never be lost. That's why we protect every student's academic journey by securely storing school records in the cloud. Whether it's needed next year or decades after graduation, the information remains safe, intact, and easy to retrieve.

We know how frustrating it is when the same information has to be entered repeatedly or important records are scattered across different places. We've brought admissions, records, communication, and everyday school operations together into one connected platform. With everything in one place, we help schools save time, reduce mistakes, and spend less energy on administration and more on educating students.

We also know that great education happens when schools and families work together. That's why we've created a secure bridge between parents and educators, giving families timely access to their children's progress while keeping sensitive student information protected. 

Our goal is simple: help schools build stronger relationships with parents through communication they can trust.
mvpDescription:
The TrosAl MVP (Minimum Viable Product) is a highly affordable, secure, multi-tenant school management platform. It uses a single global account system that allows users to manage multiple roles and switch between different school workspaces seamlessly.
School Administrator (The System Controller)

1. Creator and Admin 
​The MVP gives Admins full operational oversight to run the school digitally, moving away from slow paper files.
​What they can do: Register the school on the platform, manage institutional settings, and assign predefined roles. They use the Smart Invitation Engine to search for users via email or username and send secure onboarding links to staff, students, and parents.

2. Teacher (The Academic Operator)
​The MVP removes duplicate paperwork so teachers can focus entirely on helping children learn.
​What they can do: View assigned courses, record student assessments, and manage grades. High-priority student test scores are strictly encrypted at the database level the moment the teacher enters them, keeping academic histories perfectly secure and private.

3. Form Teacher / Class Teacher (The Classroom Manager)
​Form teachers get specialized tools to track and oversee an entire specific classroom or grade level.
​What they can do: Access their specific classroom dashboard to log daily student attendance and manage basic student files. They act as the primary bridge for data collection, updating classroom records that sync instantly across the school's single source of truth.

4. Parent / Guardian (The Progress Monitor)
​Parents are directly brought into the school ecosystem to protect their children and track performance.
​What they can do: Receive and accept onboarding invites for their children. For children under 13, the parent manages a Managed Account, fills out their child's profile form, and is automatically linked as the official parent. They can then monitor real-time grades and attendance logs across present and past terms.

5. Student (The Learner Workspace)
Students get a clean, simple dashboard to track their learning journey based on their age bracket.
What they can do:
Underage Students (Under 13): Log in using a unique username to access a restricted space showing only their current school courses, attendance, and grades.
Standard Students (13+): Receive invites directly, complete their own onboarding forms, link up to 4 parents/guardians to their profile, and switch contexts to view both current and past academic histories.

revenueModel:

1. Advertising
We will display carefully selected, non-intrusive advertisements within the platform for users on the free plan. This allows schools to access essential features at little or no cost while generating revenue to support the platform.

Schools and individual users can choose an ad-free experience.

- School Ad-Free Plan: When a school subscribes, advertisements are removed from that school's workspace for all users. Users may still see ads when accessing workspaces belonging to schools that are not subscribed.
- Individual Ad-Free Plan: Users can subscribe personally to reduce or completely remove advertisements from their own experience, regardless of the school's subscription status, depending on the plan they choose.

problem: Book readers are tired of scrolling social media to find their next read. solution: Booktrovert is a book tracker and recommendation app that matches readers to their next book based on the emotional and narrative qualities of what they've already loved not just the genre. problem:

Additionally, the market is saturated with products that are either too expensive, inconsistent in quality, or formulated with harsh chemicals that may cause skin irritation and other health concerns when used frequently.

At the same time, there is a growing demand for affordable, effective, and safer household cleaning products that meet consumers' expectations for quality and convenience. However, access to such products remains limited for many low- and middle-income households, creating a gap in the market for reliable and cost-effective cleaning solutions.
solution:
Glary Choice Ventures International Limited provides an affordable, high-quality multipurpose liquid soap designed to meet a wide range of household and commercial cleaning needs with a single product. Our product effectively cleans dishes, floors, tiles, bathrooms, and other washable surfaces, helping customers reduce the cost and inconvenience of purchasing multiple cleaning products.

Our multipurpose liquid soap is formulated to be tough on grease, stains, and dirt while remaining gentle on users' hands when used as directed. By combining effectiveness, affordability, and convenience, we enable households and small businesses to maintain clean and hygienic environments without compromising on quality.

It is suitable for cleaning dishes, floors, tiles, bathrooms, sinks, countertops, and other washable surfaces, allowing customers to use one product for multiple cleaning tasks instead of purchasing several different cleaners. This saves users money, reduces storage needs, and simplifies their cleaning routine.

Since launching the MVP, we have validated market demand through sales and customer feedback. We have built a base of over 30 repeat customers, with approximately 80% of our customers making repeat purchases, demonstrating strong customer satisfaction and product acceptance. We currently produce 50 litres monthly and generate average monthly sales of ₦50,000–₦80,000.

Customer feedback has helped us continuously improve our product formulation, packaging, and user experience. These results confirm that our MVP effectively addresses a genuine market need and provides a strong foundation for scaling production, obtaining certification, and expanding into larger retail and institutional markets.

problem:
Finding trusted service providers is still harder than it should be.

Today, most people rely on friends, family referrals, WhatsApp groups, Facebook posts, and random online listings to find professionals such as plumbers, electricians, cleaners, beauticians, laundry services, and other skilled workers. This process is often time-consuming, unreliable, and lacks transparency.

Customers struggle to verify quality, availability, pricing, and trustworthiness before hiring, while many skilled service providers struggle to gain visibility and attract consistent customers.

As a result, customers waste time searching, experience missed appointments and poor service, and professionals miss opportunities to grow their businesses.

Oniix solves this problem by providing a centralized platform where users can discover, verify, and book trusted professionals quickly and confidently, powered by AI-assisted search and streamlined booking experiences.
solution: Oniix is a trusted marketplace that connects customers with verified service providers. Through AI-powered search, users can quickly find, compare, and book professionals across multiple service categories, while providers gain visibility and new business opportunities.
mvpDescription:
### MVP (Minimum Viable Product)

Oniix's MVP is an AI-powered marketplace that connects customers with trusted service providers across multiple service categories.

The initial version focuses on solving the core problem of service discovery and booking through a simple, reliable experience.

**Customer Features**

* User registration and authentication
* AI-powered service search
* Browse service categories
* View provider profiles
* Ratings and reviews
* Service booking
* Booking management
* Notifications and updates

**Service Provider Features**

* Provider registration
* Profile creation
* Portfolio uploads
* KYC verification
* Service category selection
* Availability management
* Booking requests
* Customer reviews

**Core Categories**

* Beauty & Wellness
* Cleaning
* Plumbing
* Electrical
* Laundry
* Tailoring
* Home Repairs

**Key Differentiator**
Unlike traditional directories or social media referrals, Oniix uses AI-powered search to help users describe their needs in natural language and quickly discover relevant, verified professionals.

The MVP validates three core assumptions:

1. Customers want a faster way to find trusted professionals.
2. Service providers need better visibility and customer acquisition.
3. AI-assisted discovery improves the service booking experience.

The primary goal of the MVP is to establish marketplace liquidity by onboarding customers and service providers while validating demand for AI-powered service discovery and booking.
tractionMetric: Our primary traction metric is the number of verified service providers onboarded to the platform. We are focused on building supply across key service categories while growing customer demand and bookings.
teamExpertise:
Our team combines expertise in software engineering, product development, and marketplace operations.

We have experience building web and mobile applications using modern technologies, with a strong focus on creating scalable, user-friendly products. Our background includes full-stack development, mobile engineering, cloud infrastructure, AI integration, and product design.

Beyond technical execution, we have firsthand experience with the problem we're solving. We've experienced the challenges of finding reliable service providers and understand the operational realities faced by both customers and professionals.

This combination of technical capability and deep market understanding allows us to build a platform that addresses real user needs while creating value for service providers. As we grow, we plan to expand the team with expertise in marketplace growth, operations, partnerships, and customer success.
challenges:
As an early-stage marketplace, our biggest challenge is building marketplace liquidity—growing both the supply of service providers and the demand from customers at the same time.

We're currently focused on onboarding quality service providers, increasing user awareness, and driving consistent bookings across our key service categories. Building trust is also a major priority, as customers need confidence that the professionals they discover are reliable and qualified.

In addition, we're continuously improving our AI-powered discovery experience to help users find the right service providers faster and more accurately. Our goal is to create a marketplace where finding and booking trusted professionals is as simple as ordering food or requesting a ride.

growthTargets:
Over the next 12 months, our focus is on establishing Oniix as a trusted platform for discovering and booking professionals while building strong marketplace liquidity.

Our targets are:

* Onboard 5,000+ verified service providers across multiple service categories.
* Reach 50,000+ registered users.
* Facilitate 10,000+ service bookings through the platform.
* Expand coverage across major cities in Nigeria.
* Improve AI-powered search and matching accuracy.
* Achieve strong customer retention through repeat bookings and provider trust.

Success for us is not only measured by user growth, but by creating a reliable marketplace where customers can confidently find professionals and providers can consistently generate business opportunities.
revenueModel:
Oniix operates a marketplace business model with multiple revenue streams designed to scale as the platform grows.

**1. Booking Commissions (Primary Revenue Stream)**
Oniix earns a percentage commission on successful bookings completed through the platform.

**2. Featured Listings**
Service providers can pay for increased visibility and priority placement within search results and category listings.

**3. Provider Subscriptions (Future)**
Premium plans will offer additional tools such as enhanced profiles, analytics, lead management, booking insights, and business growth features.

**4. Advertising & Promotions**
Businesses and service providers can promote their services to targeted users within the platform.

**5. Value-Added Services (Future)**
Additional revenue opportunities include verification services, business tools, payment processing services, and AI-powered business assistance for professionals.

Our initial focus is on driving bookings and marketplace activity, with commissions serving as the primary monetization strategy while we build marketplace liquidity and user trust.
socialImpact:
Oniix creates social and economic impact by improving access to income opportunities for service professionals while making trusted services more accessible to consumers.

For service providers, Oniix helps increase visibility, attract new customers, and generate more consistent income. Many skilled professionals rely heavily on referrals and word-of-mouth marketing, limiting their growth potential. Oniix provides a digital platform that helps them reach a larger audience and build sustainable businesses.

For consumers, Oniix reduces the time, uncertainty, and risk involved in finding reliable professionals by providing a trusted and transparent discovery and booking experience.

As the platform grows, we aim to:

* Create income opportunities for thousands of service professionals.
* Support small business growth and entrepreneurship.
* Promote digital inclusion among informal service providers.
* Improve trust and transparency within the service economy.
* Contribute to job creation and economic activity across multiple sectors.

Our long-term vision is to become the infrastructure that connects people with opportunities, making services more accessible while empowering professionals to grow their businesses.
sustainabilityPath:
Oniix will become self-sustaining through a combination of marketplace commissions, premium provider services, and business tools.

Our primary revenue stream will be commissions earned from successful bookings completed through the platform. As more customers and service providers join Oniix, transaction volume increases, creating a scalable revenue model.

In addition, we plan to introduce premium subscription plans for service providers, offering enhanced visibility, business analytics, lead generation tools, profile promotion, and customer management features.

As the platform matures, additional revenue opportunities will include featured listings, advertising, verification services, and AI-powered business tools for professionals.

Our strategy is to first build trust, marketplace liquidity, and user engagement, then scale revenue through recurring and transaction-based income streams. This creates a sustainable business model that grows alongside the success of both customers and service providers.

problem:
G2G Delivery App solves the problem of unavailable, unreliable and inefficient delivery systems for individuals and businesses within Edo state. G2G Delivery App is a technology-driven logistics platform designed to simplify last-mile delivery for businesses, small merchants, and individual customers. The platform connects customers who need delivery services with verified riders through a mobile application, creating a fast, reliable, and affordable logistics ecosystem.
In Benin city, Edo state, and across Nigeria, small businesses and e-commerce vendors face significant challenges with delivery process. These challenges include unreliable dispatch riders, lack of real-time tracking, high delivery costs, poor accountability, delayed deliveries, and difficulty managing multiple orders. These inefficiencies often lead to lost sales, dissatisfied customers, and operational bottlenecks for businesses that rely on timely product distribution.
G2G Delivery App addresses these problems by providing a centralized digital platform that allows users to request deliveries instantly, track the packages in real time, and manage logistics operations efficiently. Through the app, customers can schedule deliveries, monitor rider location, receive delivery confirmations, and ensure transparency throughout the entire delivery process.
Our target customers include e-commerce businesses, restaurants, pharmacies, grocery stores, and individuals who require same-day or scheduled deliveries. Small and medium-sized businesses benefit from cost-effective logistics that help them scale, while individuals enjoy the convenience of sending packages, documents, and gifts quickly and safely.
solution:
G2G Delivery App provides a technology-driven logistics and business automation platform that enables businesses and individuals to access fast, reliable, and secure last-mile delivery services. The platform addresses the challenges of unreliable dispatch services, lack of accountability, fluctuating costs, delayed deliveries, poor inventory management, and manual record-keeping by connecting users with verified riders through a centralized mobile application.
Through G2G, customers can request deliveries, monitor rider locations in real time, receive digital proof of delivery using One-Time Password (OTP) verification which prevents cases of item theft and failed deliveries. Customers enjoy transparent, standardized pricing based on delivery distance and size of goods, thereby eroding inconsistent pricing. Our rider verification, performance rating, and accountability systems promote professionalism while reducing the risk of theft, package mishandling, and delivery disputes. To further protect users, G2G provides insurance coverage for eligible deliveries, minimizing financial losses arising from unforeseen incidents such as accidents or damaged goods.
Beyond logistics, G2G Delivery App equips businesses with digital tools to improve operational efficiency. Businesses can automatically generate electronic receipts for every completed transaction, maintain real-time inventory records without manual bookkeeping, and gain better visibility into sales and stock movement. This eliminates paper-based processes, reduces administrative workload, and provides business owners with accurate records.
The platform operates a decentralized rider marketplace that matches delivery requests with the nearest available rider, significantly reducing pickup times and improving delivery efficiency. By combining secure logistics, transparent pricing, inventory bookkeeping, digital receipting, and real-time delivery tracking in a single platform, G2G helps businesses reduce operating costs, improve customer satisfaction, increase productivity, and scale more efficiently while giving individuals a dependable way to send packages safely and affordably.

problem: 1 in 2 patients in Nigeria leave a pharmacy without their complete prescription, not because the medicine does not exist but because no system exists to tell them which nearby pharmacy has it. Pharmacists manage this gap informally through WhatsApp groups with no guarantee of response. This information failure causes treatment interruption, medicine rationing, preventable hospitalisations, and death. PharmaStackX witnessed this firsthand when a colleague died because one injection could not be located in Benin City despite being available around the corner.
solution: PharmaStackX is a real-time medicine discovery network that syncs live pharmacy inventory and connects patients and pharmacists instantly. An autonomous desktop agent called Synkk automatically syncs each pharmacy’s stock to the PSX network without disrupting existing operations. Patients and pharmacists can search for any medicine and find which nearby licensed pharmacy has it in real time. A WhatsApp AI pipeline classifies and broadcasts medicine requests instantly.
mvpDescription:
PharmaStackX is a live production platform not a prototype. It consists of three components. 
First, a web platform at psx.ng where patients search for medicines and pharmacies and pharmacists in a city-wide radius gets notification and respond instantly. 
Second, Synkk, an autonomous desktop agent installed on pharmacy computers that automatically syncs live inventory from any existing pharmacy software using machine learning, computer vision, and network interception. 
Third, a WhatsApp AI pipeline that identifies medicine requests in pharmacist group chats and broadcasts them to nearby pharmacists on the network in real time.
tractionMetric: Pharmacy onboarding rate
teamExpertise:
Osakpolor Ogiemudia - Founder and CEO. Licensed pharmacist with a Doctor of Pharmacy. Former WHO Field Officer who supervised vaccination of over 100,000 individuals in Delta State. Former Regulatory Pharmacist at NAFDAC. Built the entire PSX platform including Synkk, the WhatsApp AI pipeline, and the medicine classification engine. 

Joy - Co-Founder and Head of Growth. Leads community engagement, pharmacy relationship management, and growth strategy. Responsible for pharmacist onboarding support, customer success, and brand communications across PharmaStackX’s pharmacy network.
challenges:
Field onboarding capacity is our primary bottleneck. Converting warm leads into installed paying pharmacies is constrained by time and logistics.

Technical integration complexity is our second challenge. Every pharmacy in Nigeria uses a different point-of-sale system -VirtualRx, Moniebook, Smapp, or custom software. Synkk’s autonomous agent handles most cases but each new POS type requires investigation and configuration time that takes the founder away from sales and growth.

Notification infrastructure is our third challenge. PharmaStackX currently operates without a dedicated mobile app, which limits how effectively we can deliver real-time medicine request notifications to pharmacists. Pharmacists miss time-sensitive requests because push notifications require an app. Our current WhatsApp pipeline partially bridges this gap but it is not a scalable long term solution. Building a lightweight pharmacist mobile app is a near-term technical priority.

Revenue conversion speed is our fourth challenge. Pharmacies agree verbally but payment collection and full installation sometimes takes multiple visits. A dedicated Customer Success function would close this gap significantly.

socialImpact:
PharmaStackX directly addresses medicine access failure across Edo State. Every pharmacy onboarded increases medicine discoverability for the surrounding community. Every patient who finds their medicine through PSX avoids rationing doses, travelling between pharmacies, delaying treatment, or abandoning prescriptions entirely.

The platform addresses documented public health gaps. Nigeria accounts for 27% of global malaria deaths. 1 in 3 Nigerian adults has hypertension with less than 1 in 10 under control. Sickle cell disease affects 150,000 Nigerian children born annually. In every case consistent medicine access is the gap between manageable and catastrophic health outcomes.

Beyond health outcomes, PharmaStackX creates digital infrastructure for Edo State’s pharmacy sector. Pharmacies gain online visibility, social media presence, inventory analytics, and access to a growing patient network. This strengthens the economic viability of community pharmacies and keeps essential health services accessible in areas they might otherwise exit due to commercial pressure.

problem: Nigeria imports over $1 billion in dairy annually while losing 40% of local soyabeans to post harvest spoilage. The root cause is unreliable energy , most food processors depend on diesel or an unstable grid, meaning crops rot before they can be processed. Meanwhile, 30% of Nigerian children suffer from vitamin A deficiency, and rural families cannot afford imported fortified foods. This is a broken system where farmers lose income, families pay high prices for imported milk, and children go without essential nutrition. Sambal Enterprise was built to fix this.
solution: Sambal Enterprise is a solar powered food manufacturer that processes local soybeans into fortified, affordable SoyaMilk Powder. Our modular solar hub runs 100% off grid, eliminating diesel costs and grid dependence. We buy directly from smallholder farmers at premium prices, process their soybeans into nutritionally fortified powder, and convert 100% of processing waste into organic fertilizer for farmers. Our SoyaMilk Powder is blended with Nigerian dates and real vanilla , which is lactose free, cholesterol free, omega 3 rich, and fortified with vitamins A, D, and B complex. It is CAC, SMEDAN , SON, FDA, and NEPC certified, available in 250g, 500g retail packs, 10kg/50kg B2B bulk, and soon in affordable 50g sachets. We are creating a circular economy that reduces import dependency, creates jobs for women, and delivers affordable nutrition to low income families.
mvpDescription: Our MVP is a fully operational solar powered processing hub located in Egor LGA, Edo State, Nigeria. It runs on a modular solar PV system with battery storage, enabling 24/7 off grid production. The hub includes food grade milling, drying, and packaging equipment, along with smart sensors for real time monitoring of energy consumption, temperature, humidity, and production metrics. An integrated anaerobic biodigester converts 100% of organic processing waste into  organic fertilizer. The hub produces certified SoyaMilk Powder.  Our MVP proves that solar powered, circular food manufacturing is viable, profitable, and scalable in the Nigerian context.

revenueModel:
The way the business makes money is through a few connected areas that all revolve around footwear and foot health.
First, a big part of the income comes from making custom shoes. People place orders for footwear that fits their style and comfort needs, and that’s one of the main ways money comes in.

Then there’s shoe repair and cleaning. Instead of people throwing away old shoes, they bring them in to be fixed or cleaned, and they pay for that service. This creates steady and repeat income.

There’s also training. People who want to learn shoemaking or start their own small footwear business pay to be trained, and that adds another stream of income.

As the brand grows, there’s also room for things like partnerships, special collections, and awareness programs around foot health that can be sponsored or paid for.
The income doesn’t come from just one thing. It comes from making shoes, fixing shoes, teaching skills, and building services around foot health.
socialImpact:
The impact of our brand is both social and economic and it shows up in real, practical ways in people’s lives.
On the social side, it helps people understand foot health and why proper footwear matters. A lot of discomfort and long-term foot issues come from wrong shoe choices, so this awareness alone makes a difference. Through training and outreach, people also learn shoemaking and business skills they can actually use to build something for themselves.

On the economic side, it creates opportunities for people to earn income. Some are directly employed, while others go through training and start small businesses on their own, like shoe repair or small footwear production. It also supports local suppliers and others in the value chain, because more production means more demand for materials and services.

We are big on helping people live more comfortably, learn valuable skills and create ways to earn a living around footwear and foot health.
sustainabilityPath:
Sustainability for us is really about building something that can keep running and growing without depending too much on outside support.

The business earns from different areas making custom shoes, repairing and cleaning shoes, and training people. So even if one part is slow, the others keep the business stable.

A big part of it is also training people. Instead of everything staying within one workshop, people are taught shoemaking and entrepreneurship so they can go on to create their own income or support production. That way, the impact spreads and keeps multiplying.

There is also the creative hub, which is like the heart of innovation. It’s where new designs are created, where ideas are developed into real products, and where young creatives and artisans can learn and collaborate. It helps the brand stay fresh and continuously improve.

Another important part is using waste materials in making footwear. Instead of letting certain materials go to waste, they are carefully reused or repurposed in creative ways. This not only reduces environmental impact but also adds uniqueness to the designs.

Then there’s how work is done. Materials are used carefully, waste is reduced, and processes are improved so the business becomes more efficient over time.

Finally, customers keep coming back because of quality, comfort, and trust, which helps the business grow steadily on its own.

So in simple terms, it stays sustainable because it has multiple income sources, trains people, runs a creative hub for innovation, reuses waste materials responsibly, works efficiently, and builds strong customer loyalty.

problem:
Shopping for clothes online is a broken experience for both everyday shoppers and fashion designers.
1. The Customers: Many consumers are hesitant to buy clothes online because they prefer physical stores where they have the assurance of a fitting room. Without trying things on, shoppers face sizing inconsistencies and cannot visualize how a garment will look on their specific body type. This guesswork causes massive hesitation before purchasing.  
2. The Retailers: Because customers cannot accurately judge the fit, online fashion retailers suffer from incredibly high return rates.  
3. The Designers: Independent fashion designers and smaller clothing brands want to fix this, but they face a major technological barrier. 

They lack the capital and technical expertise needed to develop their own proprietary Augmented Reality (AR) or virtual try-on software to showcase their lines.  Ultimately, shoppers lose the convenience of digital retail due to a lack of confidence, while small creators lose out on sales because they cannot afford the high-tech tools needed to compete.
solution:
Ready2Wear.ng is a smart, two-sided fashion technology platform that bridges the gap between shoppers and designers.

1. For Shoppers (ready2wear.ng): We are creating a curated B2C marketplace featuring a wide array of ready-to-wear outfits. It features a "Virtual Fitting Room" powered by rtw.ai. Shoppers can use their smartphone cameras or upload a photo to see a realistic overlay of a dress on their body. This removes the guesswork, giving users the confidence to buy.
2. For Designers (r2w.ai): We provide an affordable SaaS and marketplace solution for independent fashion designers. Designers can easily create a vendor account to upload their 2D or 3D clothing designs. They get instant access to our advanced AR try-on infrastructure without needing technical expertise or heavy capital.

Additionally, the platform provides designers with data and analytics. By seeing which items are tried on the most, creators can forecast trends and manage their inventory effectively. This powerful combination boosts digital sales, cuts down high return rates, and gives smaller brands a premium shopping experience.
mvpDescription:
Our MVP integrates:
1. AR Frontend and E-commerce Backend: We have successfully connected the user-facing virtual try-on features with a functional digital marketplace system.
2. Live r2w.ai Engine: Built using established AR frameworks, the engine actively processes and realistically overlays 3–5 sample dresses onto users' bodies.
3. Dual-Sided Web Interfaces: The system seamlessly connects a live e-commerce storefront for shoppers on ready2wear.ng with a dedicated vendor dashboard for fashion designers.
4. Beta Tester Ecosystem: A working platform configured for our initial cohort of 10 onboarded local fashion designers who are actively beta testing the system.
tractionMetric:
1. SaaS Subscription Sign-ups: The total number of onboarded designers who convert from the free tier to a paid monthly or annual subscription (Basic or Premium Tiers) to use the rtw.ai infrastructure.
2. AR Try-On Conversion Rate: The percentage of shoppers on readytowear.ng who make a purchase after using the virtual fitting room feature compared to those who do not.
3. Return Rate Reduction: The percentage decrease in garment returns from orders that utilized the rtw.ai virtual try-on tool.
4. Marketplace Transaction Volume (GMV): The total value and volume of successful clothing sales processed through the platform, which directly drives our marketplace commission revenue.
5. Promoted Listing Adoption: The number of independent designers actively paying to have their clothing collections featured on the homepage or at the top of search results.
6. Item Upload Velocity: The total number of clothing designs uploaded by vendors for AR processing, showing active backend utility.
teamExpertise:
1. Esosa Aimienoho, CEO: steers the overall platform direction and market positioning, leveraging firsthand expertise as a professional fashion designer to acquire local creators as early adopters.
2. Joseph Origho, CTO: Directs the technical development of the rtw.ai engine and marketplace backend, drawing on Google AR expertise, a B.Eng. in Electrical Electronics, and leadership as GDG Benin Lead.
3. Gift Favour, Tech Support & Onboarding: Manages the hands-on setup, technical troubleshooting, and feedback collection for early adopter designers navigating the platform.
challenges:
1. Making the AR Technology Scale: While our r2w.ai engine works perfectly for our 3–5 sample dresses, our biggest engineering hurdle is making the process automatic. Turning a designer’s physical or 2D clothing patterns into high-quality 3D digital outfits that look real and fit different body types takes a lot of time and computing power, which costs a lot of money for cloud services.

2. Helping Designers Use the Tech: Many local fashion designers and tailors are incredibly talented at making clothes, but they are not used to complex tech tools. Onboarding them onto a digital dashboard, teaching them to upload accurate sizing data, and helping them manage online inventory requires training and support.

3. Changing How People Shop: Getting everyday shoppers to trust a virtual fitting room instead of a real physical dressing room is a major shift in human behavior. We must make sure the smartphone camera overlay is incredibly accurate so customers feel completely confident that what they see on screen will fit them perfectly in real life.
fundUsage:
We will use the ₦5M grant to move from our ready MVP to a fully commercial platform across three key areas:
1. AR Engine & Infrastructure (₦2M): We will upgrade the rtw.ai engine to automate how clothing designs are converted into 3D virtual outfits. These funds provide the cloud computing power and advanced software tools needed to process hundreds of designer clothes quickly and accurately.  

2. Designer Onboarding & Support (₦1.5M): We will set up a dedicated onboarding hub to help our initial cohort of 10–15 local fashion designers transition smoothly. This budget covers hands-on training, creating simple step-by-step video guides, and providing physical logistics support to help them digitize their inventories.  
3. Marketing & User Acquisition (₦1.5M): We will launch targeted online campaigns to drive fashion-forward shoppers to the ready2wear.ng marketplace. This includes working with local fashion influencers to showcase the virtual fitting room in action, proving to everyday buyers that the technology works.  This funding will directly help us turn a technical prototype into a thriving, trusted ecosystem for both creators and shoppers.
growthTargets:
1. Month 1–3: Beta Launch & Optimization: Successfully onboard our initial cohort of 10 local fashion designers onto the live platform. We aim to successfully process at least 50 unique clothing designs through the r2w.ai engine and gather deep feedback from our early users to refine the system.  

2. Month 4–6: Commercial Expansion: Scale our vendor network to 100+ independent fashion designers and local tailors transitioning to ready-to-wear. During this phase, we target launching our tiered subscription packages (Basic and Premium) to start generating steady SaaS revenue. 

3.  Month 7–12: Market Scaling & Traction: Drive consumer adoption on ready2wear.ng to reach over 5,000 active shoppers. Our ultimate target is to process over 2,000 successful marketplace transactions and maintain a garment return rate under 5% by leveraging our virtual try-on technology.
revenueModel:
Our revenue model uses a hybrid structure that combines business-to-business (B2B) software services with a business-to-consumer (B2C) e-commerce marketplace:

1. SaaS Subscription Tiers (B2B): Independent fashion designers pay a monthly or annual subscription fee to use the r2w.ai infrastructure. The Basic Tier grants access to standard 3D garment rendering tools, while the Premium Tier offers advanced analytics, unlimited item uploads, and custom sizing configurations.
2. Marketplace Commission (B2C): We charge a percentage-based transaction fee on every successful clothing sale processed through the ready2wear.ng marketplace. This model ensures our revenue scales directly alongside our vendors' sales volumes.
3. Promoted Listing Fees: Designers can pay an extra advertising fee to feature their collections on the homepage banner or at the top of category search results, giving them higher visibility among active shoppers.
socialImpact:
Our platform helps the local creative economy grow in three main ways:
1. Increasing Income for Local Creators: We give independent fashion designers and tailors simple digital tools to sell ready-made clothes online. This helps small businesses find more customers, grow their sales, and make more money.
2. Creating New Tech Jobs: We are bringing brand new, well-paying tech jobs to the local area—like 3D digital art assistants and tech support specialists—while helping traditional tailors learn useful digital skills.
3. Cutting Down on Fabric Waste: Because our r2w.ai virtual fitting room helps people pick the exact right size, customers return fewer clothes. This means less wasted fabric and a cleaner environment.
sustainabilityPath:
We will become self-sustaining by focusing on low running costs and steady revenue from our two main services:
1. SaaS Subscription Income: Once the ₦5M grant period ends, our main income will come from monthly subscription fees paid by fashion designers to use our r2w.ai tech tools. This gives us a predictable, steady cash flow every month to cover our software and cloud server costs.
2. Marketplace Sales Fees: We take a small commission fee from every clothing sale made on ready2wear.ng. As more shoppers use the platform and order clothes, our transaction revenue grows naturally without increasing our operational costs.
3. Low Overhead Costs: Because our core team is small and we use automated cloud software to process the 3D outfits, our daily business expenses are very low. This means we only need a small number of active monthly transactions to completely cover our bills and break even.

startupName: Gokleen Cleaning and maintenance services ltd
problem:
In Edo State, poor sanitation and youth unemployment exist side by side, but rarely are they addressed as one connected problem.

While households and businesses struggle to access reliable, professional cleaning services, thousands of young people remain unemployed or trapped in informal work with no structure, training, or growth pathway.

The cleaning and environmental maintenance sector, capable of absorbing large numbers of entry-level workers and improving public health, remains largely informal, unregulated, and underutilized as an economic opportunity.

It is as a result of this gap that Gokleen Cleaning and Maintenance Services was born, built to professionalize the industry, improve sanitation standards, and create structured employment pathways for young people in Edo State.

This gap means communities continue to face avoidable hygiene and sanitation challenges, while young people miss out on a scalable, skill-based industry that could provide dignified employment and long-term economic inclusion.
solution:
Gokleen was created to directly address the gap between poor sanitation standards and youth unemployment in Edo State by building a structured, professional, and scalable cleaning ecosystem.

We provide reliable, eco-friendly cleaning and maintenance services to homes, offices, and corporate organizations using trained personnel and standardized service systems that improve hygiene outcomes and customer experience.

Beyond service delivery, Gokleen functions as a skills and employment pipeline. We recruit and train young people, especially unemployed youths, equipping them with practical cleaning, environmental hygiene, customer service, and operational skills needed to work professionally in the industry.

Through this model, we are gradually transforming cleaning from an informal survival job into a structured employment sector that promotes dignity of work, environmental responsibility, and income generation.

With increased support, we will expand our training capacity through a cleaning academy, scale our equipment base, and increase the number of youths we can train and employ across Edo State.
mvpDescription:
The Gokleen MVP is an active cleaning service that delivers professional, eco-friendly cleaning for homes and businesses using trained youth teams. Operations run through a simple booking system via phone and WhatsApp, with services executed using standardized procedures and supervised field teams.

The MVP combines two functions: providing reliable cleaning services to paying clients and training unemployed youths through hands-on work experience.

Customers receive consistent, high-quality cleaning services, while youths are trained, deployed, and paid within a structured system. This model validates demand for professional cleaning services while proving that unemployed youths can be effectively trained and employed in a scalable cleaning system.
tractionMetric:
Number of clients served and youth employed through structured cleaning services.

Currently, Gokleen has served 100+ residential and commercial clients, demonstrating consistent demand for professional cleaning services.

In addition, traction is also measured through:

Number of cleaning jobs completed monthly
Number of repeat clients (customer retention)
Number of unemployed youths trained and actively deployed into paid cleaning work

This combination shows both market validation (clients) and social impact (youth employment), which reflects the dual-purpose nature of the business model.
teamExpertise:
The Gokleen team brings together a blend of operational experience, technical expertise, and strategic oversight. The founder provides leadership in business development, management consulting, entrepreneurship, and environmental sustainability, with formal certifications in management consulting and environmental management. She has practical experience building and restructuring service-based businesses and leading community impact initiatives.

The team also includes an industrial chemist who supports product and process quality assurance, particularly in the use and handling of cleaning agents, ensuring safety, effectiveness, and eco-friendly standards in service delivery.

In addition, Gokleen is guided by a Board of Directors with over 50 years of combined experience across business management, operations, and organizational development, providing strategic direction, governance, and long-term growth oversight. Operational execution is handled by trained cleaning personnel recruited and developed internally through a structured, hands-on training system focused on professional cleaning standards, hygiene practices, and customer service.

Together, this structure combines strategic governance, technical quality assurance, and ground-level execution capacity to ensure both service excellence and scalable impact.
challenges:
The primary challenge at this stage is limited access to funding required to fully scale operations. This affects the ability to acquire additional professional cleaning equipment, expand the workforce, and increase service coverage across more locations.

Secondly, the demand for structured training systems in the cleaning industry is high, but current capacity limits how many unemployed youths can be trained and deployed at the same time. This creates a gap between existing demand for services and available trained personnel. In addition, customer acquisition and expansion into larger corporate contracts require stronger visibility, systems, and operational capacity than the business currently has at its present stage.

Despite these constraints, the existing model remains functional, tested, and generating consistent service delivery and employment at a small scale.
fundUsage:

Economically, the business generates direct income for youths through paid cleaning jobs while also improving productivity for households and businesses by providing reliable, professional cleaning services. This helps formalize a previously informal sector and increases the value of environmental services within the local economy.

At community level, improved access to structured cleaning services contributes to better sanitation, healthier environments, and improved hygiene standards across residential and commercial spaces.

To strengthen delivery and impact, Gokleen collaborates with key stakeholders including the Edo State Waste Management Board, Junior Chamber International (JCI) Edo Bronze, and the University of Benin (UNIBEN). Overall, the model delivers a dual impact: youth employment creation and improved environmental hygiene, reinforcing sustainable social and economic development in Edo State.
sustainabilityPath:
