problem:
Access to affordable, hygienic and well-packaged agro-products in many communities in Nigeria, especially among low and middle income households, remains a major challenge. Consumers face problems such as lack of food preservation, inconsistency in quality of products, inflated prices due to numerous middlemen, and lack of availability of reliable local agro-products.

Many local farmers and small-scale agro producers face challenges such as poor access to markets, post-harvest losses, inadequate packaging systems and low profitability. This results in food wastage, lower income for farmers and unstable food supply chains.

Therefore, the demand for a dependable agro-business that can connect the gap between local producers and consumers by supplying quality, affordable, accessible, well-packaged and efficiently delivered agro-products is increasing.
solution:
Heebah Agro-Products is building a modern agro-distribution and food supply business that focuses on sourcing, processing, packaging, and delivering quality agricultural products to households, retailers, restaurants and corporate clients.

Our solution: to build a trusted agro-products brand that connects local farmers directly to consumers whilst reducing post-harvest losses and increasing access to food. Our expertise lies in hygienic packing, quality control, affordable prices and quick distribution of grains, food products and other farm produce.

Heebah Agro-Products will use technology, social media marketing and structured logistics to provide easier access to quality food products and empower local farmers with better market opportunities and more revenue.

The grant funding will allow us to:

grow product sourcing and inventory, upgrade packaging and branding, purchase processing/storage equipment, enhance distribution and delivery, generate jobs for young people, and expand operations to serve more customers efficiently.

In the long term, we aspire to be a trusted agro-products brand that contributes to food security, youth employment and sustainable agricultural growth in Nigeria.
mvpDescription:
Heebah Agro-Products currently operates a basic, but functional agro-products supply and distribution system serving individual customers and small businesses. Our MVP entails sourcing quality agricultural products from local farmers and suppliers to be packaged hygienically and supplied to customers through direct sales, WhatsApp orders, referrals and social media channels.

Customers may:

order food and agricultural products, buy in bulk or retail, order delivery services, have access to affordable and quality products, and get customer support through our digital communication channels.
Our MVP also features:

sourcing products and managing inventory, basic packaging and branding, customer order management, local delivery management and online customer communication through WhatsApp and social media.

We have already tested market demand through early customer sales and positive customer feedback, showing strong potential for growth and expansion.
tractionMetric:
The main traction indicator that we use to measure traction is an increase in the number of repeat customers and monthly sales of products made directly, through referrals, and via customer engagement activities online.

Following the launch of our MVP, Heebah Agro-Products has been able to secure:

repeated customer purchases,
rising demand for agro-products and food supply products,
greater customer engagement via WhatsApp and social media platforms,
and rising sales per month via referral marketing and local sales.

Currently, our traction indicators include:

monthly customer base size,
repeat purchase rate,
monthly order volumes,
monthly customer referrals, and
monthly revenue growth.
teamExpertise:
Heebah Agro-Products has a team with relevant experience in sourcing of agro products, retail services, customer services, sales, and general management of businesses. Our team is well conversant with local markets, distribution of food items, customer management, and small business management.

Experience includes:

Sourcing of quality agro products from dependable suppliers and local farmers,
Product management and inventory control,
Sales at retail and wholesale levels,
Customer engagement and digital marketing using WhatsApp and social media,
Logistics management,
and Record keeping.
challenges:
The greatest challenges that we are facing at the moment include:

shortage of money for product acquisition on a large scale,
lack of adequate storage and processing machinery,
limited packaging and brand labeling capabilities,
transport limitations, and
shortage of working capital to facilitate expansion and increased sales volumes.
Apart from these, challenges in distribution, efficiency improvement without raising prices, and sustaining quality are also some of the issues faced by the company.

Despite these challenges, customer demand shows great promise for Heebah Agro-Products.
fundUsage:
The Naira five million grant will be utilized to strengthen the operations of Heebah Agro-Products in the following ways:

Product procurement and inventory – purchasing agro-products in large numbers from farmers and suppliers at a lower cost.
Processing and storage facilities – processing the products to help prevent loss of quality.
Packaging and branding – developing high-quality packaging that would ensure hygiene, attractiveness, and marketability of the product.
Distribution channels – improving the product distribution channels and ensuring that there is increased accessibility to more markets eg \purchase of bikes for delivery.
Digital marketing – building the brand image and increasing the reach to many other customers using the internet.
Employment and training opportunities – hiring and training youth for sales, packaging, logistics, and business operations.
growthTargets:
In the next 12 months, Heebah Agro-Products plans to:

increase customer base by over 200% through better marketing and distribution,
develop strong collaborations with local farmers and suppliers,
increase product lines and inventory space,
improve the quality of our packaging and branding,
provide jobs for young people both directly and indirectly, and
increase our monthly sales and income greatly.

Our other goals include improving our online marketing, making deliveries more efficient, and increasing our market presence in more local areas of Nigeria.
revenueModel:
The sources of income for Heebah Agro-Products include the following:

sales in retail for agro-products and foods,
bulk supplies for industries, retailers, and consumers,
packaging and delivery of products,
and placing orders by customers online and offline.

We strive to acquire products directly from farmers and suppliers for affordable costs, provide our services of packaging and delivery efficiently, and sell products with profitable margins.

With growth in our business, we are planning to venture into bulk supplies for restaurants, hotels, retailers, and food sellers.
socialImpact:
Heebah Agro-Products aims at making positive contributions in society by:

assisting local farmers in accessing markets,
minimizing wastage of harvested produce through efficient storage and transportation,
ensuring availability of quality food products,
providing jobs for the young generation,
promoting agriculture among locals,
and contributing to the security of food sources.

The enterprise encourages entrepreneurship and empowerment by improving the agricultural value chain and promoting local trade.
sustainabilityPath:
The Heebah Agro-Products venture is intended to be sustainable through scalability and profitability. The following are components of our sustainability approach:

reinvestment of profits for business growth,
developing sustainable relationships with suppliers and customers,
entering wholesale and bulk markets,
enhancing efficiency through improved equipment and logistics,
and adopting digital marketing for consistent customer growth.

In our efforts to provide high-quality, competitively-priced, and dependable services to our customers, we hope to create a customer base that ensures sustainability and profitability beyond the period of the grant.

problem:
‎In Nigeria, waste disposal is largely unstructured.
‎Even in places where waste management authorities exist, there are no clear, accessible systems that guide how individuals should dispose of waste daily. As a result, littering becomes normalized  on roads, in hostels, and in public spaces.
‎The problem is not just collection, it’s the absence of simple, consistent structures that people can interact with.
‎Without that structure, even well-intentioned efforts fail, and accountability is lost at the individual level.
solution:
GreenFlare introduces a structured, ground-level system for waste disposal starting from high-density environments like university hostels.
Instead of relying only on centralized waste collection, we deploy clearly designated bins (plastics, sachets, general waste) in strategic locations where people actually live and move.
The system is simple:
– Use a designated bin
– Submit that action through a lightweight digital interface
– Build consistent disposal behavior over time
By combining physical structure with simple coordination, GreenFlare turns waste disposal from an afterthought into a consistent, visible habit.
The pilot at the University of Benin is designed to prove that when structure exists, behavior follows.
mvpDescription:
Our MVP is a functional web-based platform that supports user onboarding and action submission.
Users can create accounts, connect to their environment, and log waste-related actions through a simple, accessible interface. The platform is already operational and designed to track participation, usage patterns, and behavior change in real time.
The physical bin system is the next layer of deployment and will be implemented during the University of Benin pilot. This includes strategically placed, clearly labeled bins for different waste types across selected hostel areas.
With the digital infrastructure already built, the grant enables immediate transition from platform readiness to full system activation, combining digital tracking with real-world waste disposal.
tractionMetric:
Primary metric (pre-pilot):
– Number of users onboarded and submitting waste-related actions on the platform
Primary metric (during pilot):
– Number of consistent waste disposal actions carried out through designated bins within the University of Benin pilot environment
Supporting metrics:
– Number of active participants
– Frequency of usage per participant
– Reduction of visible waste in targeted hostel areas
teamExpertise:
‎Our team is focused on building practical systems that work within the realities of Nigerian environments, not ideal assumptions.
‎We combine product development with on-ground observation and engagement. We’ve built a working MVP that supports onboarding and action submission, and we’ve begun early engagement within the University of Benin community to understand how waste is currently handled in hostels and shared spaces.
‎This approach allows us to design around real behavior, where people actually dispose waste, how often, and why systems fail and build a solution that people can consistently use in their daily lives.
challenges:
‎– Absence of structured waste disposal systems in high-density areas like hostels and campuses
‎– Funding the first deployment of clearly designated waste bins
‎– Changing normalized behavior where littering is seen as the default
‎– Weak coordination between individuals, communities, and waste management operators
‎The key challenge is moving from idea to visible execution proving that when simple structure is introduced, behavior can change at scale.
fundUsage:
The ₦5M grant will be used to set up and validate GreenFlare as a working waste participation system, beginning with a structured pilot at the University of Benin. The goal is not only to place bins, but to build the operational, behavioral, and digital foundation needed for a repeatable system that can later expand to other campuses and communities.
1. Physical bin system design, fabrication, and installation — ₦1,800,000
This covers the first set of clearly designated bins for plastics, sachets, and general waste, including fabrication, branding/labeling, and installation in selected pilot locations. The bins are central to the system because they create the physical structure people will interact with daily.
2. Pilot deployment and field operations — ₦900,000
This covers local coordination, movement, setup support, supervision, and early-stage field operations during the pilot. It includes the cost of deploying the system within the University of Benin environment and ensuring it is actively managed rather than left unattended.
3. Product development and platform improvement — ₦850,000
Although the web platform is already functional, this funding will help improve stability, onboarding, submission flow, admin visibility, and pilot-readiness. This ensures the digital side can properly support real users and capture usable participation data once the physical system is live.
4. Community onboarding, education, and awareness — ₦550,000
Behavior change requires deliberate engagement. This budget covers awareness materials, simple education campaigns, local activation within the target community, and onboarding efforts that help people understand how to use the designated bins and why the system matters.
5. Waste monitoring, collection coordination, and recycling linkage — ₦450,000
This covers early monitoring and coordination around how waste moves after disposal, including support for collection handling and engagement with local recycling/waste operators where possible. The system has to work beyond the point of disposal, not just end at the bin.
6. Measurement, reporting, and pilot documentation — ₦250,000
This covers documentation of pilot usage, impact reporting, early data gathering, and proof of execution. It will help us measure participation, track behavior patterns, and produce evidence needed for future institutional and sponsor conversations.
7. Contingency and operational buffer — ₦200,000
This is reserved for unforeseen operational costs during setup and deployment, especially in a real-world environment where logistics and installation costs can shift.
Total — ₦5,000,000
Detailed budget summary
Physical bin system design, fabrication, and installation — ₦1,800,000
Pilot deployment and field operations — ₦900,000
Product development and platform improvement — ₦850,000
Community onboarding, education, and awareness — ₦550,000
Waste monitoring, collection coordination, and recycling linkage — ₦450,000
Measurement, reporting, and pilot documentation — ₦250,000
Contingency and operational buffer — ₦200,000
Total — ₦5,000,000
Why this use of funds matters
This funding will allow GreenFlare move from an early-stage platform into a visible, working system with physical infrastructure, community usage, and measurable results. Instead of funding only software or only bins, the grant sets up the full loop: structured disposal points, user participation, operational coordination, and data-backed proof that the model can work in a Nigerian environment.
growthTargets:
– Successfully deploy and run the University of Benin hostel pilot
– Onboard 200–500 active participants within the pilot phase
– Achieve consistent daily use of designated bins in selected locations
– Expand to additional hostels or a second campus environment
– Establish at least one working partnership with a local waste/recycling operator
The focus is not rapid expansion, but proving a working model that can be replicated.
revenueModel:
GreenFlare is designed to operate as a structured waste management service, not just a pilot initiative.
Short-term (pilot phase):
The system is supported by grants and institutional partnerships to enable initial deployment and validation within the University of Benin.
Early revenue (within pilot and immediately after):
– Service fees from hostels and private property managers for maintaining structured waste disposal systems (bin placement, monitoring, and coordination)
– Subscription-based waste coordination for estates where property owners pay for organized waste infrastructure and oversight
Mid-term revenue (post-validation):
– Institutional contracts with universities, hostels, and residential estates to deploy and manage structured waste systems
– Sponsored waste infrastructure (brands fund bin deployment in exchange for visibility and environmental positioning)
– Recycling partnerships, where GreenFlare earns from facilitating access to cleaner, better-sorted recyclable waste streams
Long-term model:
GreenFlare operates as a coordination and infrastructure layer for decentralized waste systems across Nigerian communities—earning through service contracts, system deployment fees, and data-driven waste coordination.
The goal is to transition from grant-supported deployment to a self-sustaining, service-based model driven by institutions and property stakeholders who directly benefit from cleaner, more organized environments.
socialImpact:
‎GreenFlare addresses one of the most visible and persistent problems in Nigerian communities unstructured waste disposal.
‎By introducing simple, designated systems in high-density environments like university hostels, we reduce indiscriminate dumping and improve cleanliness at the community level.
‎The model also creates opportunities for local engagement, small-scale jobs, and better coordination with recycling operators.
‎Over time, this shifts waste disposal from a neglected issue into a structured, repeatable system that communities can sustain.
sustainabilityPath:
GreenFlare is designed to transition from a grant-supported pilot into a self-sustaining, service-driven system.
Following the University of Benin pilot, the model will generate revenue through structured service agreements with hostels, private estates, and property managers who require organized waste disposal systems. These stakeholders already incur costs dealing with poor sanitation, making GreenFlare a practical and cost-effective solution.
The system will operate on a recurring service model, where clients pay for bin deployment, monitoring, and coordination of waste handling. This ensures predictable revenue while maintaining system quality.
In parallel, GreenFlare will establish partnerships with recycling operators who benefit from cleaner, better-sorted waste streams, creating an additional value layer within the system.
Sponsorship opportunities will also support expansion, with organizations funding waste infrastructure in exchange for environmental visibility within high-traffic communities such as university campuses.
By combining service fees, institutional partnerships, and recycling-linked value, GreenFlare moves from pilot execution to a repeatable, revenue-generating system that can scale across campuses, estates, and urban communities in Nigeria.
The long-term sustainability of the model is driven by the fact that clean, organized environments are a continuous need, and stakeholders are willing to pay for systems that reliably provide them.
